boston-scientific-cyberattack.text: boston scientific says cyberattack could hit its 2026 outlook the marlborough-based medical-device maker said an august incident disrupted parts of its global operations and made its prior forecast harder to meet. boston scientific said tuesday that it is unlikely to meet previously issued third-quarter and full-year 2026 sales and adjusted-profit forecasts after a cyberattack disrupted global operations. reuters reported that the unauthorized activity was identified august 25 and caused network outages that affected manufacturing and order processing. the company said major distribution and manufacturing operations have resumed, while the full financial impact remains uncertain. the company had previously forecast 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.28 to $3.32 per share and sales growth of 5.5% to 6.5%. it plans to provide an updated outlook with third-quarter results in october. the incident is a reminder that cybersecurity risk can move quickly from an information-technology problem into a supply-chain and earnings issue for massachusetts manufacturers. new-england ma marlborough marlborough, ma massachusetts cybersecurity business healthcare

breaking-afghan-woman-first-terrorism-re.excerpt: The Justice Department used a court created in 1996 for the first time to remove a lawful permanent resident accused of helping conceal a terrorism plot.
breaking-afghan-woman-first-terrorism-re.text: u.s. deports afghan woman in first use of terrorism removal court the justice department used a court created in 1996 for the first time to remove a lawful permanent resident accused of helping conceal a terrorism plot. a 47-year-old afghan woman who held lawful permanent residency in the united states has been deported in the first case pursued through the alien terrorist removal court, reuters reported friday. the little-used court was created in 1996 to handle government efforts to remove people accused of terrorism-related activity. the justice department accused nazira haji zada of helping conceal a failed islamic state-inspired plan for a mass shooting on election day 2024. she was not criminally charged. her son and son-in-law pleaded guilty in related cases. proceedings in the special court can include classified evidence that the person facing removal is not permitted to review, a structure her public defender challenged on due-process grounds. haji zada agreed last month to end her challenge and consent to removal. chief judge joan ericksen approved the request, clearing the way for deportation. her attorney said the agreement should not be read as an endorsement of the court or its procedures. the case establishes a new precedent for a tribunal that had not previously been used in the three decades since congress created it, and it may draw further legal scrutiny. breaking breaking breaking / developing us united states immigration alien terrorist removal court justice department national security deportation

breaking-algeria-cuts-uae-diplomatic-tie.excerpt: Algiers cited unspecified hostile actions, while the UAE said it hoped the rupture would be temporary.
breaking-algeria-cuts-uae-diplomatic-tie.text: algeria cuts diplomatic ties with united arab emirates algiers cited unspecified hostile actions, while the uae said it hoped the rupture would be temporary. algeria severed diplomatic relations with the united arab emirates on thursday, an abrupt rupture between two arab governments whose ties had been strained for years. the algerian government cited what it called provocative and hostile actions but did not specify the conduct behind the decision. it said efforts to preserve the relationship had been exhausted. algerian media have previously accused the uae of trying to sow discord, adding to an increasingly public dispute. the uae responded that it hoped the break would be temporary and said it remained committed to relations based on shared interests. the statement left open the possibility of future diplomatic engagement but did not announce a mediation effort or timeline. ending formal relations can affect ambassadorial representation and routine government coordination, though neither side immediately detailed the practical measures that would follow. the lack of a specific allegation from algiers also leaves the immediate trigger unclear. further statements will determine whether the decision expands into broader restrictions or remains a diplomatic protest. breaking breaking breaking / developing international algiers algiers, algeria algeria united arab emirates diplomacy middle east

breaking-anak-krakatau-journalists-missi.excerpt: A speedboat carrying five photojournalists, two crew members and a guide lost contact while traveling to report on the Indonesian volcano.
breaking-anak-krakatau-journalists-missi.text: search underway for eight missing near anak krakatau a speedboat carrying five photojournalists, two crew members and a guide lost contact while traveling to report on the indonesian volcano. indonesian rescuers are searching the sunda strait for eight people whose speedboat lost contact while traveling to anak krakatau to cover volcanic activity. the group includes five photojournalists, two crew members and a route guide, the associated press reported. the boat departed carita in banten province, and relatives received its last known message at 6:13 p.m. monday saying the group had reached waters near the island. their last reported position was about 18.5 kilometers, or roughly 11.5 miles, from shore. search teams deployed tuesday had not established contact or confirmed the boat’s location by early wednesday. the journalists work for several indonesian and international news organizations, with one described as a freelance photographer. anak krakatau’s initial eruption ended sunday, but the volcano has continued intermittent activity involving explosions, lava and ash. officials had not established whether that activity, weather, mechanical failure or another cause was connected to the disappearance. the search remains active, and early details may change as rescue crews cover the area and review communications. more breaking breaking / developing international carita sunda strait, indonesia indonesia anak krakatau search and rescue journalists

breaking-bahamas-plane-family-found-dead.excerpt: Relatives located the victims after launching a search for the small plane, which lost contact while flying toward Miami.
breaking-bahamas-plane-family-found-dead.text: relative says four family members found dead after bahamas plane disappeared relatives located the victims after launching a search for the small plane, which lost contact while flying toward miami. four members of a family aboard a small plane that disappeared off the bahamas were found dead tuesday, a relative told the associated press. silvia larrieu said relatives searching by boat recovered the bodies and were working with the u.s. coast guard to bring them home. the victims were mario lamar, 80; his wife, lili lamar, 79; and their grandchildren, sofi sosa, 28, and christian sosa, 22. the pa-34 piper left great harbour cay in the berry islands on monday morning for miami executive airport. bahamas police said air traffic control lost contact when the aircraft was about 13 miles west of andros island. family members alerted authorities after messages went undelivered and the expected arrival time passed. the coast guard sent an aircraft to assist after bahamian authorities requested help, although poor weather delayed parts of the search. the developing work now centers on recovery and the investigation into what caused the plane to go down. authorities had not announced a cause in the information available tuesday night. more international bahamas bahamas plane crash u.s. coast guard aviation

breaking-bangladesh-measles-outbreak-100.excerpt: Authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases as disrupted immunization and vaccine shortages fuel a fast-moving public-health emergency.
breaking-bangladesh-measles-outbreak-100.text: bangladesh measles outbreak nears 1,000 deaths authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases as disrupted immunization and vaccine shortages fuel a fast-moving public-health emergency. bangladesh is battling what the u.s. centers for disease control and prevention lists as the world’s largest current measles outbreak, with 999 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since march, reuters reported wednesday. authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases. of those, 19,835 were laboratory confirmed, while more than 146,000 people were hospitalized. the outbreak has spread as routine immunization was disrupted during 2024 and 2025 and vaccine shortages left gaps in protection. an emergency measles-rubella campaign has reached more than 19.7 million children. health specialists say catch-up vaccination and restoration of routine immunization remain essential because a one-time campaign cannot fully repair missed doses or stop continued transmission. hospitals are also managing dengue cases, adding pressure to staff and beds. the death and case counts can change as records are reviewed, but the scale already shows how quickly measles can spread when vaccination coverage falls. measles is highly contagious, and outbreaks can become especially dangerous for young children and people with limited access to care. breaking breaking breaking / developing international dhaka bangladesh bangladesh measles vaccination public health

breaking-belgorod-drone-attacks-two-dead.excerpt: Regional authorities reported fatalities in Novy Oskol and Shebekino as attacks continued across Russia’s border region.
breaking-belgorod-drone-attacks-two-dead.text: two killed, seven injured in belgorod drone attacks, officials say regional authorities reported fatalities in novy oskol and shebekino as attacks continued across russia’s border region. two people were killed and seven were injured in drone attacks across russia’s belgorod region, regional authorities said thursday, in the latest reported violence along the border with ukraine. officials said one man died when a drone detonated at an unspecified facility in novy oskol. five people were reported injured in attacks across several other localities. in shebekino, another man was killed when a drone struck a car, while a woman traveling in the vehicle was injured. belgorod has been repeatedly targeted during the war because of its proximity to the ukrainian border. the initial report did not provide a complete account of property damage, identify all of the injured or establish whether military sites were among the targets. the casualty figures and circumstances were reported by russian regional authorities and could not be independently verified in the immediate account. responsibility was attributed to ukrainian drones by those officials. the situation remains developing, and later reports may revise the number of casualties or add details about the locations struck. breaking breaking breaking / developing russia belgorod belgorod region, russia belgorod russia ukraine drone attacks

breaking-borneo-haze-flights-forest-fire.excerpt: Smoke from fires in West Kalimantan disrupted flights for several days as thick haze reduced visibility and raised air-quality concerns.
breaking-borneo-haze-flights-forest-fire.text: thick haze disrupts flights on indonesia’s borneo island smoke from fires in west kalimantan disrupted flights for several days as thick haze reduced visibility and raised air-quality concerns. thick haze from fires disrupted flights for several days on indonesia’s portion of borneo, the associated press reported monday. visibility in parts of west kalimantan fell below one kilometer, creating problems for aircraft operations and worsening conditions for residents. the fires have burned for about a month during a prolonged dry period. more than 202,000 hectares were reported burned across indonesia from january through july, according to the ap report. smoke has also prompted school suspensions in other areas as officials monitor pollution levels. firefighters have been working to contain the outbreaks, with international support involved in the response. the flight disruptions and reduced visibility remained developing conditions, and authorities continued to assess where the smoke was thickest and how the fires were spreading. air travelers were advised to check with carriers because conditions can change quickly when smoke and visibility shift. officials continued to monitor the affected airports as the haze moved. breaking breaking breaking / developing west kalimantan west kalimantan, indonesia indonesia borneo west kalimantan forest fires

breaking-brics-adopts-new-delhi-declarat.excerpt: The 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict.
breaking-brics-adopts-new-delhi-declarat.text: brics unanimously adopts new delhi declaration on middle east war the 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict. brics leaders unanimously adopted the new delhi declaration on saturday, expressing deep concern about the middle east war and calling for maximum restraint. the formal adoption converts an earlier agreement among negotiators into the 10-member group’s official summit position. the statement advocates a multilateral approach that respects national viewpoints and reiterates support for settling international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. reaching consensus carried added significance because the expanded bloc includes both iran and the united arab emirates, a close u.s. partner, while the united states and iran have resumed exchanges of strikes after an august pause. the declaration also raised concern about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort trade, against a backdrop of u.s. sanctions on iran and russia. brics now includes brazil, russia, india, china, south africa, egypt, ethiopia, indonesia, iran and the uae. the declaration provides a common diplomatic text, but implementation will depend on whether members can translate broad calls for restraint into coordinated action. breaking breaking breaking / developing international new delhi new delhi, india brics new delhi middle east diplomacy

breaking-brics-joint-declaration-deal-20.excerpt: Negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it Saturday.
breaking-brics-joint-declaration-deal-20.text: brics reaches joint-declaration deal despite middle east divisions negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it saturday. brics negotiators reached agreement on a joint declaration saturday as leaders began summit talks in new delhi, according to four sources familiar with the discussions. the reported deal is a significant test of the expanded group’s ability to maintain consensus while members iran and the united arab emirates remain divided over the gulf conflict. the sources said the draft was unlikely to name any country but would condemn unilateral aggression. leaders were expected to consider the document later saturday. india’s foreign ministry did not immediately comment on the reported agreement. host prime minister narendra modi opened the summit by urging members to turn their shared positions into concrete results and renewed his call for reform of the united nations security council. a brics foreign ministers’ meeting in may ended without a joint statement because members could not bridge their differences. the declaration therefore represents a diplomatic advance even before final approval. brics is also seeking greater influence over international financial and trade institutions. details may change as leaders debate and approve the final text. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india brics new delhi summit india middle east diplomacy

breaking-brussels-airport-drone-traffic-.excerpt: Runway operations paused under a safety procedure that keeps traffic stopped until 30 minutes after the last sighting.
breaking-brussels-airport-drone-traffic-.text: drone sighting halts brussels airport traffic for about 30 minutes runway operations paused under a safety procedure that keeps traffic stopped until 30 minutes after the last sighting. air traffic at brussels airport was interrupted for about 30 minutes friday evening after a drone sighting, according to belgian air-traffic-control operator skeyes. runway operations resumed after the airport followed its established safety procedure for unauthorized aircraft near the airfield. the procedure pauses operations until 30 minutes after the most recent sighting, giving controllers and security authorities time to assess whether the airspace is clear. officials did not immediately disclose how many flights were delayed or diverted, and they released no details about the drone or its operator. the incident comes amid heightened concern in belgium over repeated unauthorized drone activity near airports and sensitive sites, including military facilities and a nuclear power plant. earlier episodes prompted the government to invest in counter-drone equipment. authorities have previously raised the possibility of foreign involvement in some sightings, but no evidence connecting friday’s event to any state or group was announced. although the immediate disruption ended, the lack of information about the drone leaves the security investigation open and underscores how even a short sighting can halt operations at a major international airport. breaking breaking breaking / developing belgium brussels brussels, belgium brussels airport drones aviation belgium

breaking-bukavu-school-fire-24-children-.excerpt: Officials said 19 girls and five boys were among the dead as flames also destroyed roughly 300 wooden homes in the rebel-held city.
breaking-bukavu-school-fire-24-children-.text: bukavu fire kills at least 24 children and destroys two schools officials said 19 girls and five boys were among the dead as flames also destroyed roughly 300 wooden homes in the rebel-held city. at least 24 children were killed when a fire tore through two schools and about 300 wooden homes in bukavu, a city in eastern democratic republic of congo controlled by afc/m23 rebels, a local official said thursday. the dead included 19 girls and five boys, according to south kivu’s vice governor in the rebel-appointed administration. twenty-nine people were reported injured, although accounts from hospitals and residents indicated that the toll could change as officials reconcile casualties. the fire was out by thursday afternoon, but smoke continued to rise from rubble and twisted roofing, a reuters witness reported. investigators had not determined the cause. bukavu has been under the control of the rwanda-backed afc/m23 movement since its rapid advance through eastern congo in 2025. that conflict complicates public administration and emergency response in a densely populated city. the immediate priorities are identifying victims, treating the injured, sheltering families whose homes were destroyed and establishing how flames spread into school buildings. officials and health workers cautioned that the death toll could rise, making this an active emergency with significant uncertainty around the final number of victims. breaking breaking breaking / developing international bukavu bukavu, democratic republic of congo bukavu school fire democratic republic of congo afc/m23

breaking-bulgaria-weapons-depot-explosio.excerpt: No injuries were reported after an overnight blast near Tsareva Livada, the second incident at a Bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks.
breaking-bulgaria-weapons-depot-explosio.text: explosion and fire spread through bulgarian weapons depot no injuries were reported after an overnight blast near tsareva livada, the second incident at a bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks. an explosion struck a weapons-storage site near tsareva livada in central bulgaria overnight, starting a fire that spread from one warehouse to another. authorities reported no injuries in the initial accounting. the incident is the second at a bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks, adding urgency to the investigation while firefighters and security officials assess the site. bulgarian media identified the facility as being operated by emco, an arms-trading company associated with businessman emilian gebrev. the cause of the latest blast had not been established in the early reports. that uncertainty is significant because bulgaria has previously investigated a series of explosions at facilities storing ammunition intended for ukraine and georgia. in 2024, bulgarian authorities issued warrants for six russian nationals accused in older depot explosions between 2011 and 2020 and linked those cases to an attempted poisoning. moscow denied the allegations. there was no announced evidence connecting the tsareva livada blast to those cases, and the current fire remains a developing event. the immediate verified facts are the explosion, the warehouse-to-warehouse spread and the absence of reported injuries. breaking breaking breaking / developing bulgaria tsareva livada tsareva livada, bulgaria bulgaria weapons depot explosion fire emco

breaking-burrillville-roof-collapse-2026.excerpt: Town officials are investigating after roof framing collapsed near Douglas Pike and Ironmine Road Tuesday afternoon.
breaking-burrillville-roof-collapse-2026.text: worker injured in burrillville construction-site roof collapse town officials are investigating after roof framing collapsed near douglas pike and ironmine road tuesday afternoon. a construction worker sustained a minor injury tuesday when the roof framework of a building under construction collapsed in burrillville, according to local authorities. burrillville police said the collapse happened at about 12:55 p.m. near douglas pike and ironmine road. wjar reported that one worker was hurt; officials did not report additional injuries or identify the worker. the town’s building inspector is expected to assess the site as authorities investigate why the framing failed. officials had not released the building’s intended use, the name of the contractor or details about how many people were present when the structure came down. the reported injury was minor, but a structural collapse can require the area to remain secured until inspectors determine whether other portions are stable. the cause remains unknown, and no violation or fault has been assigned. updates from the town, police and building inspector will determine whether construction can resume and whether additional safety review is needed. more ri burrillville, rhode island breaking rhode island burrillville construction

breaking-china-india-xi-modi-meeting-bri.excerpt: China’s foreign ministry says the neighboring powers are organizing bilateral talks as President Xi Jinping travels to India for the weekend gathering.
breaking-china-india-xi-modi-meeting-bri.text: china and india arrange xi-modi meeting ahead of brics summit china’s foreign ministry says the neighboring powers are organizing bilateral talks as president xi jinping travels to india for the weekend gathering. china and india are arranging a bilateral meeting between chinese president xi jinping and indian prime minister narendra modi, china’s foreign ministry said friday. the talks would take place around the brics summit in new delhi, where xi is scheduled to join other leaders this weekend. foreign ministry spokesperson mao ning said beijing is willing to approach relations with india from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication and cooperation, and manage differences. the statement did not provide a finalized time or agenda for the leaders’ meeting. xi is expected to address the brics gathering and hold broader exchanges with participating leaders about the international situation, according to the ministry. the summit gives china and india a multilateral setting for direct contact while both governments manage a relationship that combines substantial economic ties with persistent strategic disagreements. the development remains fluid because officials said the bilateral meeting was being organized rather than announcing a completed schedule. any outcome will depend on the talks themselves and on statements issued by the two governments afterward. the immediate confirmed development is that both sides are working toward leader-level discussions during xi’s visit to india. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india china india xi jinping narendra modi brics

breaking-congo-ebola-case-sud-ubangi-202.excerpt: A man who traveled from eastern Congo through Rwanda and Uganda tested positive after dying in northwestern Sud-Ubangi province.
breaking-congo-ebola-case-sud-ubangi-202.text: congo detects ebola case far from outbreak epicenter a man who traveled from eastern congo through rwanda and uganda tested positive after dying in northwestern sud-ubangi province. health officials in the democratic republic of congo confirmed an ebola infection in the northwestern province of sud-ubangi, far from the center of the country’s ongoing outbreak. the patient was a man who died tuesday in the town of gwaka, officials said friday. the man had traveled from south kivu in eastern congo through rwanda and uganda before re-entering congo and reaching sud-ubangi. congo’s national institute for biomedical research confirmed the positive test, according to reuters. authorities are tracing contacts because the patient used both road and river transport. local transmission has not been confirmed in sud-ubangi, so the province had not yet been added to the official list of affected areas at the time of the report. its borders with the republic of congo and central african republic add urgency to surveillance. the epidemic, first confirmed in mid-may, is congo’s 17th recorded ebola outbreak. government data cited by reuters listed 6,942 infections and 3,349 deaths. investigators must now determine where exposure occurred, identify fellow travelers and establish whether the case produced additional infections along the route. breaking breaking breaking / developing democratic republic of congo gwaka gwaka, democratic republic of congo ebola democratic republic of congo sud-ubangi public health outbreak

breaking-congo-ebola-seven-thousand-infe.excerpt: The Bundibugyo-virus outbreak has spread to seven provinces as health teams confront personnel, supply and funding shortages.
breaking-congo-ebola-seven-thousand-infe.text: congo ebola outbreak passes 7,000 confirmed infections the bundibugyo-virus outbreak has spread to seven provinces as health teams confront personnel, supply and funding shortages. confirmed ebola infections in the democratic republic of the congo have surpassed 7,000, with 3,398 deaths reported as the outbreak reaches seven provinces. the totals make it the country’s largest and deadliest ebola outbreak and the second-largest recorded globally after the 2014-2016 west africa epidemic. the outbreak involves the bundibugyo species of the virus. health officials confirmed a case in south ubangi province far from the original center: a 23-year-old man who had traveled from south kivu and later died. contact tracing is underway to identify people who may have been exposed during his travel or treatment, a priority because long-distance movement can establish new transmission chains. the world health organization has warned that the response is constrained by shortages of staff, partners and funding. rapidly rising figures also show how quickly the official picture is changing; a european disease tracker had listed 6,942 cases and 3,349 deaths one day earlier. authorities are trying to expand surveillance, isolation and contact monitoring while preventing additional provinces from becoming sustained centers of transmission. breaking breaking breaking / developing democratic republic of the congo kinshasa democratic republic of the congo ebola democratic republic of the congo who public health outbreak

breaking-dow-jones-hong-kong-union-convi.excerpt: A court found the Wall Street Journal publisher unlawfully blocked former reporter Selina Cheng from becoming a union officer, while acquitting it on a separate dismissal charge.
breaking-dow-jones-hong-kong-union-convi.text: hong kong court convicts dow jones over reporter’s union bid a court found the wall street journal publisher unlawfully blocked former reporter selina cheng from becoming a union officer, while acquitting it on a separate dismissal charge. a hong kong court convicted dow jones, publisher of the wall street journal, of willfully preventing former reporter selina cheng from exercising her right to become an officer of a trade union. reuters reported that the case was brought under hong kong’s trade unions ordinance. the court found against the company on the union-rights charge but acquitted it of unlawfully dismissing cheng, ruling that prosecutors had not excluded the company’s restructuring explanation beyond a reasonable doubt. cheng was elected chair of the hong kong journalists association in 2024. the case has drawn attention because it tests legal protections for labor organizing within an international news organization at a time of heightened concern about media freedom in hong kong. dow jones said it disagreed with the conviction and was evaluating its next steps. each charge carries a maximum fine of hk$100,000, and sentencing was expected later. the mixed verdict leaves both the labor-rights finding and the acquittal important: the court recognized an unlawful effort to block union participation while declining to find that the dismissal itself met the criminal standard. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl hong kong hong kong dow jones wall street journal hong kong press freedom

breaking-epa-power-plant-rule-repeal-202.excerpt: The agency says the rollback will cut industry costs, while environmental groups promise legal challenges and warn of broader pollution impacts.
breaking-epa-power-plant-rule-repeal-202.text: epa moves to repeal power-plant climate rule, setting up court fights the agency says the rollback will cut industry costs, while environmental groups promise legal challenges and warn of broader pollution impacts. the environmental protection agency said monday it is repealing rules that limit greenhouse-gas emissions from coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants, the associated press reported. the agency also proposed a separate step that could prevent future administrations from regulating climate pollution from power plants. the repeal is expected to take effect after publication in the federal register, and environmental groups are preparing legal challenges. the epa said the rollback would save industry more than $300 billion in costs and give utilities more flexibility in deciding how to supply electricity. environmental and public-health groups said removing the limits could increase pollution and harm communities. the associated press reported that coal, gas and oil-fired power plants account for about one-quarter of the nation’s climate pollution. the epa’s separate proposal is expected to be finalized next year if it survives the rulemaking process. the announcements came as epa and other u.s. energy officials hosted a g20 ministerial meeting in houston. the changes represent a major shift in federal power-plant regulation and are likely to remain contested in court and in congress. breaking breaking breaking/developing dc washington washington, d.c. breaking epa power plants climate policy

breaking-everett-city-hall-cyber-2026.excerpt: The city said its internal network and technology systems were affected Tuesday, while police, fire, schools, libraries and online payments continued operating.
breaking-everett-city-hall-cyber-2026.text: everett city hall closes after cybersecurity incident the city said its internal network and technology systems were affected tuesday, while police, fire, schools, libraries and online payments continued operating. everett city hall closed tuesday after the city announced a cybersecurity incident affecting its internal network and technology systems, boston 25 news reported. city officials said everett police, the fire department, the department of public works, public schools and libraries would operate as normal. online bill payments and third-party online transactions were not affected, according to the report. the city did not publicly identify the cause, the systems involved or whether information was accessed. everett officials said they were continuing to assess the incident and share updates as details emerged. the closure is a developing municipal disruption rather than a declaration about the incident’s ultimate scope. residents should rely on city updates for service changes while officials work to restore normal city hall operations and determine what protections are needed. municipal cyber incidents can affect routine services even when emergency response and public-facing operations continue, making clear status updates important for residents. more breaking breaking / developing ma everett everett, ma massachusetts everett cybersecurity municipal government

breaking-first-circuit-usps-mail-ballot-.excerpt: The Boston-based appeals court declined to pause an injunction against federal requirements involving voter lists and ballot barcodes before the November election.
breaking-first-circuit-usps-mail-ballot-.text: first circuit keeps block on new usps mail-ballot rule the boston-based appeals court declined to pause an injunction against federal requirements involving voter lists and ballot barcodes before the november election. a federal appeals court in boston declined thursday to let the u.s. postal service implement new mail-ballot requirements while litigation continues, leaving a lower-court injunction in place ahead of the november election. the rule would require states to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients and place unique barcodes on ballot envelopes. the postal service could refuse ballots that did not meet the requirements. a three-judge first circuit panel said election regulation belongs primarily to states and congress and cited the risk that voters could be disenfranchised if ballots were rejected. the justice department argued that the requirements were modest mail-processing regulations and asked the court to pause the injunction. the postal service has said it acted lawfully. states challenging the rule contend that the executive branch lacks authority to impose the conditions and that election systems cannot be reworked safely so close to voting. the administration has separately asked the supreme court to lift the injunction. thursday’s ruling does not resolve the underlying lawsuit; it determines which rules apply while the case proceeds. all 50 states permit mail voting in at least some circumstances. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states boston boston, ma first circuit usps mail ballots elections

breaking-first-us-horse-screwworm-case-t.excerpt: Animal-health authorities restricted movement in parts of two Texas counties after confirming the flesh-eating parasite in a working ranch horse.
breaking-first-us-horse-screwworm-case-t.text: first u.s. horse case of new world screwworm confirmed in texas animal-health authorities restricted movement in parts of two texas counties after confirming the flesh-eating parasite in a working ranch horse. the first confirmed u.s. horse case of new world screwworm has been detected in presidio county, texas, near the mexican border, according to federal and state animal-health information reported by reuters. the parasite's larvae feed on living tissue and can spread quickly through livestock and wildlife if wounds are not identified and treated. the texas animal health commission restricted movement of warm-blooded animals from an infested zone covering parts of presidio and jeff davis counties. the u.s. equestrian federation said the case involved a working ranch horse with an infestation in a hind limb. officials had not established the animal's origin in the initial report. the united states eradicated a major screwworm outbreak in the 1960s after thousands of livestock deaths. experts estimate that a widespread return could create as much as $1.8 billion in economic damage. animal-health authorities are urging owners to inspect animals regularly, treat wounds promptly, control flies and strengthen biosecurity. the confirmed horse infection is a developing agricultural-health event, and authorities have not announced evidence of broader u.s. transmission from this case. breaking breaking breaking / developing tx presidio county, texas new world screwworm texas horses livestock animal health

breaking-foxborough-i95-car-fire-2026.excerpt: A large vehicle fire temporarily closed two southbound lanes near Exit 18 Tuesday afternoon while officials worked at the scene.
breaking-foxborough-i95-car-fire-2026.text: car fire stalls afternoon traffic on i-95 in foxborough a large vehicle fire temporarily closed two southbound lanes near exit 18 tuesday afternoon while officials worked at the scene. a large car fire stalled afternoon traffic on interstate 95 south near exit 18 in foxborough tuesday, boston 25 news reported. the station said the fire call came in around 1:31 p.m. and that the right and middle southbound lanes were closed as crews responded. the report did not immediately identify the vehicle or say what caused the fire. traffic conditions were changing while emergency crews worked in the area. drivers approaching the foxborough stretch of i-95 should allow extra time and follow directions from police and transportation officials. the incident remained developing at the time of publication. additional information about injuries, the vehicle and the reopening of the lanes was not immediately available in the initial report. boston 25 said the cause was not immediately clear and did not report whether anyone was injured in the initial traffic alert. motorists should check current traffic information before using the route because lane closures and backups can change quickly. more breaking breaking / developing ma foxborough foxborough, ma massachusetts foxborough i-95 traffic fire

breaking-france-train-derailment-normand.excerpt: Authorities said 180 passengers were aboard the train near Cleon, where 140 firefighters responded Friday evening.
breaking-france-train-derailment-normand.text: train derailment in northern france injures about 20 authorities said 180 passengers were aboard the train near cleon, where 140 firefighters responded friday evening. a passenger train derailed between rouen and caen in northern france on friday evening, injuring about 20 people, french authorities said. the incident occurred near cleon in normandy at about 7:54 p.m. local time. french transport minister philippe tabarot said 180 passengers were aboard the train. about 140 firefighters were sent to the scene to assist injured passengers and help others leave the train. the prefecture of seine-maritime asked the public to avoid the area while emergency crews worked. authorities had not immediately released details on the severity of the injuries or the cause of the derailment. rail service on the corridor was expected to face disruption during the response and investigation. the situation remained developing friday as emergency teams accounted for passengers and secured the site. travelers in the region should rely on official rail and local-authority updates before beginning a trip, because early casualty and service information can change as responders complete their work. breaking breaking breaking / developing france cleon cleon, france france train derailment normandy cleon developing

breaking-gaza-beit-lahiya-family-killed-.excerpt: Health officials said a man, his wife and their daughters, ages 8 and 12, were killed in a Beit Lahiya home as strikes intensified.
breaking-gaza-beit-lahiya-family-killed-.text: israeli strike kills family of four in northern gaza, medics say health officials said a man, his wife and their daughters, ages 8 and 12, were killed in a beit lahiya home as strikes intensified. an israeli airstrike killed a man, his wife and their two daughters, ages 8 and 12, in a house in beit lahiya in the northern gaza strip on thursday, health officials told reuters. the israeli military did not immediately comment on the reported strike. residents and medics said at least six homes across gaza had been hit during the previous two days, damaging nearby houses and tent shelters and prompting families to leave affected areas. a u.s.-backed ceasefire reached in october 2025 ended large-scale fighting but did not stop all strikes or produce substantial progress toward a permanent settlement. hamas and israel have each accused the other of violating the agreement. gaza health officials say more than 1,300 palestinians, most of them civilians, have been killed since the ceasefire took effect. the israeli military says four israeli soldiers have been killed over the same period. those figures come from the respective parties and remain part of a developing conflict. further information about thursday’s strike is expected. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl beit lahiya gaza strip gaza beit lahiya israel ceasefire

breaking-gaza-hospital-generator-power-c.excerpt: Engine-oil and spare-parts shortages are forcing medical facilities to ration generator power while aid groups warn that essential services are at risk.
breaking-gaza-hospital-generator-power-c.text: generator failures deepen power crisis at gaza hospitals engine-oil and spare-parts shortages are forcing medical facilities to ration generator power while aid groups warn that essential services are at risk. hospitals and displaced families in gaza are struggling to keep generators running as shortages of engine oil and replacement parts worsen an already severe electricity crisis. at nasser hospital in khan younis, one of four generators was out of service, reuters reported. staff were rotating power cuts to reduce the load on the remaining units, leaving patients who depend on ventilators, nebulizers and other powered equipment waiting for limited electricity. gaza has had no grid power since 2023, making generators central to hospitals, ambulances, water pumps and shelters. médecins sans frontières warned that dwindling oil and parts threaten those services. residents told reuters that privately generated electricity now costs about 20 times its earlier price, putting it beyond the reach of many families. israel’s cogat agency said a monitored mechanism facilitates the entry of equipment while seeking to prevent advanced items from reaching hamas and to ensure supplies reach civilians. aid groups say current access remains insufficient. with roughly two million people living largely in displacement sites, further generator failures could quickly interrupt medical and water services. breaking breaking breaking / developing gaza khan younis gaza strip gaza hospitals generators humanitarian crisis

breaking-germany-charges-seven-hamas-att.excerpt: Federal prosecutors say the men obtained firearms and ammunition for a planned 2025 attack in Germany or Austria.
breaking-germany-charges-seven-hamas-att.text: germany charges seven suspected hamas members over attack plot federal prosecutors say the men obtained firearms and ammunition for a planned 2025 attack in germany or austria. german federal prosecutors charged seven suspected hamas members in berlin on friday with belonging to a foreign terrorist organization and preparing an attack, including by obtaining weapons. prosecutors said the men acted on orders from senior hamas figures and secured a fully automatic rifle, 13 pistols and more than 700 rounds of ammunition. authorities allege the weapons were intended for an attack in germany or austria around the second anniversary of the october 7, 2023 hamas-led attacks on israel. the intended targets were israeli representatives, jewish people or people viewed as pro-israel, prosecutors said. german domestic intelligence has previously warned that hamas or affiliated individuals were attempting to establish covert logistics networks in the country for weapons procurement and attack planning. all seven suspects remain in custody, reuters reported. the charges move the case into a new legal phase but do not establish guilt; the allegations will be tested in court. german authorities have not announced a trial date in the initial report. breaking breaking breaking / developing germany berlin berlin, germany germany hamas berlin security prosecutors

breaking-germany-leipzig-airport-drone-r.excerpt: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said a disaster was narrowly avoided; Russia has denied involvement in the airport incident.
breaking-germany-leipzig-airport-drone-r.text: germany says leipzig airport drone attack was prepared in russia chancellor friedrich merz said a disaster was narrowly avoided; russia has denied involvement in the airport incident. german chancellor friedrich merz said wednesday that an attempted drone attack at leipzig/halle airport had been prepared in russia over an extended period and was specifically aimed at germany. speaking to the lower house of parliament, merz said major damage and injuries were narrowly avoided. reuters reported his comments as germany continues assessing the incident and its wider security implications. russia has rejected involvement. its foreign minister characterized the accusation as escalatory, leaving the central claim disputed between berlin and moscow. reuters’ initial report did not provide public evidence independently establishing who planned or directed the drone operation. the allegation is significant because leipzig/halle is a major cargo airport and because unmanned-aircraft incidents have become a growing concern around european infrastructure. this remains a developing story: investigators may release additional technical findings, and statements from either government should be treated as claims until supported by evidence from the inquiry. further official updates could materially change the initial assessment. breaking breaking breaking / developing international leipzig leipzig, germany germany leipzig airport drones russia

breaking-hong-kong-tiananmen-vigil-leade.excerpt: Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung were sentenced under the national security law after convictions tied to a disbanded group’s pro-democracy activities.
breaking-hong-kong-tiananmen-vigil-leade.text: hong kong court gives tiananmen vigil leaders seven-year terms lee cheuk-yan and chow hang-tung were sentenced under the national security law after convictions tied to a disbanded group’s pro-democracy activities. a hong kong court sentenced two former leaders of the group that organized the city’s annual tiananmen square vigils to prison terms of at least seven years friday, the latest major ruling under the territory’s national security law. lee cheuk-yan, 69, received seven years, while chow hang-tung, 41, received seven years and three months after their convictions for inciting subversion. both had pleaded not guilty and have been in custody since 2021, reuters reported. albert ho, 74, another former chairman of the now-disbanded hong kong alliance in support of patriotic democratic movements of china, pleaded guilty in january and was sentenced to five years and two months. the court also imposed a hk$1.5 million fine on the alliance. the group organized public commemorations of beijing’s 1989 crackdown for years, when such gatherings were legal in hong kong. those vigils were effectively halted after the security law took effect in 2020. the sentences are developing news because any appeals, defense responses or further court action had not been announced in the initial report. breaking breaking breaking / developing hong kong hong kong hong kong hong kong tiananmen national security law courts

breaking-hormuz-vessel-projectile-report.excerpt: A British maritime agency said damage and crew conditions were unknown as energy-route security concerns intensified early Sunday.
breaking-hormuz-vessel-projectile-report.text: projectile reportedly hits vessel in strait of hormuz a british maritime agency said damage and crew conditions were unknown as energy-route security concerns intensified early sunday. a vessel moving through the strait of hormuz was reportedly struck by a projectile early sunday, according to the british navy-linked united kingdom maritime trade operations agency. ukmto said the extent of any damage and the condition of the crew were not immediately known, leaving the incident under active assessment. the report arrived one day after saudi arabia temporarily closed its east-west oil pipeline following a drone attack. that 1,200-kilometer route has carried roughly 4 million to 5 million barrels per day while wartime disruption has sharply reduced traffic through hormuz. saudi officials said injuries and damage from the pipeline strike were still being assessed. no immediate claim of responsibility was reported for the vessel incident. the latest alert adds pressure to two strategically important energy corridors at once: hormuz at the entrance to the gulf and the red sea route served by the saudi pipeline. shipping operators and governments were awaiting verified information about the vessel, its crew and any effect on traffic. breaking breaking breaking / developing oman strait of hormuz strait of hormuz strait of hormuz shipping ukmto middle east

breaking-hormuz-vessel-traffic-seven-tra.excerpt: Preliminary Kpler data recorded sharply fewer commercial crossings Thursday than the recent average as war and shipping restrictions squeeze a critical energy route.
breaking-hormuz-vessel-traffic-seven-tra.text: hormuz vessel traffic falls to seven transits, tracking data shows preliminary kpler data recorded sharply fewer commercial crossings thursday than the recent average as war and shipping restrictions squeeze a critical energy route. commercial vessel traffic through the strait of hormuz fell into single digits thursday, according to preliminary ship-tracking data that underscores how sharply war and shipping restrictions have disrupted one of the world’s most important energy corridors. kpler recorded seven transits, down from 11 wednesday and below the recent 10-day average of 15, reuters reported. five vessels entered the strait and two exited. the tracked cargoes included fertilizer, grain, steel, dry bulk material and petroleum products. the count may not capture vessels traveling with automatic identification system transponders switched off. before the iran war began february 28, roughly 125 large commercial ships typically passed through the strait each day, carrying a significant share of global crude-oil and liquefied-natural-gas supplies. traffic data can change as tracking services receive new signals, so the thursday count remains preliminary. still, the decline adds a fresh measure of stress on maritime trade as a u.s. blockade has halted iranian crude exports and instability has spread to nearby routes. traders, shippers and consumers are watching the corridor for further restrictions or attacks. breaking breaking breaking / developing international strait of hormuz strait of hormuz strait of hormuz shipping oil middle east

breaking-houthi-mocha-red-sea-advance-20.excerpt: Sources told Reuters that Iranian guidance and weapons supported a rapid coastal advance that strengthened the group’s position near Bab el-Mandeb.
breaking-houthi-mocha-red-sea-advance-20.text: houthi seizure of mocha tightens pressure on red sea route sources told reuters that iranian guidance and weapons supported a rapid coastal advance that strengthened the group’s position near bab el-mandeb. yemen’s houthi forces have seized the southwestern port city of mocha after a rapid advance along the red sea coast, strengthening their position near the bab el-mandeb strait. reuters reported that yemeni government, iranian and regional sources described direct guidance from iran’s revolutionary guards during the campaign. two iranian sources said tehran had urged the houthis to increase attacks on saudi arabia and offered additional funding, weapons and senior officers. iran publicly rejects descriptions of the houthis as a proxy. one iranian official told reuters that the decision to move on mocha was the group’s own, while acknowledging that the advance increased pressure on oil markets and on u.s. and saudi interests. control around bab el-mandeb matters because the narrow waterway connects the red sea with the gulf of aden and is a major route for shipping and energy cargoes. the reported seizure is a developing military and trade-route risk. independent access to the battlefield is limited, and claims about command arrangements rely on the sources cited by reuters. breaking breaking breaking / developing international mocha mocha, yemen yemen houthis red sea iran

breaking-houthis-dhubab-bab-el-mandeb-st.excerpt: Two Yemeni government sources told Reuters that Houthi forces reached the coastal town opposite Perim island, placing them at a critical Red Sea chokepoint.
breaking-houthis-dhubab-bab-el-mandeb-st.text: houthis reach dhubab on strategic bab el-mandeb strait, sources say two yemeni government sources told reuters that houthi forces reached the coastal town opposite perim island, placing them at a critical red sea chokepoint. iran-backed houthi forces have reached dhubab, a yemeni town directly on the bab el-mandeb strait, two yemeni government sources told reuters on friday. the town sits across the water from perim island at one of the world’s most consequential maritime chokepoints. government sources said control of dhubab and perim is important to gaining control over the strait. bab el-mandeb links the red sea with the gulf of aden, making developments along its shores significant for vessels using routes between europe and asia. reuters attributed the battlefield update to government sources, and the report did not include an independent on-the-ground verification or a detailed response from the houthis. the exact extent and durability of the reported advance therefore remained unclear at publication. the movement is a developing regional-security story because territorial control near the strait can affect military calculations and perceptions of shipping risk even before navigation patterns change. operators and governments will be watching for confirmation of positions around dhubab and perim, statements from the parties, and any effect on maritime traffic. the report follows wider fighting and pressure around yemen’s red sea coast, but this update concerns the forces’ reported arrival at dhubab specifically. breaking breaking breaking / developing yemen dhubab dhubab, yemen yemen houthis bab el-mandeb red sea shipping

breaking-houthis-hanish-islands-red-sea-.excerpt: Houthi rebels say they seized Greater and Lesser Hanish in the southern Red Sea, a claim that could signal a new front near the Bab el-Mandeb shipping route.
breaking-houthis-hanish-islands-red-sea-.text: houthis claim control of two strategic red sea islands as yemen fighting widens houthi rebels say they seized greater and lesser hanish in the southern red sea, a claim that could signal a new front near the bab el-mandeb shipping route. houthi rebels in yemen said they had seized control of greater and lesser hanish, two islands in the southern red sea, as fighting in the region widened, the associated press reported monday. the islands sit near the bab el-mandeb strait, a passage connecting the red sea with the gulf of aden and an important route for commercial shipping. control of the territory could give the houthis a new position near maritime traffic, although the group’s claim was not independently verified in the report. saudi-backed forces were trying to retake territory, according to the ap. the report also linked the latest development to a broader escalation in yemen, where tens of thousands of people have been displaced since fighting intensified this month. the situation remains fluid, and the reported island seizure could not be confirmed by independent observers. any change in control or new restrictions near the strait could affect shipping risk assessments and add pressure to an already volatile regional conflict. breaking breaking breaking/developing yemen hanish islands, red sea breaking news yemen red sea

breaking-houthis-reach-perim-island-2026.excerpt: Yemeni government forces withdrew from the strategic island as the group’s rapid Red Sea advance raised pressure on a vital shipping corridor.
breaking-houthis-reach-perim-island-2026.text: houthis reach perim island at mouth of bab el-mandeb yemeni government forces withdrew from the strategic island as the group’s rapid red sea advance raised pressure on a vital shipping corridor. yemen’s iran-aligned houthis reached perim island in the bab el-mandeb strait on friday, according to four yemeni government sources cited by reuters. two sources said saudi-backed government forces had withdrawn from the island after the houthis also took the mainland town of dhubab, which faces it. perim sits at the mouth of a shipping lane connecting the red sea with the gulf of aden. control of the island could increase pressure on commercial traffic at a time when the strait of hormuz is already severely disrupted, forcing more attention onto the western route used by saudi energy shipments. the movement is a material extension of the houthis’ rapid coastal advance. yemeni government forces said they plan to deploy weapons and aircraft in an effort to retake captured areas and warned civilians to avoid a route between taiz and mocha. the houthis captured mocha and the hanish islands on thursday. the situation remains fluid, and control on the ground may change as government forces organize a counteroffensive. the immediate risk extends beyond yemen: any sustained disruption at bab el-mandeb could affect shipping schedules, insurance costs and energy supply routes linking asia, the middle east and europe. breaking breaking breaking / developing yemen perim island, yemen houthis perim island bab el-mandeb shipping

breaking-hungary-reverse-gay-adoption-re.excerpt: Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced a reversal of the 2020 system but did not yet provide legislation or a timetable.
breaking-hungary-reverse-gay-adoption-re.text: hungary moves to reverse restriction on gay adoption prime minister peter magyar announced a reversal of the 2020 system but did not yet provide legislation or a timetable. hungarian prime minister peter magyar said saturday that his government will change a 2020 adoption rule that effectively barred gay and lesbian couples from adopting children. the announcement marks a significant policy reversal after magyar defeated former prime minister viktor orban in april, ending orban’s 16 years in power. before the 2020 law, one partner in a same-sex couple could apply to adopt as a single person. the orban-era measure required single applicants to obtain approval from the family affairs minister, creating what reuters described as an effective ban. magyar said adoption decisions should be made by qualified professionals rather than a politician, though he did not provide a timetable or legislative text. hungary recognizes civil unions but does not allow same-sex marriage. the european court of justice ruled in april that separate hungarian restrictions on lgbtq content violated european law. rewriting the adoption process would therefore become an early test of the new government’s approach to civil rights and its relationship with european institutions. the next concrete steps are the introduction of legislation and details about how professional adoption reviews would operate. breaking breaking breaking / developing hungary budapest budapest, hungary hungary adoption lgbtq rights peter magyar

breaking-hurricane-lowell-kauai-damage-2.excerpt: Nearly all of the island utility’s members lost electricity as destructive winds, heavy rain and large waves battered western Hawaii.
breaking-hurricane-lowell-kauai-damage-2.text: hurricane lowell knocks out power across kauai and damages coast nearly all of the island utility’s members lost electricity as destructive winds, heavy rain and large waves battered western hawaii. hurricane lowell’s outer winds and rain caused widespread damage across kauai tuesday, knocking out power to nearly all of the island utility’s roughly 35,000 members and sending hundreds of residents to shelters. the associated press reported that trees fell, coastal infrastructure was damaged and debris washed inland along parts of kauai’s southern shore. lihue airport recorded sustained winds above 50 mph, with gusts reaching 80 mph. the storm’s center passed west of hawaii, but its broad circulation still affected several islands. warnings were lifted tuesday morning, while authorities continued to caution about flooding, mudslides, blocked roads and lingering high water. oahu also reported flooded routes. recovery conditions remain fluid. emergency managers asked residents to avoid unnecessary travel while crews assess roads and restore electricity. the power-outage total describes the disruption reported during the storm, not a live restoration figure. updated utility counts, damage inspections and rainfall measurements will provide a clearer view of the hurricane’s full impact. more hi kauai, hawaii breaking hurricane lowell hawaii power outages

breaking-indonesia-school-meals-police-c.excerpt: Sixty parents are seeking a negligence investigation and compensation after hundreds of students became ill in North Sumatra.
breaking-indonesia-school-meals-police-c.text: indonesian parents file first legal challenge over free school meals sixty parents are seeking a negligence investigation and compensation after hundreds of students became ill in north sumatra. sixty indonesian parents have filed a police complaint seeking a negligence investigation and compensation after their children became sick through the government’s free school-meal program, reuters reported friday. it is the first legal challenge reported against the flagship initiative. the complaint concerns an outbreak in karo, north sumatra, where at least 300 students became ill in mid-august and some required hospital treatment. the filing was made august 31 and shared with news organizations on thursday. forensic testing of food connected to the incident is still pending. parents also plan a separate lawsuit in district court. the legal action increases pressure on authorities to explain how meals were prepared, transported and checked, and who may be responsible if investigators establish that safety failures caused the illnesses. more than 50,000 food-poisoning cases have been linked to the nationwide program, according to figures cited by reuters. the scale makes the complaint a potentially significant test of oversight and accountability. investigators have not yet announced findings in the karo case, and the requested compensation has not been awarded. breaking breaking breaking / developing indonesia karo, north sumatra, indonesia indonesia school meals food safety public health

breaking-indonesia-wildfire-emissions-wo.excerpt: Satellite-based estimates put Indonesia’s fire emissions at 19.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide from September 1–7 as drought fuels a severe season.
breaking-indonesia-wildfire-emissions-wo.text: indonesia wildfire emissions rise to world’s highest satellite-based estimates put indonesia’s fire emissions at 19.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide from september 1–7 as drought fuels a severe season. indonesia produced the world’s highest fire-related carbon dioxide emissions during the first week of september as wildfires burned through drought-stricken forest and peatland on borneo and sumatra. fire emissions watch, developed by the european union’s copernicus climate service, estimated 19.7 million metric tons from september 1 through september 7. that was more than one-third of the global total and 273% above indonesia’s seasonal average, though below the same week in the severe 2015 fire year. authorities described the current season as the country’s most intense in 11 years. more than 13,000 hotspots were recorded from august 1 through september 8. in pontianak, west kalimantan, the air-quality index reached 394 on wednesday; readings above 300 are considered hazardous. the emergency remains developing because el niño-driven heat and drought can sustain fires into october. satellite estimates may also miss low-temperature or underground peat fires. later field assessments will be needed to measure burned area, health effects and cross-border haze, while current air-quality readings can vary by place and hour. breaking breaking breaking / developing international pontianak borneo and sumatra, indonesia indonesia wildfires el niño air quality

breaking-iran-jordan-hormuz-attacks-2026.excerpt: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard launched missiles toward a U.S. base and said it struck 10 ships after American forces destroyed five Iranian tankers.
breaking-iran-jordan-hormuz-attacks-2026.text: iran attacks u.s. base in jordan and ships near hormuz iran’s revolutionary guard launched missiles toward a u.s. base and said it struck 10 ships after american forces destroyed five iranian tankers. iran’s revolutionary guard launched ballistic missiles toward a u.s. military base near azraq, jordan, and attacked ships in the strait of hormuz in a new escalation reported early wednesday. reuters reported that iran said it targeted 10 vessels, including two u.s. ships. iranian authorities claimed damage at the jordanian base, while jordanian and u.s. officials reported no casualties and said most incoming missiles were intercepted. independent confirmation of iran’s damage claims was not immediately available. the attacks followed the u.s. military’s destruction of five iranian oil tankers, which washington said was retaliation for strikes on an american warship. the exchange comes as fighting also threatens energy facilities and commercial shipping around the gulf. the strait of hormuz is a critical route for global oil exports, making any attack on vessels there consequential beyond the immediate military confrontation. details about damage to the ships and the exact sequence of the attacks remained limited in the first report. this is a developing story, and casualty or damage assessments may change as governments and shipping operators release verified updates. more breaking breaking / developing international azraq jordan and the strait of hormuz iran jordan strait of hormuz u.s. military

breaking-iran-missiles-jordan-2026.excerpt: Jordan said it intercepted most of 18 ballistic missiles as the latest U.S.-Iran exchange raised fears of a wider regional conflict.
breaking-iran-missiles-jordan-2026.text: iran launches missiles toward u.s. targets in jordan after tanker strikes jordan said it intercepted most of 18 ballistic missiles as the latest u.s.-iran exchange raised fears of a wider regional conflict. iran launched ballistic missiles toward u.s. targets in jordan after american forces struck five iranian oil tankers, according to iranian state media and reporting by the associated press. jordan said its forces intercepted most of 18 missiles. the ap reported no immediate american casualties from the launch. the exchange followed u.s. central command’s announcement that it destroyed or disabled five tankers after iranian missile attacks on a u.s. navy warship. the latest action expands the immediate geography of the confrontation and increases risks for military personnel, commercial shipping and neighboring countries. iran’s revolutionary guard also warned tankers near kuwait and bahrain to leave the area, while shipping through the strait of hormuz remains under pressure. information is still developing. claims from the combatants may change as governments release radar data, damage assessments and casualty reports. the reported missile count and interceptions come from official statements cited by the ap, not an independent northeast news assessment. the next verified military response will determine whether the exchange remains limited or draws in additional regional forces. more us jordan breaking iran jordan u.s. military

breaking-iran-oman-hormuz-talks-no-signe.excerpt: A senior Iranian official described Monday’s Oman meeting as a negotiating step, with major disagreements over the strategic waterway unresolved.
breaking-iran-oman-hormuz-talks-no-signe.text: iran says oman talks unlikely to produce signed hormuz deal a senior iranian official described monday’s oman meeting as a negotiating step, with major disagreements over the strategic waterway unresolved. a planned monday meeting between iran and gulf states in oman is expected to cover the strait of hormuz but is unlikely to produce a signed agreement, a senior iranian official told reuters. the assessment tempers expectations around talks focused on one of the world’s most consequential shipping routes. iran has spent months negotiating with oman and says it plans to attend the gathering. oman has not formally announced the meeting, while other invited governments have remained largely silent; bahrain has said it will not participate. tehran has sought fees from vessels using the strait, a proposal oman rejects, leaving a central point of disagreement unresolved before delegates meet. roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies moved through hormuz before the war that began in february, making any change in access important to energy markets and shipping costs. oil prices surged during the past week as regional risks intensified. the official’s comments indicate that monday may function as a negotiating step rather than a deadline. confirmation of attendance, the meeting’s agenda and any practical navigation arrangements remain the key developments to watch. breaking breaking breaking / developing oman muscat muscat, oman iran oman strait of hormuz gulf states

breaking-iran-us-underwater-drone-2026.excerpt: The Pentagon confirmed a Dive-LD vehicle malfunctioned during a survey mission but said it carried no classified or sensitive equipment.
breaking-iran-us-underwater-drone-2026.text: iran says it captured u.s. underwater drone near strait of hormuz the pentagon confirmed a dive-ld vehicle malfunctioned during a survey mission but said it carried no classified or sensitive equipment. iran’s revolutionary guards said tuesday that they captured a u.s. uncrewed underwater vehicle near the entrance to the strait of hormuz, adding another point of tension around the strategically important shipping passage. reuters reported that the pentagon confirmed a dive-ld drone had malfunctioned more than a day earlier during regional survey work. u.s. officials described it as an older version and said it carried no classified or sensitive equipment. reuters said it could not independently verify iran’s full account of the capture. the roughly 19-foot autonomous vehicle was developed by anduril for missions that can include seabed mapping, mine countermeasures and infrastructure inspection. anduril confirmed the loss and said the system is intended for high-risk operations where equipment may not return. the competing descriptions matter: iran is presenting the episode as an intelligence and military gain, while the pentagon is minimizing the sensitivity of the hardware. the incident remains developing because the vehicle’s exact condition, location and route to iranian custody have not been independently established. more international strait of hormuz iran united states strait of hormuz underwater drone

breaking-iraq-closes-shalamcheh-border-2.excerpt: Baghdad ordered the Shalamcheh crossing shut as a precaution while security forces pursue those responsible for attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.
breaking-iraq-closes-shalamcheh-border-2.text: iraq closes iran border crossing after saudi drone attacks baghdad ordered the shalamcheh crossing shut as a precaution while security forces pursue those responsible for attacks on saudi energy infrastructure. iraq ordered the shalamcheh border crossing with iran closed late friday as a precaution after drone attacks on saudi arabia, two iraqi security sources told reuters. the crossing, near basra, is a significant route for travelers and trade between the two countries. authorities had not announced how long the closure would remain in effect. the order came as iraqi security forces launched a broad operation to identify and pursue those responsible for the attacks. saudi arabia said drones launched from iraqi territory struck its east-west oil pipeline, sharply raising pressure on baghdad to prevent its territory from being used for regional attacks. the claim and the investigation remain part of a fast-moving security situation. closing shalamcheh gives iraqi authorities tighter control over movement near the southern border while they examine possible launch networks and routes. it also risks disrupting civilian travel and commerce if extended. officials had not publicly identified suspects or established a direct connection between the border crossing and the drone operation, making the measure precautionary rather than evidence that the crossing was used in the attacks. breaking breaking breaking / developing iraq baghdad iraq-iran border iraq iran saudi arabia shalamcheh drone attacks

breaking-israel-britain-east-jerusalem-c.excerpt: The order gives the British mission 30 days to close and follows settlement-related sanctions imposed by Britain, France and Canada.
breaking-israel-britain-east-jerusalem-c.text: israel orders britain to close east jerusalem consulate the order gives the british mission 30 days to close and follows settlement-related sanctions imposed by britain, france and canada. israel has told britain to close its consulate in east jerusalem within 30 days, according to israeli officials and other sources cited by reuters. the move would end the diplomatic status of british personnel based in jerusalem after the deadline. reuters also reported that diplomats working in ramallah were given seven days to leave and that britain would no longer be permitted to train palestinian security personnel. the order follows sanctions imposed by britain, france and canada connected to israeli settlements. it marks a sharp deterioration in diplomatic relations and could affect britain’s long-standing work with palestinians in jerusalem and the west bank. because the instructions and timelines were reported through officials and sources, implementation details may still change. britain’s government had not announced a reversal in the initial account. the closure order is therefore a developing diplomatic action, with practical questions remaining about consular services, staffing and how british engagement with palestinian institutions will continue. breaking breaking breaking / developing international jerusalem east jerusalem israel united kingdom east jerusalem diplomacy

breaking-israel-hezbollah-ali-al-taher-c.excerpt: Israeli leaders said forces demolished a tunnel network at the Ali al-Taher ridge, about 15 kilometers from the border.
breaking-israel-hezbollah-ali-al-taher-c.text: israel says it destroyed hezbollah underground complex in lebanon israeli leaders said forces demolished a tunnel network at the ali al-taher ridge, about 15 kilometers from the border. israel said thursday that its military had destroyed an underground hezbollah complex at the ali al-taher ridge in southern lebanon, marking a new development in the conflict along the border. prime minister benjamin netanyahu and defense minister israel katz said the operation completed the consolidation of what israel describes as a security zone. they said israeli forces would remain in the area to prevent hezbollah from rebuilding positions. the ridge is roughly 15 kilometers, or 10 miles, from the israeli border. the israeli military said the underground network extended more than two kilometers and contained rockets, missiles, drones, anti-tank weapons, mines and explosives. it also described the site as a command complex for hezbollah’s badr unit. those battlefield claims were made by israel and were not independently verified in the source report. lebanon’s state news agency reported a powerful blast that was felt around nabatieh. the destruction and israel’s statement that its troops will stay in the area underscore the continuing risk of escalation and leave questions about the duration and legal status of the military presence. breaking breaking breaking / developing international nabatieh nabatieh, lebanon israel lebanon hezbollah ali al-taher

breaking-israel-says-hamas-commander-kil.excerpt: Hamas’s armed wing confirmed Mohammed Abdel Salam al-Yazouri died in Thursday’s strike, which Israel said killed two other commanders.
breaking-israel-says-hamas-commander-kil.text: israel says gaza strike killed senior hamas commander hamas’s armed wing confirmed mohammed abdel salam al-yazouri died in thursday’s strike, which israel said killed two other commanders. israel’s military said friday that a senior hamas commander was killed in an airstrike in gaza a day earlier, as bombing continued despite u.s.-backed efforts to restore a 2025 ceasefire. hamas’s armed wing confirmed the death of mohammed abdel salam al-yazouri. the group said he played a prominent role in planning the october 7, 2023 attacks on israel that triggered the two-year israeli military assault in gaza, reuters reported. the israeli military said the strike targeting yazouri also killed two other commanders. the initial statement did not provide a broader casualty count or identify the other two people. reuters reported no immediate additional comment from hamas beyond its confirmation of yazouri’s death. the report is developing because military operations and ceasefire diplomacy remain active, and information from the conflict zone can change rapidly. the announced death removes a figure both sides described as important to hamas’s armed operations while adding another pressure point to negotiations aimed at limiting renewed fighting. breaking breaking breaking / developing palestinian territories gaza gaza gaza israel hamas mohammed abdel salam al-yazouri middle east

breaking-jordan-base-us-aircraft-damaged.excerpt: A U.S. official told Reuters that an A-10 lost a wing and about eight F-15s sustained light damage during this week’s attack.
