breaking-jordan-base-us-aircraft-damaged.text: iranian strike damages u.s. aircraft at jordan base, official says a u.s. official told reuters that an a-10 lost a wing and about eight f-15s sustained light damage during this week’s attack. iranian strikes damaged several u.s. military aircraft at muwaffaq salti air base in jordan this week, according to a u.s. official who spoke to reuters. the official said one a-10 thunderbolt ii lost a wing, while roughly eight f-15 aircraft sustained light damage and returned to service. the account did not identify the exact timing of each impact or provide a full estimate of repair costs. u.s. forces fired about 30 patriot interceptors to counter incoming missiles during the attack, the official said. the strike followed u.s. attacks on five iranian crude carriers, which washington said answered two attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a navy warship. the new damage assessment shows that the jordan strike reached equipment on the base even as defenses responded. it also adds to concerns about aircraft losses and the rate at which air-defense interceptors are being used during the widening conflict. the situation remains developing, and the figures may change as military assessments continue. breaking breaking breaking / developing international azraq muwaffaq salti air base, jordan jordan iran u.s. military middle east

breaking-judge-fema-workforce-cuts-unlaw.excerpt: The court found that Homeland Security overstepped FEMA’s control of its personnel; remedies will be considered separately next month.
breaking-judge-fema-workforce-cuts-unlaw.text: federal judge rules plan to halve fema workforce unlawful the court found that homeland security overstepped fema’s control of its personnel; remedies will be considered separately next month. a federal judge has ruled that the administration acted unlawfully by directing the federal emergency management agency to cut its workforce in half. u.s. district judge susan illston said the department of homeland security improperly took over fema’s authority over its personnel and steered the agency toward eliminating thousands of disaster-response jobs. the late-friday decision cited a federal law enacted after hurricane katrina that bars dhs from substantially reducing fema’s authorities, responsibilities or functions. illston agreed with unions challenging the cuts that the department violated the law when it moved to stop fema from renewing temporary contracts for on-call reservists who respond to disasters. the ruling does not yet impose a remedy or penalty. the judge said the scope of relief will be addressed separately next month after additional briefing. she also noted that fema projected staffing of 11,383 for the coming fiscal year, roughly half its prior level, without a documented basis for that number. fema, dhs and the largest federal-worker union did not immediately comment saturday. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states san francisco san francisco, california fema federal court disaster response workforce

breaking-kyiv-apartment-fire-russian-str.excerpt: Kyiv authorities reported a fire in a nine-story residential building after overnight air attacks, while Russia’s Saratov region reported infrastructure damage.
breaking-kyiv-apartment-fire-russian-str.text: russian strikes injure two and ignite kyiv apartment fire, officials say kyiv authorities reported a fire in a nine-story residential building after overnight air attacks, while russia’s saratov region reported infrastructure damage. russian air strikes injured two people and started a fire in a nine-story apartment building in kyiv early friday, city authorities said. officials posted the preliminary account on telegram after air-raid warnings urged residents to take shelter from drones. emergency crews were responding to the residential fire, and authorities had not yet provided a full assessment of damage or whether additional people were trapped or displaced. separately, the governor of russia’s saratov region said ukrainian drones damaged civilian infrastructure there but caused no casualties. saratov is home to a rosneft refinery as well as industrial and military facilities. the precise targets and extent of the damage were not immediately clear. reuters said it could not independently verify the battlefield accounts. russia and ukraine both deny deliberately targeting civilians, although residential areas and civilian infrastructure have repeatedly been damaged during the war. casualty and damage figures may change as emergency teams complete searches and local authorities release additional information. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine kyiv kyiv, ukraine ukraine russia kyiv air strikes

breaking-kyiv-october-trilateral-talks-p.excerpt: A senior Ukrainian official said planning is underway, though no date or venue has been finalized and core territorial disputes remain.
breaking-kyiv-october-trilateral-talks-p.text: kyiv prepares for october resumption of u.s.-mediated talks with russia a senior ukrainian official said planning is underway, though no date or venue has been finalized and core territorial disputes remain. ukraine is preparing for u.s.-mediated trilateral talks with russia to resume in october, a senior ukrainian official said saturday, signaling a possible restart of diplomacy after months without a three-party meeting. kyrylo budanov, chief of staff to president volodymyr zelenskiy, described the planned discussions as an effort to address a war now more than four and a half years old. the last trilateral meeting took place in geneva in february. more recent visits by u.s. envoys steve witkoff and jared kushner to moscow and kyiv have renewed diplomatic activity, and zelenskiy has said ukraine received proposals that could support another round. possible host countries mentioned by the ukrainian side include turkey, the united arab emirates and switzerland. no date or venue has been finalized. the kremlin has said russia is open to renewed talks, while also saying the timing and location remain unsettled. major disagreements continue, including the status of the donbas region and other territory occupied or claimed by russia. the announcement therefore represents preparation for negotiations, not an agreement on terms or a ceasefire. developments in the coming weeks will show whether the tentative october timetable becomes a confirmed meeting. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine kyiv kyiv, ukraine ukraine russia peace talks united states

breaking-kyiv-petrol-station-strike-2026.excerpt: Emergency crews responded after an overnight attack ignited a fuel complex in southwestern Kyiv, as the city endured another wave of Russian drones.
breaking-kyiv-petrol-station-strike-2026.text: russian strike hits kyiv petrol station and injures four emergency crews responded after an overnight attack ignited a fuel complex in southwestern kyiv, as the city endured another wave of russian drones. a russian strike hit a petrol station complex in southwestern kyiv early thursday, injuring four people and setting off fires, ukrainian officials said. reuters reported that the attack marked the first time a petrol station had been struck in the ukrainian capital during the war. images from the scene showed heavy damage, including at least one destroyed vehicle. fire also spread to a neighboring building before emergency crews worked to contain it. the strike came during another night of drone attacks on kyiv. the city has faced an almost continuous barrage of jet-powered drones for nearly two weeks, increasing pressure on air defenses and emergency services. officials were still assessing the full damage and did not immediately provide detailed information about the condition of those injured. claims and casualty figures in an active conflict can change as responders search damaged areas and authorities verify reports. the core facts in this article are attributed to ukrainian officials and reuters reporting available thursday morning. the attack remains a developing story, with additional information expected from kyiv’s emergency and military authorities. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl kyiv kyiv, ukraine kyiv ukraine russia drone attack

breaking-kyiv-petrol-station-strikes-kil.excerpt: Eight people were injured at two fuel sites as Russia and Ukraine continued attacks on logistics and economic targets overnight.
breaking-kyiv-petrol-station-strikes-kil.text: russian strikes on kyiv petrol stations kill two, officials say eight people were injured at two fuel sites as russia and ukraine continued attacks on logistics and economic targets overnight. russian attacks on two petrol stations in kyiv killed two people early friday, mayor vitali klitschko said. eight others were injured at the fuel sites, and emergency services said a rescue worker was among those hurt when one location was struck again. the attacks followed an overnight strike on a residential block in the capital that injured eight people. a woman was also killed in the region surrounding kyiv, according to the regional governor. russia has resumed frequent waves of jet-powered drone attacks on the capital and its suburbs after a short pause during a visit by u.s. peace envoys. ukraine also carried out overnight strikes inside russia. officials said a drone attack killed two people in the tula region, while ukrainian forces targeted logistics and other economic sites, including an ozon distribution hub in the saratov region. both sides have increasingly focused on fuel, transport and logistics infrastructure as the war moves toward another winter. casualty figures and damage assessments can change as emergency crews search affected sites. the renewed attacks show that diplomatic contacts have not stopped the expanding campaign against economic targets and nearby civilian areas. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine kyiv kyiv, ukraine kyiv ukraine war drone strikes russia

breaking-mcconnell-senate-return-2026-09.excerpt: The Kentucky Republican said he would cast his first Senate vote since a June fall as he continues physical therapy.
breaking-mcconnell-senate-return-2026-09.text: mitch mcconnell returns to senate after three-month health-related absence the kentucky republican said he would cast his first senate vote since a june fall as he continues physical therapy. sen. mitch mcconnell returned to capitol hill monday after a three-month absence linked to health problems, according to cnn reporting carried by whdh. the kentucky republican was seen leaving his home in a wheelchair and said he planned to cast his first senate vote since a june fall. he also said he was continuing physical therapy and was not yet fully recovered. mcconnell was hospitalized june 14. weeks later, he disclosed that he had fallen, briefly lost consciousness and later contracted pneumonia. he then continued his recovery at home after a period in rehabilitation. the senate returned to session monday after a five-week summer recess, putting mcconnell back in the chamber as lawmakers resumed work. his long absence had prompted public questions about his health and ability to serve. mcconnell has said he will not seek reelection in 2026 and intends to finish his term, which is scheduled to end in january. he remains a republican senator from kentucky and a former senate majority leader. breaking breaking breaking/developing ky washington washington, d.c. breaking u.s. senate mitch mcconnell kentucky

breaking-merchant-vessels-disabled-fires.excerpt: A British maritime agency reported several ships disabled during overnight military activity, with casualties and environmental effects not yet confirmed.
breaking-merchant-vessels-disabled-fires.text: merchant vessels disabled by fires in gulf and gulf of oman a british maritime agency reported several ships disabled during overnight military activity, with casualties and environmental effects not yet confirmed. several merchant vessels in the northern gulf and gulf of oman were hit by disabling fires during overnight military activity, the united kingdom maritime trade operations agency reported wednesday. the british navy-affiliated agency said it could not initially confirm casualties or environmental damage. in a separate incident about 24 nautical miles from port rashid in the united arab emirates, ukmto reported a vessel listing at anchor, possibly after taking on water following an attack by an unknown projectile. the incidents came after u.s. central command said it destroyed five iranian crude tankers following attempted missile attacks on a u.s. navy warship. iran’s revolutionary guards then claimed attacks on two u.s. vessels and eight oil tankers. those claims remained attributed statements in the early reporting, not independently confirmed findings. the situation is developing, and basic facts may change as crews, ship operators and maritime authorities report damage. confirmed casualty numbers, pollution effects, vessel identities and consequences for commercial traffic were not available in the initial account. shipping advisories and official notices will be the key sources for operational updates. breaking breaking breaking / developing international gulf of oman gulf and gulf of oman gulf of oman merchant shipping ukmto strait of hormuz

breaking-mi5-chief-strategic-shock-warni.excerpt: Ken McCallum says security agencies must not prepare only for familiar threats as terrorism, sabotage and cyber risks continue to evolve.
breaking-mi5-chief-strategic-shock-warni.text: mi5 chief warns next strategic shock may emerge beyond current focus ken mccallum says security agencies must not prepare only for familiar threats as terrorism, sabotage and cyber risks continue to evolve. britain’s domestic intelligence chief is warning that the next major security shock could be developing outside the areas receiving the most attention, arguing that agencies should avoid preparing only for the last crisis. mi5 director general ken mccallum made the case in an opinion article marking 25 years since the september 11 attacks. he said al qaeda has been diminished but remains a threat, while governments must also contend with state-backed sabotage and cyberattacks capable of disrupting essential infrastructure such as power systems. the warning did not identify a specific imminent plot. instead, it framed the central challenge as anticipating changing methods and actors while maintaining defenses against known terrorist networks. mccallum called for closer work among government, private companies and academic specialists. that coordination has become more important as critical services rely on interconnected technology and as hostile activity can move between physical operations, online systems and influence campaigns. his remarks add to an ongoing debate over how security resources should be divided between counterterrorism and broader state-linked threats. breaking breaking breaking / developing united kingdom london london, united kingdom mi5 security cyberattacks terrorism

breaking-miami-cargo-jet-victims-van-202.excerpt: Investigators say the victims were inside a plane-cleaning vehicle when a Boeing 767 ran off the runway at Miami International Airport.
breaking-miami-cargo-jet-victims-van-202.text: five killed in miami cargo-jet crash were in ground-crew van investigators say the victims were inside a plane-cleaning vehicle when a boeing 767 ran off the runway at miami international airport. all five people killed when an amazon cargo jet ran off a runway at miami international airport were inside a van used by aircraft cleaners, investigators said tuesday. the associated press reported that the flight was operated by north carolina-based carrier 21 air. the 32-year-old boeing 767 began service as a passenger jet and was converted for cargo use in 2015, according to flight-tracking data cited by the ap. two of the airport’s four runways remained closed while national transportation safety board investigators documented the wreckage and gathered evidence. more than 225 flights were canceled sunday and monday, with hundreds of additional delays, airport officials said. the latest information clarifies where the victims were when the crash occurred but does not establish why the aircraft left the runway. the ntsb investigation will examine the plane, crew actions, weather, airport conditions and available recordings before reaching conclusions. officials said runways would reopen after investigators completed necessary work at the scene. more fl miami, florida breaking aviation miami ntsb

breaking-miami-cargo-ntsb-data-2026.excerpt: Investigators say throttle and brake movements suggest the pilots briefly tried a go-around after touchdown before the Boeing 767 overran the runway.
breaking-miami-cargo-ntsb-data-2026.text: ntsb data indicates miami cargo crew considered aborting landing investigators say throttle and brake movements suggest the pilots briefly tried a go-around after touchdown before the boeing 767 overran the runway. new flight-data evidence suggests the pilots of a cargo jet that crashed at miami international airport considered aborting the landing after touchdown, the national transportation safety board said. the boeing 767, operated by 21 air, overran the runway by about 1,300 feet sunday and struck two vehicles, killing five people and injuring five. investigators said the nose and right main landing gear touched down 30 seconds before the recording ended at about 158 knots; the main gear touched down 19 seconds before the end at about 134 knots. the brakes were then released and the throttles advanced, movements consistent with an attempted go-around. the throttles returned to idle and braking resumed 11 seconds before the recording stopped. investigators said the data showed no deployment of the speed brakes or thrust reversers. the ntsb plans to interview the pilots wednesday and release information from the cockpit voice recorder afterward. the findings are preliminary and do not establish a cause. one runway has reopened, but investigators still need to reconcile the aircraft data, crew actions, runway conditions and physical evidence before reaching conclusions. more fl miami, florida miami ntsb cargo aviation boeing 767

breaking-modi-putin-delhi-talks-2026.excerpt: The leaders met in New Delhi to discuss energy, defense and industrial cooperation as India prepares to host the wider summit.
breaking-modi-putin-delhi-talks-2026.text: modi and putin hold trade and defense talks before brics summit the leaders met in new delhi to discuss energy, defense and industrial cooperation as india prepares to host the wider summit. indian prime minister narendra modi and russian president vladimir putin held talks in new delhi on friday, meeting shortly before india hosts the brics summit. reuters reported that the agenda covered trade, energy and defense as well as civil nuclear cooperation, fertilizers, manufacturing, railways, steel and critical minerals. the meeting was the leaders’ second in two weeks and underscored india’s effort to maintain strategic ties with moscow despite western sanctions tied to russia’s war in ukraine. russian oil supplied a record 51% of india’s imports in july, although that share later eased as china increased purchases. modi reiterated india’s support for diplomacy to end the war and defended the country’s need for reliable energy supplies. the discussions also follow agreements reached during putin’s december 2025 visit to deepen commercial and defense cooperation. the talks are developing in the context of the brics gathering, where leaders from china and iran are also expected. their outcome could affect energy flows, defense procurement and coordination among member countries. any concrete commitments will depend on formal announcements following the bilateral session and summit meetings. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india india russia narendra modi vladimir putin brics

breaking-mount-fuji-landslide-heavy-rain.excerpt: Three vehicles were buried and a major access road closed as intense rainfall also caused flooding and injuries elsewhere in central Japan.
breaking-mount-fuji-landslide-heavy-rain.text: heavy rain triggers landslide at mount fuji access point three vehicles were buried and a major access road closed as intense rainfall also caused flooding and injuries elsewhere in central japan. heavy rain triggered a landslide at a main access point for climbers on japan’s mount fuji on wednesday, burying three vehicles and forcing authorities to close the fuji subaru line, reuters reported. no injuries were reported at the landslide site. officials separately found two climbers unconscious on the mountain, but authorities had not linked those cases to the landslide. that distinction remains important while rescue teams and investigators establish what happened in each incident. the storm also caused damaging conditions elsewhere. a separate landslide at kawanehon killed a worker, while flooding injured 41 people in aichi and gifu prefectures. nagoya recorded 104.5 millimeters of rain in one hour, an unusually intense burst that overwhelmed some local drainage and transportation systems. more rain was expected through wednesday afternoon, leaving the situation subject to change. travelers should follow local closure notices and avoid affected mountain roads. mount fuji’s access routes can become hazardous quickly in severe weather, and the closure gives crews time to inspect slopes, clear debris and assess whether additional ground movement is likely. breaking breaking breaking / developing international mount fuji mount fuji, japan japan mount fuji landslide flooding

breaking-nato-russian-subsea-cable-exerc.excerpt: A Reuters investigation says British, Norwegian and U.S. forces confronted vessels near Svalbard during a secret Russian undersea operation.
breaking-nato-russian-subsea-cable-exerc.text: western officials say nato disrupted russian subsea-cable exercise a reuters investigation says british, norwegian and u.s. forces confronted vessels near svalbard during a secret russian undersea operation. nato allies tracked and confronted russian vessels near norway’s svalbard archipelago during a secret undersea exercise this spring, according to two western officials who described the operation to reuters. the officials said russia’s main directorate for deep sea research, known as gugi, used deep-sea submersibles to simulate deploying technology intended to disable critical subsea cables while obscuring responsibility. britain, norway and the united states participated in the response, and the russian vessels left after being prevented from completing the exercise, reuters reported. britain and norway disclosed in april that they had uncovered a covert russian operation in arctic waters. reuters said the specific technology, the location near svalbard and the u.s. role had not previously been reported. subsea communications and energy cables carry essential international traffic, making suspected interference a major security concern for governments and network operators. the new report is based on unnamed officials because of the operation’s sensitivity. the disclosure may prompt further responses from nato governments and russia as authorities assess the capability and the protection of infrastructure across arctic waters. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl svalbard svalbard, norway nato russia subsea cables svalbard

breaking-nh-governor-primary-winners-202.excerpt: The incumbent Republican governor and former Democratic Executive Councilor advance to the November general election.
breaking-nh-governor-primary-winners-202.text: ayotte and warmington win new hampshire governor primaries the incumbent republican governor and former democratic executive councilor advance to the november general election. republican gov. kelly ayotte and democrat cinde warmington won their parties’ new hampshire gubernatorial primaries tuesday, setting the matchup for november. citizens count’s election results page listed both candidates as winners tuesday evening. ayotte entered the election seeking a second two-year term, while warmington, a former member of the executive council, is making another run for governor after competing in the 2024 democratic primary. the results move the contest from intraparty campaigning to a general election likely to focus on housing costs, public education, energy prices, abortion policy and management of the state budget. ayotte will run on her first term in office, while warmington will argue for a change in direction after years of republican control of the corner office. results posted on election night are preliminary until local returns are reviewed and the state completes its canvass. the nominations nevertheless clarify the top of new hampshire’s state ballot and give both campaigns less than two months to consolidate supporters and reach independent voters. more nh new hampshire breaking new hampshire governor elections

breaking-nh-school-id-voting-test-2026.excerpt: A new identification rule was challenged in federal court but appeared to create few problems for Durham voters during Tuesday’s primary.
breaking-nh-school-id-voting-test-2026.text: new hampshire school-id voting rule gets first test at unh a new identification rule was challenged in federal court but appeared to create few problems for durham voters during tuesday’s primary. a new new hampshire law removing school-issued ids from the approved identification list got its first major test tuesday at the university of new hampshire’s durham polling place. nhpr reported that the law, signed by gov. kelly ayotte this summer, is being challenged in federal court. at oyster river high school, voters were advised that a school id alone would not be accepted for registration or obtaining a ballot. one unh student told nhpr she registered with a driver’s license and a utility bill and found the process easy. durham’s town moderator said operations were running smoothly and turnout was steady, though voting-rights groups continued warning students about the change. the durham experience does not resolve the legal challenge or answer how the policy will work in every community. it does show how election workers and campus groups are adapting in real time as college students arrive with questions about acceptable documents. more breaking breaking / developing nh durham durham, nh new hampshire voting unh elections developing

breaking-north-korea-live-fire-drill-202.excerpt: North Korea said it conducted a live-fire exercise involving missiles, artillery and drones as South Korea reported short-range ballistic-missile launches.
breaking-north-korea-live-fire-drill-202.text: north korea says live-fire drill demonstrated combined missile and drone power north korea said it conducted a live-fire exercise involving missiles, artillery and drones as south korea reported short-range ballistic-missile launches. north korea said monday that a recent live-fire exercise involving missiles, artillery and drones demonstrated the country’s ability to combine several weapons systems, the associated press reported. the exercise took place saturday and was described by north korean officials as a test of an integrated weapons-control system. south korea’s military separately said it detected several short-range ballistic missiles launched from the eastern coastal area near wonsan. the missiles traveled about 250 kilometers, or roughly 155 miles, toward waters off north korea, according to south korean officials cited by ap. that range is consistent with systems designed to reach targets in south korea, including u.s. military facilities. north korea’s claims about the exercise could not be independently verified. the drill came after a joint exercise involving the united states, south korea and japan, which pyongyang has criticized as provocative. the situation remains developing. further statements from south korean, u.s. or north korean authorities could clarify the number of launches, the systems used and whether additional exercises are planned. breaking breaking breaking/developing south korea wonsan, north korea breaking north korea south korea missiles security

breaking-north-korea-short-range-missile.excerpt: South Korea said several missiles launched from the Wonsan area flew about 250 kilometers early Saturday.
breaking-north-korea-short-range-missile.text: north korea fires short-range ballistic missiles toward sea south korea said several missiles launched from the wonsan area flew about 250 kilometers early saturday. north korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea early saturday, south korea's military said. the launches were detected from the wonsan area at about 5:20 a.m. local time, and the missiles traveled roughly 250 kilometers before falling into waters east of the korean peninsula. south korean and u.s. authorities were analyzing the flight details and shared information with japan. seoul convened an emergency security meeting following the launches. the u.s. pacific command said its initial assessment found no immediate threat to american personnel or territory, or to u.s. allies, while emphasizing continued monitoring and coordination. the launches add a new military development to an already tense regional environment. the reported range places the weapons in the short-range category, but officials had not yet released information about missile type, altitude or launch purpose. those technical findings, along with any statement from pyongyang, will help determine whether the firing was a test, exercise or political signal. the episode remains developing as governments compare tracking data. breaking breaking breaking / developing north korea wonsan wonsan, north korea north korea south korea ballistic missiles wonsan regional security

breaking-north-korea-yongbyon-enrichment.excerpt: The nuclear watchdog says a two-story building at Yongbyon could hold up to 28 centrifuge cascades as infrastructure expands at multiple sites.
breaking-north-korea-yongbyon-enrichment.text: iaea reports new north korea uranium-enrichment facility the nuclear watchdog says a two-story building at yongbyon could hold up to 28 centrifuge cascades as infrastructure expands at multiple sites. north korea has built a new uranium-enrichment facility at its main yongbyon nuclear complex, the international atomic energy agency said in a report disclosed wednesday. the agency assessed that the two-story building could hold as many as 28 centrifuge cascades. it also reported expanded operations at an annex of the kangson enrichment site near pyongyang, pointing to growth in nuclear infrastructure at more than one location. iaea inspectors have not had access to north korea since 2009. the agency said its assessment relies on satellite imagery and other open-source material, including photographs released by north korean state media after a june visit by leader kim jong un. the findings do not provide a public measurement of current enriched-uranium output. they document new capacity and operating indicators that the agency considers serious. north korea says its nuclear status is irreversible and disputes the iaea’s authority over its program. additional imagery or official disclosures may refine the assessment, making the development subject to continued monitoring. more international yongbyon, north korea north korea iaea uranium enrichment yongbyon

breaking-novorossiysk-drone-attack-casua.excerpt: Russian authorities reported four deaths and 29 injuries in an attack on the Black Sea city, a major oil and grain export hub.
breaking-novorossiysk-drone-attack-casua.text: four killed in drone attack on russian port city, governor says russian authorities reported four deaths and 29 injuries in an attack on the black sea city, a major oil and grain export hub. a ukrainian drone attack on the russian black sea port city of novorossiysk killed four people, including a child, regional governor veniamin kondratyev said wednesday. kondratyev said 29 people were injured, according to reuters. the casualty figures and attribution came from russian authorities and had not been independently verified in the initial report. ukraine did not immediately provide a response in the account. novorossiysk is a major hub for russian oil and grain exports, giving any attack there potential significance beyond the immediate damage. early reporting did not establish whether port operations or export flows were disrupted. the situation remains developing as local authorities assess damage and identify victims. casualty totals can change after emergency crews complete searches and hospitals update patient conditions. any claims about the target, the drones’ origin or the effect on shipping should be treated as preliminary until supported by additional evidence or official operational notices. breaking breaking breaking / developing international novorossiysk novorossiysk, russia novorossiysk russia ukraine drone attack

breaking-philippine-ferry-fire-death-tol.excerpt: Rescuers recovered 30 bodies after firefighters entered the burned vessel, while the number still missing remained uncertain.
breaking-philippine-ferry-fire-death-tol.text: philippine ferry fire death toll rises to 35 rescuers recovered 30 bodies after firefighters entered the burned vessel, while the number still missing remained uncertain. the death toll from a ferry fire off the philippine island of palawan rose to 35 on friday after rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned vessel, authorities said. firefighters were able to board after extinguishing flames that had blocked access since wednesday night. the ferry was carrying more than 130 people when fire swept through it near the end of a voyage to coron. reuters reported that 43 people had been rescued as of friday morning. officials had previously listed 84 people as missing, but the number still unaccounted for after the latest recoveries was not immediately clear. survivor accounts collected by the maritime industry authority described two successive explosions before the blaze. the cause has not been established. the vessel also carried motorcycles, an electric vehicle, a forklift, a pickup truck and other cargo, according to the coast guard. the shipowner said it was cooperating with the government investigation. search teams continued working through the heavily damaged interior as families waited for confirmed identifications and updated passenger counts. the sharp rise in fatalities is a major development from the initial reports of five deaths. breaking breaking breaking / developing philippines coron coron, palawan, philippines philippines ferry fire palawan search and rescue maritime safety

breaking-philippine-ferry-fire-toll-76-2.excerpt: Responders recovered 41 additional remains as identification work continued and 13 people remained unaccounted for.
breaking-philippine-ferry-fire-toll-76-2.text: philippine ferry-fire death toll rises to 76 responders recovered 41 additional remains as identification work continued and 13 people remained unaccounted for. the confirmed death toll from a ferry fire in the philippines rose to 76 on saturday after responders recovered 41 additional charred remains, authorities said. thirteen people were still unaccounted for, while 43 survivors had been confirmed from the vessel carrying more than 130 people. rescue teams entered the ferry on friday after the fire was extinguished and found many of the remains in the economy passenger section. the maritime industry authority said survivors reported hearing two explosions, but investigators have not established what started the blaze. identification work is continuing alongside the search for those still missing. the new toll is a substantial increase from earlier reports and may change again as recovery teams complete their work. authorities are also reviewing the passenger count and the sequence of events aboard the vessel. the disaster has shifted from an active rescue toward recovery, identification and investigation, though families are still waiting for definitive information. officials have not announced a final cause. until the inquiry is complete, reports about explosions describe witness accounts rather than a determination of why the fire spread. breaking breaking breaking / developing philippines palawan palawan, philippines philippines ferry fire palawan search and recovery

breaking-philippines-ferry-fire-missing-.excerpt: The Philippine Coast Guard said 43 people were rescued after the MV June Aster caught fire, with the casualty count still subject to change.
breaking-philippines-ferry-fire-missing-.text: five dead and more than 80 missing after philippine ferry fire the philippine coast guard said 43 people were rescued after the mv june aster caught fire, with the casualty count still subject to change. at least five people died and more than 80 were unaccounted for after a passenger ferry caught fire off palawan in the western philippines, the philippine coast guard said thursday. rescuers pulled 43 people from the water wednesday night after flames broke out aboard the mv june aster near coron. coast guard footage showed fire engulfing parts of the vessel as emergency teams worked around it in the dark. the ship’s manifest listed 117 passengers and 17 crew members, coast guard spokesperson commodore noemie cayabyab told dzxl radio. comparing that total with the confirmed survivors and deaths left more than 80 people missing, though officials cautioned that the number could change as search teams verify who was aboard and locate additional survivors. the ferry had departed from baseco in manila and was bound for coron. authorities had not determined what started the fire as of the latest report. search-and-rescue operations and the investigation remained active, making the casualty figures preliminary. breaking breaking breaking / developing international coron coron, philippines philippines ferry fire search and rescue palawan

breaking-philippines-ferry-fire-victim-i.excerpt: Forensic teams are processing remains recovered from the MV June Aster after the death toll reached at least 35 and more than 50 people remained missing.
breaking-philippines-ferry-fire-victim-i.text: philippines begins identifying ferry-fire victims as dozens remain missing forensic teams are processing remains recovered from the mv june aster after the death toll reached at least 35 and more than 50 people remained missing. philippine forensic teams began identifying victims recovered from the burned mv june aster on saturday as authorities reported at least 35 deaths and more than 50 people still missing. bodies were brought to temporary processing tents at the port in coron, where relatives waited for information about passengers who had not been accounted for. the ferry was carrying more than 130 people when it caught fire near the end of a journey lasting more than 20 hours. firefighters entered the vessel friday after extinguishing the blaze, gaining access to sections that had been unreachable because of intense heat and thick smoke. the coast guard said burned remains were found in the economy accommodation area. investigators are also working to determine the cause. the maritime industry authority said survivor accounts included reports of two explosions shortly before the fire, but officials have not established what produced them. identification and the search for missing passengers remain the immediate priorities. the casualty figures may change as teams examine the vessel and reconcile passenger information. breaking breaking breaking / developing philippines coron coron, philippines philippines mv june aster ferry fire search and rescue coron

breaking-portsmouth-rival-protests-three.excerpt: A large police operation separated an anti-immigration march and counter-demonstrators during a second weekend of tension.
breaking-portsmouth-rival-protests-three.text: three arrested as rival protests return to portsmouth a large police operation separated an anti-immigration march and counter-demonstrators during a second weekend of tension. police arrested two men and a 16-year-old boy as an anti-immigration march and counter-demonstration unfolded in portsmouth, england, on saturday. the city saw a large police deployment for a second consecutive weekend after disorder accompanied the arrival of a boat carrying 140 asylum seekers the previous sunday. a 76-year-old southampton man was detained on suspicion of concealing his identity after officers invoked new powers requiring face coverings to be removed. a 33-year-old portsmouth man was arrested on suspicion of obstructing a highway. the teenager was arrested on suspicion of violent disorder connected to the prior weekend, police said. opposing groups were assigned separate gathering areas before marching through the city center. authorities said saturday was largely peaceful outside a small number of incidents, in contrast with the earlier protest in which officers were assaulted and police vehicles and other property were damaged. a man charged over last weekend’s disorder also appeared in court saturday. police have said further arrests tied to those earlier scenes are expected, keeping the public-order investigation active. breaking breaking breaking / developing england portsmouth portsmouth, england portsmouth protests public safety immigration

breaking-qingdao-cargo-ship-fire-25-dead.excerpt: The Ocean Melody was undergoing repairs when fire broke out Thursday; 12 people escaped and five were hospitalized.
breaking-qingdao-cargo-ship-fire-25-dead.text: cargo-ship fire at qingdao shipyard kills 25 the ocean melody was undergoing repairs when fire broke out thursday; 12 people escaped and five were hospitalized. twenty-five people died thursday in a fire aboard a cargo vessel undergoing repairs at a state-owned shipyard in qingdao, eastern china, state media reported. the fire began at about 11:15 a.m. local time during repair and inspection work at the qingdao beihai shipyard. of 42 people aboard, 12 were evacuated safely and five were injured and hospitalized, according to xinhua figures reported by reuters. firefighters extinguished the blaze by early afternoon. images identified the vessel as the ocean melody. lseg ship-tracking data described it as a 20-year-old, liberia-flagged dry bulk carrier that arrived at the yard on august 31 and remained there for repairs. china’s leadership called for intensified rescue work, a rapid investigation and accountability measures. the shipyard is controlled by china state shipbuilding corporation, a major state-owned shipbuilder. the cause of the fire had not been announced. investigators will need to establish where the blaze started, what work was underway and whether fire-control systems and evacuation procedures operated as intended. the casualty count and investigation remain developing. breaking breaking breaking / developing international qingdao qingdao, china qingdao cargo ship shipyard fire ocean melody

breaking-reform-uk-funding-probe-widens-.excerpt: London’s Metropolitan Police expanded an investigation after allegations that party officials discussed ways to evade foreign-donation rules.
breaking-reform-uk-funding-probe-widens-.text: uk police widen criminal probe into reform uk funding allegations london’s metropolitan police expanded an investigation after allegations that party officials discussed ways to evade foreign-donation rules. london’s metropolitan police widened a criminal investigation wednesday after a documentary alleged that reform uk officials discussed ways to breach rules governing foreign political donations, reuters reported. police are assessing whether potential offenses occurred. the expanded inquiry is connected to an existing investigation involving donations and polling. under the relevant allegations, possible offenses could include concealing the true source of funds or supplying false information to a party treasurer. an investigation is not a finding of wrongdoing. reform uk denies misconduct and says it will cooperate with police. the party has described the documentary as a hoax built around loose talk. reuters reported the denial alongside the police announcement, and no court has determined that the party or any individual broke the law. the case remains at an investigative stage, with authorities gathering information before deciding whether charges are warranted. further details will depend on the evidence police obtain and any decisions by prosecutors, making careful attribution important as the inquiry develops. breaking breaking breaking / developing international london london, united kingdom united kingdom reform uk campaign finance police investigation

breaking-russian-strikes-six-killed-ukra.excerpt: Regional officials reported deaths in Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia and Kryvyi Rih, while 37 people were injured in Odesa.
breaking-russian-strikes-six-killed-ukra.text: russian strikes kill six and injure dozens across ukraine regional officials reported deaths in zhytomyr, zaporizhzhia and kryvyi rih, while 37 people were injured in odesa. russian attacks killed at least six people and injured dozens across ukraine on saturday, according to regional officials. two people were killed when a strike hit a grocery store in the zhytomyr region, while two deaths were reported around zaporizhzhia and two more in kryvyi rih. officials said 11 people were injured in zaporizhzhia and nearby communities. in odesa, 37 people were reported hurt, including an infant, and two people remained missing. the casualty reports were still developing as emergency crews worked at multiple damaged sites. russia said its forces struck port facilities, ships and industrial plants. ukraine separately said it hit a synthetic-rubber plant in the russian city of togliatti. reuters said it could not independently verify the battlefield claims from either side. the attacks extended the war’s pressure on civilian areas and infrastructure, with casualty counts subject to revision as rescue operations continue. the geographic spread—from central and southern regions to odesa on the black sea—underscored the scale of the latest exchange and the need to distinguish official claims from independently confirmed damage. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine kyiv ukraine ukraine russia odesa emergency response

breaking-saudi-east-west-pipeline-drone-.excerpt: Damage to Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline may take three to five weeks to repair, according to officials briefed on the situation.
breaking-saudi-east-west-pipeline-drone-.text: saudi oil pipeline could remain out of service for weeks after drone attack damage to saudi arabia’s east-west pipeline may take three to five weeks to repair, according to officials briefed on the situation. damage to saudi arabia’s east-west oil pipeline could keep the system out of service for three to five weeks, officials briefed on the situation told the associated press. the pipeline, which stretches about 1,200 kilometers across saudi arabia, carries crude from gulf ports to yanbu on the red sea. authorities shut it down after an attack thursday that saudi arabia blamed on drones launched by iranian-backed militias in iraq. officials said repairs may allow the line to operate partially, but they could not immediately say how much oil would continue moving during the work. the pipeline has recently carried an average of roughly 2.6 million to 4 million barrels per day, according to an analysis cited by ap. the reported damage adds pressure to global oil logistics at a time when fighting and attacks are already affecting shipping routes around the red sea and nearby waterways. northeast news is labeling the story developing because the repair timeline, pipeline capacity and responsibility for the attack could be revised as saudi authorities and operators release more information. breaking breaking breaking/developing saudi arabia saudi arabia breaking saudi arabia oil pipeline middle east

breaking-saudi-east-west-pipeline-drone-.excerpt: The kingdom temporarily closed the major Red Sea route as a precaution after officials said drones launched from Iraq struck the system.
breaking-saudi-east-west-pipeline-drone-.text: saudi arabia shuts east-west oil pipeline after drone attack the kingdom temporarily closed the major red sea route as a precaution after officials said drones launched from iraq struck the system. saudi arabia temporarily shut its east-west oil pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that officials in baghdad and riyadh said originated in iraq. responsibility for the strike was not immediately clear. the 1,200-kilometer system carries crude from eastern production areas to the red sea, giving the kingdom an export route that bypasses the strait of hormuz. reuters reported that tracking data and analyst estimates put recent pipeline flows at roughly 4 million to 5 million barrels a day, equal to about 4% to 5% of global oil supply. the closure therefore adds a new transportation risk at a time when regional conflict has already pressured maritime routes. no timetable for reopening was immediately announced. the attack followed reports that houthi forces had reached perim island at the mouth of the bab el-mandeb strait, another critical shipping passage. iraq dismissed a military commander and closed a border crossing with iran after the drone launches, while saudi arabia sought additional u.s. assistance. washington offered intelligence support but not direct military action. the pipeline’s status and attribution for the attack remain developing. breaking breaking breaking / developing saudi arabia riyadh saudi arabia saudi arabia east-west pipeline drones oil iraq

breaking-saudi-pipeline-drone-attack-ira.excerpt: Riyadh said it would hold off on retaliation after a request from Iraq's prime minister while reserving the right to protect critical facilities.
breaking-saudi-pipeline-drone-attack-ira.text: saudi arabia says iraq-launched drones hit east-west pipeline riyadh said it would hold off on retaliation after a request from iraq's prime minister while reserving the right to protect critical facilities. saudi arabia said drones launched from iraq struck its east-west oil pipeline on friday, adding another flashpoint to a widening regional conflict. the saudi foreign ministry announced the attack late friday without immediately detailing the extent of the damage. riyadh said it would not retaliate for now after a request from iraq's prime minister. the kingdom nevertheless reserved the right to take measures it considers necessary to protect its sovereignty, security and critical facilities. the east-west pipeline carries crude from eastern production areas toward the red sea, making it an important alternative route when shipping through the strait of hormuz is disrupted. the announcement came amid attacks affecting energy and shipping infrastructure across the gulf and red sea region. any sustained interruption to the saudi pipeline could further complicate oil exports, but authorities had not immediately provided operating or flow data. the source of the drones and responsibility for the attack remained subject to investigation. the situation was developing friday evening, with attention focused on damage assessments and whether diplomatic efforts can prevent a direct saudi response. breaking breaking breaking / developing saudi arabia saudi arabia saudi arabia iraq drone attack oil pipeline middle east

breaking-saudi-us-houthi-military-help-r.excerpt: Three sources told Reuters that Washington declined direct strikes while offering intelligence sharing and targeting assistance as Red Sea tensions rose.
breaking-saudi-us-houthi-military-help-r.text: saudi crown prince sought u.s. military help against houthis, sources say three sources told reuters that washington declined direct strikes while offering intelligence sharing and targeting assistance as red sea tensions rose. saudi crown prince mohammed bin salman asked president donald trump for military assistance against yemen’s iran-aligned houthis, three sources familiar with the matter told reuters. the sources said the leaders spoke at least twice thursday and that the united states did not agree to conduct strikes, instead offering help with intelligence sharing and targeting. the white house did not confirm the calls. a senior administration official said the united states remained in continuous dialogue with saudi arabia and yemen’s government, with a focus on freedom of navigation and support for regional partners. saudi arabia’s government media office did not immediately respond to reuters’ request for comment. two sources also said the head of u.s. central command traveled to saudi arabia for talks thursday. the reported request came as houthi forces advanced along yemen’s red sea coast and reached perim island in the bab el-mandeb strait, according to yemeni government sources. control near that shipping corridor could add pressure to energy and cargo routes already strained by reduced traffic through the strait of hormuz. the situation remains fluid. breaking breaking breaking / developing saudi arabia riyadh riyadh, saudi arabia saudi arabia united states houthis red sea yemen

breaking-sochi-sea-drones-injure-eight-2.excerpt: Regional authorities reported injuries and damage to beach infrastructure after explosions late Wednesday; Reuters verified video from the waterfront.
breaking-sochi-sea-drones-injure-eight-2.text: sea drones injure eight in russia’s black sea resort of sochi regional authorities reported injuries and damage to beach infrastructure after explosions late wednesday; reuters verified video from the waterfront. sea drones injured eight people in the russian black sea resort of sochi late wednesday, authorities in the surrounding krasnodar region said in a statement reported by reuters. officials said beach infrastructure was partially damaged. reuters verified social-media video showing weapons fire and an explosion near an embankment, with people heard screaming. the report did not provide details on the conditions of those injured or identify who launched the drones. sochi is a major resort city and hosted the 2014 winter olympics. russian president vladimir putin also has an official residence in the area, increasing the security significance of an attack near the city’s waterfront. ukraine has carried out frequent aerial-drone strikes against russian energy, export and logistics infrastructure during the war, but attacks using sea drones have been less common. no claim of responsibility was included in the initial report, so attribution remains unresolved. the casualty count and damage assessment may change as regional authorities release additional information. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl sochi sochi, russia sochi sea drones black sea russia

breaking-south-africa-crash-21-killed-20.excerpt: At least 21 people died in a head-on collision in South Africa’s Western Cape, authorities said, with the death toll potentially changing as the investigation continues.
breaking-south-africa-crash-21-killed-20.text: at least 21 killed in south africa crash involving two taxis and suv at least 21 people died in a head-on collision in south africa’s western cape, authorities said, with the death toll potentially changing as the investigation continues. at least 21 people were killed in a crash involving two minibus taxis and an suv in south africa’s western cape, according to authorities cited by the associated press. the collision happened sunday night on a road between prince albert and leeu-gamka. the two taxis collided head-on before the suv became involved, the ap reported. three people were declared dead after being taken to a hospital, and four others were reported in serious condition. the crash closed the n1 highway while emergency crews worked at the scene. officials warned that the death toll could change as investigators identify victims and assess the condition of those hospitalized. an investigation has been opened into what caused the collision. the road connects communities in a remote part of the province, and the number of passengers and the sequence of impacts were still being reviewed in the initial reports. the report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances. breaking breaking breaking/developing south africa western cape, south africa breaking news south africa traffic crash

breaking-south-korea-iran-hormuz-call-20.excerpt: The foreign ministers agreed to keep communication open while South Korea reviews possible support for maritime security in the Gulf.
breaking-south-korea-iran-hormuz-call-20.text: south korea and iran discuss hormuz security as seoul weighs role the foreign ministers agreed to keep communication open while south korea reviews possible support for maritime security in the gulf. south korean foreign minister cho hyun spoke by telephone with iranian foreign minister abbas araqchi about the strait of hormuz and worsening instability in the middle east, seoul said friday. reuters reported that iran requested the call and that both sides agreed to keep diplomatic channels open. cho emphasized freedom of navigation and said south korea would support international efforts to maintain maritime security. araqchi presented iran’s position on the regional conflict. the discussion comes as disruption around the strait has pressured shipping and energy markets far beyond the gulf. south korea is reviewing whether it should contribute personnel to the region and recently sent an inspection team, but officials said no final deployment decision has been made. iran has warned seoul against joining military activity that tehran views as aligned with the united states. the exchange is developing because seoul must balance the security of shipping routes with the risk of deeper involvement in the conflict. south korea depends heavily on imported energy, giving safe passage through hormuz direct economic importance. continued contact with tehran may help clarify intentions while the government assesses its options. breaking breaking breaking / developing south korea seoul seoul, south korea south korea iran strait of hormuz maritime security diplomacy

breaking-springfield-school-cyber-incide.excerpt: All public schools and after-school activities were canceled Tuesday while officials investigated an incident affecting systems used for essential operations.
breaking-springfield-school-cyber-incide.text: springfield public schools close after cyber incident all public schools and after-school activities were canceled tuesday while officials investigated an incident affecting systems used for essential operations. all public schools in springfield, massachusetts, were closed tuesday after a cyber incident interrupted systems needed for essential school operations, new england public media reported. the district also canceled after-school activities and directed staff to stay off district network systems. students with district-issued laptops were told to do the same while officials worked to determine what happened. the incident’s scope remained under investigation. the district’s central office stayed open, although officials warned that some services, including phone lines, could be affected. the closure was described as a step to give technology and school leaders time to address the disruption. officials had not publicly identified the cause, the systems affected or a timetable for full restoration in the report. those details will determine whether the closure remains a one-day response or expands into a larger operational problem. school officials said the closure was intended to protect essential operations while the district worked through the immediate response. more breaking breaking / developing ma springfield springfield, ma massachusetts springfield cybersecurity schools developing

breaking-states-esa-rules-lawsuits-2026.excerpt: Two lawsuits challenge federal changes to habitat protections and the treatment of newly threatened species.
breaking-states-esa-rules-lawsuits-2026.text: twenty states and d.c. sue over weakened endangered-species rules two lawsuits challenge federal changes to habitat protections and the treatment of newly threatened species. twenty states and the district of columbia filed two lawsuits wednesday challenging federal rules that narrow protections under the endangered species act, reuters reported. the cases seek to block changes adopted by the trump administration. one lawsuit contests a revised definition of “harm” that excludes habitat encroachment unless it directly kills or injures wildlife. the second challenges rules that remove broad default protections for newly listed threatened species and require consideration of business objections before critical habitat is designated. the administration says the revisions better reflect the law’s original intent and reduce unnecessary burdens. the states argue that the changes unlawfully weaken safeguards for species and the ecosystems they need to survive. those competing claims will now be tested in court. enacted in 1973, the endangered species act has been credited with helping recover multiple species. the new litigation does not immediately decide whether the rules remain in force; judges must first consider the states’ legal arguments and any requests for interim relief as the cases proceed. breaking breaking breaking / developing us new york united states endangered species act environment lawsuit federal policy

breaking-sumy-shopping-center-drone-stri.excerpt: Regional officials said two other people were injured as rescuers responded to a fire and heavy damage at the site.
breaking-sumy-shopping-center-drone-stri.text: russian drone strike on sumy shopping center kills three regional officials said two other people were injured as rescuers responded to a fire and heavy damage at the site. a russian drone strike hit a shopping center in ukraine’s northern sumy region on wednesday, killing three people and injuring two, according to regional governor oleh hryhorov. emergency crews were responding to a fire at the site. images released by regional authorities showed a heavily damaged building and rubble spread across the area. officials had not published a fuller accounting of the victims in the initial report. the governor’s published image also showed emergency vehicles positioned outside the structure. sumy lies near the russian border and has faced repeated attacks during the war. moscow has said it wants to create a buffer zone in the region, while ukrainian officials have reported sustained pressure on communities and infrastructure close to the frontier. the casualty count and damage assessment could change as rescue work continues. this report relies on statements from ukrainian regional authorities carried by reuters; russia had not provided an immediate public account of the strike in the first update. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine sumy sumy, ukraine ukraine sumy russia drone strike

breaking-susch-switzerland-coach-crash-2.excerpt: Police said a travel coach carrying 48 Dutch passengers crashed near Susch in eastern Switzerland, leaving multiple people dead and injured.
breaking-susch-switzerland-coach-crash-2.text: several killed in swiss alpine coach crash police said a travel coach carrying 48 dutch passengers crashed near susch in eastern switzerland, leaving multiple people dead and injured. several people were killed and several others injured thursday when a travel coach crashed near the alpine village of susch in eastern switzerland, regional police said. emergency teams were sent to the crash site in the canton of graubünden. a spokesperson for the dutch travel industry association anvr, speaking for tour operator oad, said the bus carried 48 passengers and that all were dutch nationals. images published from the scene showed the coach lying on its side with helicopters and emergency vehicles nearby. authorities had not released an exact death toll, the identities of those killed or details about the severity of the injuries in the initial report. the cause of the crash was also not immediately reported. susch is in the lower engadine region, where alpine roads connect communities and mountain passes in southeastern switzerland. because casualty figures and investigative details remained incomplete, the situation was still developing thursday evening. officials were expected to provide further information after emergency work and passenger notifications. breaking breaking breaking / developing international susch susch, switzerland switzerland susch coach crash developing

breaking-sweden-parliamentary-election-v.excerpt: Voters are choosing between the governing right-wing bloc and a narrowly leading centre-left opposition.
breaking-sweden-parliamentary-election-v.text: sweden begins close parliamentary election with government at stake voters are choosing between the governing right-wing bloc and a narrowly leading centre-left opposition. voting began sunday in sweden’s parliamentary election after opinion polls showed a close contest between prime minister ulf kristersson’s governing right-wing bloc and the centre-left opposition led by social democrat magdalena andersson. polls were scheduled to open at 8 a.m. local time and close at 8 p.m., with exit polling expected after voting ends. kristersson has said the sweden democrats would enter a four-party government for the first time if the right wins. the party has supported his minority administration in parliament during the past four years. the centre-left entered election day with a narrow polling lead, but the gap tightened late in the campaign. the result may turn partly on whether the liberals clear the 4% threshold required to win parliamentary seats. both blocs support ukraine and higher military spending, but differ over welfare spending, taxes, immigration and nuclear power. coalition talks could be complicated regardless of which side wins the most support, making the count and party thresholds central to the developing outcome. breaking breaking breaking / developing sweden stockholm stockholm, sweden sweden election parliament europe

breaking-switzerland-hydroelectric-plant.excerpt: Police, firefighters and emergency crews responded in Piotta as investigators worked to determine the cause of the workplace accident.
breaking-switzerland-hydroelectric-plant.text: two seriously injured in explosion at swiss hydroelectric plant police, firefighters and emergency crews responded in piotta as investigators worked to determine the cause of the workplace accident. two people were seriously injured wednesday morning in an explosion at a hydroelectric power station in southern switzerland, according to local authorities. police in the canton of ticino described the incident as a workplace accident in the village of piotta. police officers, firefighters and emergency responders were sent to the site, reuters reported. authorities had not determined the cause or released the exact circumstances in the initial update. the report also did not identify the injured people or provide further details about their conditions beyond saying the injuries were serious. the lack of an established cause makes this a developing incident. officials will need to assess the plant, interview witnesses and determine whether operations or nearby communities face any continuing risk. readers should rely on later police and emergency-management updates for confirmed changes, including any revised injury count, operational disruption or safety guidance. the plant operator had not yet announced the extent of any service interruption. breaking breaking breaking / developing international piotta piotta, switzerland switzerland hydroelectric plant explosion piotta

breaking-syria-idlib-weapons-depot-explo.excerpt: State television reported 11 others injured near Sarmada as officials had not yet disclosed a cause.
breaking-syria-idlib-weapons-depot-explo.text: at least 14 killed in explosion at weapons depot in syria’s idlib state television reported 11 others injured near sarmada as officials had not yet disclosed a cause. at least 14 people were killed and 11 injured wednesday in an explosion at a temporary weapons depot near sarmada in syria’s idlib province, state television reported, according to reuters. the depot contained weapons and remnants of war materials, the report said. authorities had not disclosed the cause of the blast in the first public accounts, leaving unclear whether it resulted from an accident, unstable munitions or another event. casualty figures can change during the first hours after a major explosion as rescue teams search the site and hospitals update patient information. the initial toll and description came from syrian state television; independent details from the location remained limited at the time of publication. the incident underscores the continuing danger posed by stored weapons and explosive remnants in areas affected by years of conflict. investigators will need to determine what material was kept at the temporary facility, how it was secured and what triggered the detonation. this article will be updated when emergency officials or other verified sources provide additional information. breaking breaking breaking / developing international sarmada sarmada, syria syria idlib explosion sarmada

breaking-syria-mezzeh-airport-mass-grave.excerpt: Rights groups and residents say converting the former Mezzeh military airport into a private-jet hub could disturb evidence and unresolved property claims.
breaking-syria-mezzeh-airport-mass-grave.text: damascus airport plan raises mass-grave and land-rights alarm rights groups and residents say converting the former mezzeh military airport into a private-jet hub could disturb evidence and unresolved property claims. syria’s plan to convert the former mezzeh military airport in damascus into a private-jet hub is drawing warnings from rights groups and nearby residents. they say construction could disturb suspected mass graves and forensic evidence while moving ahead of unresolved claims over land taken from local families decades ago. documents reviewed by reuters indicate that the site was used for detention and executions under bashar al-assad’s government. the syria justice and accountability centre says its records point to graves containing more than 1,150 detainees who died after torture or execution. preserving those locations could be essential to identifying victims and documenting abuses. residents of nearby moadamiya also say land was expropriated for the military airport in the 1950s without compensation. they have protested and asked for a role in decisions about the redevelopment, including a process for ownership and compensation claims. united nations officials have called on syria to address property rights, but authorities had not provided substantive public safeguards for either the suspected graves or the disputed land. the project therefore remains under active scrutiny. breaking breaking breaking / developing syria damascus damascus, syria syria damascus mezzeh airport mass graves land rights

breaking-tasia-fortune-homicide-more-arr.excerpt: One man has been arrested after the medical examiner ruled the 29-year-old mother’s August death a homicide.
breaking-tasia-fortune-homicide-more-arr.text: mississippi police expect more arrests in tasia fortune homicide one man has been arrested after the medical examiner ruled the 29-year-old mother’s august death a homicide. police in jackson, mississippi, say additional arrests are expected in the homicide investigation of tasia fortune, a 29-year-old mother of four who was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home on august 3. the state medical examiner ruled the death a homicide, shifting the case from an unexplained death inquiry to an active criminal investigation. authorities arrested 51-year-old jarques ratliff on warrants connected to fortune’s death. police have not publicly described ratliff’s relationship with fortune or provided a suspected motive. investigators also have not detailed what evidence led to the homicide finding, saying the inquiry is continuing. fortune’s family has pressed for answers since her death and welcomed the arrest while emphasizing that key questions remain. relatives described her as resilient and said she had been working to rebuild her life after periods of homelessness and domestic abuse. the announcement that more arrests are anticipated makes the case an active developing story; police are asking that conclusions about responsibility wait for verified findings and court proceedings. breaking breaking breaking / developing mississippi jackson jackson, mississippi jackson tasia fortune homicide investigation mississippi

breaking-trump-iran-pickaxe-mountain-thr.excerpt: The president said he expects the war to continue beyond the U.S. midterms and again raised a possible strike on Pickaxe Mountain.
breaking-trump-iran-pickaxe-mountain-thr.text: trump threatens iran nuclear-linked site as shipping attacks widen the president said he expects the war to continue beyond the u.s. midterms and again raised a possible strike on pickaxe mountain. president donald trump said he expects the war with iran to end after the november u.s. midterm elections and again threatened a possible attack on pickaxe mountain, a site associated with iran’s nuclear program, reuters reported early thursday. the statement came after iran and the united states carried out their largest wave of attacks on shipping during the six-month conflict. iran said it struck 10 ships near the strait of hormuz on wednesday after the united states sank five iranian oil tankers. reuters reported that routes through hormuz and the red sea remained heavily disrupted. regional tensions also spread toward saudi arabia. saudi civil-defense authorities issued repeated emergency alerts in khamis mushait as clashes with yemen’s iran-aligned houthis intensified. the shipping attacks and wider fighting kept energy-supply concerns elevated. trump’s remarks described an expectation and a threat, not a newly completed strike on pickaxe mountain. details about any operational decision were not announced in the reuters report. the situation remains developing, with governments and maritime authorities assessing attacks, vessel damage and risks to commercial traffic across multiple waterways. breaking breaking breaking / developing intl washington washington, d.c. / middle east iran war donald trump shipping middle east

breaking-turkey-southern-wildfires-death.excerpt: Crews are still fighting active fires in parts of Antalya and Adana while other outbreaks are mostly under control.
breaking-turkey-southern-wildfires-death.text: one dead as turkey battles wildfires in southern provinces crews are still fighting active fires in parts of antalya and adana while other outbreaks are mostly under control. one person died after suffering a heart attack linked to smoke inhalation during a wildfire in turkey’s southern antalya province, local officials said wednesday, according to reuters. authorities said fires in antalya’s kumluca district and mersin’s bozyazi district were mostly under control, but crews had not completed extinguishment work. active firefighting continued in antalya’s aksu district and adana’s kozan district as officials worked to contain several outbreaks that began this week. helicopters, aircraft and fire engines were supporting ground crews. residents and farmers also helped move water with tractors and tankers, reuters reported. images from the affected areas showed flames moving through forested land and heavy smoke rising over the region. the emergency remains developing because containment does not mean a fire is fully extinguished, and changing wind or dry conditions can create new risks. officials had not released a comprehensive damage assessment in the first report. residents near active fire zones should rely on local emergency instructions for evacuation, road closures and air-quality guidance as operations continue. breaking breaking breaking / developing international antalya antalya, turkey turkey wildfire antalya emergency response

breaking-uk-air-traffic-failure-2026.excerpt: NATS said a flight-data processing fault was resolved, but cancellations and delays continued across major British airports as airlines repositioned aircraft and crews.
breaking-uk-air-traffic-failure-2026.text: uk airports work through backlog after air-traffic system failure nats said a flight-data processing fault was resolved, but cancellations and delays continued across major british airports as airlines repositioned aircraft and crews. major british airports were working through a travel backlog early wednesday after a technical failure in the united kingdom’s air-traffic control system disrupted roughly 1,000 flights. nats, the country’s air-navigation service, said the fault affected flight-data processing and had been resolved. it said safety was not compromised. heathrow, gatwick, manchester and stansted were among the airports reporting delays or cancellations while airlines rebuilt schedules and repositioned aircraft and crews. ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers were affected and that it canceled more than 50 flights. those figures are the airline’s account of its own operation, while the broader effects varied by carrier and airport. the technical fault is over, but the travel disruption remains a developing story because delays can carry into later departure waves even after air-traffic capacity returns. passengers due to fly wednesday should check directly with their airline before traveling and allow for changes to gates or departure times. britain’s aviation regulator expects a full report on the incident, which will be central to understanding the cause and preventing a repeat. more international united kingdom united kingdom air travel nats flight delays

breaking-uk-nats-outage-investigation-we.excerpt: Flights resumed after Tuesday’s systems failure, but airlines and passengers continued to face disruption from roughly 2,000 cancellations.
