breaking-uk-nats-outage-investigation-we.text: uk gives air-traffic provider one week to investigate nationwide outage flights resumed after tuesday’s systems failure, but airlines and passengers continued to face disruption from roughly 2,000 cancellations. britain’s government has given air-traffic-control provider nats one week to investigate the systems failure that halted flights tuesday and stranded travelers across the country. flights resumed at major airports wednesday, but airlines were still working through displaced aircraft and crews. reuters reported that the hours-long outage led to about 2,000 cancellations and affected hundreds of thousands of passengers. it was the second major nats failure in three years. transport minister heidi alexander summoned nats chief executive martin rolfe for an explanation. she told parliament that the available evidence did not point to a cyberattack, while saying the disruption should not have happened. the civil aviation authority will conduct a separate independent review expected to report within six months. nats said this week’s problem affected its flight-data system and differed from the issue behind the 2023 shutdown. passengers may continue to see knock-on delays while airlines return planes and crews to their planned routes. breaking breaking breaking / developing united kingdom london united kingdom united kingdom air travel nats aviation

breaking-ukraine-moldova-border-drone-st.excerpt: Ukraine’s border service reported deaths, injuries and fires after an overnight strike, while Kyiv also faced attacks without reported casualties.
breaking-ukraine-moldova-border-drone-st.text: russian drones hit ukraine-moldova border crossing ukraine’s border service reported deaths, injuries and fires after an overnight strike, while kyiv also faced attacks without reported casualties. russian drones struck a crossing on the ukraine-moldova border overnight, causing deaths, injuries and fires, ukraine’s border guard service said early wednesday. officials had not provided a precise casualty count in the initial report carried by reuters. the limited information makes the scale of the attack unclear, and emergency crews were still responding at the time of the first public statements. kyiv also came under attack overnight. ukraine’s emergency service reported fires in the capital but said no casualties had been recorded there in the initial assessment. the two locations were part of a broader overnight threat, though officials had not released a complete accounting of launches, interceptions or damage. this is a developing story because casualty figures and site conditions may change as local authorities complete searches and damage assessments. early wartime claims can also be revised. the confirmed core facts at publication are that ukraine reported a russian drone strike at the border crossing, acknowledged casualties without an exact number, and separately reported fires in kyiv. more international ukraine-moldova border ukraine russia drone strike moldova

breaking-ukraine-nine-dead-nearly-500-dr.excerpt: The updated toll and drone count marked a significant escalation from earlier reports of Saturday’s nationwide strikes.
breaking-ukraine-nine-dead-nearly-500-dr.text: ukraine reports nine dead as russia launches nearly 500 drones the updated toll and drone count marked a significant escalation from earlier reports of saturday’s nationwide strikes. ukraine reported at least nine people killed in russian attacks across the country saturday as president volodymyr zelenskiy said moscow had launched nearly 500 drones since early morning. the updated figures represented a substantial rise from earlier reports and kept the nationwide strike wave an active developing story. local authorities reported three deaths in kramatorsk, two at a grocery store in the zhytomyr region, two in zaporizhzhia and two in kryvyi rih. nearly 40 people were injured in the odesa region. russia said its forces targeted industrial sites, while ukraine said civilian buildings and infrastructure were among the locations hit. reuters said it could not independently verify all battlefield accounts. the drone activity also disrupted neighboring moldova, which temporarily closed its airspace and reported seven crossings. ukraine said it struck an industrial facility in togliatti, russia, that produces synthetic rubber used in missile fuel. russian-controlled authorities separately reported three deaths in donetsk from ukrainian strikes. breaking breaking breaking / developing ukraine kyiv kyiv, ukraine ukraine russia drone attacks developing

breaking-ukraine-patriot-missile-contrac.excerpt: Kyiv’s defense chief says most deliveries will take years and is asking allies to release interceptors from existing stocks sooner.
breaking-ukraine-patriot-missile-contrac.text: ukraine contracts for about 1,000 patriot missiles kyiv’s defense chief says most deliveries will take years and is asking allies to release interceptors from existing stocks sooner. ukraine is contracting for roughly 1,000 patriot air-defense missiles with allied help and financing tied to a european union loan, defense minister yevhenii khmara said. khmara told a meeting of the ukraine defense contact group that most of the missiles would arrive over several years. he asked partner countries to provide interceptors from existing stockpiles now, arguing that immediate defenses are needed against continuing russian missile and drone attacks. germany separately said it would urgently supply additional patriot pac-2 interceptors from its own stocks and expand deliveries of other air-defense equipment. nato secretary-general mark rutte urged members to increase support. the contracts represent planned supply, not 1,000 missiles already delivered or available for use. timing, participating suppliers and annual delivery volumes were not fully detailed in the initial report. ukraine also identified a major financing gap for drone purchases. the story remains developing because allied commitments, production schedules and near-term transfers will determine how quickly the announced plan strengthens air defenses. more international ukraine ukraine patriot missiles air defense nato

breaking-us-caribbean-vessel-strike-2026.excerpt: U.S. Southern Command said three people were killed in the latest military action against a vessel it alleged was using drug-trafficking routes.
breaking-us-caribbean-vessel-strike-2026.text: u.s. military says caribbean vessel strike killed three u.s. southern command said three people were killed in the latest military action against a vessel it alleged was using drug-trafficking routes. the u.s. military said it struck a fast-moving vessel in the caribbean sea on wednesday, killing three people aboard in the latest operation washington describes as targeting drug-trafficking networks. u.s. southern command said the vessel was traveling along established trafficking routes and alleged that intelligence confirmed its involvement in narcotics activity. the command did not publicly provide evidence supporting that claim or release the identities of those killed. the action is part of a campaign of strikes on vessels in the caribbean and eastern pacific that began in september 2025. the military says the operations are aimed at people it calls narco-terrorists, while legal experts and human-rights organizations have questioned whether the strikes comply with international and u.s. law. reuters reported that more than 220 people have been killed across the campaign. details about wednesday’s location, the vessel’s cargo and any recovery operation were not immediately disclosed. the account is based on the military’s statement and remains subject to further verification. breaking breaking breaking / developing international washington caribbean sea u.s. military caribbean vessel strike southern command

breaking-us-destroys-iranian-oil-tankers.excerpt: Central Command said the strikes answered two attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a U.S. warship over two days.
breaking-us-destroys-iranian-oil-tankers.text: u.s. says it destroyed five iranian oil tankers after warship attacks central command said the strikes answered two attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a u.s. warship over two days. the u.s. military said tuesday that it destroyed five iranian crude-oil tankers after iran’s revolutionary guard tried twice to strike an american warship with ballistic missiles over the previous two days. u.s. central command announced the action in a social media post, according to the associated press. the military described the tanker strikes as a response to the attempted attacks on the warship. the ap did not immediately report the names of the vessels, their locations or independent confirmation of the damage. the exchange marks a new escalation in more than six months of conflict between washington and tehran. it also adds uncertainty around energy shipping at a time when attacks on saudi facilities and disruptions near major gulf export routes have already pushed oil prices higher. because the situation is developing, early military claims may change as more information becomes available. the immediate questions include whether there were casualties, how iran will respond and whether commercial traffic faces new restrictions. shipping notices and statements from regional governments will be critical to verifying the wider impact. more us middle east breaking iran u.s. military oil shipping

breaking-us-iran-aviation-sanctions-2026.excerpt: The Treasury Department designated dozens of airlines and related entities while suspending authorizations for some Iranian aviation activity.
breaking-us-iran-aviation-sanctions-2026.text: u.s. expands iran aviation sanctions in new treasury action the treasury department designated dozens of airlines and related entities while suspending authorizations for some iranian aviation activity. the u.s. treasury department imposed 36 new iran-related sanctions tuesday, with most of the designations focused on aviation companies and their support networks, reuters reported. the action targeted 27 iranian airlines and related businesses, along with front companies, cargo handlers and intermediaries in turkey, the united arab emirates, malaysia and kazakhstan. treasury also suspended aviation authorizations that had allowed certain overflights and some commercial aircraft operations. the measures expand financial and operational pressure on iran’s aviation sector, including mahan air. a designation generally blocks property subject to u.s. jurisdiction and restricts transactions by u.s. persons, but the practical effect on individual flights and carriers will depend on implementation and compliance outside the united states. the sanctions are part of a developing u.s. policy response and are distinct from recent military events in the region. treasury published the designations through its office of foreign assets control. additional guidance or licensing decisions could clarify the scope, so this report reflects the agency action announced tuesday rather than predicting its longer-term impact. more us washington, d.c. iran treasury department sanctions aviation

breaking-us-sanctions-iran-proxy-network.excerpt: Treasury targeted entities and individuals in four countries and tightened its approach to Iran-related licensing as the regional conflict continues.
breaking-us-sanctions-iran-proxy-network.text: u.s. expands sanctions on networks tied to iranian proxies treasury targeted entities and individuals in four countries and tightened its approach to iran-related licensing as the regional conflict continues. the u.s. treasury department announced new sanctions thursday against companies and individuals it says support hezbollah and other iranian-aligned groups, expanding washington’s economic campaign during the continuing regional conflict. the office of foreign assets control targeted people and entities in iraq, the united arab emirates, lebanon and turkey. treasury said the networks supported kata’ib hezbollah, an iraqi paramilitary group linked to iran’s revolutionary guard corps, and lebanon’s hezbollah. the measures fall under operation economic outcast, a campaign treasury announced august 24 to restrict funding tied to iran’s military, missile development, cyber activity and the revolutionary guard. ofac also said it would deny most iran-related license requests except in exceptional circumstances. separately, a u.s. citizen agreed to pay $1.43 million to resolve potential civil liability involving 39 apparent sanctions violations. the newest designations did not target yemen’s houthis, whose red sea advances are creating a separate threat to shipping. the practical effect of the latest sanctions will depend on enforcement and the ability of designated networks to find alternative financial channels. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states washington washington, dc iran sanctions hezbollah u.s. treasury

breaking-vanuatu-mv-matui-ferry-sinks-20.excerpt: Search teams continued looking for passengers and crew from the MV Matui after the inter-island vessel went down in bad weather.
breaking-vanuatu-mv-matui-ferry-sinks-20.text: one dead and more than 30 missing after vanuatu ferry sinks search teams continued looking for passengers and crew from the mv matui after the inter-island vessel went down in bad weather. at least one person was confirmed dead and more than 30 remained missing sunday after an inter-island ferry sank off vanuatu, prime minister jotham napat’s office said. search-and-rescue operations were continuing in the pacific nation as authorities worked to account for the passengers and crew aboard the mv matui. the prime minister’s office said 15 people had been found alive. the vessel went down in bad weather friday while traveling between the islands of ambae and santo, according to new zealand public broadcaster rnz. officials had not yet released a complete passenger manifest or a definitive total for everyone aboard. the continuing operation leaves the toll provisional. teams face the challenge of searching open water around an island chain spread across a large area of the southwest pacific. authorities were expected to provide further information as survivors were located and identities confirmed. the cause of the sinking had not been established in the initial official account. breaking breaking breaking / developing vanuatu ambae waters between ambae and santo, vanuatu vanuatu mv matui ferry sinking search and rescue

breaking-white-house-dpa-refinery-expans.excerpt: Officials are considering tools to improve and expand existing facilities, but Reuters reports that no final decision has been made.
breaking-white-house-dpa-refinery-expans.text: white house weighs defense production act for refinery expansion officials are considering tools to improve and expand existing facilities, but reuters reports that no final decision has been made. the white house is considering whether to use the defense production act to expand u.s. oil-refining capacity as elevated fuel costs increase pressure on the domestic energy system, reuters reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. no final decision has been made, and further talks with refiners are expected. the discussions are focused on improving efficiency and adding capacity at existing facilities rather than relying only on the construction of entirely new refineries, which can take years and require large capital commitments. reuters reported that u.s. refining utilization has been running near 98%, leaving limited room to increase output through higher operating rates alone. the administration is also evaluating permitting changes, regulatory steps and investment incentives. the defense production act can give the federal government tools to prioritize contracts and support production considered important to national security, but any specific application to refining would depend on the policy ultimately selected. the review is developing against the backdrop of disrupted middle east energy flows and higher transportation costs. until an action is announced, the proposal remains one option under consideration rather than a new requirement for the industry. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states washington washington, d.c. defense production act oil refining white house energy fuel supply

breaking-who-regional-director-saima-waz.text: who regional director resigns amid fraud investigations saima wazed left her southeast asia post effective immediately after being placed on unpaid leave; she denies the allegations. saima wazed resigned wednesday as the world health organization’s regional director for southeast asia, effective immediately, according to a resignation letter reviewed by reuters. wazed, the daughter of former bangladeshi prime minister sheikh hasina, began a five-year term in early 2024. the who placed her on unpaid administrative leave in 2025 after bangladesh’s anti-corruption commission filed charges alleging fraud and forgery. reuters reported that the who separately alleged financial fraud connected to travel, misrepresentation of academic credentials and improper acquisition of land. wazed has denied the allegations and has said the land was obtained before she joined the organization under a law covering the family of bangladesh’s independence leader. the departure creates an immediate leadership vacancy across a who region that includes 11 countries. reuters reported that the organization is expected to begin the process of electing a replacement next month. the investigations and related legal proceedings remain unresolved. interim leadership arrangements were not detailed in the report. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi / geneva who saima wazed bangladesh public health

breaking-xi-brics-middle-east-peacemakin.text: xi urges brics to pursue peacemaking role in middle east war the chinese president called for a peace role as the expanded bloc navigates differences between iran and the united arab emirates. chinese president xi jinping urged brics members to take a peacemaking role in the middle east war during an address to the bloc’s leaders in new delhi on saturday. xi said the conflict does not serve the international community and that china would work with other members on efforts aimed at peace. the appeal came as brics leaders tried to bridge divisions between iran and the united arab emirates, both members of the expanded group but positioned differently in the regional conflict. their summit agenda includes diplomacy, economic cooperation and the bloc’s effort to increase the influence of emerging and developing nations in global institutions. xi also said china will take over the brics chairmanship in 2027 and host the organization’s 19th summit. the group now includes brazil, russia, india, china, south africa, egypt, ethiopia, indonesia, iran and the uae. xi’s remarks do not establish a peace process on their own, but they signal that middle east diplomacy has become a central test of whether the expanded bloc can coordinate across competing national interests. further summit statements and bilateral meetings are expected as the gathering continues. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india brics xi jinping middle east diplomacy new delhi

breaking-xi-delhi-brics-modi-talks-2026.text: xi arrives in delhi for brics summit and modi talks the chinese president’s first visit to india in seven years moves a planned meeting with prime minister narendra modi from preparation to a closely watched diplomatic test. chinese president xi jinping arrived in new delhi on saturday for the brics summit and a scheduled meeting with indian prime minister narendra modi, indian television channels reported. it is xi’s first visit to india in seven years and turns days of planning into a direct diplomatic test for asia’s two most populous countries. the leaders are expected to meet saturday evening. their talks come after a gradual effort to stabilize relations damaged by the 2020 border clash in the himalayas, which killed 20 indian soldiers and four chinese troops. xi and modi have met twice in the past three years, but unresolved border and strategic tensions continue to shape the relationship. the brics gathering provides a broader setting for discussions among major emerging economies, while the bilateral meeting offers a measure of whether recent contacts can produce practical progress. no outcome had been announced at the time of xi’s arrival. attention will center on the language used after the talks and whether the two governments identify concrete steps on border management, trade or diplomatic engagement. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india xi jinping narendra modi brics china india

breaking-yankee-stadium-legionella-cooli.excerpt: New York City officials found Legionella bacteria in one Yankee Stadium cooling tower as they investigated a Bronx outbreak that has sickened 10 people.
breaking-yankee-stadium-legionella-cooli.text: legionella found in yankee stadium cooling tower amid bronx outbreak new york city officials found legionella bacteria in one yankee stadium cooling tower as they investigated a bronx outbreak that has sickened 10 people. legionella bacteria were found in one of 10 cooling towers at yankee stadium as new york city officials investigated a legionnaires’ disease outbreak in the bronx, the associated press reported monday. ten cases and one death had been reported in the outbreak, with three people hospitalized. officials were testing to determine whether the bacteria found at the stadium were live. the new york yankees said no current cases had been linked to the stadium and said the affected tower was cleaned on sunday. city officials ordered building owners in the affected area to clean and disinfect cooling towers. legionnaires’ disease is not spread person to person, according to the report. culture testing can take up to two weeks, leaving the investigation open while health officials compare samples and continue monitoring new cases in the bronx. the investigation will need to distinguish a contaminated tower from any source connected to the reported illnesses, and officials had not said that the stadium caused any of the cases. breaking breaking breaking / developing new york new york the bronx, new york bronx legionella yankee stadium public health

breaking-zelenskiy-plane-drone-norway-20.text: norway’s prime minister says drone nearly hit zelenskiy’s plane jonas gahr stoere said the incident occurred tuesday as ukraine’s president traveled to oslo, but gave few details. norwegian prime minister jonas gahr stoere said wednesday that a drone almost struck the plane carrying ukrainian president volodymyr zelenskiy during a trip to oslo. stoere told public broadcaster nrk that the incident happened tuesday as zelenskiy departed moldova. he did not identify the source of his information or provide details about the drone, its operator or how close it came to the aircraft. zelenskiy arrived in norway for the funeral of king harald v and joined other leaders in the procession. he was also scheduled to discuss ukraine’s air defenses with stoere and meet companies involved in the freyja european anti-ballistic defense initiative. the funeral drew world leaders into a procession behind the late king’s coffin. zelenskiy left norway after the ceremony. the limited public information leaves important questions unresolved, including whether aviation or security authorities independently confirmed the encounter. officials may release additional details as they review the flight and any surveillance data. breaking breaking breaking / developing norway oslo oslo, norway ukraine norway volodymyr zelenskiy aviation security

copper-ai-infrastructure.excerpt: Demand from data centers, electrical grids and electric vehicles is colliding with supply constraints and trade-policy uncertainty.
copper-ai-infrastructure.text: record copper prices show the material cost of the ai boom demand from data centers, electrical grids and electric vehicles is colliding with supply constraints and trade-policy uncertainty. copper prices reached a record tuesday as demand from ai data centers and other power-intensive industries met concerns about supply and possible tariffs. barron’s reported that new york front-month copper futures rose 2.8% to $6.78 per pound, surpassing the previous record. mining shares also advanced as investors priced in the possibility of sustained demand. copper is a useful marker for the physical buildout behind digital services. data centers, transmission upgrades and electric vehicles all require substantial amounts of the metal, even as miners face long development timelines. the move is a reminder that the ai economy is not only a software story. materials, electricity, construction and regional infrastructure are part of the same investment cycle. markets ma markets copper ai commodities energy

ct-small-business-health-insurance-tax-c.excerpt: Businesses with 50 or fewer employees can seek up to $1,000 per covered worker each year for two years when they offer individual coverage through Access Health CT.
ct-small-business-health-insurance-tax-c.text: connecticut opens health-insurance tax credit for small businesses businesses with 50 or fewer employees can seek up to $1,000 per covered worker each year for two years when they offer individual coverage through access health ct. connecticut has opened a new state tax credit for small businesses that help employees buy health coverage through access health ct, gov. ned lamont's office announced wednesday. eligible businesses with 50 or fewer employees can receive up to $1,000 per covered worker each year for two consecutive years. to qualify, an employer must offer an individual coverage health reimbursement arrangement through the marketplace's businessplus platform. the credit was approved by the general assembly during the 2026 regular session and is available through the state department of revenue services. the program is capped at $5 million, according to the governor's office, enough to support roughly 5,000 covered employees if businesses claim the full amount. under an ichra, an employer sets a monthly contribution and eligible workers use that allowance toward an individual plan available through access health ct. the state says the program is intended to give smaller employers another way to offer benefits while helping workers manage premium costs. new-england new-england new england ct hartford connecticut connecticut health insurance small business tax credit access health ct

ct-west-haven-state-funding-2026-09-24.excerpt: The announced funding would support public-space and small-business improvements downtown, plus a University of New Haven center focused on workforce training and applied technology.
ct-west-haven-state-funding-2026-09-24.text: west haven backs $7.5 million state package for downtown and innovation projects the announced funding would support public-space and small-business improvements downtown, plus a university of new haven center focused on workforce training and applied technology. west haven is set to receive a combined $7.5 million in state-backed support for downtown improvements and a university of new haven innovation center, state sen. james maroney announced wednesday. the package includes $2.5 million for public-space work at the west haven green and 9 curtiss place plaza and alleyway. the city says the project also would create a microgrant program for businesses in the village improvement district, helping fund leaseholder improvements, vacant-storefront work and facade upgrades. the remaining $5 million is designated for renovation of the former railroad salvage property in allingtown. the university of new haven plans to use the site for a center for innovation and applied technology with workforce-training facilities and space for industry partners. the projects are part of connecticut's community investment fund 2030, which directs state bond funding toward community development and economic revitalization. west haven said the downtown grant's approval by the fund board clears the way for the state bond commission to consider final approval, while the university project has been described as a $10 million innovation-center effort supported by a $5 million state grant. new-england new-england new england ct west haven west haven, connecticut connecticut west haven economic development community investment fund university of new haven workforce training

Franklin Residents Encourage Bradley Minnich to Consider 2027 Mayoral Run
Several Franklin residents are encouraging Bradley Minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election.
franklin-residents-encourage-minnich-to-.text: franklin residents encourage minnich to run for mayor franklin residents encourage bradley minnich to consider 2027 mayoral run several franklin residents are encouraging bradley minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election. franklin residents are encouraging bradley minnich to consider running for mayor in the city’s next municipal election. their encouragement reflects early community interest, although no formal campaign or candidacy has been announced by bradley minnich. bradley minnich, 25, is a large land owner in franklin, nh and a former district manager of a food chain in neighboring town, tilton, where he employed dozens of franklin’s youth over the course of several years. there he led supporting events in collabortion with the franklin highschool and neigboring town fairs. minnich’s acts have led to him being recognized as a "postive influence” from sources. franklin’s municipal elections take place in odd-numbered years, typically in early october. the most recent contest, held on october 7, 2025, saw challenger glenn morrill defeat incumbent desiree mclaughlin. morrill was sworn in as mayor in january 2026 along with newly elected city councilors. under the city’s charter, the mayor is elected every two years, making the 2027 race the next opportunity for residents to choose franklin’s chief elected official. sources say: "morrill, a lifelong franklin resident, campaigned in 2025 on themes of collaboration at city hall, support for local recreation, and carefully managed capital projects. since taking office, he has highlighted priorities that include expanding affordable housing options, encouraging local business and industry growth, and establishing a citywide recycling program. outgoing mayor mclaughlin used her final council meeting to praise the incoming leadership while expressing concern about the loss of institutional knowledge among newer officials." minnich has not released a campaign platform or confirmed whether he intends to enter the race. if he chooses to run, issues facing franklin—including economic development, housing, municipal services, infrastructure, and the city’s long-term growth—would likely shape the discussion surrounding a potential candidacy. these same topics dominated candidate forums and voter conversations during the 2025 election cycle, when turnout rose noticeably compared with the prior municipal vote. the expressions of support for minnich remain informal, and no petition, campaign committee, or organized political group has been announced. the next formal steps would include minnich deciding whether to become a candidate and completing any filing requirements established for franklin’s 2027 municipal election. filing periods for city offices in new hampshire cities generally open in the summer of the election year, with exact dates set by the city clerk. franklin, a city of roughly 8,850 residents in merrimack county, operates under a mayor–city manager form of government. the mayor works with a nine-member city council (three wards) and appoints or serves on various boards. local leaders and residents continue to focus on balancing growth with the preservation of franklin’s character as a small lakes region community. more information about minnich’s professional background is available on his [linkedin profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bradleyminnich/). new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh franklin franklin, nh franklin mayor local government

ma-agawam-ambulance-crash-police-update-.excerpt: A new police account links the weekend Springfield crash to an earlier traffic stop; two paramedics suffered minor injuries.
ma-agawam-ambulance-crash-police-update-.text: police say jeep fled chicopee stop before striking agawam ambulance a new police account links the weekend springfield crash to an earlier traffic stop; two paramedics suffered minor injuries. chicopee police said tuesday that a jeep involved in a weekend crash with an agawam ambulance had fled an attempted traffic stop earlier that night. western mass news reported that the ambulance was traveling on a mutual-aid call when the vehicles collided around 1:30 a.m. saturday at boland way and east columbus avenue in springfield. two agawam firefighter-paramedics were treated for minor injuries. a passenger in the jeep was ejected and taken to a hospital. police said there were no reported serious injuries from the crash, though the passenger’s specific condition was not released. the jeep’s driver, a palmer man, was detained by springfield police and transferred to chicopee police. authorities said the driver faces multiple charges, but the station’s update did not provide the complete list or identify him. the allegations have not been proven in court. the new account clarifies the sequence before the collision while leaving questions about speed, impairment and the final crash reconstruction unanswered. the ambulance had been in service for less than a month. new-england ma springfield, massachusetts massachusetts agawam chicopee ambulance

ma-alpha-school-three-ai-powered-campuse.excerpt: The private K-8 network is bringing its two-hour personalized-academics model to Lexington, Beacon Hill and Jamaica Plain at $65,000 a year.
ma-alpha-school-three-ai-powered-campuse.text: ai-focused alpha school opens three greater boston campuses the private k-8 network is bringing its two-hour personalized-academics model to lexington, beacon hill and jamaica plain at $65,000 a year. alpha school is opening three greater boston locations this fall, bringing an artificial-intelligence-centered private-school model to lexington, beacon hill and jamaica plain. the jamaica plain campus will occupy the former croft school site. tuition is $65,000 a year, and the network says the three campuses can eventually serve about 500 students from kindergarten through eighth grade. the school says personalized software assesses each child’s academic level and lets students complete core subjects in roughly two hours a day. adults in the classrooms are called guides and focus on motivation and emotional support; alpha says those positions pay at least $100,000. the remainder of the school day is organized around workshops in entrepreneurship, financial literacy, public speaking and other practical skills. the model is also prompting scrutiny. mit education-technology researcher justin reich told nbc10 boston that individualized computer work can reduce opportunities for students to deliberate and learn alongside classmates with different perspectives. alpha argues that shorter academic blocks leave more time for human connection and applied learning. the openings will give massachusetts families and educators a local test of those competing claims as enrollment builds over several years. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston greater boston, massachusetts alpha school artificial intelligence education greater boston private schools

ma-amy-sweeney-flight-11-courage-remembe.excerpt: The Massachusetts flight attendant relayed crucial details about the hijacking before the plane struck the World Trade Center.
ma-amy-sweeney-flight-11-courage-remembe.text: friend remembers flight 11 attendant amy sweeney’s final act of courage the massachusetts flight attendant relayed crucial details about the hijacking before the plane struck the world trade center. a close friend of madeline “amy” sweeney is remembering the massachusetts flight attendant’s courage aboard american airlines flight 11 on the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks. sweeney was working the boston-to-los angeles flight when it was hijacked after departing logan airport. before the aircraft struck the world trade center’s north tower, she contacted american airlines and relayed critical information about what was happening aboard the plane. barbara bowen, a fellow flight attendant and longtime friend, told whdh that the two had built a friendship through years of trips and shared family milestones. bowen had switched crews so she could be home when her son started school, leaving her away from flight 11 that morning. massachusetts later created the madeline amy sweeney award for civilian bravery in her name. the annual honor recognizes people who show exceptional courage while trying to save another person’s life. friday’s remembrance linked sweeney’s final call to that continuing public legacy and to boston’s central role in the history of the attacks. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts amy sweeney flight 11 logan airport september 11 civilian bravery

ma-ashlyn-mercier-westborough-police-ret.excerpt: The patrol officer is back at the department after the Miss America competition, continuing two public-service roles centered on community support.
ma-ashlyn-mercier-westborough-police-ret.text: miss massachusetts ashlyn mercier returns to westborough police duty the patrol officer is back at the department after the miss america competition, continuing two public-service roles centered on community support. ashlyn mercier has returned to patrol duty with the westborough police department after representing massachusetts in the miss america competition. mercier won the miss massachusetts title june 20, becoming the first police officer to hold the state crown, and has continued balancing pageant appearances with the demands of local law enforcement. mercier joined the westborough department in 2025 after earning a college degree in national security. she had stepped away from pageant competition the previous year to attend the police academy, then returned after completing that training. her path places two different forms of public-facing work on the same schedule: emergency response and community outreach. her service platform, “nick’s courage: one smile goes a mile,” is named for her younger brother nicholas, a two-time pediatric cancer survivor. the initiative promotes encouragement and support for critically ill children and their families. back in uniform, mercier is emphasizing the common ground between her roles: showing up for people during difficult moments, whether through police work in westborough or appearances connected to her statewide title. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma westborough westborough, massachusetts ashlyn mercier westborough miss massachusetts police community service

ma-attleboro-donut-shop-hammer-robbery-2.excerpt: Police released surveillance images while searching for a masked man accused of threatening an employee with a claw hammer.
ma-attleboro-donut-shop-hammer-robbery-2.text: police seek suspect in attleboro donut-shop hammer robbery police released surveillance images while searching for a masked man accused of threatening an employee with a claw hammer. attleboro police are asking the public to help identify a masked man accused of robbing a south attleboro donut shop while carrying a claw hammer. officers responded to a hold-up alarm at vista donuts, 1096 washington street, at about 5:08 a.m. sunday, september 6. an employee told investigators that the man entered shortly after the shop opened, displayed the hammer and threatened to take what he wanted. police described the suspect as a thin white man, possibly in his late 20s or early 30s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall. surveillance images released by the department show him wearing a surgical-style mask and carrying a backpack with distinctive colors. he was last seen running north on washington street. no injuries were reported in the initial account, and police have not announced an arrest. anyone who recognizes the suspect or has information about the robbery is asked to contact attleboro police detective alexander d’agostino at 508-222-1212 and reference case number 26-75673. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma attleboro attleboro, ma attleboro robbery police search vista donuts

ma-attleboro-global-war-terrorism-monume.excerpt: The Capron Park memorial honors local service members who took part in the Global War on Terrorism and those whose losses continued after deployment.
ma-attleboro-global-war-terrorism-monume.text: attleboro dedicates monument to post-september 11 service the capron park memorial honors local service members who took part in the global war on terrorism and those whose losses continued after deployment. attleboro leaders and residents dedicated a new global war on terrorism monument at capron park on friday, placing a permanent marker for local military service in the city’s central public space. the memorial recognizes attleboro service members who served in the conflicts and operations that followed the september 11, 2001, attacks. the ceremony was held on the attacks’ 25th anniversary. speakers emphasized that the human cost of the wars extended beyond combat deaths to veterans and families who continued to carry losses after deployments ended. the monument was organized by attleboro’s global war on terrorism committee, bringing the project from a community effort to a completed civic memorial. funding came from the state and from donations by residents and small businesses, according to nbc 10. that mix of public and local support made the dedication both a veterans observance and a community project. with the monument now installed in capron park, attleboro has added a specific place for future ceremonies and private reflection on more than two decades of service connected to the post-september 11 era. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts attleboro attleboro, massachusetts attleboro veterans september 11 capron park memorial

ma-audit-finds-unemployment-assistance-f.excerpt: The state auditor found that more than half of recorded calls took at least 30 minutes to reach an agent or prompt, while the agency says wait times have since fallen.
ma-audit-finds-unemployment-assistance-f.text: massachusetts audit finds long waits and missed standards at unemployment agency the state auditor found that more than half of recorded calls took at least 30 minutes to reach an agent or prompt, while the agency says wait times have since fallen. a massachusetts state audit released monday found that the department of unemployment assistance failed to set and monitor call-center response standards, missed federal timeliness targets for first benefit payments and did not provide the in-person help required by state law at three regional offices. the auditor's office said 381,915 calls — 52% of the inbound calls in the records it reviewed — took at least 30 minutes to reach an agent or automated prompt. more than 173,000 callers, about 24%, waited over an hour. the department also did not retain call logs for the three years required by state records rules, limiting the auditor's review. the report covered department operations from july 2022 through june 2024, with call-center data reviewed from august 2024 through august 2025 because older logs were unavailable. auditors said first-payment timeliness standards were missed during the audit period, and found dua itself was not providing required in-person assistance at its lawrence, brockton and springfield offices. at least 33,000 email exchanges between the department and legislative offices involved lawmakers seeking help for constituents, the auditor said. the department told wcvb that changes made after the audit period — including a modernized system, added adjudicators and seasonal staff, and a claimant-support pilot — have reduced call waits to 4 to 11 minutes, cleared a longstanding backlog and sped up claims. the auditor noted that those later changes do not resolve whether the agency met the standards during the period reviewed, and said it will follow up on the findings. the audit recommends documented call-response targets, complaint tracking and required in-person services. the findings affect workers relying on unemployment benefits while they search for jobs, as well as employers that fund the state program. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston massachusetts massachusetts unemployment department of unemployment assistance state audit labor

ma-benefit-fraud-nine-charged-2026.excerpt: Federal prosecutors say stolen identities were used to obtain nearly $1 million through SNAP, MassHealth and Social Security programs.
ma-benefit-fraud-nine-charged-2026.text: nine charged in alleged massachusetts benefit-fraud scheme federal prosecutors say stolen identities were used to obtain nearly $1 million through snap, masshealth and social security programs. nine people have been charged in an alleged fraud scheme involving nearly $1 million in public benefits, according to federal prosecutors cited by nbc 10 wjar. the government alleges that stolen identities were used to obtain identification documents and benefits through the supplemental nutrition assistance program, masshealth and social security. prosecutors say some of the activity continued for extended periods, allowing benefits to accumulate under identities that did not belong to the defendants. in one example described by the justice department, mercedes soto capellan allegedly used a stolen identity to obtain approximately $65,521 in snap and masshealth benefits. the broader total cited by authorities covers the alleged conduct of all nine defendants, not a single person. the charges begin a court process and are not findings of guilt. each defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. the case also highlights why benefit agencies cross-check identity, eligibility and payment records: fraud can divert limited program resources, but enforcement claims still must be tested through evidence and due process in court. new-england ma massachusetts massachusetts benefit fraud snap masshealth

ma-blue-envelope-autistic-drivers-statew.excerpt: The free, voluntary envelopes give autistic motorists a recognizable way to share documents and communication guidance during traffic stops.
ma-blue-envelope-autistic-drivers-statew.text: blue envelope program expands statewide support for autistic drivers the free, voluntary envelopes give autistic motorists a recognizable way to share documents and communication guidance during traffic stops. massachusetts has launched a statewide blue envelope program intended to make traffic stops safer and clearer for autistic drivers and passengers. the free, voluntary envelope can hold a driver’s license, vehicle registration and emergency-contact card. its exterior provides communication guidance for law-enforcement officers, while a qr code offers additional information. drivers may keep the envelope on a sun visor or in another visible, accessible place and hand it to an officer during an interaction. the program became state law in june and expanded availability at registry of motor vehicles locations beginning september 1. envelopes are also available through state police barracks and participating local police departments, with mail requests offered through the statewide program. using an envelope is optional and does not change a driver’s legal obligations during a stop. its purpose is to reduce anxiety and help both the motorist and officer recognize communication needs before misunderstanding escalates. families and drivers should keep the documents inside current and check the state’s program page for locations and request instructions. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston massachusetts blue envelope autism traffic stops massachusetts

ma-bmc-nurses-strike-authorization-vote-.excerpt: The two-day union vote follows months of contract talks, but approval would not itself schedule a walkout.
ma-bmc-nurses-strike-authorization-vote-.text: nearly 2,000 boston medical center nurses vote on strike authorization the two-day union vote follows months of contract talks, but approval would not itself schedule a walkout. nearly 2,000 nurses at boston medical center began voting wednesday on whether to authorize a possible strike, wcvb reported. the balloting is scheduled to continue through thursday as the union and hospital remain in contract negotiations. a yes vote would give union leaders authority to call a strike later, but it would not automatically start or schedule a walkout. any strike would require an additional decision and formal notice, leaving time for negotiations to continue after the vote. the nurses held a one-day informational picket in july while talks were underway. that demonstration did not interrupt patient care. the new vote represents a further escalation in the labor process, though its immediate outcome is limited to authorizing future action. boston medical center is a major safety-net hospital, so any potential disruption would carry regional importance. for now, patients should distinguish between an authorization vote and an announced strike date. the count and any subsequent bargaining developments will determine whether the dispute advances beyond this week’s balloting. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, ma boston medical center nurses labor health care

ma-boston-animal-cruelty-dogs-charges-20.excerpt: Lester James, 39, faces seven animal-cruelty counts after police found one dead dog and six living dogs in an apartment, according to prosecutors.
ma-boston-animal-cruelty-dogs-charges-20.text: boston man charged after police find dead dog and six emaciated dogs lester james, 39, faces seven animal-cruelty counts after police found one dead dog and six living dogs in an apartment, according to prosecutors. a boston man faces seven counts of animal cruelty after police found a dead pit bull and six other dogs described as emaciated inside an old colony avenue apartment, boston 25 news reported. lester james, 39, was arraigned after officers responded to a 911 call on sept. 7. the six living dogs were removed from the apartment and taken for veterinary care. the deceased dog was also taken from the unit as investigators documented the conditions. the charges concern allegations and have not been proved in court. a judge set bail at $5,000 and ordered james not to possess animals. the court also ordered a mental-health evaluation, according to the report. james is due back for another hearing on oct. 20, while the case proceeds through the criminal court system. the hearing will give the defense and prosecutors another opportunity to address the animals’ condition and the evidence supporting the charges. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston animal cruelty dogs suffolk county

ma-boston-college-bodie-kahoun-injury-20.text: boston college linebacker has movement after serious injury bodie kahoun was taken to a hospital after being immobilized and carried from friday night's game against rutgers. boston college linebacker bodie kahoun had movement in all of his extremities after suffering a serious injury during friday night's game against rutgers, the school said. medical personnel immobilized kahoun, placed him on a stretcher and moved him by ambulance to a local hospital for further evaluation. the injury occurred in the second quarter after kahoun tackled rutgers running back antwan raymond. players from both teams gathered nearby while trainers worked, and kahoun gave a thumbs-up as he was carried from the field. boston college's update offered an important initial sign, but the school did not announce a diagnosis or timetable. kahoun is in his first season with the eagles after transferring from notre dame. he had recorded six tackles in the game before leaving. the episode shifted attention away from the score as players and spectators waited for information about his condition. further testing will determine the extent of the injury and any next steps in his recovery; the initial statement should not be read as a complete medical assessment. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts chestnut hill chestnut hill, massachusetts boston college bodie kahoun college football rutgers injury

ma-boston-college-rutgers-red-bandanna-w.text: boston college holds off rutgers 28-21 in red bandanna game four interceptions and a 78-yard fourth-quarter touchdown helped the eagles earn their first win of the season. boston college defeated rutgers 28-21 in the 13th annual red bandanna game at alumni stadium, earning its first win of the season before a crowd of more than 40,000. the game honored former eagle welles crowther on the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks. quarterback mason mckenzie completed 18 of 29 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown, while adding 94 rushing yards and another score. dawson pough caught four passes for 106 yards, including a 78-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter that restored a two-score lead after rutgers had narrowed the gap. the eagles’ defense intercepted four passes, its highest total in a game since november 2023, and stopped rutgers twice on fourth down. anthony palano made two interceptions, including the late takeaway that ended the scarlet knights’ final chance to tie. boston college, now 1-1 after the emotional home victory, remains home to face maine on september 19. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts chestnut hill chestnut hill, massachusetts boston college rutgers red bandanna game college football

ma-boston-college-welles-crowther-red-ba.excerpt: Boston College and Rutgers used uniforms and stadium tributes to remember Welles Crowther and alumni killed in the September 11 attacks.
ma-boston-college-welles-crowther-red-ba.text: boston college honors welles crowther in red bandanna game boston college and rutgers used uniforms and stadium tributes to remember welles crowther and alumni killed in the september 11 attacks. boston college marked the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks with its annual red bandanna game, honoring alumnus welles crowther during friday night’s 28-21 football victory over rutgers. the matchup carried a connection for both universities: crowther graduated from boston college, while rutgers commemorated 37 alumni killed in the attacks. crowther, a former boston college lacrosse player and volunteer firefighter, helped people escape the world trade center’s south tower before he died. survivors remembered the red bandanna covering his face as he guided them through smoke and returned to help others, giving the cloth lasting significance in the school’s memorial tradition. boston college players wore red-and-white paisley elements and “for welles” on their uniforms. rutgers incorporated the number 37 and american flag details into its tribute. fans at alumni stadium also carried red bandannas and participated in a coordinated whiteout. the 2026 game was held on september 11 itself, giving the established campus tradition added meaning while linking the schools’ remembrance to service, courage and the alumni communities affected by the attacks. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts chestnut hill chestnut hill, massachusetts boston college welles crowther september 11 rutgers college football

ma-boston-community-health-centers-3-3-m.excerpt: Ten centers will receive $300,000 each, while a statewide league gets another $300,000 for financial-stability work.
ma-boston-community-health-centers-3-3-m.text: boston awards $3.3 million to community health centers ten centers will receive $300,000 each, while a statewide league gets another $300,000 for financial-stability work. boston and its public health commission are awarding $3.3 million to community health centers as the providers prepare for expected changes in insurance coverage and continued staffing pressure. the money comes from the city’s final year of american rescue plan act funding. ten centers will receive $300,000 apiece for existing staff, insurance-enrollment assistance and care programs. a further $300,000 will go to the massachusetts league of community health centers to support longer-term financial stability, according to the city’s september 10 announcement. masshealth projects that new federal work and education requirements beginning in january 2027 could affect around 40,000 boston residents. city figures place about 40% of that group in dorchester and roxbury, with another 20% in hyde park, the south end and mattapan. the selected providers include neighborhealth, the dimock center, dothouse health, codman square health center and boston health care for the homeless program. community health centers treat patients regardless of insurance status, so the city expects them to absorb more demand if residents lose coverage. the award is one-time funding, separate from boston’s annual support and other grants. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston community health centers masshealth health coverage arpa

ma-boston-embrace-masso-salsa-block-part.text: boston block party celebrates black and latino culture downtown el gran combo de puerto rico headlined the free embrace massó “¡con salsa!” gathering at summer street plaza. a free downtown boston block party brought salsa music and cultural programming to summer street plaza on saturday. the embrace massó “¡con salsa!” event ran from 3 to 7 p.m. in downtown crossing, with puerto rican salsa orchestra el gran combo de puerto rico serving as the headline act. organized by embrace boston, the gathering was designed to celebrate the links among black culture, latino identity and the wider african diaspora. the program combined live music, dancing and public art in a central pedestrian area, turning a city block into an open-air community venue. the event also came as embrace boston expands its presence near boston common. the organization recently acquired 33 west street, a building close to “the embrace” memorial, as a future base for its civic and cultural work. saturday’s party offered a public-facing version of that mission: using music and shared space to bring together communities whose histories in boston overlap but are not always presented together. admission was open to the public. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston embrace boston salsa downtown crossing

ma-boston-judge-federal-hiring-essay-que.excerpt: U.S. District Judge George O’Toole halted a question asking civil-service applicants how they would advance presidential policies and executive orders.
ma-boston-judge-federal-hiring-essay-que.text: boston judge blocks federal hiring essay question u.s. district judge george o’toole halted a question asking civil-service applicants how they would advance presidential policies and executive orders. a federal judge in boston on friday blocked the government from continuing to ask applicants for career civil-service jobs to write essays explaining how they would help advance the president’s policies and executive orders. u.s. district judge george o’toole issued the ruling in a case brought by three unions representing public employees. o’toole concluded that the unions were likely to show the question infringed applicants’ speech rights and violated the administrative procedure act. his decision noted that federal civil-service law bars hiring decisions based on political affiliation. the unions said more than 70,000 job postings had included the question, covering positions as varied as air traffic control specialist, crane operator and nuclear materials courier. the office of personnel management did not immediately comment on the ruling. the agency previously said the response was optional and that political beliefs could not be used in hiring decisions. the question was adopted as part of a hiring plan developed after a january 2025 executive order. the order halts the essay requirement while the unions’ challenge proceeds. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, massachusetts federal hiring civil service boston federal court office of personnel management first amendment

ma-boston-judge-visa-duration-rule-2026-.excerpt: A federal judge in Boston temporarily blocked a Homeland Security rule that would have limited the duration of several student, exchange and journalist visas.
ma-boston-judge-visa-duration-rule-2026-.text: boston judge blocks visa-duration rule affecting foreign students and journalists a federal judge in boston temporarily blocked a homeland security rule that would have limited the duration of several student, exchange and journalist visas. a federal judge in boston has blocked a homeland security rule that would have changed how long certain foreign students, exchange visitors and journalists could remain in the united states, reuters reported monday. the rule was due to take effect tuesday. it would have capped f visas for international students and j visas for exchange visitors at four years, while i visas for foreign journalists would have been limited to 240 days, subject to the rule’s procedures. u.s. district judge f. dennis saylor said the department’s reasoning was insufficient and that the agency had not met its legal obligations, according to reuters. the order prevents the limits from taking effect while the case proceeds. the ruling has particular importance in massachusetts, home to universities including harvard and mit that enroll large international communities. the judge said schools could face substantial costs and enrollment declines if students were forced to leave or repeatedly seek extensions under the policy. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts massachusetts immigration higher education

ma-boston-medical-center-nurses-strike-a.text: boston medical center nurses authorize three-day strike nearly 90% of voting nurses backed strike authority as contract talks remain divided over pay and staffing, though no walkout has been scheduled. nurses at boston medical center have voted to authorize a three-day strike as contract negotiations continue over wages and staffing. nearly 90% of participating nurses supported the authorization, according to their union, 1199seiu. the bargaining unit covers almost 2,000 nurses at the hospital’s boston campus and brockton behavioral health center. the vote does not automatically trigger a walkout. union leaders would still have to set dates and provide the required 10-day notice before a strike could begin. nurses and the hospital have been negotiating for more than six months. the union says compensation remains well below competing systems and argues that vacancies and turnover place additional pressure on bedside staff. boston medical center has said its proposal would raise pay by 15% to 20% over two years, depending on seniority, and has pointed to financial constraints facing the safety-net system. the union says a substantial gap remains between the sides. the authorization gives negotiators leverage for the next round of talks while leaving time for an agreement that would avoid disruption for patients and employees. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston medical center nurses 1199seiu labor health care

ma-boston-providence-rail-disruptions-se.text: locomotive fire and police activity disrupt boston-providence trains a fire at ruggles station and a separate police response south of boston caused delays and shuttle-bus transfers wednesday afternoon. two separate incidents disrupted passenger rail service between boston and providence on wednesday afternoon, affecting both mbta commuter rail and amtrak riders. nbc 10 reported that firefighters responded after smoke came from the locomotive of a commuter train stopped at ruggles station in boston. the train had originated at wickford junction. no injuries were reported, and the affected train was removed from service. elsewhere on the corridor, police activity south of boston delayed trains between the two cities. the mbta said at least one providence line train ended its trip at attleboro, where passengers were transferred to shuttle buses. officials had not publicly described the police investigation by early wednesday evening. the combination left travelers facing delays during the evening commute on a corridor shared by regional and intercity trains. riders were advised to monitor notices from the mbta and amtrak before heading to stations, because equipment and crews can remain out of position even after the immediate incidents are cleared. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, ma mbta commuter rail ruggles station providence line

ma-boston-small-clean-energy-zoning-2026.excerpt: The framework creates a consolidated local permitting process and adds standards for battery storage systems.
ma-boston-small-clean-energy-zoning-2026.text: boston adopts zoning rules for small clean-energy infrastructure the framework creates a consolidated local permitting process and adds standards for battery storage systems. the boston zoning commission has adopted rules for small clean-energy infrastructure, creating a consolidated local permitting process required under the massachusetts state climate act. the framework covers facilities such as solar panels, wind turbines, battery storage and short transmission lines. the zoning change also sets dimensional and use regulations for battery energy storage systems. state law requires cities and towns to offer the permitting process by october 1, 2026, and boston said the new rules align with its plans to expand electric-grid capacity. city planners will next develop design guidelines intended to fit projects into neighborhood settings and address public-space safety. the rules are designed to make requirements more predictable for smaller projects while preserving local review of their placement and form. boston’s 2030 climate action plan calls for a 50% reduction in community-wide greenhouse-gas emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050. the city says permitting changes are one piece of that strategy, alongside electrification and grid upgrades. actual projects will still need to meet the new zoning, design and safety standards before construction. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston clean energy zoning battery storage permitting
