ma-boston-weekend-sunday-rain-forecast-2.text: boston forecast calls for sunny start before sunday soaking friday and saturday should stay dry with highs in the mid-70s before a widespread rain system moves through early sunday. greater boston is expected to begin the weekend with two dry, sunny days before a more organized rain system arrives sunday. friday and saturday should feature gentle breezes, cool starts in the 50s and afternoon highs in the mid-70s, according to nbc10 boston meteorologists. rain is forecast to spread into the region early sunday and continue into at least part of the afternoon. current guidance points to roughly three-quarters of an inch to one inch across much of the area, though exact totals and the timing of the final showers remain subject to change. the sunday system could be the most substantial rain opportunity in the next seven to 10 days. that makes the dry window on friday and saturday the more dependable period for outdoor plans, while drivers and event organizers should prepare for wet roads and reduced visibility as the system moves through. humidity will increase with the rain and then fall behind it. sunshine and a gradual warmup are expected early next week. residents should still check an updated local forecast before sunday travel because small shifts in the storm track could change when the heaviest rain arrives and how quickly conditions improve. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts boston weather weekend forecast rain massachusetts

ma-brownsberger-lander-recount-35-votes-.excerpt: A two-day hand count of more than 24,000 ballots changed the incumbent senator’s advantage by one vote, leaving a 35-vote margin.
ma-brownsberger-lander-recount-35-votes-.text: brownsberger keeps massachusetts senate nomination by 35 votes a two-day hand count of more than 24,000 ballots changed the incumbent senator’s advantage by one vote, leaving a 35-vote margin. massachusetts state sen. william brownsberger retained the democratic nomination in the suffolk and middlesex district after a two-day recount left him 35 votes ahead of challenger daniel lander. the hand count covered more than 24,000 ballots and changed the incumbent’s advantage by one vote from the unofficial 34-vote margin. brownsberger has represented the district since 2012 and serves in the state senate’s leadership. the district includes belmont, watertown and portions of boston and cambridge. lander, a former boston city hall aide, carried boston, watertown and the district’s cambridge precincts, while brownsberger’s performance in belmont supplied the margin that preserved his lead. both campaigns requested recounts after the close september 1 primary. election workers reviewed paper ballots across the four municipalities, with campaign representatives and public observers present. lander congratulated brownsberger after the count, and brownsberger said he was ready to return to work for the district. the certified result moves the contest into the november general election and closes one of the narrowest massachusetts legislative primaries of the 2026 cycle. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts massachusetts senate william brownsberger daniel lander recount suffolk and middlesex

ma-cambridge-memorial-drive-shooting-new.excerpt: Tyler Brown is expected to appear in person as prosecutors add armed-assault, firearm and property-damage counts tied to the May shooting.
ma-cambridge-memorial-drive-shooting-new.text: memorial drive shooting suspect faces dozens of new charges tyler brown is expected to appear in person as prosecutors add armed-assault, firearm and property-damage counts tied to the may shooting. a man accused in a may shooting along memorial drive in cambridge is expected to appear in court in person for the first time while facing dozens of newly filed charges. whdh identified the defendant as 47-year-old tyler brown. the station reported that the new counts include six charges of armed assault to murder, seven charges of malicious damage to a motor vehicle, carrying a firearm without a license and possessing a firearm after a felony conviction. prosecutors allege brown fired dozens of rounds from a rifle at drivers along memorial drive. two people were struck and later recovered. brown’s earlier court appearance took place by video from a hospital bed, according to the report. the charges are allegations, and brown is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. his upcoming appearance advances a case that has been developing for nearly four months and will allow the court to address the expanded charging document. whdh also reported that brown was on parole at the time in connection with a 2020 shooting involving boston police officers. any plea, bail decision or schedule for further proceedings will be determined in court. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma cambridge cambridge, ma cambridge memorial drive court shooting investigation

ma-camp-braveheart-grief-support-20-year.excerpt: The HopeHealth program brings children from Massachusetts and Rhode Island together for activities, counseling and practical coping strategies after a death.
ma-camp-braveheart-grief-support-20-year.text: camp braveheart marks 20 years helping grieving children the hopehealth program brings children from massachusetts and rhode island together for activities, counseling and practical coping strategies after a death. camp braveheart is marking its 20th year of bringing children from massachusetts and rhode island together for support after the death of a loved one. the hopehealth program combines camp activities with conversations and practical strategies for living with grief. nbc 10 highlighted longtime volunteer harry potter, a retired rhode island educator and former principal of providence’s hope high school. potter has spent much of the program’s two decades greeting campers, building trust and helping children become comfortable enough to talk about difficult losses. the camp uses art, music and group activities to help participants express feelings and develop a personal set of coping tools. organizers say the shared setting can reduce isolation by showing children that other young people are navigating similar experiences. although the report focused on one volunteer, the milestone also reflects the work of the broader hopehealth team and the families who return to the program. camp braveheart serves both sides of the state line, making it a regional resource for young people whose grief may not be visible in school or everyday routines. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma fall river fall river, ma camp braveheart hopehealth grief support children

ma-cannabis-sales-10-billion-2026.excerpt: The state’s licensed recreational market crossed the milestone on September 5, nearly eight years after the first stores opened.
ma-cannabis-sales-10-billion-2026.text: massachusetts adult-use cannabis sales pass $10 billion the state’s licensed recreational market crossed the milestone on september 5, nearly eight years after the first stores opened. massachusetts’ adult-use cannabis market has surpassed $10 billion in gross sales, according to the state cannabis control commission. licensed retailers crossed the threshold on september 5, nearly eight years after the first recreational stores opened in november 2018. the commission said sales reached $10,008,567,111 at the milestone. june 2026 set a monthly record of about $156 million, while sales through august totaled roughly $1.09 billion. the market generated about $1.65 billion in 2025. state regulators reported 782 operating marijuana businesses, including more than 100 equity-owned or equity-operated businesses and 91 medical dispensaries. the industry includes about 15,000 employees among nearly 20,000 registered agents. cannabis sales also produced an estimated $336 million in state sales, excise and local-option taxes during fiscal 2026. adult-use purchases carry the state’s 6.25% sales tax and a 10.75% excise tax, with municipalities allowed to add a local tax. voters will decide in november whether to repeal the state’s adult-use cannabis law. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma worcester massachusetts cannabis business tax revenue cannabis control commission

ma-canton-banner-michael-uliano-septembe.excerpt: The town remembered the Army veteran and Canton native who was working in the World Trade Center’s North Tower.
ma-canton-banner-michael-uliano-septembe.text: canton unveils banner honoring september 11 victim michael uliano the town remembered the army veteran and canton native who was working in the world trade center’s north tower. canton unveiled a banner thursday night honoring michael uliano, a hometown army veteran who was killed in the september 11 attacks 25 years ago. uliano grew up in canton and later worked for a financial firm in the north tower of the world trade center. he was 42 when american airlines flight 11 struck the building on september 11, 2001, according to whdh’s account of the town ceremony. the banner was placed at a memorial already dedicated to uliano. during the gathering, participants read the names of people killed in the attacks, lit candles and laid a wreath. the ceremony connected canton’s local loss to the broader anniversary being marked across massachusetts and the country. the tribute gives residents a lasting, visible reminder of uliano beyond the annual service. it also preserves the personal history of the attacks for younger residents who know september 11 only through family stories, school lessons and public memorials. canton was among several massachusetts communities holding observances on thursday night and friday. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts canton canton, massachusetts canton michael uliano september 11 memorial massachusetts

ma-capron-park-zoo-kayla-st-george-2026.excerpt: The 39-year-old animal-care professional died after a stroke, leaving a record of work at several New England zoos and with a threatened deer species.
ma-capron-park-zoo-kayla-st-george-2026.text: capron park zoo mourns zookeeper kayla st. george the 39-year-old animal-care professional died after a stroke, leaving a record of work at several new england zoos and with a threatened deer species. capron park zoo in attleboro is mourning longtime zookeeper kayla st. george, who died at age 39 following a stroke. st. george had worked at capron park for about five years. her path in animal care included studies at the university of rhode island, internships at mystic aquarium and chicago’s shedd aquarium, and positions at buttonwood park zoo and franklin park zoo before she joined the attleboro facility. the zoo highlighted her commitment to reeves’ muntjacs, a small deer species native to asia. st. george served as vice coordinator of the association of zoos and aquariums program that manages the species’ population in accredited institutions, work that connects daily animal care with long-term conservation planning. according to her family, st. george developed a migraine and numbness earlier this week. doctors later found a clot near the base of her skull, and she died after a major stroke. her family has asked that memorial donations be directed to capron park zoo in place of flowers. the zoo said her loss is being felt by colleagues and the animals she cared for. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma attleboro attleboro, ma attleboro capron park zoo zookeeper wildlife

ma-car-free-seniors-mbta-pilot-2026-09-2.excerpt: Massachusetts residents age 75 and older who no longer drive will be able to apply for a pilot credential covering MBTA buses, subways, ferries and Commuter Rail.
ma-car-free-seniors-mbta-pilot-2026-09-2.text: free mbta fares for non-driving seniors open to enrollment oct. 13 massachusetts residents age 75 and older who no longer drive will be able to apply for a pilot credential covering mbta buses, subways, ferries and commuter rail. massachusetts will begin enrollment oct. 13 for a pilot program giving residents age 75 and older who no longer drive free fares on mbta buses, subways, ferries and commuter rail, state officials announced sept. 23. participants must have a massachusetts identification card rather than a driver's license. the mbta and registry of motor vehicles are partnering on the program, which is intended to help older residents keep traveling to appointments, services and family connections after giving up driving. eligible residents will be able to apply online beginning oct. 13 or visit the charlie service center at 296 washington st. in boston. people who apply in person can receive a temporary credential that day; a permanent credential will be mailed later, according to the state announcement. residents who do not already have a massachusetts id will need to obtain one through the rmv before applying. the pilot is part of a broader set of mbta affordability changes announced by the healey administration this year, including reduced commuter rail fares and expanded transfer options. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston and eastern massachusetts massachusetts mbta senior services public transit transportation affordability

ma-cathedral-pines-joint-patrol-arrest-2.excerpt: A joint Essex and Manchester-by-the-Sea patrol followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the wooded recreation area.
ma-cathedral-pines-joint-patrol-arrest-2.text: joint patrol leads to arrest at cathedral pines recreation area a joint essex and manchester-by-the-sea patrol followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the wooded recreation area. an 83-year-old man was arrested during a joint police operation at cathedral pines, a wooded recreation area shared by essex and manchester-by-the-sea. nbc10 boston reported friday that the operation followed complaints about inappropriate activity in the area, including a report that someone had grabbed another visitor and behaved lewdly. police from both communities assigned plainclothes and uniformed officers to the property. authorities said the man was taken into custody after propositioning a detective during the patrol. his name and the specific charge were not included in the initial public report, and officials did not say whether he was suspected in the earlier grabbing allegation. the arrest comes as the two departments increase their presence at cathedral pines in response to visitor concerns. police said the patrols are intended to deter misconduct and keep the public recreation area accessible. the reported conduct remains under investigation, and an arrest is not a finding of guilt. visitors who witness threatening, unwanted or illegal behavior should leave the immediate area when safe and contact local police with the time, location and description of what occurred. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma manchester-by-the-sea essex and manchester-by-the-sea, ma essex manchester-by-the-sea cathedral pines police public safety

ma-chicopee-electric-dirt-bike-charges-2.excerpt: Police say the unregistered and uninsured bike had no headlight or taillight when it collided with a vehicle near an I-391 offramp.
ma-chicopee-electric-dirt-bike-charges-2.text: chicopee electric dirt-bike rider faces charges after crash police say the unregistered and uninsured bike had no headlight or taillight when it collided with a vehicle near an i-391 offramp. a 28-year-old man is facing criminal charges after the electric dirt bike he was riding collided with a vehicle in chicopee, police said tuesday. western mass news reported that emergency crews were called to chicopee street at about 10:15 p.m. friday. investigators said the dirt bike struck a vehicle that was leaving the interstate 391 offramp and turning left onto chicopee street. police said the dirt bike had no headlight or taillight and was not registered or insured for public-road use. the rider was injured and taken to a hospital; the driver of the other vehicle was not hurt. authorities did not publicly detail the rider’s condition. the case is one of several recent western massachusetts incidents involving off-road vehicles used on streets. police emphasized that electric dirt bikes and similar vehicles must meet applicable registration, insurance and equipment rules when operated on public roads. the allegations have not been proven in court, and the report did not identify the rider or list a court date. new-england ma chicopee, massachusetts massachusetts chicopee traffic safety electric bikes

ma-clancy-lawyer-trump-pardon-request-20.excerpt: The request faces a basic jurisdictional obstacle: presidential pardon power covers federal offenses, while the Massachusetts case was brought under state law.
ma-clancy-lawyer-trump-pardon-request-20.text: lindsay clancy’s lawyer asks trump for pardon after mistrial the request faces a basic jurisdictional obstacle: presidential pardon power covers federal offenses, while the massachusetts case was brought under state law. an attorney for lindsay clancy asked president donald trump to pardon his client tuesday, days after a massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the closely watched plymouth county murder case. reuters reported that defense lawyer kevin reddington made the request during a television interview. clancy was prosecuted in state court, however, and the constitution gives presidents authority to pardon federal offenses, not state crimes. any relief in a massachusetts case would ordinarily have to come through the state’s own clemency process. the mistrial followed jurors’ inability to reach a unanimous verdict. prosecutors have not ruled out trying the case again, so the pardon appeal does not end the legal proceedings or prevent state authorities from moving forward. the new request adds a political element to a case that has centered on criminal responsibility and mental health. it is also legally distinct from a formal clemency application. as of tuesday evening, reuters reported no indication that the white house had acted on the appeal. court filings and statements from prosecutors will determine the case’s next steps. new-england ma plymouth county, massachusetts massachusetts courts legal plymouth county

ma-federal-court-protects-social-service.text: federal ruling protects massachusetts access to social-service programs a coalition led in part by massachusetts won a summary-judgment ruling blocking immigration-verification rules for programs including head start, title x clinics and adult education. a federal court has vacated the trump administration’s attempt to require immigration verification across a broad group of federally supported health, education and social-service programs, massachusetts attorney general andrea joy campbell’s office said tuesday. the ruling granted a coalition of 21 attorneys general summary judgment and barred the administration from enforcing its reinterpretation of federal-benefit law against massachusetts and the other plaintiff states. the programs named in the case include head start, title x family-planning clinics, food banks, domestic-violence shelters, adult education and community health centers. campbell’s office said nearly 96,000 patients use massachusetts title x clinics, which provide sexual and reproductive health care. it also said more than 44,000 adult learners use federally funded career and technical education programs in the state each year; the office argued that mandatory status checks could have added costs and discouraged providers from participating. the lawsuit began in july 2025 after the coalition challenged the federal government’s reinterpretation of a decades-old law governing access to public benefits. the massachusetts attorney general said the judgment preserves access to the services regardless of immigration status, while the ruling’s practical effects will depend on how the administration responds and whether further proceedings follow. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston massachusetts massachusetts social services head start title x federal court immigration policy

ma-healey-two-month-gas-tax-suspension-2.text: healey files bill with two-month gas-tax suspension and broader relief the supplemental budget would suspend massachusetts' 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax for two months while also capping ticket fees, lowering projected electric costs and expanding maternal-health support. massachusetts gov. maura healey filed a supplemental budget bill on sept. 23 that includes a two-month suspension of the state's 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax. the administration says the measure would give temporary relief to families, truckers and rideshare drivers facing higher fuel costs. the bill also includes a proposal to cap ticket-resale prices and fees and ban speculative tickets, along with changes to how electric utilities purchase power for basic-service customers. the administration estimates those electricity changes could save ratepayers about $610 million. healey's filing sets aside $2.25 million for postpartum care and maternal mental-health support. it also includes $41.5 million for department of transitional assistance caseworkers and technology upgrades intended to help people remain enrolled in the supplemental nutrition assistance program. the administration estimates the gas-tax suspension would reduce revenue by about $120 million. it says that cost would be covered with unbudgeted fiscal 2027 fair share surtax collections and would not interrupt transportation projects financed through the commonwealth transportation fund. the legislation would appropriate $2.24 billion in gross spending, or $1.46 billion after revenue offsets, as part of an effort to close fiscal 2026 with a balanced budget. the gas-tax suspension and the rest of the package still require approval from the massachusetts legislature. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, massachusetts massachusetts gas tax maura healey transportation state government

ma-lexington-hirshfield-ponzi-guilty-ple.text: lexington woman pleads guilty in $11 million ponzi scheme federal prosecutors say more than 200 people lost about $10.9 million after investing through companies run by barbara a. hirshfield. a lexington woman has pleaded guilty to five counts of wire fraud in a long-running investment scheme that federal prosecutors say caused roughly $10.9 million in losses to more than 200 victims. barbara a. hirshfield, 83, admitted operating the scheme through ideal financial services and ideal financial holdings from 2012 through 2025. prosecutors said she solicited money with promises tied to investment products, then used funds from newer participants to make payments to earlier investors, a structure commonly associated with a ponzi scheme. authorities said massachusetts regulators ordered the companies to stop raising money in 2012 and revoked relevant licenses in 2014, but hirshfield continued to seek investments afterward. the guilty plea resolves the criminal charges without a trial; sentencing is scheduled for january 7, 2027. each wire-fraud count carries a potential maximum sentence of 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, though the court will determine the actual sentence under federal law and sentencing guidelines. the case adds to enforcement scrutiny of investment solicitations aimed at individuals who may rely heavily on personal trust and promised returns. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma lexington lexington, massachusetts lexington ponzi scheme wire fraud federal court

ma-license-plate-readers-1200-2026-09-14.excerpt: A new tally finds automated license-plate readers operating across Massachusetts, renewing questions about how police technology is deployed and overseen.
ma-license-plate-readers-1200-2026-09-14.text: massachusetts has more than 1,200 automated license-plate readers, axios finds a new tally finds automated license-plate readers operating across massachusetts, renewing questions about how police technology is deployed and overseen. more than 1,200 automated license-plate readers are operating across massachusetts, according to an axios boston tally that maps the technology’s growing footprint and the debate around how vehicle data is collected. the count includes roughly 990 cameras made by flock safety. middlesex county has about 252 cameras, followed by norfolk county with 220 and essex county with 173, the report found. the systems can alert agencies when they detect plates associated with stolen or wanted vehicles. supporters say the cameras can help investigators locate vehicles and respond to crimes more quickly. privacy advocates and some local officials have raised concerns about retention, access, possible misuse and the tracking of people who are not suspected of wrongdoing. several communities have taken different approaches. abington, ayer, stow and groton voted to ban flock cameras, while new bedford paused its use after an allegation involving the system. the varying responses leave municipalities to balance investigative tools with local rules and public oversight. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts public safety privacy

ma-lindsay-clancy-defense-not-guilty-mot.text: lindsay clancy’s defense seeks not-guilty finding after mistrial attorney kevin reddington filed a six-page motion asking the judge to enter a required finding of not guilty after jurors deadlocked. lindsay clancy’s defense attorney has asked a plymouth superior court judge to enter a required finding of not guilty after the recent jury deadlock ended her trial in a mistrial. whdh reported that attorney kevin reddington filed the six-page motion thursday. the request argues that prosecutors did not present enough evidence for a juror seeking the truth to find guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. the filing also challenges whether the state proved that clancy was mentally capable of conforming her conduct to the law. that issue was central to the case and to the jury’s inability to reach a unanimous verdict. the motion asks judge william sullivan to resolve the case rather than send it toward another trial. a filing is a request, not a ruling, and the court has not yet granted the defense’s motion. the next significant step will be the judge’s response after the prosecution has an opportunity to address the arguments. until then, the mistrial remains the case’s latest completed proceeding and the criminal charges have not been dismissed. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma plymouth plymouth, ma massachusetts plymouth courts lindsay clancy

ma-lindsay-clancy-jurors-interview-2026.text: three lindsay clancy jurors describe deadlock after mistrial the jury foreperson and two other panelists told nbc10 boston that one holdout prevented agreement in the closely watched murder case. three jurors from lindsay clancy’s murder trial have described the deliberations that ended in a mistrial, offering a new account of the panel’s internal deadlock. the jury foreperson and two other panelists told nbc10 boston that one juror would not join the rest of the panel in a verdict. they said deliberations became tense and that several jurors changed their views while reviewing the evidence and competing arguments about criminal responsibility. their interview reflects the recollections of three jurors, not a formal court finding about every member of the panel. nbc10 boston said it tried to contact the juror described by the others as the holdout. a judge declared the mistrial last week after the jury reported it could not reach a unanimous decision. the case remains unresolved, and prosecutors and the court must determine the next procedural steps. nothing said after the mistrial changes the presumption of innocence or constitutes a verdict. the interview is significant because it adds firsthand context to the note and courtroom discussions that preceded the judge’s decision. new-england ma plymouth county, massachusetts lindsay clancy mistrial massachusetts courts jury deliberations

ma-lindsay-clancy-jurors-mistrial-split-.text: jurors describe split that produced lindsay clancy mistrial five panel members have spoken publicly after a week of deliberations failed to produce a unanimous decision on criminal responsibility. jurors in the lindsay clancy murder trial are describing the disagreement that led to a mistrial after roughly a week of deliberations over whether she was criminally responsible for the 2023 deaths of her three children in duxbury. five jurors have now spoken to news organizations, nbc 10 reported. three, including the foreperson, said one member of the panel would not join the others in finding clancy not guilty by reason of insanity. another juror said the panel’s vote shifted as members reviewed evidence before most of them reached the same position. the public accounts are the jurors’ descriptions of closed deliberations; they are not new court findings. clancy remains charged, and the mistrial did not resolve guilt or criminal responsibility. defense attorney kevin reddington has asked judge william sullivan to enter a not-guilty finding, arguing that prosecutors presented legally insufficient evidence of criminal responsibility. the defense is also pressing a double-jeopardy argument against another trial. a status conference is scheduled for september 29, when the judge is expected to consider the pending motions and the case’s next steps. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma duxbury duxbury, massachusetts duxbury lindsay clancy courts mistrial

ma-logan-airport-tsa-egates-3d-bag-scann.text: logan airport plans e-gates and scanners that digitally unpack bags tsa says facial-comparison gates and 3d bag scanners are coming to logan, while a separate visitor-access program remains under review. boston logan international airport is expected to add tsa precheck e-gates using facial-comparison technology, along with 3d scanners designed to inspect bags without requiring travelers to unpack them manually. tsa administrator david cummins told cbs news boston that precheck travelers would be able to keep a driver’s license and boarding pass in their pocket while moving through the gate. the bag scanners would create a three-dimensional view that lets screeners digitally inspect contents. travelers outside precheck are also expected to see walk-through body-scanning technology that does not require passengers to raise their hands. the report did not provide a firm installation date, so travelers should not assume the new process is available on a particular trip until logan or tsa confirms it. a separate program allowing some precheck members without tickets to accompany arriving or departing travelers is operating at 13 airports. logan has not joined that program; an airport spokesperson said officials are monitoring it. that distinction matters because the planned screening equipment and visitor-access policy are separate changes. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, massachusetts logan airport tsa precheck airport security boston

ma-lynn-flock-camera-safeguards-audit-20.excerpt: The police department is reducing data retention to seven days, limiting users and adding mandatory monthly audits.
ma-lynn-flock-camera-safeguards-audit-20.text: lynn tightens flock camera access after audit flags search pattern the police department is reducing data retention to seven days, limiting users and adding mandatory monthly audits. lynn police are tightening access to the department’s flock license-plate camera system after an audit found a concerning pattern of searches, police chief christopher reddy told the city council on tuesday night. the revised policy will require monthly audits, stronger access controls and written acknowledgements of the rules from users. data retention will fall from 30 days to seven, and initial access will be limited to 23 department members ranked lieutenant or higher. any additions will require the chief’s direction. the department also plans a public transparency portal showing categories of data that trigger alerts and the organizations receiving shared information. lynn intends to limit data sharing to massachusetts law-enforcement agencies, according to boston 25 news. two officers were placed on paid administrative leave in mid-august after an earlier audit identified the search pattern, and an internal-affairs investigation was opened. the department has not publicly resolved that review. automated plate readers can support investigations involving stolen vehicles, missing people and violent crime, but the policy changes reflect continued scrutiny over who can search the systems and how long records remain available. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma lynn lynn, ma lynn flock cameras privacy police

ma-lynn-special-needs-school-bus-delay-2.excerpt: A mother says her 5-year-old arrived hours late and without the car seat required by his education plan; the district says vendors must follow student accommodations.
ma-lynn-special-needs-school-bus-delay-2.text: lynn family raises safety concerns after special-needs school bus delay a mother says her 5-year-old arrived hours late and without the car seat required by his education plan; the district says vendors must follow student accommodations. a lynn mother is asking the school district and its transportation contractor for answers after her 5-year-old son arrived home hours late on the first day of school. kelly trickett told nbc10 boston that her son ben, a kindergartner at connery elementary who has a communication disorder, could not tell the family where he was while they tried to locate his bus. trickett said she eventually called police because the family was unable to get clear location information. on wednesday, she said, the bus again arrived about an hour late even though the school is roughly a mile and a half from home. the family also raised a safety concern: trickett said ben was not riding in the car seat required by his individualized education program. she said he weighs less than 30 pounds. the district did not directly address that allegation in its response to the station. lynn public schools said contracted transportation vendors are expected to comply with student education plans, and that complaints are logged and followed up. the bus provider, nrt, said safe and reliable transportation is its priority and that it works with the district, but it did not explain the delays or describe any corrective action. the family says it wants clear accountability before the next ride. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma lynn lynn, ma lynn school transportation special education student safety

ma-malden-new-england-coffee-reopening-2.text: new england coffee cafe sets september 14 reopening in malden the charles street shop has been closed since a may vehicle crash damaged the building and hospitalized two people. new england coffee cafe plans to reopen in malden on monday, september 14, ending a closure of nearly four months after a multi-vehicle crash damaged the charles street property. the cafe at 108 charles street closed after the may 19 collision. two people were hospitalized, and the impact forced repairs before the retail operation could welcome customers again. the company announced the reopening date this week. the shop is part of a business with deep ties to the city. new england coffee was founded in boston in 1916 and moved its operations to malden in 1966. its flagship retail store opened in 1986, making the cafe a familiar stop for workers and residents near the company’s roasting operations. the reopening restores a longstanding local storefront while marking another step in the property’s recovery from the crash. customers should check the cafe’s current operating hours before visiting, as schedules can change during the first days after an extended closure. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma malden malden, ma malden new england coffee small business reopening

ma-maternal-mental-health-expansion-2026.text: massachusetts proposes expanded postpartum mental-health support gov. maura healey is seeking $2.25 million to broaden newborn home visits and strengthen a clinician-consultation program, alongside planned screening-rule changes. massachusetts gov. maura healey proposed new spending and regulatory changes tuesday aimed at identifying postpartum mental-health concerns earlier and connecting more families with care. healey plans to seek $2 million in a supplemental budget to expand the department of public health’s welcome family program statewide. the program offers parents and caregivers a free, one-time home visit from a maternal and child health nurse during the first weeks after a birth. the governor’s office says welcome family currently serves about 3,000 births a year, compared with roughly 68,000 births statewide. the proposed appropriation would make a visit available to every parent or caregiver, though lawmakers must approve the funding. a separate $250,000 proposal would strengthen the massachusetts child psychiatry access program for moms, which helps clinicians address perinatal mental-health needs. the department of public health also plans to revise regulations governing screening for mood and anxiety disorders during and after pregnancy. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, massachusetts massachusetts maternal health postpartum care mental health

ma-mattapan-blue-hill-bus-lane-concerns-.text: mattapan residents question center-running blue hill avenue bus lanes a boston and mbta proposal would place buses in the median, prompting questions about street crossings, businesses and other transit options. hundreds of mattapan residents packed a listening session thursday to raise concerns about a proposed redesign of blue hill avenue. the boston and mbta plan would put dedicated bus lanes in the center of the street, with riders crossing general traffic lanes to reach median boarding areas. opponents at morning star baptist church focused on pedestrian safety, access to neighborhood businesses and the effect of construction on the corridor. some speakers asked officials to consider alternatives, including a long-discussed extension of the orange line, rather than commit to the center-running layout. mayor michelle wu and mbta general manager phillip eng attended the session. wu said the design remains in progress and can change as public feedback is collected. the meeting was the first of four community sessions planned over the next several weeks, leaving additional opportunities for residents to review details and respond. the proposal aims to make bus trips more reliable on one of boston’s busiest transit corridors. the unresolved issue is how to balance that goal with safe crossings, traffic flow and commercial access. further design work will determine whether the city modifies station locations, lane arrangements or other street features before moving ahead. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston mattapan, massachusetts blue hill avenue mbta mattapan bus lanes

ma-mbta-federal-safety-oversight-2026-09.text: federal safety oversight of mbta ends after years-long review the federal transit administration closed its safety management inspection and transferred direct oversight of the massachusetts system back to the state department of public utilities. the federal transit administration has closed its safety management inspection of the massachusetts department of public utilities' oversight of the mbta, state officials said friday. the move transfers direct federal oversight that began in 2022 back to the dpu. the inspection followed years of federal concern about the transit system's safety practices. the healey administration and mbta said the closure reflects progress on corrective action plans, workforce changes and infrastructure investment, while acknowledging that the system still has work ahead. dpu commissioner staci rubin said the agency had strengthened its rail-safety staff, technical expertise and oversight processes. mbta general manager phillip eng said 99% of the system's corrective action plans had been submitted, according to the state and the transit authority. the mbta remains under state oversight as it continues track, signal, vehicle and accessibility projects across the region. the federal action marks a change in supervision, not the end of safety monitoring. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston and eastern massachusetts massachusetts mbta public transit transportation safety

ma-mcas-results-2026-09-22.text: massachusetts mcas results show grade 8 math gains but wider ela challenges the state says 42 percent of eighth-graders met or exceeded math expectations, while grades 3-8 ela performance fell two points from 2025. massachusetts released its 2026 mcas and school-accountability results tuesday, reporting a notable improvement in eighth-grade math alongside continued gaps in english language arts and science. the department of elementary and secondary education said 42 percent of eighth-graders met or exceeded expectations in math, up four percentage points from 2025. across grades 3-8, 41 percent of students met or exceeded math expectations, roughly unchanged from last year. english language arts results were weaker. forty percent of students in grades 3-8 met or exceeded expectations, down two percentage points from 2025, while the grade 10 ela rate fell six points to 45 percent. in science, eighth-grade performance rose two points to 39 percent, but fifth-grade and high-school results declined. the release comes as massachusetts moves beyond the former requirement that students earn a qualifying mcas score to graduate. state officials are developing a broader graduation framework that includes rigorous coursework, end-of-course assessments, postsecondary planning and career or work-based learning. dese also said 80 percent of schools received accountability designations indicating they did not require state assistance or intervention, and 56 schools were selected for recognition based on strong improvement or overall achievement. families can review statewide, district and school results through the department's mcas reporting portal. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma boston massachusetts massachusetts mcas education schools student achievement

ma-mcdevitt-senior-homes-south-boston-20.text: former south boston convent begins conversion to 35 affordable senior homes the $15.7 million adaptive-reuse project will preserve the historic property while adding income-restricted apartments for older adults. construction is underway to convert the former st. augustine’s convent and paraclete center in south boston into affordable housing for older adults. the $15.7 million mcdevitt senior homes project will create 35 income-restricted apartments and one manager’s unit in the historic building. the approximately 31,000-square-foot development combines restoration of the existing structure with a five-story rear addition. plans call for preserving recognizable architectural features while adapting the interior for accessible residences and common areas. the project is intended to add senior housing without removing the property’s long-standing neighborhood identity. public financing includes $5.145 million from the city of boston and community preservation act funds, plus $850,000 from the federal home loan bank of boston. construction began in july, and project partners held a formal groundbreaking on august 20. the reuse adds a relatively small but targeted supply of below-market homes in a city where older residents can face steep housing costs and limited accessible options. work will now move through the renovation and new-construction phases before residents can occupy the building. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston south boston, massachusetts affordable housing senior housing south boston adaptive reuse

ma-medway-bicycle-crash-2026.text: bicyclist seriously injured in medway collision a car-and-bicycle crash tuesday night sent one person to the hospital and temporarily closed part of milford street near clark street. one person suffered serious injuries in a collision involving a car and a bicycle in medway on tuesday night, authorities said. police and emergency crews responded on milford street near clark street. the injured person was taken to a hospital, according to boston 25 news. officials did not immediately release the person’s name, age or current condition. milford street was closed in the area while first responders worked and police began their investigation. the initial report did not identify the driver, describe the direction of travel or say whether any citations or charges were being considered. because the available information remains preliminary, the cause of the crash and the sequence leading to impact are not yet established. road users should avoid drawing conclusions until police release additional findings. the closure was announced as an active-scene measure; drivers should check medway police updates for the road’s current status. anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant video should follow the department’s instructions if investigators request information. new-england massachusetts massachusetts ma medway medway, massachusetts medway bicycle crash milford street public safety

ma-new-bedford-teens-shooting-3d-printer.text: two teens arrested after gunfire damages new bedford homes police said the intended target was not hurt and investigators recovered two firearms, ammunition and a handgun frame believed to be 3d-printed. two 17-year-old boys were arrested after gunfire struck homes in new bedford’s west end, police said thursday. no injury to the intended target was reported. officers went to the intersection of chestnut and willis streets at about 3:30 p.m. wednesday following reports of shots. they found spent cartridge casings and damage to several nearby houses. investigators allege that two masked teenagers fired toward a person in the area before leaving the scene. police located the teenagers inside a nearby home and recovered two firearms believed to have been used in the shooting. detectives also seized ammunition, clothing, masks, a 3d printer and a handgun frame that investigators believe was produced with the printer. both teenagers face charges that include assault with intent to murder, carrying a loaded firearm without a license and intentionally firing near a building and causing property damage. one also faces allegations tied to manufacturing a firearm with a 3d printer. the accusations remain charges, and the source report did not identify the juveniles. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts new bedford new bedford, ma new bedford shooting juvenile arrests 3d-printed firearm

ma-renters-broker-fee-demands-law-2026.text: massachusetts renters report broker-fee demands despite year-old law complaints and misleading listings persist even though the party that hires a broker has generally been responsible for the fee since august 2025. massachusetts renters are still encountering listings and payment demands that appear inconsistent with the state's broker-fee law more than a year after it took effect, nbc10 boston reported. since august 1, 2025, the person or business that hires a real-estate broker has generally been responsible for paying that broker's fee. the rule matters in a high-cost rental market because a broker fee often equals one month's rent. combined with the first month's rent, security deposit and other permitted charges, move-in costs can exceed $10,000 for some households. the attorney general's office has received hundreds of complaints, while renters continue to report listings that suggest the tenant must pay regardless of who retained the broker. state guidance says a tenant should owe the fee only when the tenant independently hires a broker under a written agreement. potential violations can lead to fines, licensing consequences or civil action, and consumer-protection law may allow triple damages in some cases. renters reviewing a fee demand should preserve the listing and messages, identify who hired the broker and seek guidance before paying a charge they believe is improper. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston massachusetts renters broker fees housing massachusetts law attorney general

ma-shellfish-haverhill-sewage-relief-202.text: massachusetts shellfish harvesters receive $300,000 after haverhill sewage leak relief checks went to about 130 clammers after a 12-day emergency closure along the north shore. massachusetts gov. maura healey handed out $300,000 in relief payments monday to shellfish harvesters affected by a sewage leak in haverhill, whdh reported. the payments were distributed to eligible harvesters at woodman’s of essex. the state’s division of marine fisheries is administering the program, which healey announced in july after the emergency closure disrupted the start of the summer shellfish season. officials said a pressurized sewer line broke in two places near haverhill’s main pumping station during a june storm, sending millions of gallons of wastewater into the merrimack river. the leak led to beach closures and a 12-day emergency shellfish closure along parts of the north shore. about 130 clammers received checks, according to whdh. the recipients were from salisbury, newburyport, newbury, rowley, ipswich, essex, gloucester and rockport. the payments are intended to offset lost income during the closure, when many harvesters were working through a high-demand period. the episode also highlighted how a sewer failure upriver can affect coastal businesses and public access to shellfish beds. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma essex north shore, massachusetts massachusetts north shore shellfish haverhill

ma-sjc-reprimands-judge-joseph-ice-case-.text: massachusetts high court reprimands judge in ice courthouse case the state’s supreme judicial court imposed a public reprimand while emphasizing that investigators did not prove the judge knew of an evasion plan. massachusetts’ highest court publicly reprimanded judge shelley joseph on thursday, closing a disciplinary case that grew out of allegations that a defendant avoided a federal immigration arrest at a newton courthouse in 2018. federal prosecutors charged joseph in 2019 and dropped the case in 2022 after she agreed to face a state disciplinary review. prosecutors had alleged that a dominican man appearing before her was allowed to leave through a rear courthouse door while an immigration and customs enforcement agent waited elsewhere in the building. a disciplinary hearing officer later found that the judicial conduct commission had not proved joseph knew of a plan to help the defendant evade ice. the commission ultimately sought a public reprimand rather than suspension or removal. in a unanimous unsigned opinion, the supreme judicial court found separate violations of judicial conduct rules. it cited an off-the-record discussion with the defendant’s lawyer and joseph’s suggestion that the man might be held overnight after she learned an ice officer was present. the court said those actions created an improper appearance even though the alleged knowing role in an escape plan was not established. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts boston boston, ma massachusetts sjc shelley joseph judiciary immigration

ma-spotted-lanternfly-widespread-2026-09.text: spotted lanternfly spreads across more than 150 massachusetts communities state officials say massachusetts is shifting from trying to eradicate spotted lanternflies to managing their impact on crops, trees and vineyards. the spotted lanternfly has spread to more than 150 massachusetts cities and towns, and state officials now say the focus is shifting from eradication to management, new england public media reported monday. the invasive insect feeds on the sap of trees and woody plants. it also favors tree-of-heaven, another invasive species that is common in urban areas and can help the lanternfly establish new populations. massachusetts officials say the pest can threaten agricultural resources, including grapevines. researchers and growers are working on identification, monitoring and treatment, while the state continues watching areas that do not yet have confirmed infestations. the insects can spread when egg masses attach to vehicles, outdoor equipment and other surfaces. residents are encouraged to inspect cars, clothing and belongings before moving them from infested areas. state recommendations include reporting sightings in areas believed to be free of the pest, along with using approved treatments and crop netting where appropriate. officials say biological-control research is promising but remains years away from broad use. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts spotted lanternfly agriculture environment
