markets-american-eagle-shares-margin-out.text: american eagle shares slide on flat margin outlook and core-brand weakness the retailer kept its annual comparable-sales forecast after a revenue beat, but discounting and excess inventory continued to weigh on expectations. american eagle outfitters shares fell sharply thursday after the apparel retailer forecast flat gross margins for the current quarter and described continued weakness at its namesake brand. the company kept its annual comparable-sales forecast unchanged after reporting second-quarter revenue above analysts’ expectations. reuters said uneven discretionary spending and excess inventory have forced heavier promotions, particularly in women’s denim, putting pressure on profitability even as the aerie intimates and activewear business remained stronger. american eagle has increased its investment in denim marketing to reach younger shoppers, but the core label continues to lose ground to competitors. inventory costs were 14% higher from a year earlier, reflecting tariffs and other expenses, according to the report. the share decline cited by reuters occurred during thursday’s trading and should not be read as a live price. the market reaction highlights investors’ concern that revenue resilience may not translate into stronger earnings while clearance activity remains elevated. american eagle’s next results will show whether inventory reductions and new product campaigns can stabilize the flagship brand. markets markets markets / stocks united states u.s. markets american eagle outfitters retail stocks consumer spending

markets-apollo-johnson-johnson-orthopedi.excerpt: The private-equity firm is said to be in talks for DePuy Synthes, though Johnson & Johnson could still pursue a public separation instead.
markets-apollo-johnson-johnson-orthopedi.text: report: apollo explores deal for j&j orthopedics unit near $20 billion the private-equity firm is said to be in talks for depuy synthes, though johnson & johnson could still pursue a public separation instead. apollo global management is in discussions to acquire johnson & johnson’s depuy synthes orthopedics business in a transaction that could value the unit near $20 billion, according to a bloomberg report carried by reuters. the talks could produce an agreement within weeks, but the process remains unsettled and other private-equity firms have also shown interest. johnson & johnson may still choose a public separation instead of a sale. the company previously said it expected the orthopedics operation to become independent over an 18- to 24-month period. depuy synthes makes joint implants and surgical devices and generated about $9.3 billion in 2025 revenue, giving any transaction substantial scale within the medical-device sector. reuters said it could not independently verify the talks, and apollo and johnson & johnson did not immediately respond to requests for comment. that makes the reported valuation and timing provisional. a sale would give apollo a large established healthcare platform, while a spinoff could let public investors value the operation separately from j&j’s pharmaceutical and other device businesses. the unit has also faced litigation concerning some hip products. markets markets markets / stocks nj new brunswick new brunswick, new jersey apollo global management johnson & johnson depuy synthes private equity healthcare

markets-asian-stocks-oil-bond-yields-202.excerpt: Asia-Pacific shares fell as oil stayed above $100 and U.S. Treasury yields held near their highest level since 2023.
markets-asian-stocks-oil-bond-yields-202.text: asian stocks slide as oil and bond yields pressure risk appetite asia-pacific shares fell as oil stayed above $100 and u.s. treasury yields held near their highest level since 2023. asian equity markets moved lower thursday as investors weighed oil prices above $100 a barrel, elevated bond yields and upcoming u.s. inflation reports. reuters reported that msci’s broad asia-pacific index outside japan fell about 1% in early trading, while japan’s nikkei and south korea’s kospi each declined more than 1%. brent crude traded near $101 a barrel after crossing $100 on wednesday amid widening attacks on shipping in the middle east. u.s. 10-year treasury yields held around 4.84%, near their highest level since 2023. higher oil and borrowing costs renewed inflation concerns before u.s. producer-price and consumer-price data due thursday and friday. those readings may shape expectations for the federal reserve’s september 15–16 policy meeting. the figures reflect market conditions reported during asian trading and are not live quotes. investors are also preparing for european central bank and bank of japan decisions, with the interaction between energy costs, currencies and interest rates likely to drive near-term volatility. markets markets markets / stocks international singapore singapore asian markets brent crude treasury yields inflation

markets-australian-shares-two-month-low-.excerpt: The S&P/ASX 200 ended Friday down 0.9%, with mining stocks leading losses as elevated oil prices and bond yields weighed on sentiment.
markets-australian-shares-two-month-low-.text: australian shares close at two-month low as miners retreat the s&p/asx 200 ended friday down 0.9%, with mining stocks leading losses as elevated oil prices and bond yields weighed on sentiment. australian shares closed at their lowest level in more than two months friday as a sharp decline in mining companies outweighed gains in financial stocks. the s&p/asx 200 ended 0.9% lower at 8,741.20, its weakest close since july 2, according to reuters. the benchmark lost 2.1% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since mid-march. mining stocks fell 3.7%, with bhp down 4.1% and rio tinto down 3.5%. lithium producers were also hit: liontown resources dropped 8.6% and pls fell 7.4%. these are closing figures from friday’s session, not live prices. investors were balancing commodity-company weakness against higher energy costs and rising interest-rate expectations. oil above $100 a barrel added to concern that inflation could remain elevated. australian government bond yields moved above 5%, their highest level since mid-2011, increasing the pressure on rate-sensitive valuations. financial shares provided a partial offset, gaining 1.1%. the split session showed how the current oil and bond-market shock can affect sectors differently: banks may benefit from parts of the rate environment, while resource shares remain exposed to commodity demand, currency moves and shifts in global risk appetite. markets markets markets / stocks australia sydney sydney, australia australia asx 200 mining stocks bond yields

markets-baker-hughes-forecast-chart-2026.excerpt: The energy-technology company lifted its annual revenue and earnings outlook after completing the $13.6 billion purchase.
markets-baker-hughes-forecast-chart-2026.text: baker hughes raises 2026 forecasts after chart acquisition the energy-technology company lifted its annual revenue and earnings outlook after completing the $13.6 billion purchase. baker hughes raised its 2026 forecasts wednesday after incorporating the recently completed acquisition of chart industries, reuters reported. the $13.6 billion transaction closed in july after receiving conditional approval from european union regulators. the company now expects annual revenue of $28.50 billion to $30.30 billion, up from its previous range of $26.65 billion to $28.05 billion. its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization forecast rose to $4.88 billion to $5.48 billion. baker hughes had previously projected adjusted ebitda of $4.6 billion to $5.1 billion. the revised outlook includes chart’s operations, making direct comparison with the earlier standalone forecast important when evaluating the apparent increase. chief executive lorenzo simonelli said visibility is improving for a recovery in liquefied-natural-gas orders in 2027. baker hughes expects 55% to 65% of the acquired chart segment’s core profit to be recognized in the fourth quarter, while equipment timing and softer hydrogen demand may pressure margins in the near term. markets markets markets / stocks tx houston houston, tx baker hughes chart industries earnings outlook energy

markets-baldwin-dell-sequence-7-7-billio.excerpt: DFO Management and Sequence Holdings will acquire insurance broker Baldwin Group in a deal designed to give the company more flexibility for AI investment.
markets-baldwin-dell-sequence-7-7-billio.text: michael dell-backed group agrees to take baldwin private for $7.7 billion dfo management and sequence holdings will acquire insurance broker baldwin group in a deal designed to give the company more flexibility for ai investment. dfo management, the investment vehicle backed by dell technologies founder and ceo michael dell, and sequence holdings have agreed to take baldwin group private in a transaction valued at $7.7 billion, reuters reported monday. baldwin shareholders are expected to receive $32.50 in cash per share. reuters said the offer represented an 88% premium to the company’s unaffected share price before reports of a possible deal began circulating. baldwin provides insurance brokerage, risk-management and technology-enabled underwriting services. the buyers said private ownership would give the company more flexibility to make long-term investments, including in artificial-intelligence capabilities, without the same pressure as a public quarterly reporting cycle. the transaction is expected to close during the first quarter of 2027, subject to the required approvals and closing conditions. eligible employees will have an opportunity to retain a minority stake by rolling over part of their holdings, according to the report. the deal is another example of investors using private capital to fund technology upgrades in established service businesses. it also places a large insurance brokerage transaction among the day’s notable mergers and acquisitions. markets markets markets/stocks new york united states markets stocks insurance mergers and acquisitions dell

markets-biotech-shares-novartis-trial-20.excerpt: Dyne, Sarepta and PepGen fell after a late-stage Novartis drug failed to show a statistically significant benefit in a muscle-disease trial.
markets-biotech-shares-novartis-trial-20.text: biotech shares slide after novartis muscle-disease trial setback dyne, sarepta and pepgen fell after a late-stage novartis drug failed to show a statistically significant benefit in a muscle-disease trial. shares of several biotech companies fell tuesday after novartis said a late-stage study of its drug del-desiran failed to show a statistically significant improvement in a measure of hand function for people with myotonic dystrophy type 1. reuters reported that dyne therapeutics led the decline, dropping 18%, while sarepta and pepgen also fell more than 9% and 5%, respectively. novartis shares were down nearly 11% in the reported session. the result matters beyond one drug because the companies are pursuing related approaches to rare muscle diseases. analysts were still assessing whether the setback reflected the treatment mechanism, the trial design or both. these are reported market moves, not live quotes. novartis acquired the program through its purchase of avidity, adding a deal-making angle to the market reaction. investors are now watching whether other companies’ trial data can separate a single-study failure from a broader problem for the field. markets markets markets / stocks u.s. markets markets stocks biotech novartis clinical trials

markets-bis-ai-boom-financial-stability-.excerpt: Pablo Hernández de Cos pointed to concentrated valuations and increasingly opaque debt financing while acknowledging AI’s productivity potential.
markets-bis-ai-boom-financial-stability-.text: bis chief warns ai investment boom is creating financial-stability risks pablo hernández de cos pointed to concentrated valuations and increasingly opaque debt financing while acknowledging ai’s productivity potential. the global ai investment boom has become large enough to influence economic conditions and deserves closer financial-stability scrutiny, bank for international settlements chief pablo hernández de cos said thursday. the bis estimates that the five largest technology companies will invest more than $1 trillion in ai across 2025 and 2026. industry projections cited by the central-bank organization put global ai investment at about $500 billion now and as much as $4 trillion by 2030. hernández de cos said high valuations, concentrated markets and less transparent financing could create vulnerabilities if corporate profits fail to meet expectations. a growing share of ai infrastructure spending is being financed with debt and private credit instead of current earnings, increasing links between technology investment and financial markets. the warning was not a forecast of a crash. the bis chief also cited studies finding productivity gains of 10% to 65% in particular tasks, including coding and professional writing. for investors and policymakers, the central issue is whether those task-level gains spread across the economy quickly enough to justify the scale and financing cost of current spending. markets markets markets / stocks international basel basel, switzerland bis artificial intelligence financial stability private credit

markets-bis-ai-rally-vulnerability-2026-.excerpt: The central-bank umbrella group says investors are more cautious about future AI profitability as tech leverage rises, though it sees no broad market stress.
markets-bis-ai-rally-vulnerability-2026-.text: bis says ai-led market rally showing signs of vulnerability the central-bank umbrella group says investors are more cautious about future ai profitability as tech leverage rises, though it sees no broad market stress. the bank for international settlements said monday that the ai-driven rally in global stock markets is showing signs of vulnerability as investors question future profits and technology companies take on more debt, reuters reported. the bis said the market was not in immediate stress and that risk appetite had remained resilient. it nevertheless warned that rising bond yields, geopolitical uncertainty and volatile energy prices could make the rally harder to sustain. private-market borrowing by technology firms has grown sharply, according to the bis report. aggregate borrowing rose from about $22 billion, or 22% of private credit, in 2010 to more than $1 trillion, or 44%, in 2025. outstanding loans of all types totaled nearly $2.5 trillion. the report focused on leverage and the opacity of some financing arrangements, including deals that sit outside company balance sheets. that makes it harder for investors to judge how much risk is tied to the ai investment cycle. the bis findings arrive after a period of heavy spending on chips, data centers and ai models. they do not predict an imminent crash, but they give central-bank officials another reason to watch technology debt and bond-market yields. markets markets markets/stocks united kingdom london london, united kingdom markets/stocks artificial intelligence bis debt

markets-boj-rate-hike-reuters-poll-sept-.excerpt: Ninety-seven percent of economists surveyed expect a September 18 move to 1.25%, with a faster path toward 1.75% next year.
markets-boj-rate-hike-reuters-poll-sept-.text: reuters poll points to bank of japan rate increase this month ninety-seven percent of economists surveyed expect a september 18 move to 1.25%, with a faster path toward 1.75% next year. a reuters poll shows a strong consensus that the bank of japan will raise its policy rate to 1.25% on september 18 as officials confront broadening inflation pressure and a weak yen. all but two of 68 economists surveyed from september 1 through september 8 expected an increase, a 97% share that was substantially higher than in the prior poll. more than one-third of respondents also expected another increase to 1.50% in october or december. looking further ahead, 57 of 64 economists expected the rate to reach at least 1.50% by the end of march. about 62% projected a level of at least 1.75% by the end of the second quarter of 2027, three months earlier than the previous survey indicated. the poll is a forecast, not a policy decision. a faster tightening path can influence the yen, japanese government bonds and global capital flows, particularly strategies that rely on borrowing cheaply in japan to invest elsewhere. markets markets markets / stocks japan tokyo tokyo, japan bank of japan interest rates yen economy

markets-bond-etf-shorter-maturities-rate.excerpt: Recent ETF flows show demand concentrating in short and intermediate bonds while long-term funds attract far less money.
markets-bond-etf-shorter-maturities-rate.text: bond etf investors favor shorter maturities as rate risks rise recent etf flows show demand concentrating in short and intermediate bonds while long-term funds attract far less money. u.s. exchange-traded fund investors are favoring short- and intermediate-term bonds as concern grows that inflation and heavy borrowing could keep long-term interest rates elevated, reuters reported wednesday. short-term treasury etfs drew about $12.2 billion during the 20 trading sessions through september 8, while intermediate-term treasury funds received roughly $5.7 billion. morningstar data through august showed a similar pattern: intermediate core bond etfs attracted $54.2 billion and short-term funds $25.3 billion, compared with $2.5 billion for long-term products. shorter maturities generally move less when interest-rate expectations change, which can make them attractive when investors want income without taking as much duration risk. they still carry market and credit risks, and flows show where money has moved rather than what will perform best. rising oil prices, government financing needs and competition for capital have pushed yields higher. the positioning suggests investors are seeking flexibility while they wait for clearer inflation data and central-bank signals instead of making a larger commitment to long-dated bonds. markets markets markets / stocks ny new york new york, ny bond etfs treasuries interest rates investing

markets-brent-crude-above-100-september-.excerpt: Reuters reported Brent touched $100.19 before easing, crossing the threshold for the first time since July 24 amid Middle East supply concerns.
markets-brent-crude-above-100-september-.text: brent crude breaks above $100 as supply fears deepen reuters reported brent touched $100.19 before easing, crossing the threshold for the first time since july 24 amid middle east supply concerns. brent crude briefly rose above $100 a barrel wednesday as the conflict in the middle east intensified concerns about oil production and shipping routes. reuters reported that brent reached $100.19 during trading before easing to $99.93. u.s. west texas intermediate was reported at $94.52. the move put brent above $100 for the first time since july 24. those figures were snapshots from wednesday’s session, not live prices, and they can change quickly. traders were assessing risks to supply infrastructure and traffic through the strait of hormuz, a key route for global energy exports. the threshold matters because sustained crude gains can raise fuel and transportation costs and complicate the inflation outlook. a brief move above $100 does not establish where oil will close or remain. investors and consumers should check current market data for later prices and watch confirmed shipping, production and inventory updates rather than treating conflict headlines alone as proof of a lasting shortage. markets markets markets / stocks international london global oil markets brent crude oil prices strait of hormuz energy markets

markets-canada-grocers-boycott-sourcing-.excerpt: Retailers are expanding origin labels and finding alternatives to U.S. produce as consumer preferences and trade tensions alter supply decisions.
markets-canada-grocers-boycott-sourcing-.text: canadian grocers shift sourcing as buy-local boycott reshapes shelves retailers are expanding origin labels and finding alternatives to u.s. produce as consumer preferences and trade tensions alter supply decisions. canadian supermarkets are changing labels and supply relationships as more shoppers seek domestic products and avoid u.s. goods amid a renewed trade dispute. independent grocers are sourcing produce from canada and countries including mexico, morocco, south africa, spain, brazil and honduras, according to retailers interviewed by reuters. vince’s market, which operates four stores in the greater toronto area, said about 90% of its produce is now canadian. the chain switched strawberry sourcing to quebec and reduced advertising spending as the procurement changes increased operating pressure. loblaw brought back large maple-leaf signs in fresh-food sections and reintroduced tags identifying products affected by tariffs. metro said it would continue prioritizing canadian goods. the shift matters because canada remains heavily dependent on imported fruits and vegetables. the united states supplies more than half of canadian fresh-vegetable imports, although its share fell to 62.6% in july from 69% in july 2023. ottawa is also planning about c$3 billion in spending on greenhouses and vertical farms over a decade, seeking to reduce seasonal supply constraints. markets markets markets / stocks ontario toronto toronto, ontario canadian retail grocers supply chains loblaw trade

markets-chime-stride-bank-acquisition-20.excerpt: The fintech company is seeking a national bank charter and more control over the infrastructure behind its accounts and lending expansion.
markets-chime-stride-bank-acquisition-20.text: chime agrees to buy stride bank for $590 million the fintech company is seeking a national bank charter and more control over the infrastructure behind its accounts and lending expansion. financial-technology company chime agreed tuesday to acquire nationally chartered stride bank for $590 million, a move intended to bring core banking infrastructure under chime’s direct control. reuters reported that the transaction would give chime access to stride’s national charter and capabilities as it expands lending and other financial products. chime has historically relied on partner banks to hold customer deposits and provide regulated banking services behind its app. investors pushed chime shares higher after the announcement, reuters said, reflecting optimism that the structure could improve economics and reduce dependence on outside institutions. the acquisition still requires regulatory approval, and ownership of a bank would also subject chime to direct supervision, capital requirements and compliance obligations. the deal is significant beyond its $590 million price tag because it reflects a broader shift among large fintech companies toward tighter control of regulated infrastructure. closing terms and the exact timing could change during review. any share move cited in connection with the announcement reflects reported trading at that time, not a live quote. markets us united states chime banking fintech acquisitions

markets-coffee-shipments-exchange-stocks.excerpt: Traders are seeking to certify at least 300,000 bags of Brazilian arabica as ICE inventories sit near 26-year lows.
markets-coffee-shipments-exchange-stocks.text: large coffee shipments could rebuild exchange stocks traders are seeking to certify at least 300,000 bags of brazilian arabica as ice inventories sit near 26-year lows. coffee traders are preparing large deliveries of brazilian arabica to ice exchange warehouses, a move that could more than double certified stocks from 26-year lows and place downward pressure on benchmark prices, reuters reported. market participants are seeking to certify at least 300,000 60-kilogram bags for delivery against the december futures contract. ice-certified inventories have fallen below 220,000 bags after harvest delays and extreme weather disrupted supplies. more than 62,000 brazilian bags had already reached depots for grading and quality checks. brazilian coffee exports to belgium jumped 245.3% from a year earlier in august to 31,500 metric tons, government data analyzed by terra investimentos showed. much of ice’s available arabica is stored in antwerp, making those shipments an important signal of possible exchange supply. certification is not automatic, and it remains unclear how many bags will pass inspection. even the full expected volume would leave stocks below the roughly 1 million bags traders regard as comfortable. still, rising inventories can influence algorithmic funds and physical-market expectations, making the delivery pipeline a closely watched commodity-market development. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york london and new york coffee arabica ice futures brazil commodities

markets-coforge-chairman-resignation-202.excerpt: The Indian IT-services company dropped more than 7 percent after Om Prakash Bhatt left following concerns identified in an internal audit.
markets-coforge-chairman-resignation-202.text: coforge shares fall after chairman resigns over board-review concerns the indian it-services company dropped more than 7 percent after om prakash bhatt left following concerns identified in an internal audit. shares of indian technology-services firm coforge fell more than 7 percent wednesday after chairman om prakash bhatt resigned following concerns tied to the company’s board-evaluation process. at 9:16 a.m. india standard time, the stock was down 7.12 percent at 1,809.20 rupees, according to reuters. that figure is a dated early-session snapshot, not a live quote, and the price may move as trading continues. bhatt’s departure followed concerns identified through an internal audit of how the board evaluation was conducted. investors often treat unexpected board-level resignations as a governance risk because they can create uncertainty about oversight, controls and future disclosures, even before the underlying issue is fully explained. the next material information will come from coforge’s formal filings and any account of corrective steps. a one-day price move does not by itself establish the long-term effect on operations or financial performance. for now, the decline reflects an immediate market reaction to leadership and process concerns at a company serving global clients in software and information-technology services. markets international india coforge india it services corporate governance

markets-colgate-personal-care-brand-sale.excerpt: Sources say the personal-care brands under review could fetch more than $1 billion as consumer groups narrow their portfolios.
markets-colgate-personal-care-brand-sale.text: colgate explores sale of softsoap, irish spring and speed stick sources say the personal-care brands under review could fetch more than $1 billion as consumer groups narrow their portfolios. colgate-palmolive is exploring the sale of several mass-market personal-care brands, including softsoap, irish spring and speed stick, reuters reported friday, citing people familiar with the matter. the company is working with goldman sachs on the possible divestiture. the brands under review could bring in more than $1 billion, according to the sources. colgate's broader personal-care business includes deodorants, soaps, shower gels and skin-care products, but the company is considering selling only part of the unit. colgate and goldman sachs declined to comment to reuters. the review comes as major consumer-products companies reshape portfolios in response to tariffs, pressure on household spending and higher energy and input costs. selling smaller brands can free capital and management attention for products a company considers central to future growth. a review does not guarantee a transaction, and no buyer or timetable was disclosed. investors will be watching whether a sale proceeds, what valuation the brands receive and how colgate would use any proceeds. the report concerns a potential deal, not a completed sale. markets markets markets / stocks us united states colgate-palmolive softsoap irish spring speed stick consumer goods

markets-cvc-final-talks-ginko-china-busi.excerpt: Sources say a possible deal for the contact-lens maker’s mainland operations could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt.
markets-cvc-final-talks-ginko-china-busi.text: cvc enters final talks for eqt’s ginko china business sources say a possible deal for the contact-lens maker’s mainland operations could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt. cvc capital partners has entered final negotiations to buy the mainland china operations of contact-lens maker ginko international from eqt, four people familiar with the matter told reuters. the potential transaction could value the business at $700 million to $800 million including debt. eqt had sought at least $1 billion, and the financial terms have not been finalized. the talks could still end without an agreement. ginko was founded in taiwan and makes conventional and disposable contact lenses along with lens-care products. mainland china is its largest sales market. the investment was made in 2022 by baring private equity asia, which later combined with eqt. eqt previously agreed to sell the business to advent international, but that deal fell through. eqt and jpmorgan declined to comment on the latest talks, while cvc and goldman sachs did not respond to reuters. a completed sale would give investors another measure of private-equity appetite for chinese consumer-health assets. markets markets markets / stocks china hong kong hong kong cvc eqt ginko international private equity deals

markets-deloitte-us-holiday-retail-sales.excerpt: The firm forecasts sales could rise as much as 4.8%, supported by disposable income even as shoppers remain focused on value.
markets-deloitte-us-holiday-retail-sales.text: deloitte sees faster u.s. holiday retail-sales growth in 2026 the firm forecasts sales could rise as much as 4.8%, supported by disposable income even as shoppers remain focused on value. u.s. holiday retail sales are expected to grow faster in 2026, with deloitte forecasting an increase of as much as 4.8% during the crucial year-end shopping period, reuters reported thursday. deloitte tied the outlook to growth in disposable income, which could support spending even as households absorb higher fuel and other everyday costs. the forecast suggests consumers will continue searching for value while reserving room for selected discretionary and seasonal purchases. the projection matters for retailers because the holiday quarter often determines annual performance. merchants must balance promotions for budget-conscious households with inventory for customers willing to spend more on a smaller number of items. forecast growth does not guarantee equal gains across chains, product categories or income groups. the estimate is a forward-looking forecast rather than a report of completed sales. results will depend on inflation, employment, fuel costs, promotions and the timing of purchases. retailers and investors will compare the outlook with incoming consumer-spending data and company guidance as the season approaches, while watching whether higher costs change the mix of goods shoppers buy. markets markets markets / stocks us new york united states holiday retail deloitte consumer spending retail sales

markets-dollar-oil-fed-hike-2026-09-14.excerpt: The U.S. dollar index was up 0.3% at 99.41 in Reuters’ Monday report as investors weighed Middle East oil risks and a possible Fed hike.
markets-dollar-oil-fed-hike-2026-09-14.text: dollar gains as oil, rate-hike expectations reshape market mood the u.s. dollar index was up 0.3% at 99.41 in reuters’ monday report as investors weighed middle east oil risks and a possible fed hike. the u.s. dollar rose against major currencies monday as middle east conflict lifted oil prices and investors prepared for what could be the federal reserve’s first interest-rate increase in more than two years, reuters reported. the dollar index was up 0.3% at 99.41 in the report after touching 99.735, its highest level since sept. 2. those figures describe reuters’ monday market report and are not a live quote. brent crude rose as much as 5% to $109.80 a barrel before giving back part of the gain and trading at $105.61. the move pushed global bond yields higher and reinforced concern that energy costs could keep inflation elevated. money markets were pricing about a 90% chance of a fed rate hike on wednesday, up from roughly 60% a week earlier, according to the cme fedwatch tool cited by reuters. the shift supported the dollar but also increased uncertainty for stocks and bonds. the yen weakened 0.5% against the dollar to 154.355 after recent gains, while bitcoin rose 2% to $79,152.23 in the same report. markets remain sensitive to developments in the conflict, oil flows and the fed’s decision. markets markets markets/stocks united states new york new york, new york markets/stocks u.s. dollar oil federal reserve

markets-ecb-lane-energy-prices-consumpti.excerpt: The central bank’s chief economist said the duration of higher energy costs remains an important uncertainty for euro-zone households and policymakers.
markets-ecb-lane-energy-prices-consumpti.text: ecb’s lane says persistent energy rise could hit autumn consumption the central bank’s chief economist said the duration of higher energy costs remains an important uncertainty for euro-zone households and policymakers. a sustained increase in energy prices could begin to weigh on household consumption in the euro zone by autumn, european central bank chief economist philip lane said friday. speaking at a conference in ireland, lane emphasized that the effect depends on whether the current rise persists. the warning puts household demand at the center of the energy shock facing europe. higher power and fuel bills can leave consumers with less money for other purchases, while also complicating the inflation outlook that guides interest-rate decisions. lane did not announce a policy change or provide a new forecast, describing the issue instead as a continuing source of uncertainty. for markets, the comment highlights the two-sided challenge confronting the ecb: energy costs can lift inflation even as they weaken growth by reducing spending. investors will therefore be watching incoming consumption and price data for evidence of which effect is becoming stronger. lane’s remarks were made before new autumn data are available, so they are a risk assessment rather than a conclusion that demand has already declined. markets markets markets / stocks europe wexford wexford, ireland european central bank energy prices consumption euro zone

markets-ecb-makhlouf-rate-hikes-growth-w.excerpt: Ireland's central-bank governor said prolonged Middle East conflict may sustain inflation, but additional tightening carries increasing economic costs.
markets-ecb-makhlouf-rate-hikes-growth-w.text: ecb policymaker warns further rate hikes could damage growth ireland's central-bank governor said prolonged middle east conflict may sustain inflation, but additional tightening carries increasing economic costs. european central bank policymaker gabriel makhlouf warned that substantial additional interest-rate increases could impose meaningful costs on economic growth. the governor of ireland's central bank said a prolonged middle east conflict may keep inflation elevated, leaving officials to balance price stability against the risk of tightening financial conditions too far. the ecb raised borrowing costs thursday for the second time in 2026. reuters reported that policymakers may consider another move in october, although no decision has been made. makhlouf's comments highlight a widening tradeoff: energy-driven inflation can justify restraint, but higher rates also raise financing costs for households and businesses and can suppress investment and demand. markets will use incoming inflation, wage and activity data to judge whether further increases are likely. makhlouf did not argue that the inflation threat has passed; his warning centered on the cumulative effect of going much further. for investors, that means the next policy meeting will turn not only on headline inflation but also on evidence that the euro-area economy can absorb another increase without a sharper slowdown. markets markets markets / stocks ireland dublin dublin, ireland european central bank gabriel makhlouf interest rates inflation economic growth

markets-ecb-raises-deposit-rate-2-5-2026.excerpt: The European Central Bank delivered its second increase of 2026 and lifted its inflation forecast while warning that price risks remain tilted upward.
markets-ecb-raises-deposit-rate-2-5-2026.text: ecb raises deposit rate to 2.5% as energy inflation accelerates the european central bank delivered its second increase of 2026 and lifted its inflation forecast while warning that price risks remain tilted upward. the european central bank raised its benchmark deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% on thursday, delivering its second rate increase of 2026 as higher energy costs pushed eurozone inflation above target. the ecb said risks were tilted toward higher inflation and weaker growth. it now expects average inflation of 3.0% in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027, while lifting its 2026 growth projection slightly to 0.9% from 0.8%. oil and natural-gas prices have risen during the iran war, creating pressure that policymakers are trying to prevent from spreading into wages and a wider range of goods and services. underlying inflation slowed in the latest data, however, and wage growth has moderated, giving officials reasons to proceed carefully. financial markets had widely anticipated thursday’s decision, so attention shifted to the timing of any follow-up move. higher government-bond yields are already tightening financing conditions, which can slow demand independently of central-bank action. for investors and businesses, the key question is whether the energy shock remains concentrated in fuel costs or becomes persistent across the economy. the ecb did not commit to a preset path for rates. markets markets markets / stocks international frankfurt eurozone european central bank interest rates inflation eurozone

markets-ecb-rate-hike-energy-inflation-s.excerpt: Economists see a move to 2.50% Thursday after renewed U.S.-Iran attacks pushed oil and gas costs higher.
markets-ecb-rate-hike-energy-inflation-s.text: ecb expected to raise rates as energy shock revives inflation risk economists see a move to 2.50% thursday after renewed u.s.-iran attacks pushed oil and gas costs higher. the european central bank is expected to raise its policy rate thursday as higher oil and gas prices renew inflation concerns across the euro zone. economists cited by reuters expect the ecb to lift the rate to 2.50% from 2.25%, its second increase of 2026. renewed attacks involving the united states and iran have pushed energy prices higher after a period of relative calm, complicating the outlook for the 21-country currency bloc. the euro-zone economy has also held up better than anticipated, giving policymakers more room to tighten. bank lending accelerated in july, while financial markets were pricing additional increases through the end of 2027. long-term bond yields have already risen as investors weigh inflation, government debt and heavy borrowing by technology companies. the ecb is also expected to update growth and inflation projections. core inflation eased to 2.4% last month, but headline inflation remains above the bank’s 2% target. the decision and new forecasts, rather than expectations published beforehand, will determine the next market response. markets markets markets / stocks germany frankfurt frankfurt, germany european central bank interest rates inflation energy

markets-eia-oil-price-forecast-september.excerpt: The agency now expects Brent crude to average about $91 a barrel in 2026 after conflict-driven supply losses reduced stockpiles.
markets-eia-oil-price-forecast-september.text: eia raises oil-price forecasts as global inventories shrink the agency now expects brent crude to average about $91 a barrel in 2026 after conflict-driven supply losses reduced stockpiles. the u.s. energy information administration raised its oil-price forecasts wednesday, citing rapidly declining global inventories and persistent disruptions to middle eastern supply. in its latest short-term energy outlook, the agency projected that brent crude will average about $91 a barrel in 2026, nearly 5% above its prior forecast. it put the west texas intermediate average at $84.65. those figures are annual forecasts, not live market prices. the eia estimated that global oil inventories have fallen by roughly 400 million barrels this year and will continue declining through year-end. middle eastern production shut-ins reached about 6.7 million barrels per day in august, with an average of 5.7 million barrels per day expected to remain offline during the fourth quarter. the outlook assumes some recovery through strait of hormuz shipments and ship-to-ship transfers, but the agency does not expect regional production and exports to normalize before the second quarter of 2027. that leaves prices sensitive to further infrastructure or shipping disruptions. markets markets markets / stocks dc washington washington, dc eia oil brent crude energy markets

markets-energy-holdings-ventura-offshore.excerpt: The stock transaction would create a larger deepwater drilling group and could be followed by a U.S. dual listing.
markets-energy-holdings-ventura-offshore.text: energy holdings to buy ventura offshore in $1 billion combination the stock transaction would create a larger deepwater drilling group and could be followed by a u.s. dual listing. cyprus-based energy holdings has agreed to acquire deepwater drilling contractor ventura offshore in a share transaction that values the combined group at about $1 billion. ventura shareholders would receive 605 million newly issued energy holdings shares, tying their return to the future performance of the merged offshore-drilling business. the companies say the combination is intended to create a larger, more profitable operator with stronger cash generation and more capacity for growth and shareholder returns. the transaction brings together energy holdings’ capital base with ventura’s drilling operations at a time when high oil prices and constrained offshore capacity are reshaping investment decisions across the energy-services sector. the combined company is also considering a dual listing in the united states, which could broaden access to investors and improve trading liquidity. no u.s. listing has been finalized. the roughly $1 billion pro forma equity value is based on energy holdings’ latest closing price and the maximum number of shares contemplated in the deal, so it is a transaction benchmark rather than a live valuation guarantee. markets markets markets / stocks cyprus limassol limassol, cyprus energy holdings ventura offshore offshore drilling mergers and acquisitions dual listing

markets-enflame-shanghai-debut-2026.excerpt: The Tencent-backed AI-chip company opened far above its offer price as investors continued to favor domestic semiconductor listings.
markets-enflame-shanghai-debut-2026.text: enflame shares triple in shanghai debut after $912 million ipo the tencent-backed ai-chip company opened far above its offer price as investors continued to favor domestic semiconductor listings. tencent-backed enflame technology surged roughly 200% in its shanghai trading debut friday after raising 6.12 billion yuan, about $912 million, in one of china’s closely watched ai-chip listings. the shares were offered at 142.18 yuan, opened at 410 yuan and rose as high as 475 yuan before trading around 430 yuan in the early reuters report. at that level, the company was valued at about 185 billion yuan. those figures were time-stamped during the session and should not be read as live prices. enflame is developing domestic graphics and ai accelerators as china seeks alternatives to u.s. suppliers. tencent owns 17.95% of the company and was also responsible for 83.79% of its 2025 revenue, creating both a powerful commercial relationship and a concentration risk. the chipmaker reported a 2025 net loss of 1.16 billion yuan on revenue of 990.2 million yuan, which rose 37%. ipo proceeds are earmarked for next-generation chips and related development. the first-day jump shows strong demand for the theme, but it does not resolve enflame’s losses, customer concentration or the execution risks of scaling advanced semiconductor products. markets markets markets / stocks china shanghai shanghai, china enflame ipo ai chips shanghai

markets-esma-abrupt-correction-warning-2.excerpt: ESMA said weakening economic signals, geopolitical stress and elevated asset prices are widening a gap that leaves markets vulnerable to a sharp reversal.
markets-esma-abrupt-correction-warning-2.text: eu watchdog warns optimistic valuations could trigger abrupt market correction esma said weakening economic signals, geopolitical stress and elevated asset prices are widening a gap that leaves markets vulnerable to a sharp reversal. the european union’s securities regulator warned thursday that upbeat asset valuations are increasingly disconnected from a weakening economic outlook, raising the risk of an abrupt market correction. reuters reported that european securities and markets authority chair verena ross cited geopolitical tension and rising energy prices among the pressures testing investor confidence. esma also described operational risk as very high and increasing, in part because advances in artificial intelligence can help attackers find and exploit cyber vulnerabilities. the regulator repeated concerns that shocks in crypto markets could spread more widely as links with traditional finance grow. tokenized equities remain a very small share of global markets, but esma said wider adoption could alter market structure. it also highlighted manipulation and insider-trading risks in fast-growing prediction markets that allow wagers on elections, wars and sports. a regulatory warning is not a forecast that a selloff will occur, and it does not set a timeline. it identifies channels through which losses or operational failures could spread if sentiment changes suddenly. for investors, the report adds a cautionary counterweight to high valuations at a time when energy costs, interest rates and geopolitical events are moving together. markets markets markets / stocks intl paris european union esma market risk cybersecurity crypto

markets-essar-sgn-retail-118-sites-2026-.excerpt: India’s Essar Group is expanding its U.K. fuel-retail network through an acquisition that could be worth up to $608 million.
markets-essar-sgn-retail-118-sites-2026-.text: essar buys u.k. petrol-station operator in deal adding 118 sites india’s essar group is expanding its u.k. fuel-retail network through an acquisition that could be worth up to $608 million. india’s essar group has acquired u.k. petrol-station operator sgn retail, adding 118 locations to its fuel-retail network, reuters reported monday. the acquisition raises the number of stations operated by essar energy transition retail to 235. the company said it is pursuing a long-term plan to reach 800 outlets by 2031, building a larger network tied to its fuel-supply and refining operations. two sources familiar with the transaction told reuters the deal is valued at between £400 million and £450 million, equivalent to roughly $540 million to $608 million. essar declined to confirm the deal value. the purchase is expected to be financed with cash and a £250 million senior debt facility from a group of banks, including first abu dhabi bank, macquarie bank, mizrahi tefahot bank, royal bank of canada and smbc bank international. the transaction gives essar a larger retail presence while extending its strategy of linking fuel production, distribution and service-station operations. the deal remains subject to the customary closing process. markets markets markets/stocks united kingdom united kingdom markets stocks energy mergers and acquisitions

markets-euronext-deutsche-boerse-merger-.excerpt: Shares of Euronext and Deutsche Boerse rose after Euronext’s chief executive said he was open to a tie-up, though he said no talks were underway.
markets-euronext-deutsche-boerse-merger-.text: euronext, deutsche boerse rise after renewed merger talk shares of euronext and deutsche boerse rose after euronext’s chief executive said he was open to a tie-up, though he said no talks were underway. shares of euronext and deutsche boerse rose monday after euronext chief executive stéphane boujnah said he remained open to a combination between the exchanges, reuters reported. boujnah said no discussions were currently taking place, leaving the comments as an expression of interest rather than an announced transaction. at 9:44 a.m. greenwich mean time, euronext shares were up 2.1% and deutsche boerse shares were up 2.9%, according to reuters. london stock exchange group shares were also higher, gaining 3.8% in the same early-market snapshot. any deal would face regulatory and competition questions because the companies operate major trading venues and clearing businesses. for now, the market response reflects renewed speculation, not a merger agreement, formal offer or completed transaction. exchange mergers can change where trading and clearing occur, which is why regulators in several jurisdictions would likely review any proposal. the executive’s comments revived the idea without creating a deal for investors to evaluate. markets markets markets / stocks netherlands amsterdam amsterdam, netherlands euronext deutsche boerse stock exchanges mergers

markets-europe-stocks-friday-gain-weekly.excerpt: The STOXX 600 closed at 639.1 after a Friday rebound, though inflation worries and rising bond yields produced its sharpest weekly loss since July.
markets-europe-stocks-friday-gain-weekly.text: european stocks gain friday but record sharp weekly loss the stoxx 600 closed at 639.1 after a friday rebound, though inflation worries and rising bond yields produced its sharpest weekly loss since july. european shares rose friday but finished a difficult week under pressure from inflation concerns and higher bond yields. the pan-european stoxx 600 gained 0.5% to close at 639.1, reuters reported, while france's cac 40 added 0.8%. telecommunications companies and banks led the regional gains. the daily advance was not enough to prevent the stoxx 600's steepest weekly loss since early july. oil fell more than 3% from a five-month high during friday's session, offering some relief, but elevated energy costs remained a concern for inflation and corporate margins. recent central-bank signals also kept attention on the possibility of tighter policy. individual moves showed that company-specific news still mattered alongside the macroeconomic backdrop. german online broker flatexdegiro fell 7.9% after the resignation of its supervisory-board chairman. the index levels and percentage changes are friday closing figures, not live quotes. investors enter the next week balancing the benefit of the late-session rebound against persistent uncertainty over energy supply, borrowing costs and the pace at which inflation might ease. markets markets markets / stocks europe europe stoxx 600 european stocks inflation bond yields market close

markets-everbank-wafd-merger-2026.text: everbank and wafd agree to $3.9 billion reverse merger the all-stock transaction would create a bank with about $75 billion in assets and give everbank’s investors a majority stake. everbank financial and wafd agreed to a $3.9 billion all-stock reverse merger that would create a publicly traded bank with about $75 billion in assets. under the companies’ agreement, everbank will merge into wafd at the holding-company level, while wafd bank will merge into everbank’s national-bank charter. the public company would take the everbank financial name and trade on nasdaq under the ticker evbk. everbank investors are expected to own 59.2% of the combined company, with current wafd shareholders holding 40.8%. the banks project roughly $58 billion in loans and $59 billion in deposits after the transaction. everbank chief executive greg seibly is expected to lead the combined business. the deal is targeted to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory and wafd shareholder approvals. the announced $3.9 billion value and projected financial benefits are transaction estimates, not live market prices or guaranteed results. investors will weigh the larger deposit base and geographic reach against integration costs, credit risk and the possibility that regulators impose conditions. markets us united states banking mergers everbank wafd

markets-fed-hike-odds-producer-prices-se.excerpt: Futures markets put the chance of a quarter-point move near 70% after August wholesale inflation, with consumer prices still due Friday.
markets-fed-hike-odds-producer-prices-se.text: traders raise odds of september fed rate increase after producer-price data futures markets put the chance of a quarter-point move near 70% after august wholesale inflation, with consumer prices still due friday. interest-rate futures shifted toward a federal reserve increase next week after new data showed u.s. producer prices rose 5.4% in the 12 months through august. reuters reported that traders placed the probability of a quarter-point increase at the fed’s september 15–16 meeting near 70%, up from roughly 65% before thursday’s reports. the central bank has held its policy rate in a 3.50% to 3.75% range since december. the overall wholesale-price increase matched economists’ expectations, but details suggested inflation pressure may be broadening. transportation and warehousing costs rose, along with hospital-service prices and airfares. reuters also noted that disrupted oil distribution from the middle east conflict and heavy electronics demand linked to ai investment are adding pressure. friday’s consumer-price report is likely to shape the final market view before the meeting. futures probabilities are not a guarantee of federal reserve action and can change quickly as new data arrive. investors are watching whether inflation remains too persistent for policymakers to keep rates unchanged while the labor market appears stable. markets markets markets / stocks united states washington washington, dc federal reserve interest rates producer prices inflation

markets-fed-rate-poll-september-2026.excerpt: Expectations for a near-term increase have grown, but a majority of surveyed economists still forecast no change for the rest of the year.
markets-fed-rate-poll-september-2026.text: most economists expect fed to hold rates through 2026, reuters poll finds expectations for a near-term increase have grown, but a majority of surveyed economists still forecast no change for the rest of the year. most economists surveyed by reuters expect the federal reserve to keep its benchmark rate unchanged through the end of 2026, though support for that view has narrowed. in the september 4-9 poll, 52 of 93 respondents forecast no move this year. for the fed’s next meeting, 65 of 93 economists expected the target range to remain at 3.50% to 3.75%. the other respondents anticipated a quarter-point increase, which would be the first rate hike since july 2023. the split was tighter among the 22 primary dealers surveyed: 11 expected rates to stay unchanged all year, 10 forecast at least one increase and one expected a cut. strong recent economic data and the august consumer-price report due friday are central to the debate. these figures describe economists’ forecasts, not a federal reserve commitment or live market pricing. policymakers can change course as inflation, employment and financial conditions evolve. for households and investors, the poll mainly shows that the path once viewed as settled has become more uncertain. markets markets markets / stocks us washington united states federal reserve interest rates economy reuters poll

markets-foreign-buyers-asian-stocks-augu.text: foreign investors return to asian stocks after nine-month selloff lseg data showed $4.72 billion of net purchases across seven asian markets in august, led by renewed interest in ai-linked exporters. foreign investors returned to net buying of asian equities in august after nine consecutive months of selling, reuters reported using lseg market-flow data. investors purchased a net $4.72 billion of shares in taiwan, south korea, india, indonesia, thailand, vietnam and the philippines during the month. they added another $1.52 billion through tuesday’s close in september. those figures are historical snapshots and do not represent live flows. the shift was concentrated around technology exporters linked to artificial-intelligence spending. taiwan received $11.15 billion of net inflows in august, while south korea still recorded an $8.65 billion outflow for a fourth consecutive month. early september data showed foreign buying returning to both markets. corporate results helped improve sentiment: asian companies beat analyst earnings estimates by an average 10.2% in the latest quarter, according to lseg data cited by reuters. profit growth was 44.7% from a year earlier across the sample, with technology growth at 88.3%. the concentration suggests renewed ai exposure, rather than a uniform return to every asian market. markets markets markets / stocks intl singapore asia-pacific asian stocks foreign investment ai stocks lseg

markets-ge-aerospace-cpp-acquisition-202.excerpt: The planned acquisition would bring a critical engine-parts supplier in-house as manufacturers work through persistent production bottlenecks.
markets-ge-aerospace-cpp-acquisition-202.text: ge aerospace to buy castings supplier cpp for $11.75 billion the planned acquisition would bring a critical engine-parts supplier in-house as manufacturers work through persistent production bottlenecks. ge aerospace agreed to acquire consolidated precision products for $11.75 billion, a major bet that owning more of its supply chain will help relieve shortages constraining aircraft-engine production. reuters reported that cpp makes precision castings used in ge’s leap and genx engines as well as other commercial and defense programs. castings have been a persistent bottleneck for engine manufacturers as airlines and aircraft makers press for faster deliveries. ge plans to finance the purchase with $7 billion in cash and additional debt. the company expects the transaction to close in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. it is ge aerospace’s largest acquisition since becoming an independent company in 2024. for investors, the deal trades a large upfront cost for greater control over a strategically important supplier. it could improve production reliability if integration goes well, but it also brings execution risk and may draw scrutiny because cpp supplies other engine makers, including ge competitors. the announced value and timeline are deal terms, not live market prices. markets us united states ge aerospace aviation mergers supply chain

markets-global-bond-yields-oil-rate-bets.excerpt: Government debt sold off and Asian equities fell after rising energy prices and U.S. producer inflation pushed investors toward tighter-rate expectations.
markets-global-bond-yields-oil-rate-bets.text: global bond yields surge as oil shock revives rate-hike bets government debt sold off and asian equities fell after rising energy prices and u.s. producer inflation pushed investors toward tighter-rate expectations. government bond yields rose sharply and asian stocks fell friday as surging oil prices and stronger u.s. producer inflation increased expectations that major central banks may keep policy tighter. in early asian trading reported by reuters, the u.s. 10-year treasury yield reached 4.9708%, its highest level in about three years, while the 30-year yield rose to 5.3803%, a 19-year high. futures markets put the chance of a federal reserve rate increase at roughly 70%. those figures are snapshots from the article, not live quotes. the selloff spread across regions. japan’s nikkei fell 2.8%, the csi 300 dropped 1.2% and hong kong’s hang seng declined 1.5%. australian three-year yields reached a 15-year high, while japan’s 10-year yield approached 3%. energy was the central pressure point: brent crude had climbed nearly 13% for the week after middle east disruptions intensified supply concerns. higher fuel costs can feed inflation while reducing household and business spending, a combination that complicates central-bank decisions and weighs on both bonds and equities. markets markets markets / stocks global new york global markets bonds oil federal reserve asian markets
