markets-gold-us-inflation-data-september.text: gold edges higher as markets await u.s. inflation data a softer dollar supported bullion early thursday while investors watched producer- and consumer-price reports for clues on interest rates. gold moved modestly higher early thursday as a weaker u.s. dollar supported demand and investors awaited inflation reports that could reshape expectations for federal reserve policy, reuters reported. at the time of the reuters update, spot gold was up 0.3% at $4,414.28 an ounce. december u.s. gold futures were down 0.1% at $4,457.20. those figures are a dated market snapshot, not live prices, and can change throughout the trading session. the u.s. producer-price index is due thursday, followed by consumer inflation data friday. both reports will be watched for evidence that higher energy and transportation costs are feeding into broader prices. interest-rate expectations affect gold because bullion pays no yield, while moves in the dollar change its cost for holders of other currencies. reuters said most economists expect the fed to hold rates at its september meeting and through year-end, while market pricing showed a different view, assigning a 60% chance of an increase this month. that gap makes the inflation releases particularly important for bonds, currencies, precious metals and rate-sensitive stocks. markets markets markets / stocks us new york new york, ny gold inflation federal reserve commodities

markets-google-finland-ai-investment-202.excerpt: Alphabet’s Google says it will spend at least €13 billion over two years on data centers, power grids and supporting clean-energy projects.
markets-google-finland-ai-investment-202.text: google plans $15 billion ai infrastructure investment in finland alphabet’s google says it will spend at least €13 billion over two years on data centers, power grids and supporting clean-energy projects. google plans to invest at least €13 billion, about $15.1 billion, in artificial-intelligence infrastructure in finland over 2027 and 2028. the company said the program will include new data centers, grid improvements, clean-energy projects and battery capacity, reuters reported. google described it as its largest single investment in europe. finland’s cold climate and relatively low-carbon electricity supply have made the country attractive for large computing facilities. the commitment adds to a sharp rise in capital spending by major technology companies as they compete to secure electricity, land and specialized hardware for ai services. alphabet has said its global spending could reach $195 billion to $205 billion, putting pressure on the company to show that higher infrastructure costs produce durable revenue growth. the finnish projects will unfold over multiple years, so the announced total is a planned commitment rather than money already spent. construction schedules, permitting and energy availability can still affect timing. for investors, the development is another measure of how quickly ai competition is shifting from software releases toward long-lived physical assets. markets markets markets / stocks international finland alphabet google finland ai infrastructure

markets-hdfc-bank-two-ceo-candidates-rbi.excerpt: The unnamed nominees require Reserve Bank of India approval before Sashidhar Jagdishan’s second term ends in October.
markets-hdfc-bank-two-ceo-candidates-rbi.text: hdfc bank submits two ceo candidates to india’s central bank the unnamed nominees require reserve bank of india approval before sashidhar jagdishan’s second term ends in october. hdfc bank’s board has submitted two candidates to the reserve bank of india for approval as the private lender’s next chief executive, reuters reported. the candidates were not named. the selection will determine the successor to sashidhar jagdishan, who is scheduled to retire when his second term ends in october. indian private banks must obtain the central bank’s prior approval before appointing a chief executive, giving the regulator a direct role in the succession. hdfc bank has also reappointed v. srinivasa rangan as a whole-time director and named jimmy tata to the same type of position. the incoming ceo is expected to fill a fourth whole-time director role. leadership continuity matters for hdfc bank because of its scale and the operational demands of its expanded franchise. the board’s submission moves the process into the regulatory phase but does not indicate which candidate is preferred or when the rbi will decide. investors will be watching for the nominee’s priorities on growth, asset quality and integration. until approval is announced, the bank’s existing leadership remains responsible for managing the transition toward jagdishan’s october departure. markets markets markets / stocks india mumbai mumbai, india hdfc bank banking reserve bank of india leadership

markets-holtec-nuclear-ipo-2026.excerpt: The New Jersey company plans to offer 50 million shares as investor interest grows around nuclear power and data-center electricity demand.
markets-holtec-nuclear-ipo-2026.text: holtec nuclear seeks up to $10.2 billion valuation in u.s. ipo the new jersey company plans to offer 50 million shares as investor interest grows around nuclear power and data-center electricity demand. holtec nuclear is seeking a valuation of up to $10.2 billion in a u.s. initial public offering, opening a closely watched fall listing window for energy and infrastructure companies. reuters reported that the camden, new jersey-based company plans to offer 50 million shares at $15 to $18 each, potentially raising as much as $900 million. holtec expects to list on nasdaq and nasdaq texas under the ticker hnuc. the company makes reactor components and spent-fuel storage systems, handles nuclear-plant decommissioning and is developing small modular reactors. it is also working to restart the 800-megawatt palisades plant in michigan, an effort that would return a previously decommissioned u.s. commercial reactor to service. the targeted valuation and proceeds are terms in an offering plan, not a completed sale or live market price. investor demand can still change the range, timing or final amount raised. the ipo will test how much public-market enthusiasm for rising data-center electricity demand extends to companies with long nuclear-project timelines and substantial regulatory requirements. markets nj camden, new jersey ipo nuclear power holtec energy

markets-hong-kong-ipo-rebound-finance-ta.excerpt: A surge in fundraising and company expansion is supporting hiring and tightening premium office space after a prolonged slowdown.
markets-hong-kong-ipo-rebound-finance-ta.text: hong kong ipo rebound draws finance talent back a surge in fundraising and company expansion is supporting hiring and tightening premium office space after a prolonged slowdown. hong kong’s renewed deal activity is pulling financial professionals back to the city as initial public offerings and other fundraising recover. total capital raised in the first eight months of 2026 reached $83.5 billion, reuters reported, an increase of 76% from the same period a year earlier. the expansion is spreading beyond trading desks. more than 400 companies established or enlarged hong kong operations during the first half, up 9% from a year earlier. those commitments are expected to bring hk$53 billion, or about $6.8 billion, in direct investment and create roughly 8,600 jobs. the city’s economy grew 5.9% in the first quarter, adding momentum to the hiring rebound. office data provide another sign of firmer demand. savills said prime central rents rose 4.8% in the second quarter as vacancy fell to 9.4% from 10.2%; knight frank measured a decline from 14.5% at the start of the year to 9.7% in july. high living costs and closer integration with mainland china remain considerations, but the financing surge is improving hong kong’s appeal relative to singapore, london and dubai. markets markets markets / stocks hong kong hong kong hong kong hong kong ipos finance office market investment banking

markets-hormuz-oil-transit-insurance-cos.excerpt: An ENOC executive said insurance and war-risk premiums can push some voyage costs into an eight-figure range through the key oil route.
markets-hormuz-oil-transit-insurance-cos.text: hormuz oil-transit costs surge as insurers price war risk an enoc executive said insurance and war-risk premiums can push some voyage costs into an eight-figure range through the key oil route. the cost of moving oil through the strait of hormuz has climbed into a range of $10 million to $20 million for some voyages after the iran war, an emirates national oil company executive said wednesday. enoc director paul bradshaw told the appec conference that cargo insurance could reach 5% to 6% of a shipment’s value, potentially adding about $10 million. additional war-risk premiums that were previously zero can now run as high as 10%, reuters reported. bradshaw said some market participants were choosing to go without insurance, while a limited number of shipowners were willing to accept the safety risk. some national oil companies have taken greater control of their own shipping operations. the figures are an industry executive’s reported estimates, not a universal tariff for every vessel. actual costs vary by cargo, route, insurer and risk assessment. even so, the increase shows how conflict can affect energy markets without an immediate change in production: higher insurance, longer routes and fewer willing ships can tighten vessel availability and raise delivered costs. markets markets markets / stocks international singapore strait of hormuz strait of hormuz oil shipping insurance enoc

markets-hsbc-sp500-target-2026.excerpt: The bank cited stronger corporate earnings and AI-infrastructure investment while warning that inflation, rates and geopolitics could still unsettle markets.
markets-hsbc-sp500-target-2026.text: hsbc raises s&p 500 year-end target to 8,100 the bank cited stronger corporate earnings and ai-infrastructure investment while warning that inflation, rates and geopolitics could still unsettle markets. hsbc raised its year-end target for the s&p 500 to 8,100 from 7,650, citing stronger corporate earnings and continued investment in ai infrastructure, reuters reported tuesday. the new target implies a potential 4.9% gain from the index’s latest close. hsbc expects earnings per share growth to accelerate in the second half of 2026, while reuters said 86% of 492 s&p 500 companies reporting so far had exceeded analyst estimates. the bank also listed risks, including possible federal reserve rate increases, geopolitical tension, the november midterm elections and the liquidity demands of new stock offerings and ai investment. an index target is an analyst forecast, not a live market price or guarantee. investors are still weighing whether strong earnings can offset higher energy costs, uncertain rates and the narrow valuation range in which technology stocks have been trading. the forecast is therefore best read as a view on earnings and capital spending, not as a promise that the broad market will follow a straight line higher. markets markets markets / stocks ma markets markets stocks s&p 500 ai federal reserve

markets-imf-global-growth-three-percent-.excerpt: The fund said the world economy has absorbed the energy shock better than feared, while elevated prices and near-record public debt remain concerns.
markets-imf-global-growth-three-percent-.text: imf sees 3% global growth but warns risks remain high the fund said the world economy has absorbed the energy shock better than feared, while elevated prices and near-record public debt remain concerns. the international monetary fund said the global economy remains on track to expand about 3% in 2026, although elevated energy prices and debt leave the outlook unusually uncertain. an imf spokesperson told reuters that the economy had absorbed the middle east war’s energy shock better than initially feared. countries used reserves, shifted energy sources and reduced demand, but the fund cautioned that the shock is not over and that oil and gas prices remain high. the imf’s july estimate was 3.0%, below the average 3.5% growth recorded in 2024 and 2025. the organization plans to issue a revised forecast during its october meetings with the world bank in bangkok. public debt is approaching 100% of global economic output, the highest level since world war two, according to the imf. the fund also said progress in lowering inflation has stalled. for markets, the combination matters because slower growth, persistent inflation and heavy government borrowing can pull interest rates, currencies and asset valuations in different directions. markets markets markets / stocks international washington washington, dc imf global growth public debt energy

markets-india-fx-reserves-record-high-20.excerpt: Central-bank data show reserves rose by nearly $45 billion in a week after policy measures drew large overseas inflows.
markets-india-fx-reserves-record-high-20.text: india’s foreign-exchange reserves jump to record $785.7 billion central-bank data show reserves rose by nearly $45 billion in a week after policy measures drew large overseas inflows. india’s foreign-exchange reserves reached a record $785.7 billion in the week ended september 4, rising by nearly $45 billion from the prior week, central-bank data released friday showed. the reserve pool has increased for 10 consecutive weeks and gained almost $120 billion over that span. the reserve bank of india attracted $136.3 billion between june 5 and august 31 through measures designed to bring in dollars, including discounted hedging for overseas borrowing and no-cost hedging for banks raising foreign-currency deposits. non-resident indian deposits accounted for $127 billion of the inflows. in the latest week, foreign-currency assets rose by $47.4 billion while the value of gold holdings fell by about $2.6 billion to $113.8 billion. the larger buffer can strengthen india’s ability to manage currency volatility and external shocks. bankers told reuters that intervention to support the rupee likely absorbed some inflows, while analysts noted that hedged deposits also create future obligations in the central bank’s forward book. markets markets markets / stocks india mumbai mumbai, india india foreign exchange reserve bank of india rupee capital flows

markets-india-lifts-jpmorgan-unit-tradin.excerpt: Copthall Mauritius may resume trading but remains excluded from closing auctions while an investigation continues.
markets-india-lifts-jpmorgan-unit-tradin.text: india lifts most of trading ban on jpmorgan unit, sources say copthall mauritius may resume trading but remains excluded from closing auctions while an investigation continues. india’s securities regulator has lifted most of a trading ban imposed on copthall mauritius investment, a jpmorgan chase unit, two people familiar with the matter told reuters on wednesday. the unit may return to regular trading, but it remains barred from participating in the market’s closing auction session while the regulator continues an investigation tied to an index-manipulation allegation. the partial restriction matters because closing auctions help establish widely referenced end-of-day prices. the decision represents a change in the unit’s operating status rather than a conclusion to the underlying case. reuters attributed the information to sources familiar with the matter, and the continued auction ban signals that regulatory review remains active. for investors, the core development is access: copthall can again participate in most market activity while facing a narrower limit at the close. the report does not establish wrongdoing, and an allegation is not a final regulatory finding. any eventual order from the regulator could provide more detail about the conduct under review, the reason for easing the broader ban and whether further restrictions or penalties are possible. markets markets markets / stocks international mumbai mumbai, india jpmorgan india market regulation trading

markets-india-sebi-derivatives-expiry-pr.excerpt: SEBI is consulting on two alternatives after sharp end-of-day swings raised concerns about how expiring contracts are settled.
markets-india-sebi-derivatives-expiry-pr.text: india proposes overhaul of derivatives expiry pricing sebi is consulting on two alternatives after sharp end-of-day swings raised concerns about how expiring contracts are settled. india’s market regulator has proposed changing how settlement prices are set for derivatives on expiry days after sharp closing moves raised concerns about the new auction process. the securities and exchange board of india is seeking public comment on two alternatives for calculating the final value used to settle expiring contracts. one option would blend prices from the final 30 minutes of regular trading with those from the 10-minute closing auction session. the other would return, for at least a year, to using only the final 30 minutes of normal trading and exclude the auction. sebi also proposed limiting cancellation of orders placed more than 1% away from the indicative price and shortening the post-close window from 10 minutes to five. the regulator said the auction has generated volatility around expiry and is considering withholding an indicative index close during that period. the consultation does not immediately change settlement rules, and market participants have until october 3 to submit comments. the final approach will matter to exchanges, brokers and investors because small closing-price moves can materially affect large derivatives positions. markets markets markets / stocks india mumbai mumbai, india sebi india derivatives market regulation settlement prices

markets-india-stocks-three-month-low-oil.excerpt: The Nifty 50 and Sensex fell for a third session as higher crude prices revived inflation and import-cost concerns.
markets-india-stocks-three-month-low-oil.text: indian stocks close at three-month low as brent tops $100 the nifty 50 and sensex fell for a third session as higher crude prices revived inflation and import-cost concerns. indian shares ended wednesday at their lowest levels in three months as brent crude moved above $100 a barrel and renewed concern about inflation and import costs. reuters reported the nifty 50 fell 0.86% to 23,431.50, while the bse sensex dropped 1.08% to 74,764.23. both benchmarks recorded their lowest closes since june 11 and extended their losing streak to three sessions. thirteen of 16 major sectors declined. information-technology stocks slid 3.2%, while broader small- and mid-cap indexes each lost 0.5%. energy and metals moved against the trend, gaining 0.6% and 1.8%, respectively. adani enterprises rose 5.1% after agreeing to sell part of its airport unit. india imports much of its oil, so a sustained price increase can pressure inflation, corporate costs and the currency. these are official wednesday closing moves cited by reuters, not live quotes. future sessions will depend on energy prices, the middle east conflict and u.s. inflation data that may influence global interest-rate expectations. markets markets markets / stocks international mumbai mumbai, india india stocks nifty 50 sensex brent crude

markets-indian-rupee-rbi-intervention-oi.excerpt: Traders said the Reserve Bank of India likely intervened after rising oil costs and dollar outflows pushed the currency to a session low.
markets-indian-rupee-rbi-intervention-oi.text: indian rupee recovers after reported central-bank support traders said the reserve bank of india likely intervened after rising oil costs and dollar outflows pushed the currency to a session low. the indian rupee recovered from a session low wednesday after traders said the reserve bank of india likely entered the currency market to slow a decline driven by higher oil prices and dollar outflows. reuters reported that the rupee fell to 95.2250 per u.s. dollar before recovering to 95.07 following the suspected intervention. the central bank did not confirm the action in the initial account, so the explanation remains based on traders’ assessment of market activity. india is a major oil importer, making its currency particularly sensitive when crude prices rise because importers need more dollars to pay energy bills. portfolio outflows can add to that demand and increase depreciation pressure. the quoted exchange rates were intraday snapshots from september 9, not live prices, and may have changed after publication. the move shows the challenge facing the rbi: intervention can reduce abrupt volatility, but sustained oil costs and capital flows can continue to influence the currency. later official data may clarify the scale of any central-bank operation. markets markets markets / stocks international mumbai mumbai, india indian rupee reserve bank of india oil prices currency markets

markets-investors-fed-rate-hike-meeting-.excerpt: Bond yields near 5% and persistent inflation have raised the stakes for Wednesday’s central-bank decision.
markets-investors-fed-rate-hike-meeting-.text: investors brace for a possible federal reserve rate hike bond yields near 5% and persistent inflation have raised the stakes for wednesday’s central-bank decision. investors are preparing for a federal reserve meeting in which a rate increase remains a meaningful possibility, a sharp change from the easing expectations that dominated earlier in the cycle. the decision is due wednesday and follows inflation data that kept pressure on policymakers to contain price growth. the u.s. 10-year treasury yield has approached the 5% threshold, raising borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt and other credit markets. higher yields can also challenge stock valuations because future earnings are discounted at a steeper rate. reuters reported that market pricing leaned toward an increase, though the final decision and the fed’s guidance remained uncertain. the s&p 500 was still up about 12% for the year at the time of the report, leaving investors to weigh strong equity performance against tighter financial conditions. attention will extend beyond the rate itself to the central bank’s projections and explanation of how it views persistent inflation, labor conditions and growth. because the meeting has not occurred, current market positioning is an expectation rather than confirmation of a policy move. markets markets markets / stocks united states new york new york, united states federal reserve interest rates treasury yields wall street

markets-italy-ilva-taranto-blast-furnace.excerpt: The ruling over environmental and safety shortfalls threatens production and thousands of jobs at Italy’s largest steelworks.
markets-italy-ilva-taranto-blast-furnace.text: italian court upholds shutdown of ilva blast furnaces the ruling over environmental and safety shortfalls threatens production and thousands of jobs at italy’s largest steelworks. a milan appeals court has upheld an order to shut down blast furnaces at the former ilva steelworks in taranto, rejecting an appeal by operator acciaierie d’italia. the order cites unresolved environmental and safety shortcomings at italy’s largest steel plant, raising the risk of a prolonged production halt at a strategically important industrial site. the taranto complex directly employs about 8,000 people and supports additional contractor jobs. it is italy’s only plant making steel from iron ore and coal through blast furnaces. the operator has warned that cooling the furnaces could cause irreversible damage, which would make restarting traditional production more difficult and expensive even if the legal and environmental disputes are later resolved. the ruling intensifies pressure to settle the plant’s ownership and future technology. options under discussion have included a public stake and a transition toward electric-arc furnaces and direct-reduced iron, which would lower emissions but require substantial investment. for steel buyers, workers and potential investors, the immediate issue is operational: the court has left the shutdown order in place, and no durable replacement plan has yet been completed. markets markets markets / stocks italy taranto taranto, italy ilva steel taranto italy industrial policy

markets-japan-august-wholesale-inflation.excerpt: Producer prices stayed above forecasts in August, reinforcing expectations that the central bank could raise its policy rate next week.
markets-japan-august-wholesale-inflation.text: japan wholesale inflation holds at 7.6% before bank of japan meeting producer prices stayed above forecasts in august, reinforcing expectations that the central bank could raise its policy rate next week. japan’s wholesale prices rose 7.6% in august from a year earlier, keeping pipeline inflation elevated before the bank of japan’s policy meeting next week. the increase in the corporate goods price index was slightly above the 7.4% rise economists had forecast in a reuters poll. july’s gain was revised to 7.7%. on a month-to-month basis, producer prices slipped 0.2% after a revised 0.4% increase in july. the yen-based import price index climbed 24.8% from a year earlier, slowing from a revised 29.3% increase in july but still signaling substantial pressure from imported goods and currency moves. markets had nearly fully priced a bank of japan rate increase to 1.25% from 1%, reuters reported. a separate poll expected the central bank to reach 1.25% next week and 1.75% in the second quarter of 2027. those expectations are market forecasts, not announced decisions. the boj raised its policy rate to a 31-year high of 1% in june and left it unchanged in july. markets markets markets / stocks japan tokyo tokyo, japan japan inflation bank of japan interest rates

markets-japan-bond-yields-domestic-inves.excerpt: Higher local returns are prompting banks and insurers to reassess domestic debt as Japan’s benchmark 10-year yield reaches a three-decade high.
markets-japan-bond-yields-domestic-inves.text: rising japanese bond yields could keep more investment at home, fitch says higher local returns are prompting banks and insurers to reassess domestic debt as japan’s benchmark 10-year yield reaches a three-decade high. rising japanese government-bond yields may encourage banks, insurers and other domestic institutions to keep more investment in japan, fitch ratings said wednesday. japan’s benchmark 10-year yield reached 3% last week for the first time since september 1996, reflecting concerns about inflation, public finances and the pace of bank of japan tightening. fitch expects policy rates to rise faster than market consensus in 2026 and 2027. higher domestic returns reduce the incentive to seek yield overseas. fitch said japanese megabanks are cautiously rebuilding government-bond holdings, while life insurers are selling lower-coupon securities and reinvesting in bonds with higher coupons. it saw no sign that the roughly $2 trillion government pension investment fund had changed its allocation. reuters reported that markets had priced in a near certainty of a rise in the central bank’s key rate to 1.25% next week, but that was a market snapshot rather than a confirmed decision. fitch said it did not expect a fire sale of japanese government bonds even if yields continue rising. markets markets markets / stocks international tokyo tokyo, japan japan bond yields fitch ratings bank of japan

markets-japan-manufacturer-sentiment-sep.excerpt: A Reuters survey showed electronics demand lifting factory confidence, while services sentiment also edged higher.
markets-japan-manufacturer-sentiment-sep.text: japan manufacturer sentiment reaches nearly five-year high a reuters survey showed electronics demand lifting factory confidence, while services sentiment also edged higher. confidence among major japanese manufacturers rose to its strongest level in nearly five years in september, supported by demand for semiconductors and data-center equipment. the reuters tankan manufacturing index increased to plus 21 from plus 18 in august, its highest reading since december 2021. electronics manufacturers recorded a particularly strong improvement, climbing to plus 39 from plus 24. a positive reading means optimists outnumber pessimists. sentiment among nonmanufacturers also improved, reaching plus 29 from plus 28. looking three months ahead, manufacturers expected their index to rise further to plus 27, while service-sector respondents anticipated a slight easing to plus 27. the survey was conducted from august 26 through september 4 and received responses from 224 of 510 companies. businesses still cited risks including middle east tensions, higher raw-material costs and softer consumer spending. the results are a survey of corporate sentiment, not a direct measure of current production or stock prices, but they provide an early view of business conditions before official data. markets international tokyo, japan japan manufacturing semiconductors reuters tankan

markets-jetblue-revenue-outlook-costs-se.excerpt: The New York-based airline lifted its third-quarter unit-revenue forecast but cut capacity growth and projected higher fuel and nonfuel expenses.
markets-jetblue-revenue-outlook-costs-se.text: jetblue raises seat-revenue outlook as fuel and disruption costs climb the new york-based airline lifted its third-quarter unit-revenue forecast but cut capacity growth and projected higher fuel and nonfuel expenses. jetblue airways raised its third-quarter unit-revenue forecast thursday, pointing to steady travel demand even as higher fuel prices and operational disruptions increased the carrier’s expected costs. the new york-based airline now projects revenue per available seat mile to rise 17% to 20% from a year earlier, up from its previous range of 12.5% to 16.5%. that is a forward-looking company estimate, not a completed quarterly result. cost pressure moved in the same direction. jetblue increased its expected average fuel price to $3.96 per gallon from $3.49. it also projected nonfuel unit costs to rise 6% to 8%, compared with an earlier 2.5% to 4.5% range, after weather and air-traffic-control disruptions increased cancellations during july and august. jetblue cut its capacity-growth forecast to 1.5% to 3.5% from 3% to 6%. the revisions give investors a mixed picture: stronger revenue for each unit of flying, but fewer planned seats and a higher expense base. the ultimate margin effect will depend on realized fares, fuel prices and operations through the quarter’s end. markets markets markets / stocks ny new york new york jetblue airlines fuel costs earnings outlook

markets-jpmorgan-situational-awareness-l.excerpt: The bank ended its lending relationship after leveraged artificial-intelligence bets produced steep losses, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.
markets-jpmorgan-situational-awareness-l.text: jpmorgan curbs lending to ai-focused situational awareness fund the bank ended its lending relationship after leveraged artificial-intelligence bets produced steep losses, a source familiar with the matter told reuters. jpmorgan chase ended lending activity for situational awareness after leveraged bets tied to artificial intelligence produced large losses and brought the hedge fund close to collapse, a person familiar with the matter told reuters. the fund liquidated most of its public-equity holdings to citadel after a global rout in chip stocks exposed the scale of its borrowing. situational awareness was launched in 2024 by former openai researcher leopold aschenbrenner and built concentrated positions across the ai ecosystem. the fund told investors its portfolio fell 67% in july, when the selloff generated a margin call and pressure to raise capital or dispose of holdings. jpmorgan was one of its key lenders before notifying the fund that the relationship would end. other banks, including goldman sachs, citigroup and bank of america, remain active brokers for the fund, and it recently began working with clear street. the episode illustrates how leverage can amplify a crowded technology trade when markets reverse. reuters said the banks declined to comment and situational awareness did not immediately respond to a request for comment. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york new york, new york jpmorgan situational awareness hedge funds artificial intelligence leverage

markets-khosla-ventures-new-york-office-.excerpt: The venture firm expects to open a small New York outpost this fall with an executive briefing center for portfolio companies.
markets-khosla-ventures-new-york-office-.text: khosla ventures plans first office outside sand hill road the venture firm expects to open a small new york outpost this fall with an executive briefing center for portfolio companies. khosla ventures plans to open its first office outside silicon valley this fall, establishing a new york outpost on 14th street. investor keith rabois confirmed the move at a techcrunch event, describing it as a significant expansion for a firm that has operated from menlo park and does not maintain a san francisco office. the new location is expected to house a small group of investors, including rabois. it will also include an executive briefing center designed to bring groups of portfolio companies together with large corporate customers. the format is intended to help startups pursue pilot projects and commercial relationships rather than functioning only as a traditional deal office. the expansion adds another major venture-capital name to new york’s startup ecosystem, where firms including sequoia capital and andreessen horowitz already have partners. khosla’s plan is not a fundraise or a stock event, but it is a concrete capital-market signal: a prominent west coast investor sees enough portfolio and customer activity to support a permanent east coast base. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york new york, new york khosla ventures new york venture capital startups

markets-kimberly-clark-kenvue-eu-concess.text: kimberly-clark prepares concessions to win eu approval for kenvue deal kimberly-clark is preparing remedies for european regulators reviewing its planned $40 billion acquisition of kenvue, according to people familiar with the matter. kimberly-clark is preparing concessions aimed at addressing european union antitrust concerns over its planned $40 billion acquisition of kenvue, reuters reported monday, citing people familiar with the matter. the european commission is expected to outline its concerns this week. the commission’s preliminary review is scheduled to end sept. 29, after which the deal could move into a longer investigation that may last about four months. the companies have not disclosed a final remedy package. kimberly-clark’s proposed purchase of kenvue would combine major consumer-health and personal-care brands, making regulatory review important in markets where the businesses overlap. shares of both companies rose more than 2% in early trading, according to reuters, as investors assessed the possibility that concessions could keep the transaction on track. australia and south africa have already granted conditional clearances that require divestitures. the report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances. the report remains subject to further verified updates as officials continue reviewing the circumstances. markets markets markets/stocks united states and europe markets/stocks kimberly-clark kenvue

markets-kioxia-us-listing-ai-investor-ac.excerpt: The Japanese memory-chip maker is preparing an American depositary-share listing as fund managers emphasize liquidity and global visibility.
markets-kioxia-us-listing-ai-investor-ac.text: kioxia’s planned u.s. listing could widen ai-investor access the japanese memory-chip maker is preparing an american depositary-share listing as fund managers emphasize liquidity and global visibility. kioxia’s plan to list american depositary shares in the united states could broaden the japanese memory-chip maker’s investor base and improve trading liquidity, according to a voya investment management fund manager interviewed by reuters. the company announced in may that it was preparing the u.s. listing; it has not yet completed the transaction. kioxia’s tokyo-listed shares have risen 456% this year, reflecting intense investor interest in memory suppliers connected to artificial-intelligence infrastructure. sebastian thomas, who helps manage voya’s $14 billion artificial-intelligence fund, said a u.s. listing could raise kioxia’s global visibility. thomas said the fund does not currently own kioxia. voya’s ai strategy holds about $5 billion from japanese investors but tends to favor larger, more liquid companies. its semiconductor exposure includes south korea’s sk hynix and u.s.-based micron. a depositary-share listing would not change kioxia’s underlying business, but it could make the stock easier for some u.s. institutions to access and compare with global peers. execution, timing and investor demand remain uncertain until the company files final terms and completes the process. the share-performance figures are year-to-date data reported by reuters, not live market quotes. markets markets markets / stocks japan tokyo tokyo, japan kioxia us listing memory chips ai investing

markets-kroger-cuts-sales-forecast-consu.excerpt: The grocer kept its profit outlook after a quarterly earnings beat, but lowered its comparable-sales range amid softer demand.
markets-kroger-cuts-sales-forecast-consu.text: kroger trims sales forecast as shoppers pull back the grocer kept its profit outlook after a quarterly earnings beat, but lowered its comparable-sales range amid softer demand. kroger lowered its full-year comparable-sales forecast friday as slower consumer spending weighed on demand, while leaving its annual profit target unchanged. the grocer now expects identical sales excluding fuel to rise 0.2% to 0.8%, down from its previous 1% to 2% range. second-quarter identical sales excluding fuel rose 0.2% in the period ended august 15, compared with 3.4% a year earlier and below the 0.9% estimate compiled by lseg. adjusted earnings of $1.09 a share were three cents above the estimate. kroger said cost controls, e-commerce and retail media helped support profitability despite weaker unit growth. the company also cited two unusual pressures: a cyclospora outbreak reduced quarterly sales by about 35 basis points, and medicare drug-pricing changes created an estimated 140-basis-point headwind for pharmacy revenue. kroger kept its profit guidance as management focuses on sourcing, simpler operations, store openings and faster delivery. the revised sales view adds to evidence that middle- and lower-income shoppers are emphasizing essentials and value as inflation continues to strain household budgets. markets markets markets / stocks us united states kroger retail consumer spending earnings sales forecast

markets-larry-ellison-cancels-oracle-sha.excerpt: Oracle said no shares were sold and its executive chairman currently has no intention to reduce his holdings.
markets-larry-ellison-cancels-oracle-sha.text: larry ellison cancels plan to sell 50 million oracle shares oracle said no shares were sold and its executive chairman currently has no intention to reduce his holdings. oracle executive chairman larry ellison has canceled a trading plan that would have allowed him to sell up to 50 million oracle shares, the company said saturday. the plan had been announced only a day earlier. oracle said no shares were sold under it and ellison currently has no intention to sell his holdings. the reversal arrives while oracle is raising substantial capital to expand cloud infrastructure for artificial-intelligence demand. the company plans to raise between $45 billion and $50 billion during calendar 2026 through debt and equity financing. it is targeting $40 billion during the current fiscal year, including a $20 billion stock sale completed in the first quarter. oracle is balancing that investment push against restructuring costs and investor sensitivity to the pace and financing of ai expansion. the company reported $700 million in restructuring expenses, including job cuts. its shares had briefly gained after a $26 billion increase in revenue backlog but closed friday about 2% lower, according to reuters. those figures describe completed market moves, not live pricing. canceling ellison’s planned sale removes one potential source of near-term share supply while oracle continues its much larger corporate financing program. markets markets markets / stocks texas austin austin, texas oracle larry ellison stock sale cloud infrastructure

markets-liv-golf-chapter-11-2026.excerpt: The league is seeking a court-supervised restructuring in New Jersey after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund ended financial support.
markets-liv-golf-chapter-11-2026.text: liv golf files for chapter 11 with more than $500 million in debt the league is seeking a court-supervised restructuring in new jersey after saudi arabia’s public investment fund ended financial support. liv golf filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in new jersey on tuesday, listing more than $500 million in debt as it attempts to reorganize after losing its principal saudi financial backing. the associated press reported that the league listed estimated assets of $100 million to $500 million and liabilities of $500 million to $1 billion. fourteen players were among its 30 largest creditors, with jon rahm listed as holding an unsecured claim of nearly $7.5 million. liv said bc partners would be the primary source of capital under a restructuring plan. saudi arabia’s public investment fund, which ended regular support earlier this year, agreed to provide $49.6 million in debtor-in-possession financing, subject to court approval. the proposed relaunch would use a smaller schedule, expand the field to 75 players and add a 54-hole cut and monday qualifiers. liv says it could emerge from bankruptcy and begin the new format as early as 2027. chapter 11 generally allows a business to keep operating while it restructures, but the league’s future will depend on court approval, financing and which players remain. markets us new jersey liv golf bankruptcy chapter 11 sports business

markets-london-shares-friday-weekly-loss.excerpt: The FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 each added 0.4% Friday, yet both finished a volatile week with substantial declines.
markets-london-shares-friday-weekly-loss.text: london shares rebound friday but post steep weekly losses the ftse 100 and ftse 250 each added 0.4% friday, yet both finished a volatile week with substantial declines. london equities recovered on friday as crude oil retreated, but the rebound was not enough to prevent a difficult week for major british indexes. the ftse 100 and the domestically focused ftse 250 each closed about 0.4% higher for the session. banks helped lead the recovery, with hsbc up 1.5% and barclays gaining 1.9% in the reported session. construction and materials shares rose about 1.8%. softer oil prices provided some relief after energy costs had added to concern about inflation and the path of interest rates. despite friday’s gain, the ftse 100 recorded its largest weekly decline since late july, while the ftse 250 posted its steepest weekly loss in more than four months. traders were pricing roughly 44 basis points of bank of england rate increases by year-end at the time of the report. those figures describe friday’s close and contemporaneous expectations, not live prices. the split between a positive final session and a negative week shows how energy markets and rate assumptions continued to drive short-term sentiment across british shares. markets markets markets / stocks united kingdom london london, united kingdom ftse 100 ftse 250 london stocks bank of england

markets-mcclatchy-cuts-90-union-newsroom.excerpt: The layoffs span 17 publications and amount to about 30% of the chain’s NewsGuild-represented workforce.
markets-mcclatchy-cuts-90-union-newsroom.text: mcclatchy cuts more than 90 unionized newsroom jobs the layoffs span 17 publications and amount to about 30% of the chain’s newsguild-represented workforce. mcclatchy laid off more than 90 unionized journalists and media workers across 17 publications, according to the newsguild-cwa. the cuts represent about 30% of mcclatchy employees represented by the union and affect papers including the miami herald, sacramento bee, kansas city star and charlotte observer. the miami herald lost 32 positions, including 28 occupied jobs and four frozen posts, according to a person familiar with the changes cited by the associated press. the eliminated roles included the writing staff of spanish-language el nuevo herald. the union also said the charlotte observer lost its two investigative reporters and that several local-government beats disappeared at other papers. an internal mcclatchy memo said the company could no longer maintain investment where subscriber interest did not support it. a company spokesperson did not respond to the ap’s request for comment. the reductions add to a broader wave of newsroom restructuring driven by declining print revenue, fragmented digital audiences and changing advertising markets. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york new york, new york mcclatchy layoffs newspapers media business

markets-mecka-ai-sequoia-valuation-2026.text: mecka ai nears $500 million valuation in reported sequoia-led round the proposed financing comes three months after the robot-training-data startup announced a $60 million raise. mecka ai is nearing a financing led by sequoia capital that would value the robot-training-data company at about $500 million, techcrunch reported, citing two people familiar with the talks. the exact size of the round was not reported, and the terms were described as unfinished and subject to change. the proposed deal follows only three months after mecka announced a $60 million round led by framework ventures, with menlo ventures, sv angel and kindred ventures participating. the short interval highlights investor demand for companies supplying real-world data used to train humanoid robots and other physical artificial-intelligence systems. founded in 2024, mecka pays people to record everyday tasks using body sensors and smartphones, then organizes that motion data for robotics development. the company has not disclosed its customers. because the latest financing remains under discussion, the reported valuation should be read as a proposed deal level rather than a completed transaction or live market price. markets markets markets / stocks california san francisco san francisco, california mecka ai sequoia capital robotics venture capital

markets-new-fortress-restructuring-debt-.excerpt: The LNG company says its completed restructuring lowered debt from $5.7 billion after a prolonged liquidity crisis.
markets-new-fortress-restructuring-debt-.text: new fortress energy completes restructuring and cuts debt to $700 million the lng company says its completed restructuring lowered debt from $5.7 billion after a prolonged liquidity crisis. new fortress energy has completed a restructuring that reduced its debt to about $700 million from $5.7 billion, the u.s. liquefied-natural-gas company said. the transaction substantially changes the balance sheet after a prolonged liquidity crisis and years of work to address heavy borrowing. regulatory approvals in the united states and united kingdom were secured in june, clearing key conditions for the plan to close. cutting roughly $5 billion of debt lowers the company’s fixed financial burden and gives the reorganized business more room to fund operations and evaluate its lng assets. the restructuring does not by itself guarantee stronger earnings or cash flow, but it removes much of the leverage that had threatened the company’s stability. for investors and creditors, the next focus will be operating performance under the new capital structure. energy infrastructure businesses require large, continuing expenditures, and new fortress still faces commodity, project-execution and customer risks. the announced debt figure is a post-restructuring balance, not a measure of market value or a live share price. completion nevertheless marks a concrete turning point: the company exits the process with a far smaller debt load and a clearer path to continue operating. markets markets markets / stocks united states new york new york, united states new fortress energy lng debt restructuring energy

markets-novartis-investors-ma-clinical-s.text: novartis investors scrutinize deal strategy after clinical setbacks a failed late-stage trial and another recent disappointment are intensifying questions about the drugmaker’s acquisitions and pipeline execution. novartis shareholders are placing fresh scrutiny on the drugmaker’s acquisition strategy after two clinical setbacks in quick succession raised questions about the value and execution of its pipeline, reuters reported friday. the latest disappointment came when the late-stage study of del-desiran failed, following another setback days earlier. the events renewed investor attention on novartis’s roughly $12 billion purchase of avidity biosciences and on whether recent dealmaking will produce enough successful medicines to support growth. novartis shares recorded an 11% one-day decline after the news, wiping out nearly $30 billion in market value and erasing their gains for the year, according to reuters. that was a reported market move, not a live price. chief executive vas narasimhan has committed more than $30 billion to acquisitions and partnerships over the past three years. some investors still expressed confidence in the broader pipeline, but the failures increase pressure for clear trial milestones and disciplined spending. drug development is inherently uncertain, making portfolio breadth and the price paid for experimental assets central to how markets judge pharmaceutical strategy. markets markets markets / stocks switzerland basel basel, switzerland novartis pharmaceuticals mergers and acquisitions clinical trials

markets-nse-india-ipo-price-range-2026.text: nse india ipo likely to target 1,700 to 1,785 rupees a share the expected range could value the exchange at about $46.4 billion at the top end ahead of a planned september listing. india’s national stock exchange is likely to price its initial public offering between 1,700 and 1,785 rupees per share, according to a source familiar with the plans cited by reuters. at the top of that expected range, the exchange would be valued at roughly 4.4 trillion rupees, or $46.4 billion. the listing is targeted for the week of september 21 and would rank among india’s largest stock-market debuts. nse is the dominant venue for indian equity derivatives and the world’s most active derivatives exchange when measured by contract volume. that scale makes the offering important beyond the amount raised: public-market investors would gain direct exposure to trading, clearing and market-data revenue tied to india’s expanding capital markets. the proposed range has not yet become a final offer price, and terms can change before books close. the valuation figures are based on the reported range and exchange rates at publication. they should not be read as a live market price or as a prediction of how the shares will trade after listing. markets international mumbai, india nse ipo india stock exchange

markets-oil-100-weekly-finish-september-.excerpt: Brent and U.S. crude extended gains after shipping and supply disruptions, while OPEC again lowered its 2026 demand-growth forecast.
markets-oil-100-weekly-finish-september-.text: oil benchmarks head for first $100-plus weekly finish since may brent and u.s. crude extended gains after shipping and supply disruptions, while opec again lowered its 2026 demand-growth forecast. oil futures extended their rally friday and were on course for their first weekly finish above $100 a barrel since mid-may as conflict-related shipping risks tightened supply expectations. at 00:45 gmt, brent crude was quoted at $108.68 a barrel and u.s. west texas intermediate at $103.45, both about 1% higher in the reuters report. each benchmark had gained more than 6% thursday and was up nearly 13% for the week. these are time-stamped market levels, not live prices. the advance followed new disruptions around the red sea and strait of hormuz, including the houthi seizure of yemen’s port city of mocha and attacks affecting regional shipping. rising transport and insurance costs are adding to concern about how much crude and refined fuel can move through key routes. opec also cut its forecast for 2026 oil-demand growth to 380,000 barrels per day, its fifth consecutive downward revision, while reporting that august output fell by 640,000 barrels per day. the combination of reduced supply and weaker demand projections leaves prices highly sensitive to further military or shipping developments. markets markets markets / stocks global london global oil markets oil brent wti opec

markets-oil-105-tanker-attacks-sept10-20.excerpt: Brent gained about 4% in a Thursday midday snapshot as attacks and restricted shipping raised fears of disruption through two major energy corridors.
markets-oil-105-tanker-attacks-sept10-20.text: oil jumps to $105 as middle east tanker attacks escalate brent gained about 4% in a thursday midday snapshot as attacks and restricted shipping raised fears of disruption through two major energy corridors. oil prices climbed about 4% thursday as a surge in attacks on shipping intensified concern that supplies could be disrupted through the strait of hormuz and the red sea. at 12:15 p.m. gmt, reuters reported brent crude futures up $4.05 at $105.26 a barrel. u.s. west texas intermediate rose $3.99 to $100.04, moving above $100 for the first time since may. those figures are a dated market snapshot, not live prices. brent has risen more than 30% from early-august lows as a lasting halt to u.s.-iran attacks failed to take hold. iran-aligned houthi forces seized yemen’s port of mocha on thursday, according to military sources, adding risk near the bab el-mandeb strait while gulf traffic through hormuz remained restricted. oil prices can reverse quickly as traders reassess military events, shipping access, inventories and demand. the immediate move nevertheless matters for new england because higher crude costs can filter into gasoline, diesel and heating oil. it also complicates the inflation outlook facing central banks and consumers ahead of the northern hemisphere winter. markets markets markets / stocks intl london london, uk oil brent crude strait of hormuz energy markets

markets-oil-near-100-asia-2026.text: oil approaches $100 as asian markets open mixed brent reached its highest level since late june in early wednesday trading while regional stock indexes split between gains and losses. oil prices climbed toward $100 a barrel in early asian trading wednesday as investors continued to assess risks to energy supplies, while regional equity markets opened mixed. at 2:27 a.m. utc, reuters reported brent crude up $1.57 at $99.49 a barrel, its highest level since late june. u.s. west texas intermediate was up $1.60 at $94.63. both were heading for a fourth consecutive session of gains. these are timestamped market snapshots, not live prices. equities did not move in one direction. australia’s benchmark was down 0.3 percent, hong kong’s hang seng fell 0.6 percent and china’s csi 300 added 0.2 percent. japan’s nikkei gained 0.6 percent, south korea’s kospi rose 1.6 percent and taiwan’s market added 0.6 percent. currency markets also reflected caution: the yen traded near a seven-month high, while the euro edged higher before a european central bank decision. for northeast households and businesses, a sustained oil move can eventually affect heating fuel, transportation and shipping costs, but the early-session price alone does not determine retail prices. markets global global markets oil brent crude asian markets energy

markets-oracle-shares-ai-backlog-2026.text: oracle shares rise as ai cloud backlog adds $26 billion the friday move followed stronger results and a larger order book, easing some concern about the cost of oracle’s data-center expansion. oracle shares were up about 6% in friday trading after the company reported stronger quarterly results and a $26 billion increase in its revenue backlog, reuters reported. the reaction reflected renewed investor confidence that demand for ai cloud capacity can support the company’s large data-center buildout. oracle’s total backlog reached $664 billion. the company expects roughly half of that amount to convert into revenue over the next three years. customer prepayments and chips supplied by clients are helping fund some projects, reducing how much capital oracle must provide directly. investors are still watching financing risk. oracle expects debt to reach about $40 billion this fiscal year, while component costs, project delays and local opposition to new data centers could complicate expansion. the shares had fallen more than 21% in 2026 before friday’s move. reuters said oracle traded at about 16.9 times expected earnings, below comparable multiples for microsoft and amazon. that gap may offer room for recovery if cloud contracts become sales on schedule, but the backlog is not the same as recognized revenue. execution and funding remain central to the stock’s outlook. markets markets markets / stocks texas austin austin, texas oracle cloud computing ai infrastructure earnings stocks

markets-qatarenergy-us-lng-contracts-203.text: qatarenergy seeks u.s. lng contracts through 2031 the energy company is pursuing multiyear american supply as damaged facilities sideline about 12.8 million metric tons of annual lng capacity. qatarenergy is negotiating multiyear agreements for u.s. liquefied natural gas through 2031 as it works to replace supply capacity damaged by iranian attacks, reuters reported, citing trading and industry sources. the discussions involve major american lng producers and mark a shift from short-term spot purchases toward longer coverage. damage at qatar’s ras laffan facilities has sidelined about 12.8 million metric tons of annual lng capacity, according to the report, and repairs could take as long as five years. qatarenergy trading is seeking roughly 2 million to 3 million metric tons a year from u.s. projects, providing a potentially significant new source of demand for uncontracted american output. the negotiations matter beyond qatar because asian customers receive about 80% of its lng exports and are also examining alternative supplies. longer u.s. contracts could help qatarenergy meet existing commitments while infrastructure is repaired and shipping through the strait of hormuz remains constrained. no completed contract or transaction price was reported, so the talks represent a developing supply strategy rather than a finalized purchase. their duration nevertheless signals that the company is preparing for disruption that may persist well beyond the current spot market. markets markets markets / stocks qatar doha doha, qatar qatarenergy lng u.s. energy natural gas supply contracts

markets-rbi-tata-sons-listing-request-re.text: rbi rejection moves tata sons closer to potential public listing india’s central bank rejected the holding company’s bid to shed its non-bank lender registration, according to two sources. the reserve bank of india has rejected tata sons’ request to deregister as a non-bank lender, according to two people familiar with the decision. the outcome leaves the closely held parent of several major indian companies nearer to a possible stock-market listing. tata sons had asked to give up its classification as a core investment company. rbi rules can require non-bank lenders with assets above 1 trillion rupees, or access to public funds, to list. tata sons reported standalone assets of 1.75 trillion rupees as of march 2025. the central bank communicated its decision in a letter saturday, the sources said. the holding company controls businesses including tata consultancy services, tata motors, tata steel and air india, and has sought to remain private. listing pressure has also come from shapoorji pallonji group, its second-largest shareholder. tata trusts owns 66% of tata sons. the rbi, tata sons and tata trusts did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and no listing timetable has been announced. markets markets markets / stocks india mumbai mumbai, india tata sons reserve bank of india ipo india

markets-samsung-sk-hynix-payouts-korea-r.text: samsung and sk hynix payouts test south korea’s market reforms the chipmakers’ combined 2026 shareholder-return plans exceed 130 trillion won, but investors say governance and capital-allocation concerns remain. large shareholder-return plans from samsung electronics and sk hynix are testing south korea’s effort to narrow the longstanding valuation gap between its companies and global peers. reuters reported that the two chipmakers’ payout plans are worth more than 130 trillion won, about $97 billion, for 2026. strong demand tied to artificial intelligence has boosted cash generation and increased investor pressure for dividends and share buybacks. investors welcomed the planned distributions but said broader changes in governance, capital allocation and shareholder rights are still needed. samsung faces particular calls to put more emphasis on repurchasing shares rather than relying mainly on dividends. at the time of the reuters report, the benchmark kospi remained about 26% below the record it reached in june, even though samsung and sk hynix account for nearly half of the index’s weight. that percentage is a dated market measure, not a live quotation. the muted response illustrates why south korea’s reform program will be judged across many companies and over time, not by two large payouts alone. markets markets markets / stocks intl seoul seoul, south korea samsung sk hynix south korea shareholder returns

markets-saudi-crude-supply-three-decade-.text: iea says saudi crude supply fell to three-decade low after attacks the agency estimated august supply at 6 million barrels per day and cut its 2026 forecast as damaged routes and facilities constrained output reaching market. saudi arabia’s crude supply dropped by 2.3 million barrels per day in august to 6 million barrels per day, its lowest level in more than three decades, the international energy agency said friday. the estimate reflects oil reaching the market and domestic facilities, not simply wellhead production. the iea attributed the decline to attacks on saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes. targets included the jazan refinery, vessels near yanbu and the abqaiq processing site, while traffic through bab el-mandeb faced additional pressure from groups linked to yemen’s houthis. saudi arabia supplied a different figure to opec, reporting 7.122 million barrels per day and production of 6.238 million barrels per day in august. methodology helps explain part of the gap: supply includes exports, withdrawals from storage and crude used in domestic refineries and power plants. the iea reduced its forecast for average saudi crude supply in 2026 by 885,000 barrels per day to 7.6 million. it also estimated that monthly saudi loadings fell by 1.1 million barrels per day to 3.5 million. the figures add a verified measure of physical-market strain as traders assess damaged infrastructure and risks to multiple middle east shipping corridors. markets markets markets / stocks saudi arabia saudi arabia saudi arabia crude oil iea energy markets

markets-singapore-airlines-air-india-fun.text: singapore airlines seeks stronger terms before new air india funding sources say the 25.1% shareholder wants greater governance influence and loss-reduction commitments before providing more capital. singapore airlines plans to seek stronger governance rights and clearer loss-reduction commitments before agreeing to provide additional capital to air india, according to sources cited by reuters. air india has requested about $1.5 billion in new equity. tata sons, the controlling shareholder, has approved roughly $1.1 billion as its proportional contribution. singapore airlines owns 25.1% of the carrier but has not made a final decision on joining the funding round. the singapore carrier wants more influence over management and board oversight as it evaluates further exposure to air india’s turnaround. air india recorded a $2.33 billion loss in its last fiscal year, increasing scrutiny of the capital request. singapore airlines said investment decisions would be made with its own resources; state investor temasek would not directly fund the contribution. the talks concern potential financing and conditions, not a completed transaction. amounts, governance terms and timing could change before any agreement. no share-price claim in this report is presented as live. markets international singapore and india singapore airlines air india tata sons aviation

markets-starbucks-turnaround-sales-margi.text: starbucks sales recover while turnaround costs squeeze margins two years into brian niccol’s tenure, comparable sales are improving but operating margins remain below earlier levels. starbucks has reversed six consecutive quarters of declining comparable sales under chief executive brian niccol, but the investments supporting that recovery have narrowed operating margins, reuters reported in an analysis marking his second year in the role. comparable sales rose 7.9% in the fiscal third quarter ended june 28, the fourth consecutive quarter of improvement. starbucks has spent at least $500 million on added labor as it works to shorten waits, simplify service and restore the coffeehouse atmosphere in stores. the spending has weighed on profitability. global operating margin was 12.9% in the fiscal third quarter, down from 15.8% in the comparable period two years earlier, according to lseg data cited by reuters. north american margin fell to 13.6% from 21% across the same comparison. starbucks shares had gained about 30% since niccol’s appointment when reuters published its analysis, compared with roughly 40% for the s&p 500. those figures are point-in-time comparisons, not live prices. the next phase of the turnaround will test whether stronger traffic and sales can translate into durable profit growth while the company manages labor, store and restructuring costs. markets markets markets / stocks wa seattle seattle, wa starbucks earnings operating margin retail
