markets-uk-economy-july-growth-ai-2026.text: uk economy grows 0.4% in july as software services expand output beat forecasts for no monthly growth, while annual gdp increased at its fastest pace since february 2025. britain’s economy grew 0.4% in july, beating a reuters poll in which economists expected output to be unchanged. gross domestic product was 1.6% higher than a year earlier, the fastest annual growth rate since february 2025, according to the office for national statistics. services drove the monthly gain, with computer programming making the largest contribution. the ons said businesses connected to software development appeared to be benefiting from the artificial-intelligence investment boom. hot weather and activity related to the men’s soccer world cup also supported parts of the economy. growth across the three months through july was 0.4%, another result above expectations. the stronger reading arrives alongside competing pressures: higher oil prices and government borrowing costs could weaken demand, while firm output may make some bank of england officials more willing to consider another interest-rate increase. the report is a snapshot of completed economic activity, not a forecast. investors will now weigh whether the software-led boost can persist as energy costs filter through to households and businesses. the combination of stronger growth and inflation risk could complicate the outlook for government finances, bond markets and the central bank’s next policy decision. markets markets markets / stocks united kingdom united kingdom united kingdom gdp software bank of england

markets-uk-gilt-yields-multidecade-highs.excerpt: Ten-year borrowing costs touched levels last seen in 2007, while 20- and 30-year yields reached their highest points since 1998.
markets-uk-gilt-yields-multidecade-highs.text: uk bond yields reach multi-decade highs amid global selloff ten-year borrowing costs touched levels last seen in 2007, while 20- and 30-year yields reached their highest points since 1998. british government borrowing costs climbed to multi-decade highs thursday as rising oil prices, firm u.s. inflation data and expectations for tighter monetary policy drove a broad bond-market selloff. the 10-year gilt yield rose to 5.378%, its highest since july 2007, reuters reported. yields on 20- and 30-year debt reached 5.895% and 5.948%, respectively, their highest levels since 1998. bond yields move inversely to prices. shorter maturities also sold off. the five-year yield recorded its largest one-day increase since may 15 and reached a three-year high near 4.95%, while the two-year yield rose to its highest since october 2023. the bank of england is expected to hold rates at its next meeting, but futures markets moved toward a greater likelihood of an increase in november as energy costs added to inflation concerns. these figures describe thursday’s market levels and are not live quotes. the jump matters beyond trading desks because government yields influence mortgage pricing, corporate borrowing and the cost of servicing public debt. investors will be watching whether energy prices stabilize and whether incoming inflation data validate expectations for additional central-bank tightening. markets markets markets / stocks international london united kingdom uk gilts bond yields bank of england fixed income

markets-us-30-year-mortgage-rate-14-mont.excerpt: The average 30-year fixed rate rose to 6.85% in the latest weekly survey as refinancing and total mortgage applications declined.
markets-us-30-year-mortgage-rate-14-mont.text: u.s. 30-year mortgage rate reaches 14-month high the average 30-year fixed rate rose to 6.85% in the latest weekly survey as refinancing and total mortgage applications declined. the average rate on a u.s. 30-year fixed mortgage rose six basis points to 6.85% in the week ended september 4, the highest level since june 2025, according to mortgage bankers association data reported by reuters. higher borrowing costs weighed on demand. applications to refinance existing mortgages fell 6.2% from the previous week, while total mortgage applications declined 2.7%. the figures measure application activity and do not represent a real-time quote available to every borrower. mortgage rates often track movements in longer-term treasury yields. the 10-year treasury yield approached 4.8% tuesday, near its highest level since october 2023, as investors weighed inflation, federal borrowing and heavy demand for capital. higher oil prices and geopolitical conflict have added to inflation concerns. markets are now watching producer-price data thursday, consumer-price data friday and the federal reserve’s september 15–16 meeting. those releases may reshape expectations for monetary policy, but mortgage offers will still vary by lender, borrower credit, down payment and loan structure. markets markets markets / stocks national washington united states mortgage rates housing treasury yields federal reserve

markets-us-august-budget-deficit-167-bil.excerpt: Treasury data showed the 11-month fiscal gap holding near $1.97 trillion, already above the full-year 2025 deficit.
markets-us-august-budget-deficit-167-bil.text: u.s. august budget deficit narrows to $167 billion on timing shifts treasury data showed the 11-month fiscal gap holding near $1.97 trillion, already above the full-year 2025 deficit. the u.s. federal budget deficit narrowed to $167 billion in august, but the treasury department said the change largely reflected calendar shifts rather than an underlying improvement. medicare and social security payments normally made on august 1 were paid in july because the date fell on a saturday. after adjusting for those timing effects, the august deficit was $248 billion, $7 billion more than a year earlier. unadjusted outlays fell 24% to $527 billion, while receipts rose 5% to $360 billion. interest payments declined by $14 billion for the month because of inflation-accounting changes, even as fiscal-year-to-date interest costs remained 13% higher. the deficit for the first 11 months of the fiscal year was about $1.97 trillion, already above the $1.775 trillion gap for all of fiscal 2025. net customs receipts rose in august after tariff refunds, while year-to-date customs collections totaled $292.5 billion before $125.2 billion in refunds, according to treasury data. markets markets markets / stocks district of columbia washington washington, d.c. u.s. treasury budget deficit federal spending economy

markets-us-august-cpi-gasoline-preview-2.excerpt: Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast a 0.4% monthly CPI increase, with Friday’s report likely to shape expectations before the Federal Reserve meets.
markets-us-august-cpi-gasoline-preview-2.text: gasoline expected to lift august u.s. inflation reading economists surveyed by reuters forecast a 0.4% monthly cpi increase, with friday’s report likely to shape expectations before the federal reserve meets. higher gasoline costs are expected to push the u.s. consumer price index up more quickly in august, making friday’s inflation report an important input for markets ahead of the federal reserve’s next policy meeting. economists surveyed by reuters forecast a 0.4% monthly increase in the headline cpi and a 3.4% rise from a year earlier. core prices, which exclude food and energy, are expected to increase 0.2% for the month. those figures are forecasts, not released results. the energy information administration reported that average gasoline prices rose to $4.192 per gallon in august from $4.064 in july. fuel can affect the headline index directly and also influence transportation and distribution costs across the economy. investors will compare the official data with expectations to reassess the likely path of interest rates. a reading above forecast could reinforce concern that energy pressures are spreading, while a softer result could ease some of those fears. the federal reserve meets next week, giving the report unusual weight even though policymakers typically examine several inflation and labor indicators rather than one month in isolation. markets markets markets / stocks us united states inflation cpi gasoline federal reserve

markets-us-august-cpi-inflation-rate-hik.excerpt: The monthly CPI increase matched expectations, while a 0.3% rise in core prices reinforced expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy.
markets-us-august-cpi-inflation-rate-hik.text: august u.s. inflation rises 0.4% as rate-hike expectations strengthen the monthly cpi increase matched expectations, while a 0.3% rise in core prices reinforced expectations of tighter federal reserve policy. u.s. consumer prices rose 0.4% in august after a 0.1% increase in july, the labor department reported friday. the consumer price index was 3.4% higher than a year earlier, matching july’s annual rate and meeting economists’ expectations for the monthly change. core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3% for the month. reuters described that as the largest rise in four months, with airline fares continuing their upward trend. the report arrived one day after firm producer-price readings and strengthened the view that underlying inflation pressure persisted despite the unchanged year-over-year headline rate. investors responded by increasing expectations that the federal reserve will raise its benchmark rate at the september 15-16 policy meeting. that market pricing was a reaction recorded after the report, not a live forecast. the central bank’s target range stood at 3.50% to 3.75% when reuters published its analysis. for households and businesses, the data reinforce the possibility that borrowing costs will remain restrictive as policymakers assess energy shocks, employment conditions and whether price increases are spreading beyond fuel-related categories. markets markets markets / stocks united states washington washington, d.c. inflation consumer price index federal reserve interest rates u.s. economy

markets-us-diesel-average-six-dollars-fr.excerpt: AAA’s September 11 national average was nearly $6.06, up about 63% from a year earlier and adding pressure across freight networks.
markets-us-diesel-average-six-dollars-fr.text: u.s. diesel average tops $6 as freight costs face pressure aaa’s september 11 national average was nearly $6.06, up about 63% from a year earlier and adding pressure across freight networks. the u.s. national average for diesel rose above $6 a gallon friday, extending a record run that is increasing costs for trucking, farming and delivery networks. aaa put the average near $6.06, up from $5.85 a week earlier and about $3.71 at the same point last year. diesel prices generally track crude oil and refined-fuel markets. brent and u.s. crude both moved above $100 a barrel during the week as conflict and shipping disruptions constrained supply. diesel is particularly sensitive because it powers much of the freight system, as well as farm equipment and some public transportation. the market impact reaches beyond fuel retailers. businesses that move packages or perishable food may absorb the increase, add delivery fees or eventually pass costs into consumer prices. refrigerated products such as meat and produce can face pressure sooner because they require frequent transport and restocking. the figures are a national snapshot reported for september 11, not a live local quote; pump prices vary by state and station. the persistence of high crude and refining costs will determine how much of the diesel surge reaches broader inflation measures. markets markets markets / stocks united states chicago united states diesel freight energy markets inflation

markets-us-diesel-price-above-six-2026.excerpt: Tight inventories and disruptions linked to the Iran war and attacks on Russian refineries have pushed freight fuel costs sharply higher.
markets-us-diesel-price-above-six-2026.text: u.s. average diesel price crosses $6, gasbuddy reports tight inventories and disruptions linked to the iran war and attacks on russian refineries have pushed freight fuel costs sharply higher. the average u.s. diesel price moved above $6 a gallon thursday for the first time, according to fuel-tracking service gasbuddy, intensifying pressure on freight operators and supply chains. gasbuddy said the national average was roughly $2.30 higher than a year earlier. the increase has followed supply disruptions tied to the iran war and ukrainian attacks on russian refineries, both of which have tightened availability of the middle distillates used in trucking and industrial activity. u.s. diesel inventories stood at 106.3 million barrels, about 13% below the five-year average, energy information administration data showed. crude prices also remained elevated thursday: brent settled at $107.63 a barrel and u.s. west texas intermediate at $102.48, reuters reported. diesel costs matter beyond the pump because they feed into shipping, agriculture and construction expenses. the reported national average is a broad benchmark and local prices can differ substantially by taxes and supply conditions. with inventories below normal, businesses and inflation watchers will be focused on whether refinery output and international flows can rebuild stocks. markets markets markets / stocks united states washington washington, dc diesel fuel prices inflation freight

markets-us-equity-fund-outflows-nine-mon.excerpt: Investors withdrew $32.27 billion in the week through September 9 as oil-driven inflation fears lifted expectations for higher rates.
markets-us-equity-fund-outflows-nine-mon.text: u.s. equity funds record largest outflow in nine months investors withdrew $32.27 billion in the week through september 9 as oil-driven inflation fears lifted expectations for higher rates. investors pulled a net $32.27 billion from u.s. equity funds in the week through september 9, the largest weekly withdrawal in nine months, according to lseg lipper data reported by reuters. rising oil prices and persistent inflation readings increased concern that interest rates could move higher. large-cap funds accounted for a record $40.44 billion in outflows, while mid-cap products lost $682 million. the pattern was not uniform: multi-cap funds attracted $3.52 billion and small-cap funds added $274 million. sector funds also received a combined $1.46 billion, led by $1.71 billion for technology strategies. money also moved toward fixed income. u.s. bond funds collected $6.56 billion, extending their inflow streak to 21 weeks, with demand concentrated in short-to-intermediate investment-grade and government or treasury products. money-market funds, however, recorded $10.41 billion in withdrawals after a much larger intake the week before. the report captures completed weekly flows rather than real-time market positioning. it nevertheless shows investors reducing broad equity exposure while selectively adding technology and bonds. upcoming inflation data and the federal reserve’s next decision could determine whether that defensive shift persists. markets markets markets / stocks united states united states u.s. equity funds fund flows inflation oil prices bond funds

markets-us-final-solar-import-duties-asi.excerpt: Solar imports from India, Indonesia and Laos face triple-digit rates in some cases, pending a final U.S. injury determination.
markets-us-final-solar-import-duties-asi.text: u.s. finalizes steep duties on asian solar imports solar imports from india, indonesia and laos face triple-digit rates in some cases, pending a final u.s. injury determination. the u.s. commerce department has finalized steep antidumping and countervailing duties on solar cells and panels imported from india, indonesia and laos. the decision advances a trade case brought by an alliance of domestic manufacturers that includes first solar, hanwha qcells and mission solar. final antidumping margins were set at 123.04% for india, 94.36% for indonesia and 65.43% for laos. countervailing-duty rates were 126.09% for india, ranged from 73.2% to 173.7% for indonesia, and ranged from 82.03% to 153.67% for laos. the rates address separate findings on below-market pricing and government subsidies, and actual importer liability can vary by company and product. the case now moves to the u.s. international trade commission, which is expected to make a final injury determination by october 14. if the commission finds that the imports harmed or threatened domestic producers, formal duty orders would follow in november. the outcome could alter sourcing costs and project planning across the u.s. solar industry, balancing domestic manufacturing goals against developers’ need for competitively priced equipment. no final orders take effect unless the injury finding is affirmative. markets markets markets / stocks district of columbia washington washington, d.c. solar energy trade tariffs manufacturing

markets-us-treasury-long-dated-buyback-2.excerpt: The department plans to purchase up to $6 billion of older 10- to 20-year securities on September 10 to support market liquidity.
markets-us-treasury-long-dated-buyback-2.text: u.s. treasury triples size of long-dated bond buyback the department plans to purchase up to $6 billion of older 10- to 20-year securities on september 10 to support market liquidity. the u.s. treasury said it will buy up to $6 billion of 10- to 20-year government bonds on thursday, september 10, tripling the size of its previous long-dated buyback operation. treasury buybacks generally target older, less liquid securities and are intended to support smoother trading rather than change the government’s overall borrowing needs. the department said last month that it planned to at least double longer-dated purchases to $4 billion during the quarter. the larger operation follows a bond selloff that pushed 30-year yields to their highest level since 2007. benchmark 10-year yields rose after wednesday’s announcement and reached 4.8528%, their highest level since november 2023, according to reuters. some market participants had expected a still larger purchase, which helps explain why yields moved higher despite the increased buyback. the operation’s results will offer a clearer measure of demand and liquidity when treasury executes the purchases thursday. the announcement was released wednesday. markets markets markets / stocks dc washington washington, dc u.s. treasury bonds buybacks market liquidity

markets-verizon-corning-fiber-deal-2026.text: verizon signs multibillion-dollar fiber deal with corning corning will supply more than 80 million miles of high-density optical fiber from 2027 through 2032 for broadband and ai infrastructure. verizon signed a multibillion-dollar agreement with corning for high-density optical fiber and connectivity products, extending a supplier relationship that has lasted about three decades. reuters reported that corning will provide more than 80 million miles of fiber between 2027 and 2032. verizon said the equipment will support broadband expansion for homes and businesses and add capacity for large ai computing customers that need fast, low-latency connections. the companies described the agreement as multibillion-dollar but did not disclose exact financial terms. that limits how precisely investors can estimate revenue timing, margins or capital requirements from the announcement alone. the deal illustrates how ai spending is expanding beyond processors and data centers into the networks connecting them. for corning, it provides a long-duration customer commitment; for verizon, it secures supply for planned construction. the ultimate financial effect will depend on deployment pace, customer demand and execution over several years. no stock price in this report should be treated as a live quote. markets us united states verizon corning fiber broadband

markets-wall-street-ai-selloff-nvidia-ch.text: wall street slides as ai anxiety pressures nvidia and chip stocks u.s. stocks were lower in a midday snapshot as nvidia and several semiconductor names fell amid renewed concern about the pace and payoff of ai investment. u.s. stocks were lower in midday trading monday as concerns about artificial-intelligence spending weighed on technology shares, reuters reported. at 11:40 a.m. eastern, the dow jones industrial average was down 0.23%, the s&p 500 had fallen 0.42% and the nasdaq composite was down 0.44%. nvidia was down about 3%, while amazon fell more than 1%. intel, amd and marvell were each down roughly 5% to 6% in the snapshot. the moves showed how quickly investor expectations around ai demand and competition can spread across both chipmakers and the large companies buying or building ai capacity. oil prices were also higher in the report, adding another variable for investors to weigh. the figures are a mid-session reading from reuters and are not closing prices or a live quote after publication; markets can move materially before the trading day ends. the session’s direction was not a final verdict on the technology sector, but it showed how concentrated ai exposure can amplify a market pullback. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york wall street, new york wall street nvidia semiconductor stocks ai investing

markets-wall-street-futures-oil-100-sept.text: wall street futures hold near flat as oil shock tests risk appetite early wednesday futures were subdued after brent briefly topped $100, with investors also awaiting inflation data and a treasury buyback announcement. u.s. stock-index futures were subdued early wednesday as investors weighed a renewed oil shock against modest strength in semiconductor shares. at 5:05 a.m. eastern, reuters reported dow futures down 0.16%, s&p 500 futures flat and nasdaq 100 futures up 0.04%. brent crude had briefly crossed $100 a barrel before trading near $99.94, keeping attention on the inflation effects of the widening middle east conflict. qualcomm, arm and nvidia gained between 0.16% and 1.73% in premarket trading, offering some support to technology benchmarks. investors were also waiting for u.s. inflation data later in the week and a treasury announcement about bond buybacks. the figures are time-stamped premarket indications, not live prices or closing levels, and can change quickly after trading begins. the setup shows competing pressures: enthusiasm for ai-linked companies remains a source of demand, while higher energy costs and expectations for tighter monetary policy can weigh on valuations across the broader market. markets markets markets / stocks us new york new york, new york wall street stock futures oil prices inflation

markets-wall-street-rises-august-inflati.text: wall street rises as oil retreats despite hotter inflation major u.s. indexes gained friday morning after august consumer prices rose 0.4%, while crude futures pulled back. u.s. stocks rose friday morning even after government data showed consumer inflation accelerated in august. at 9:38 a.m. eastern time, reuters reported the dow up 1.23%, the s&p 500 ahead 1.05% and the nasdaq composite gaining 1.08%. the consumer price index increased 0.4% in august after a 0.1% rise in july. prices were up 3.4% from a year earlier, matching july’s annual rate. the report pushed traders toward higher expectations for a federal reserve rate increase, according to futures-market pricing cited by reuters. energy offered some relief to risk sentiment. brent crude futures fell more than 3%, though they remained above $104 a barrel at the time of the report, while u.s. crude hovered near $100. elevated oil and treasury yields had weighed on markets earlier in the week. all 11 major s&p 500 sectors were positive in early trading, led by technology. the figures are a timestamped market snapshot rather than closing prices. investors still face uncertainty over inflation, monetary policy and middle east supply risks as they assess whether the friday rebound can hold through the session. markets markets markets / stocks new york new york new york, new york wall street consumer prices federal reserve oil stocks

markets-yen-carry-trade-pressure-2026.excerpt: Expectations for Bank of Japan tightening are narrowing the advantage of borrowing cheaply in yen to buy higher-yielding assets.
markets-yen-carry-trade-pressure-2026.text: stronger yen puts carry trade under renewed pressure expectations for bank of japan tightening are narrowing the advantage of borrowing cheaply in yen to buy higher-yielding assets. the japanese yen’s advance toward a seven-month high is putting renewed pressure on a long-running strategy used across global markets: the yen carry trade. in a carry trade, investors borrow in a currency with relatively low interest rates and invest the proceeds in higher-yielding currencies or assets. the approach benefited from japan’s years of very easy monetary policy, especially when u.s. rates rose sharply in 2022 and 2023. that advantage can shrink when the yen strengthens or japanese borrowing costs rise. markets now expect the bank of japan may tighten policy, raising the risk that investors must unwind leveraged positions. reuters reported yen-based cross-border borrowing reached a record 360 trillion yen in march, though the full size of carry trades is difficult to measure. the current adjustment appears more anticipated than the abrupt 2024 unwind, but currency and rate moves can still transmit volatility across stocks, bonds and emerging markets. the figures describe reported positioning and delayed market conditions, not a live quote or investment recommendation. markets international tokyo, japan japanese yen carry trade bank of japan currencies

massachusetts-boston-schools-return-2026.excerpt: Boston Public Schools welcomed students Tuesday as the district began a new year with a fully district-run elementary school and a renewed focus on bus reliability.
massachusetts-boston-schools-return-2026.text: 46,000 boston students return as schools start new year boston public schools welcomed students tuesday as the district began a new year with a fully district-run elementary school and a renewed focus on bus reliability. about 46,000 boston public schools students returned to classrooms tuesday, with mayor michelle wu and superintendent mary skipper welcoming families at holland elementary, boston 25 news reported. the school year begins with the elementary school fully under district control after boston exited state receivership. district leaders are also watching transportation closely as hundreds of buses resume daily service across the city. boston public schools is using gps tracking through its zoom system to monitor buses and student transportation. skipper said the district is aiming for a 95% on-time bus success rate as routes settle into the new year. the district also said about 15,000 students took part in summer learning programs. for families, the first days of school will provide the clearest test of whether the transportation changes and operational planning translate into reliable arrival and dismissal times. the opening-day rollout also gives families a near-term measure of how well the district’s transportation technology and staffing plans are working. new-england massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, ma massachusetts boston schools education

massachusetts-heat-resilience-officer-20.excerpt: The state is among the first to build a dedicated government response around a hazard that often causes serious health risks without obvious property damage.
massachusetts-heat-resilience-officer-20.text: massachusetts’ new heat-resilience role puts extreme heat on state agenda the state is among the first to build a dedicated government response around a hazard that often causes serious health risks without obvious property damage. massachusetts is building a new government response to extreme heat, a hazard that can strain public health, schools and workplaces even when it leaves little visible damage, axios reported tuesday. the state announced in august that it had become the first on the east coast to appoint a heat resilience officer, following arizona. the role reflects a broader shift as states write heat plans, add worker protections and invest in cooling infrastructure. axios reported that massachusetts’ early goals include reducing heat-related school closures, improving workplace safety and expanding urban greenery. those efforts put more emphasis on preparation before dangerous conditions arrive, rather than treating heat only as a weather forecast. the policy question is how the state will turn a new position into measurable local support. that could include coordination with cities, employers, public-health agencies and schools as hotter periods become a more regular planning concern. it also raises practical questions about who receives warnings, cooling help and workplace guidance when temperatures become dangerous. new-england massachusetts massachusetts ma massachusetts massachusetts extreme heat climate public health

massachusetts-mistrial-mental-health.text: massachusetts mistrial keeps postpartum-psychosis debate in view a judge declared a mistrial after jurors deadlocked in the case, while the defense argued that severe mental illness should shape how responsibility is understood. a massachusetts case ended in a mistrial after jurors could not reach a verdict, leaving a high-profile debate over postpartum psychosis and criminal responsibility unresolved. the guardian reported that the defense argued the defendant was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time of the deaths of her three children. expert testimony presented during the trial addressed the role of severe mental illness. a mistrial is not an acquittal or a conviction. the court’s decision means the case remains unresolved and any next steps will depend on the prosecution and the court. the case has renewed discussion about maternal mental-health treatment, crisis support and how courts evaluate psychiatric evidence. this summary avoids graphic detail while the legal process continues. more ma massachusetts massachusetts courts mental health public safety

massachusetts-quabbin-water-request-2026.excerpt: A request for up to 20 million additional gallons a day is prompting questions about which communities need the supply and what alternatives were considered.
massachusetts-quabbin-water-request-2026.text: eastern massachusetts seeks more quabbin water as review begins a request for up to 20 million additional gallons a day is prompting questions about which communities need the supply and what alternatives were considered. eastern massachusetts officials are seeking as much as 20 million more gallons of water each day from the quabbin reservoir, a proposal that is now moving through the state’s interbasin-transfer review process. the quabbin is a primary source for the massachusetts water resources authority system and supplies drinking water to roughly 2.7 million people. state law requires an application to explain which communities will receive the water, why it is needed and whether other options were examined. new england public media reported that state rep. aaron saunders questioned whether those answers are fully spelled out in the current application. the review places long-term growth, water demand and reservoir protection in the same public debate. the reservoir covers roughly 39 square miles and is protected as an unfiltered drinking-water source. any decision will therefore involve more than capacity: it will also require officials to explain how additional withdrawals fit with conservation and watershed protections. new-england massachusetts massachusetts ma belchertown eastern and western massachusetts massachusetts quabbin reservoir water supply mwra infrastructure

massachusetts-umass-boston-chancellor-20.excerpt: Marcelo Suárez-Orozco will leave the post after seven years, closing a tenure that included campus growth and a major capital overhaul.
massachusetts-umass-boston-chancellor-20.text: umass boston chancellor plans to step down in february marcelo suárez-orozco will leave the post after seven years, closing a tenure that included campus growth and a major capital overhaul. umass boston chancellor marcelo suárez-orozco plans to step down feb. 1 after seven years leading the university, wbur reported. he took the job as the covid-19 pandemic began reshaping higher education. suárez-orozco, who is nearing 70, said he wants to make room for the next generation of university leaders. he also plans to refocus on climate-resilience work and the ethical use of technology, including artificial intelligence. during his tenure, umass boston rose in national research-university rankings and earned top-tier research status from the carnegie foundation in 2025. the campus also moved through a long-delayed $293 million overhaul of facilities first opened in 1974. the coming leadership transition will arrive as universities balance research ambitions, capital needs and pressure to show students a clear return on the cost of attendance. umass boston has not yet announced a successor in the report. the university will now face the familiar challenge of preserving that momentum while choosing a leader for its next chapter. new-england massachusetts massachusetts ma boston boston, ma massachusetts boston higher education umass boston

me-casco-bay-clam-closures-algal-bloom-2.text: maine closes casco bay clam flats after bloom-linked die-off emergency harvesting closures cover parts of maquoit and middle bays after severe stress and mortality among soft-shell clams; brunswick says the bloom is a marine-life concern, not a shellfish-consumption toxin warning. maine regulators have closed shellfish harvesting in parts of maquoit bay and middle bay after local committees reported a die-off of soft-shell clams linked to a spreading phytoplankton bloom. maine public reported that the department of marine resources ordered the closures in brunswick and harpswell after monitoring the affected areas. brunswick officials said they had been tracking the karenia mikimotoi bloom in casco bay since early september and observed stressed or dying clams in several locations. the town says the species does not produce the kind of toxin that threatens people who eat shellfish; at high concentrations, it can harm marine organisms and contribute to low oxygen in the water. in brunswick, officials reported that about 80% of adult clams in affected areas showed extreme stress, were dying or were already dead, according to maine public’s account of the department’s findings. the town had initially asked harvesters to avoid visibly affected flats while it assessed conditions; state closures now prohibit harvesting in designated areas. the closures carry economic weight for the coastal communities. brunswick was maine’s largest soft-shell clam port in 2025, with nearly $1.8 million in reported landings, maine public said, citing state records. harvesters should check maine’s department of marine resources closure notices for the current boundaries and status before digging. new-england new-england new england me casco bay, maine maine casco bay shellfish algal bloom brunswick harpswell

me-cmmc-nurses-union-firings-2026-09-20.excerpt: The Lewiston hospital says the employment actions followed documented policy and patient-care violations, while nurses and labor advocates say the discipline is retaliation for organizing.
me-cmmc-nurses-union-firings-2026-09-20.text: central maine medical center fires or suspends 20 nurses amid union drive the lewiston hospital says the employment actions followed documented policy and patient-care violations, while nurses and labor advocates say the discipline is retaliation for organizing. central maine medical center has fired or suspended 20 nurses as employees prepare to vote on whether to unionize, escalating a dispute over staffing and patient care at the lewiston hospital, according to maine public and local reporting. at least 15 nurses had been fired and five remained suspended as of friday, a hospital spokesperson told centralmaine.com. the hospital said the actions were based on documented violations of established policies and standards, including alleged patient abandonment, timekeeping violations and conduct it said interfered with patient care or safety. the maine state nurses association and other labor advocates have characterized the discipline as retaliation for the organizing effort. prime healthcare, which owns cmmc through its nonprofit foundation, has denied targeting employees because of union activity and said its focus is patient safety and care-team support. cmmc nurses filed for a union election in august and have raised concerns about staffing, equipment and basic supplies. the vote is scheduled for sept. 24, according to centralmaine.com. new-england new-england new england me lewiston lewiston, maine maine lewiston central maine medical center health care labor

me-eviction-prevention-program-reopens-2.excerpt: Eligible renters who are behind on payments can seek help with past-due rent and up to 12 months of future assistance, but funding is limited.
me-eviction-prevention-program-reopens-2.text: maine reopens eviction-prevention program with $11 million in aid eligible renters who are behind on payments can seek help with past-due rent and up to 12 months of future assistance, but funding is limited. maine reopened applications monday for a statewide eviction-prevention program funded with $11 million from the state budget. mainehousing says the program is intended for renters who are behind on rent and at risk of losing their homes. households may qualify if their income is no more than 60% of the area median income and their rent meets program limits. assistance can cover rent owed to a current landlord and, after the overdue balance is addressed, as much as 12 months of additional rental support, with total help capped at $9,600 per household. applications will be prioritized for eligible households that have received a court summons related to eviction, followed by those with an eviction notice for nonpayment and applicants who spend more than 30% of their income on rent. complete applications are then reviewed in the order they are received, and mainehousing warns that available funds may run out. mainehousing is administering the program with project home, which handles application review and communication with tenants and landlords. maine public reported that a prior pilot served about 1,300 households and that the new program is expected to draw heavy demand; applications are available through mainehousing online, by phone or with paper assistance from project home. new-england new-england new england me augusta maine maine housing eviction prevention rental assistance mainehousing

me-ice-fifth-cumberland-corrections-offi.excerpt: Maine Public reports that Dannick Massamba-Bankela was detained during a scheduled appointment in Scarborough; his lawyer says he has a pending asylum claim and no criminal record.
me-ice-fifth-cumberland-corrections-offi.text: ice detains fifth cumberland county corrections officer in under two years maine public reports that dannick massamba-bankela was detained during a scheduled appointment in scarborough; his lawyer says he has a pending asylum claim and no criminal record. immigration and customs enforcement detained another cumberland county jail corrections officer tuesday, the fifth officer detained in less than two years, according to maine public. the officer was identified as dannick massamba-bankela. massamba-bankela arrived at ice’s scarborough field office with his lawyer for a scheduled appointment after supporters learned he had been told to return to the office. volunteers gathered outside to help his family and connect them with legal and financial support, maine public reported. his lawyer said massamba-bankela is originally from the republic of the congo, entered the united states on a visa, has a pending asylum claim and has work authorization. she also said he has no criminal record. those details were provided by his lawyer and were not independently verified in the report. the lawyer said ice agents told her massamba-bankela was being detained for overstaying a visa. an ice spokesperson did not immediately respond to maine public’s request for comment. the detention adds to a series of cases involving cumberland county corrections staff as immigration enforcement expands in maine. new-england new-england new england me scarborough scarborough and cumberland county, maine maine cumberland county cumberland county jail ice immigration scarborough asylum

me-mount-desert-grandchildren-submerged-.excerpt: A 61-year-old Mount Desert woman and her two young grandchildren were recovered Sunday from a vehicle in Roque Bluffs’ Pond Cove. The cause and manner of death remain under investigation.
me-mount-desert-grandchildren-submerged-.text: maine state police investigate deaths of woman and two children found in submerged vehicle a 61-year-old mount desert woman and her two young grandchildren were recovered sunday from a vehicle in roque bluffs’ pond cove. the cause and manner of death remain under investigation. maine state police are investigating the deaths of a mount desert woman and her two grandchildren after their vehicle was found submerged sunday morning in pond cove in roque bluffs. the victims were identified as 61-year-old sharon bukulmez of mount desert and her grandchildren, 5-year-old kinsley grubb and 3-year-old sawyer grubb, both of bar harbor, according to police information reported by the bangor daily news. police said the three had been traveling to machias after leaving a family gathering in jonesboro on saturday night and did not arrive as expected. bar harbor police used location information from bukulmez’s cellphone to identify an area near the boat ramp at the end of schoppee point road. maine state police, the state police dive team and maine marine patrol located the vehicle at about 7 a.m. and recovered the three bodies, police said. the washington county sheriff’s office and coast guard also assisted. the bodies were taken to the office of chief medical examiner in augusta for autopsies, which will help determine the cause and manner of death. police said the circumstances remain under investigation and released no additional details. new-england new-england new england me roque bluffs roque bluffs, maine maine roque bluffs mount desert washington county public safety

me-umaine-fy28-budget-layoffs-faculty-re.excerpt: The university says a projected $19 million structural shortfall is forcing personnel reductions, though details and timing are still being developed.
me-umaine-fy28-budget-layoffs-faculty-re.text: umaine says fy28 budget gap will require layoffs and faculty retrenchments the university says a projected $19 million structural shortfall is forcing personnel reductions, though details and timing are still being developed. the university of maine says it will need strategic staff layoffs and faculty retrenchments as it prepares an fy28 budget facing a projected $19 million structural gap. president joan ferrini-mundy announced the decision in a sept. 17 message to employees. the university said operating costs have grown faster than state support and tuition revenue, while enrollment pressure and changes to federal research funding and financial aid have added uncertainty. leaders said reserves and one-time savings have largely been used to limit the effect on positions in earlier budget cycles. academic affairs, which the university said represents about half of umaine’s budget, has committed to reducing its fy28 base expenses by $10 million. the plan includes permanently eliminating about one-fifth of vacant positions, reducing overload teaching and other instructional budgets, and consolidating some course sections. umaine said the remaining $5.7 million gap in academic affairs could require additional layoffs and faculty retrenchments if other savings or new revenue do not materialize. more proposals are still being developed across the university, with a budget town hall planned for october. new-england new-england new england me orono university of maine, orono, maine maine university of maine higher education jobs budgets

misc-49ers-rams-first-nfl-australia-game.excerpt: Brock Purdy threw three touchdown passes before 100,021 fans at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in the league’s landmark Australian debut.
misc-49ers-rams-first-nfl-australia-game.text: 49ers beat rams 27-7 in first nfl regular-season game in australia brock purdy threw three touchdown passes before 100,021 fans at the melbourne cricket ground in the league’s landmark australian debut. the san francisco 49ers defeated the los angeles rams 27-7 at the melbourne cricket ground, winning the first nfl regular-season game played in australia before a crowd of 100,021. quarterback brock purdy threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns as san francisco controlled the game. los angeles quarterback matthew stafford did not throw a touchdown and was removed late with the outcome out of reach. the teams took different approaches to the long trip. the 49ers arrived in australia about a week before kickoff, while the rams landed the day before the game. san francisco’s performance will add to discussion over travel timing and preparation for future international fixtures, though one result does not settle the issue. for the league, the attendance and setting provided a high-profile launch in a market long targeted for expansion of the international schedule. the mcg is better known for australian rules football and cricket, but its capacity allowed the nfl to stage a large-scale showcase. the game also carried normal standings consequences, distinguishing it from previous exhibitions held in the region. more misc misc. australia melbourne melbourne, australia san francisco 49ers los angeles rams nfl australia

misc-aaron-judge-yankees-return-2026.excerpt: The New York captain started in right field Tuesday after recovering from a stress fracture in his right first rib.
misc-aaron-judge-yankees-return-2026.text: aaron judge returns to yankees lineup after 84-game absence the new york captain started in right field tuesday after recovering from a stress fracture in his right first rib. aaron judge returned to the new york yankees lineup tuesday night after an 84-game absence, starting in right field and batting third against the colorado rockies. the yankees reinstated their captain from the 60-day injured list on monday. judge had not played since may 31 because of a stress fracture in his right first rib. the injury, which he believes occurred on a diving play in late april, was initially diagnosed as a bone bruise before later scans showed the fracture. judge resumed playing catch in mid-august after earlier running and light baseball work. he returned without a minor-league rehabilitation assignment. before the injury, the three-time american league most valuable player was batting .248 with 17 home runs and 38 rbis in 59 games. his return comes during a tight american league east race. entering tuesday, new york was 81-62, four games behind tampa bay and two ahead of boston. those standings are a dated pregame snapshot, not live results. the immediate question is how quickly judge can regain game timing after missing most of the summer. more ny new york, new york aaron judge new york yankees mlb baseball

misc-aj-brown-week-two-ankle-status-2026.excerpt: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said the receiver needs additional testing after leaving New England’s season-opening loss in Seattle.
misc-aj-brown-week-two-ankle-status-2026.text: a.j. brown’s week 2 status uncertain after ankle injury patriots coach mike vrabel said the receiver needs additional testing after leaving new england’s season-opening loss in seattle. new england patriots receiver a.j. brown will undergo additional evaluation after injuring an ankle in the season opener, leaving his availability for week 2 uncertain. coach mike vrabel said thursday that the team needed more test results before deciding whether brown could play in new england’s next game. brown was hurt early in the third quarter of the patriots’ 13-10 loss at seattle on wednesday and did not return. brown finished the opener with three receptions for 26 yards. his exit reduced the options available to quarterback drake maye as seattle erased new england’s early lead and completed its fourth-quarter comeback. the patriots’ offense will now prepare with multiple contingencies while brown’s recovery is assessed. new england is scheduled to host pittsburgh on september 20. the longer-than-usual gap following the wednesday opener gives brown additional treatment and recovery time, but the team had not announced a firm practice or game status in the source report. injury designations later in the preparation week should provide a clearer indication of whether he can return. more misc misc. massachusetts foxborough foxborough, ma new england patriots a.j. brown nfl injury

misc-angels-red-sox-series-fenway-2026.excerpt: Zach Neto’s three-run homer helped Los Angeles win 6-4 at Fenway Park and take two of three from Boston.
misc-angels-red-sox-series-fenway-2026.text: angels beat red sox 6-4 to claim series at fenway zach neto’s three-run homer helped los angeles win 6-4 at fenway park and take two of three from boston. zach neto hit a three-run homer over the green monster as the los angeles angels beat the boston red sox 6-4 wednesday night at fenway park to win the three-game series. jose siri added a two-run homer and denzer guzman hit a solo shot for los angeles, which won consecutive games for the first time since mid-august. the angels built a 6-0 lead and secured their first road-series victory since taking two of three from houston in august. boston’s comeback included a two-run homer by roman anthony and a solo homer from wilyer abreu. starter jake bennett allowed a season-high six runs, including five in one inning, on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings. ben joyce recorded the final three outs for his fourth save despite allowing a run. the red sox won monday’s opener but dropped the final two games. boston still took the season series 4-2. the club begins a three-game home series friday against kansas city, with right-hander sonny gray scheduled to start. more misc misc. ma boston boston, ma boston red sox los angeles angels fenway park mlb

misc-anthony-volpe-yankees-rockies-grand.excerpt: Volpe drove in a career-high five runs in his first game back with New York, powering a six-run seventh inning in a 10-3 win.
misc-anthony-volpe-yankees-rockies-grand.text: anthony volpe returns with grand slam as yankees sweep rockies volpe drove in a career-high five runs in his first game back with new york, powering a six-run seventh inning in a 10-3 win. anthony volpe marked his return to the new york yankees with three hits and a grand slam, driving in a career-high five runs in a 10-3 victory over the visiting colorado rockies. volpe’s slam highlighted a six-run seventh inning that broke the game open. it was his first major-league appearance since george lombard jr. replaced him at shortstop in early august. new york recalled volpe to play second base while jazz chisholm jr. recovers from a strained right thumb. luis garcia jr. also hit a two-run homer and reached 30 home runs for the first time in his career. the yankees completed a three-game sweep and won for the eighth time in 11 games, while colorado absorbed its 10th loss in 13. the result moved new york within three games of the tampa bay rays in the american league east and opened a 4½-game lead over boston for the league’s top wild-card position. volpe’s immediate production gives the yankees another lineup option as they manage chisholm’s absence and pursue both the division and postseason seeding. more misc misc. ny new york new york new york yankees anthony volpe baseball mlb

misc-arsenal-perfect-premier-league-star.excerpt: David Raya saved a penalty before Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka scored to give the defending champions 12 points from four matches.
misc-arsenal-perfect-premier-league-star.text: arsenal stays perfect with 2-0 win at sunderland david raya saved a penalty before bruno guimaraes and bukayo saka scored to give the defending champions 12 points from four matches. defending premier league champion arsenal maintained a perfect start saturday with a 2-0 victory at sunderland, moving to 12 points from four matches. goalkeeper david raya changed the match by saving enzo le fee’s penalty in the 55th minute, and arsenal took the lead two minutes later. bruno guimaraes scored his first arsenal goal with a curling finish after coming on as a substitute. bukayo saka added a penalty deep into stoppage time after reinildo mandava received a second yellow card for the foul. sunderland challenged the leaders for long stretches but could not convert its clearest opportunity. the result separated arsenal from several expected title rivals. liverpool drew 0-0 with fulham, its third draw in four league matches, while chelsea needed a second-half equalizer to draw hull city 2-2. nottingham forest won 2-1 at aston villa, and ipswich edged 10-man crystal palace 3-2 in the day’s other notable results. more misc misc. england sunderland sunderland, england arsenal sunderland premier league soccer

misc-artemis-ii-wiseman-glover-retire-20.excerpt: Commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover will continue supporting NASA’s lunar program as emeritus astronauts after April’s record-setting moon flight.
misc-artemis-ii-wiseman-glover-retire-20.text: artemis ii leaders step away from active astronaut duty commander reid wiseman and pilot victor glover will continue supporting nasa’s lunar program as emeritus astronauts after april’s record-setting moon flight. nasa astronauts reid wiseman and victor glover, who commanded and piloted the artemis ii flight around the moon in april, are stepping away from active astronaut duty. nasa said both will remain connected to the lunar exploration program as emeritus astronauts. in that role, they will volunteer time to train and mentor agency workers and share lessons from the mission with teams preparing for future flights. glover has taken a leadership position at california polytechnic state university, where he is expected to help shape long-term strategy and encourage students in science and engineering. wiseman’s next plans were not disclosed; his status change is scheduled to take effect during september. artemis ii carried wiseman, glover, nasa astronaut christina koch and canadian astronaut jeremy hansen around the moon, setting a new human distance record. hansen retired from the canadian space agency in july, leaving koch as the only crew member still on an active astronaut roster. wiseman previously spent more than five months aboard the international space station and served as nasa’s chief astronaut. glover flew a nearly six-month spacex mission to the station before artemis ii. their new emeritus roles are intended to preserve that operational experience for nasa’s continuing moon program. more misc misc. us cape canaveral cape canaveral, fl artemis ii reid wiseman victor glover nasa

misc-aspinall-ufc-title-eye-injury-2026-.excerpt: The British fighter says ongoing complications and another accident made him relinquish the title, but he is not retiring.
misc-aspinall-ufc-title-eye-injury-2026-.text: tom aspinall gives up ufc heavyweight belt while recovering from eye injury the british fighter says ongoing complications and another accident made him relinquish the title, but he is not retiring. ufc heavyweight champion tom aspinall has vacated his title while recovering from complications tied to an eye injury, the british fighter said monday, according to reuters. aspinall underwent multiple surgeries after eye injuries during his title defense against ciryl gane in abu dhabi last october. that bout was ruled a first-round no contest after he could not continue. the 33-year-old said he decided to give up the belt rather than hold up the division. he had agreed to a fight date and resumed sparring before another accident caused additional damage to his right eye, reuters reported. the move clears the way for gane, who won an interim heavyweight title by beating alex pereira in june, to be elevated to undisputed champion. ufc officials had not announced a new fight date for aspinall. aspinall said he is not retiring and hopes to return after he is healthy and medically cleared. his departure leaves the division with a new champion while his recovery timeline remains uncertain. more more misc. united kingdom manchester united kingdom misc. ufc sports tom aspinall

misc-barry-melrose-dies-70-2026.excerpt: The longtime broadcaster, known for an unmistakable style and direct analysis, spent 27 years covering hockey for ESPN.
misc-barry-melrose-dies-70-2026.text: former nhl coach and espn analyst barry melrose dies at 70 the longtime broadcaster, known for an unmistakable style and direct analysis, spent 27 years covering hockey for espn. barry melrose, a former nhl player and coach who became one of espn’s most recognizable hockey analysts, died wednesday at age 70, the network announced. melrose spent 27 years with espn and became known for direct commentary, deep familiarity with the sport and a distinctive on-air appearance. he left the network in 2023 after being diagnosed with parkinson’s disease. before broadcasting, melrose coached the los angeles kings for more than two seasons and led the wayne gretzky-captained team to the 1993 stanley cup final. a brief later stint with the tampa bay lightning brought his nhl head-coaching record to 84-108-29-4. the saskatchewan native also played nine professional seasons as a defenseman. he appeared in the world hockey association with cincinnati and later played 300 nhl games for winnipeg, toronto and detroit. espn described him as a foundational figure in its hockey coverage. his death is significant across the sport, including in new england, where espn’s bristol studios helped make his analysis a familiar part of national nhl broadcasts. more misc misc. us bristol bristol, ct barry melrose nhl espn hockey

misc-bayeux-tapestry-london-exhibition-2.excerpt: The nearly 1,000-year-old embroidery left France for the first time since the 11th century and will remain at the British Museum for 10 months.
misc-bayeux-tapestry-london-exhibition-2.text: bayeux tapestry opens sold-out london exhibition the nearly 1,000-year-old embroidery left france for the first time since the 11th century and will remain at the british museum for 10 months. the british museum opened its sold-out bayeux tapestry exhibition to the public thursday, giving visitors in london a close view of the nearly 1,000-year-old embroidery. the work has left france for the first time since the 11th century and is scheduled to remain at the museum for 10 months. its stitched scenes depict the norman invasion of england in 1066 and the events surrounding the battle of hastings, making it one of europe’s best-known visual historical records. the 70-meter tapestry is displayed in a purpose-built glass case. ticket holders receive 40 minutes on an elevated platform before moving closer to examine the stitching. the museum’s arrangement is designed to show both the full narrative sequence and small details that are difficult to appreciate in reproductions. demand exhausted the available tickets before the public opening, and the exhibition has generated widespread attention across britain. the loan is unusual because of the tapestry’s age, fragility and national significance in france. its extended london stay gives scholars and museum visitors a rare chance to study the object outside its longtime home in bayeux. more misc misc. international london london, united kingdom bayeux tapestry british museum history london

misc-be-brave-ai-documentary-venice-2026.excerpt: “Be Brave” combines interviews and archive material with generated scenes to reconstruct moments from Diesel founder Renzo Rosso’s life.
misc-be-brave-ai-documentary-venice-2026.text: ai-assisted documentary tests cinema’s boundaries at venice “be brave” combines interviews and archive material with generated scenes to reconstruct moments from diesel founder renzo rosso’s life. an ai-assisted documentary about diesel founder renzo rosso is screening out of competition at the venice film festival, offering a prominent test of how generated imagery can be used in nonfiction filmmaking. “be brave” was directed by francesco carrozzini and produced by lorenzo mieli. the film combines interviews and archival material with ai-generated visuals. the synthetic sequences reconstruct moments from rosso’s childhood and other periods for which no original footage exists, reuters reported. that makes the technology part of the documentary’s visual language rather than a substitute for every source image. the approach arrives amid intense debate over whether generative systems can expand creative choices or displace film workers. the filmmakers and rosso argued that ai should be understood and governed as a tool while maintaining that human judgment remains essential to storytelling. venice’s decision to include the film places that debate inside one of cinema’s most established festivals. the screening does not resolve questions about disclosure, authorship or labor, but it gives audiences a concrete work to evaluate. how clearly the generated scenes are distinguished from documented history will remain central to the project’s reception. more misc misc. italy venice venice, italy venice film festival documentary artificial intelligence renzo rosso cinema

misc-bedford-boys-soccer-bishop-guertin-.excerpt: Ibrahim Jusufovic scored once and set up two goals as the Bulldogs improved to 4-0 on the season.
misc-bedford-boys-soccer-bishop-guertin-.text: bedford boys soccer stays unbeaten with 3-1 win over bishop guertin ibrahim jusufovic scored once and set up two goals as the bulldogs improved to 4-0 on the season. bedford high school’s boys soccer team improved to 4-0 with a 3-1 road victory over bishop guertin in nashua on tuesday night. junior ibrahim jusufovic led the bulldogs with a goal and two assists. he opened the scoring 25 minutes into the match, sending a shot to the far side of the net after both teams struggled to create early chances. bishop guertin equalized after halftime when nick chartier scored following a blocked first attempt. bedford answered seven minutes later on a counterattack, with jusufovic setting up senior caden santerre for the go-ahead goal. manchester ink link reported that bedford later added a third goal to secure the result. the win kept the bulldogs perfect through four matches while showing they could respond after conceding an equalizer. bishop guertin increased its pressure for stretches of the game, but bedford’s transition play and finishing produced the difference. both teams now move into the next part of their regular-season schedules. more misc misc. nh nashua nashua, nh bedford bishop guertin high school soccer nhiaa

misc-being-heumann-opens-toronto-film-fe.excerpt: The drama revisits disability-rights activist Judy Heumann’s leadership in the 1977 Section 504 protest, with a cast led by Ruth Madeley and Mark Ruffalo.
misc-being-heumann-opens-toronto-film-fe.text: sian heder’s ‘being heumann’ opens toronto film festival the drama revisits disability-rights activist judy heumann’s leadership in the 1977 section 504 protest, with a cast led by ruth madeley and mark ruffalo. sian heder’s “being heumann” opened the toronto international film festival with a dramatization of disability-rights activist judy heumann’s campaign to force implementation of section 504 of the rehabilitation act. ruth madeley plays heumann, while mark ruffalo portrays joseph califano, the federal official pressed to sign the regulations. the film centers on the 1977 occupation of a federal building in san francisco. protesters remained for 26 days, demanding enforcement of protections against disability discrimination in federally funded programs. the action became a defining event in the u.s. disability-rights movement. most of the cast members are disabled, an approach consistent with heder’s focus on bringing people often left outside mainstream storytelling into view. heder won the 2022 academy award for adapted screenplay for “coda,” which also featured deaf performers in central roles. the toronto opening gives the new film a prominent festival launch ahead of its public release. “being heumann” is scheduled to reach select theaters on november 6 and apple tv one week later. the production turns a policy fight into a character-driven account of organizing, endurance and the practical consequences of laws that exist on paper but still require implementation. more misc misc. canada toronto toronto, canada being heumann toronto international film festival disability rights sian heder

misc-ben-shelton-alcaraz-us-open-quarter.excerpt: Shelton beat the defending champion in five sets at 3:33 a.m., setting up an all-American semifinal against Frances Tiafoe.
misc-ben-shelton-alcaraz-us-open-quarter.text: ben shelton stuns carlos alcaraz in latest u.s. open finish shelton beat the defending champion in five sets at 3:33 a.m., setting up an all-american semifinal against frances tiafoe. ben shelton knocked defending champion carlos alcaraz out of the u.s. open early wednesday, winning a five-set quarterfinal that produced the latest finish in tournament history. shelton prevailed 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(10-7). the match began at 11:05 p.m. tuesday and ended at 3:33 a.m. after four hours and 28 minutes, reuters reported. the result sends shelton into an all-american semifinal against frances tiafoe. it also ended alcaraz’s 13-match unbeaten record against american opponents at grand slam tournaments. the timing became part of the story as players and spectators remained at arthur ashe stadium well into the morning. shelton had to recover after dropping the opening tiebreak and again after alcaraz forced a deciding set. the final tiebreak decided a match in which momentum swung repeatedly, leaving an american guaranteed a place in the men’s final. the united states has not produced a men’s grand slam singles champion since andy roddick in 2003. more misc misc. ny new york new york, new york ben shelton carlos alcaraz u.s. open tennis

misc-ben-shelton-tiafoe-us-open-final-20.excerpt: The 23-year-old won the all-American semifinal in four sets and will face Alexander Zverev for the title Sunday.
misc-ben-shelton-tiafoe-us-open-final-20.text: ben shelton beats frances tiafoe to reach u.s. open final the 23-year-old won the all-american semifinal in four sets and will face alexander zverev for the title sunday. ben shelton reached his first u.s. open final friday night by defeating fellow american frances tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 at arthur ashe stadium. after dropping the opening set, the 23-year-old took control through the middle of the match and broke late in the fourth to close the semifinal without a deciding set. shelton became the first black american man to reach the u.s. open final since arthur ashe in 1972 and the first to reach any men’s major final since malivai washington at wimbledon in 1996. he is also one victory from ending a 23-year wait for an american men’s grand slam singles champion, dating to andy roddick’s 2003 u.s. open title. sunday’s championship match will pit shelton against top seed alexander zverev. zverev advanced by beating karen khachanov 6-3, 7-6(7), 7-6(6) and has not dropped a set in his last four matches. shelton will bring a powerful serve and strong home support into the matchup, while zverev enters with experience from multiple major finals and the 2026 french open title. more misc misc. new york new york new york, new york ben shelton frances tiafoe u.s. open tennis alexander zverev

misc-bob-mackie-fashion-designer-dies-87.excerpt: The fashion and costume designer whose work shaped 1970s Hollywood glamour died Monday in Palm Springs, according to The Associated Press.
misc-bob-mackie-fashion-designer-dies-87.text: bob mackie, designer to the stars, dies at 87 the fashion and costume designer whose work shaped 1970s hollywood glamour died monday in palm springs, according to the associated press. bob mackie, the fashion and costume designer whose theatrical work helped define hollywood glamour in the 1970s, died monday at age 87, the associated press reported. mackie became known for elaborate costumes built with sequins, rhinestones and bold silhouettes. his work dressed stars including cher, carol burnett, marilyn monroe, madonna and diana ross. his career included television, film, broadway and fashion. ap reported that mackie won nine emmy awards, received a tony award and earned multiple academy award nominations. he also designed clothing for barbie dolls and created costumes that became part of american pop-culture history. mackie’s longtime association with cher produced some of his most recognizable work, while his designs for the carol burnett show demonstrated his ability to combine comedy with high-fashion spectacle. his publicist said mackie died in palm springs from pneumonia. tributes are expected to focus on a career that treated costume design as both entertainment and visual storytelling. more more misc. california palm springs palm springs, california entertainment fashion bob mackie obituaries

misc-boston-9to5-labor-movement-2026.excerpt: A campaign organized by women office workers in the early 1970s pushed for fair pay and an end to workplace harassment, later inspiring a film and Dolly Parton anthem.
misc-boston-9to5-labor-movement-2026.text: boston-born 9to5 movement’s labor legacy returns to focus a campaign organized by women office workers in the early 1970s pushed for fair pay and an end to workplace harassment, later inspiring a film and dolly parton anthem. before “9 to 5” became a hit song and movie, it was the name of a boston organizing effort led by women office workers seeking fairer treatment on the job. the movement began in the early 1970s among secretaries and clerical workers who compared experiences with low wages, limited advancement and sexual harassment. by organizing around shared workplace problems, 9to5 helped make issues that were often treated as private frustrations part of a public labor agenda. its influence reached popular culture through the 1980 film starring jane fonda, lily tomlin and dolly parton and parton’s title song. the comedy gave a broad audience a recognizable picture of office hierarchies and the frustrations that had motivated the original organizers. the boston roots matter because they show how a local worker network can shape a national conversation. decades later, arguments over pay transparency, harassment protections and advancement still echo the movement’s early demands. the anniversary coverage is also a reminder that the familiar phrase “9 to 5” carries two histories: one in entertainment and another in organized workplace advocacy. more ma boston, massachusetts boston 9to5 movement labor history women at work

misc-boston-ground-zero-flag-relay-2026.text: flag relay begins 228-mile journey from boston to ground zero relay for america runners are carrying two flags along the route associated with the planes that departed logan airport on september 11, 2001. runners left boston carrying two american flags on a 228-mile relay to ground zero, marking 25 years since the september 11 attacks and honoring the people killed. the flags represent the two hijacked planes that departed logan international airport. relay for america organized the route as a symbolic effort to retrace and reclaim the path from boston to new york through remembrance and public service. each relay segment is 9.11 miles. boston police escorted the first leg, and organizers said police or fire escorts were confirmed for 20 portions of the journey. first responders are also joining runners along the route. the nonstop relay is designed to connect communities between the two cities while keeping the victims’ names and the role of emergency personnel in public view. its arrival at ground zero will coincide with anniversary observances in new york. organizers framed the run not as a race but as a moving memorial carried from the airport where the flights began to the site where many of the victims died. more misc misc. massachusetts boston boston, ma to new york, ny september 11 boston ground zero memorial relay

misc-boston-legacy-supporters-culture-20.text: boston legacy supporters build an identity around the nwsl newcomer an independent supporters group has supplied chants, drums and community input through the expansion club’s nomadic first season. boston legacy fc’s first nwsl season has unfolded across multiple venues, but an independent supporters group has provided a consistent game-day presence with drums, flags, chants and pregame gatherings. the boston independent supporters’ association began organizing before the expansion team had a roster or final identity. at the march opener at gillette stadium, members unveiled a large “our legacy takes flight” display before a crowd of more than 30,000. supporters also participated in focus groups after the club abandoned its original bos nation fc branding. their feedback helped rebuild the relationship between the organization and fans before the legacy name and swan identity took hold. the team has struggled at times in its debut season and has split home dates between massachusetts and rhode island while awaiting a permanent stadium. the supporters have remained visible throughout, aiming to build an inclusive local soccer culture that can carry into the planned 2028 stadium opening. more misc misc. ma boston boston, ma boston legacy fc nwsl soccer supporters

misc-brielle-saracini-derek-jeter-septem.excerpt: Brielle Saracini’s ceremonial first pitch renewed a bond formed after her father, Flight 175 pilot Victor Saracini, died in the attacks.
misc-brielle-saracini-derek-jeter-septem.text: yankees fan honors father alongside derek jeter 25 years after september 11 brielle saracini’s ceremonial first pitch renewed a bond formed after her father, flight 175 pilot victor saracini, died in the attacks. brielle saracini marked the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks by throwing a ceremonial first pitch at yankee stadium, accompanied by retired captain derek jeter. the appearance renewed a bond that began after saracini lost her father, victor, the pilot of hijacked united airlines flight 175, when the plane struck the world trade center’s south tower. saracini was a young yankees fan when she first met jeter, and their connection continued through milestones in her life. she later met her husband, sean mcguire, at a camp for children who had lost a parent in the attacks. their shared experience became part of a family story shaped by grief, remembrance and long-term support. the first pitch placed a personal history inside a public commemoration, linking a new york sports institution with one family’s path over a quarter-century. jeter’s presence reflected the value of relationships that continued long after the immediate aftermath. for saracini, the moment honored her father while also showing the life built since his death. the ceremony offered a quieter measure of september 11’s legacy: connections sustained across generations, not only anniversaries. more misc misc. new york new york new york, new york september 11 new york yankees derek jeter remembrance

misc-bruins-minten-extension-2026.text: bruins sign fraser minten to seven-year, $50.4 million extension the 22-year-old center is under contract through 2033-34 after producing 35 points in his first full season with boston. the boston bruins signed center fraser minten to a seven-year, $50.4 million contract extension tuesday, locking up the 22-year-old through the 2033-34 season. the associated press reported that the deal carries an average annual value and salary-cap hit of $7.2 million. minten will first complete the final year of his rookie contract, which pays a base salary of $850,000 this season. boston acquired minten from toronto in march 2025 in the trade that sent defenseman brandon carlo to the maple leafs. minten then played all 82 games last season, recording career highs of 17 goals and 18 assists. his 35 points were the most by a bruins rookie since 2017-18, and his plus-21 rating led nhl rookies. the extension gives boston a younger long-term piece alongside established stars david pastrnak and charlie mcavoy. it also shifts performance risk to the club: the contract becomes especially valuable if minten continues developing, but costly if his production stalls. the announced value is the full contract total, not a one-season salary. more ma boston, massachusetts boston bruins fraser minten nhl sports

misc-butch-wilmore-warwick-schools-2026.text: astronaut butch wilmore brings space stories to warwick schools the retired nasa astronaut and navy captain visited winman middle school and scott elementary after completing 464 days in space. retired nasa astronaut barry “butch” wilmore visited two warwick schools tuesday, giving rhode island students a firsthand account of life and work in space. wilmore spoke at winman middle school and scott elementary school. the retired u.s. navy captain spent a combined 464 days in space over three missions, experience that gave students a direct connection to human spaceflight beyond textbooks and video. warwick mayor frank picozzi welcomed wilmore, and former local broadcaster john loughlin helped arrange the visit, according to nbc 10 wjar. photos from the schools showed students gathered for the presentations and meeting the astronaut. the visit came after wilmore’s retirement from nasa and focused on education rather than a new mission announcement. for students, the value was the chance to ask questions of someone who has flown multiple spacecraft and lived for extended periods in orbit. school officials did not announce a continuing program tied to the appearance, making tuesday’s sessions a special one-day event. more ri warwick, rhode island barry wilmore nasa warwick schools space
