nh-manchester-veteran-homelessness-bench.excerpt: City officials and Harbor Care say a coordinated system has housed more than 130 veterans and can now make future homelessness rare, brief and nonrecurring.
nh-manchester-veteran-homelessness-bench.text: manchester says it has effectively ended veteran homelessness city officials and harbor care say a coordinated system has housed more than 130 veterans and can now make future homelessness rare, brief and nonrecurring. manchester officials and harbor care say the city has reached the benchmarks for effectively ending veteran homelessness after a two-year coordinated housing effort. the designation does not mean no veteran will ever become homeless in manchester. instead, the city says its response system can identify veterans quickly, connect them with services and move them into permanent housing so homelessness is rare, brief and nonrecurring. the initiative began in september 2024, when officials counted 47 veterans experiencing homelessness. according to the city, every veteran in that original group later obtained permanent housing; one subsequently died. the wider effort has housed more than 130 veterans, with the city saying 136 people were placed through the coordinated initiative. the manchester continuum of care reviewed and certified the benchmarks. the system brings the city, harbor care, the department of veterans affairs and community providers together around current case data and regular meetings. a sustainability fund helps address immediate barriers such as security deposits, application fees, temporary lodging and replacement identification. officials described the milestone as a measure of system performance rather than a declaration that the problem is permanently solved. maintaining the designation will require continued coordination, available housing and resources for veterans who enter homelessness in the future. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, nh manchester veterans homelessness harbor care

nh-manchester-zoning-townhouses-adus-sep.text: manchester zoning board to weigh 13-unit townhouse plan and adus thursday’s agenda includes a 13-unit titus avenue proposal, two accessory-dwelling-unit requests and several other variance cases. manchester’s zoning board is scheduled to meet thursday, september 10, at 6 p.m. with several housing proposals on its agenda. manchester ink link reported that the meeting will be broadcast on manchester public television channel 22 for residents who cannot attend in person. the largest listed case is a proposal for two townhouse buildings at 26 titus avenue: one with eight units and another with five. the 13-unit plan is proposed for a 49,484-square-foot lot where 78,000 square feet is required. both buildings would be three stories and 38 feet high, exceeding current limits of 2.5 stories and 35 feet. the board will also consider an expansion of an accessory dwelling unit at 50 delia drive. the proposed two-story garage addition would add about 416 square feet and two bedrooms, creating a 1,230-square-foot, three-bedroom second dwelling. a separate faith lane request would allow an attached adu equal to 43% of the main home’s floor area, above a 40% limit. the agenda also includes a proposed conversion of a two-family home into three units and other requests involving parking, setbacks and commercial use. the hearing will determine whether those projects receive the variances they need to proceed. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, nh manchester zoning housing adus

nh-mark-stebbins-community-center-opens-.excerpt: The 20,000-square-foot nonprofit hub brings health care, youth programs and food-access services under one roof.
nh-mark-stebbins-community-center-opens-.text: mark stebbins community center opens on manchester’s west side the 20,000-square-foot nonprofit hub brings health care, youth programs and food-access services under one roof. the mark stebbins community center is officially opening wednesday on manchester’s west side, creating a shared home for nonprofit services aimed at children and families, according to wmur. the approximately 20,000-square-foot center is designed to provide health care, affordable before- and after-school care, food-access programs and a community navigator service. amoskeag health and the boys & girls clubs of greater manchester are among the organizations expected to operate from the site. the project is named for the late mark stebbins, the longtime leader of hooksett-based design and construction company procon and a supporter of manchester nonprofit organizations. planning for the center began with local nonprofit and business leaders seeking a central, accessible location for services on the west side. bringing several providers together is intended to make it easier for families to reach multiple forms of support without traveling among separate offices. the opening marks the transition from a multiyear planning and construction effort to daily operations, with the center’s impact now depending on enrollment, staffing and how residents use the combined programs. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, nh manchester community center health care youth services

nh-medicaid-eligibility-changes-296-2026.excerpt: State health officials identified 296 people whose full coverage may end when federal eligibility rules narrow for some noncitizens.
nh-medicaid-eligibility-changes-296-2026.text: nearly 300 new hampshire residents may lose medicaid october 1 state health officials identified 296 people whose full coverage may end when federal eligibility rules narrow for some noncitizens. nearly 300 people in new hampshire may lose full medicaid coverage on october 1 as new federal eligibility limits take effect, according to state figures reported by nhpr. the department of health and human services identified 296 residents who could be affected. under the change, adults who are not pregnant generally must be a u.s. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident, a cuban-haitian entrant or a migrant covered by the compacts of free association to keep full medicaid eligibility. eligibility rules are not changing for people younger than 19, pregnant patients or women during the year after pregnancy. some residents who lose full benefits may still qualify for emergency medicaid, and others may be able to seek coverage through the insurance marketplace. the change is especially consequential for people receiving ongoing or long-term care. state officials said they contacted everyone identified as potentially affected, though one family profiled by nhpr disputed receiving notice. residents who believe their status is incorrect can contact the state or a benefits counselor before coverage changes. new-hampshire nh concord, new hampshire new hampshire medicaid health care immigration

nh-meredith-dedicates-september-11-memor.excerpt: The Lakes Region community gathered at Hesky Park before a procession to the new memorial garden at the central fire station.
nh-meredith-dedicates-september-11-memor.text: meredith dedicates september 11 memorial garden the lakes region community gathered at hesky park before a procession to the new memorial garden at the central fire station. meredith marked the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks friday with a public remembrance at hesky park and the formal dedication of a new memorial garden at the town’s central fire station. the town scheduled a procession from the meredith fire department to hesky park before the noon ceremony. police, firefighters and members of american legion griggs wyatt post 33 joined the observance, which honored the people killed in the attacks and the responders whose service followed. after the service, participants were invited to march back to the fire station for the garden dedication. the town arranged overflow parking at the municipal lot on route 3 and shuttle service beginning before the ceremony to help people reach both locations. the two-part program connected a statewide day of remembrance to a permanent local site. by placing the memorial at the fire station, meredith created a place where residents can return after the anniversary ceremonies end. the dedication also added another community memorial to the network of new hampshire observances held friday from portsmouth to the lakes region. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire meredith meredith, new hampshire meredith september 11 memorial hesky park lakes region

nh-merrimack-valley-bow-first-2-0-2026.text: merrimack valley beats bow 26-6 for program’s first 2-0 start the pride followed an opening win over hollis-brookline by holding bow to one touchdown in a 26-6 home victory. merrimack valley defeated bow 26-6 on friday night in penacook, giving the pride the first 2-0 start in the football program’s history. the result followed an opening victory over hollis-brookline and left bow 0-2 through its first two games. holding bow to one touchdown was central to the win. merrimack valley paired that defensive performance with enough scoring to keep the game beyond a one-possession margin, reversing the outcome of last season’s meeting, when bow won decisively under its new home lights. the early results mark a sharp improvement for a program that entered the new season looking to build consistency. the 2-0 record will be tested quickly. merrimack valley’s next scheduled opponent is st. thomas aquinas, followed by games against kennett, trinity, kingswood and milford. bow is scheduled to face kingswood next. september records do not settle a season, but the pride’s first two games have already established a program milestone and given the team a meaningful platform for the tougher division schedule ahead. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire penacook penacook, new hampshire merrimack valley bow high school football penacook

nh-mickey-gasper-ninth-home-run-royals-2.excerpt: The New Hampshire native homered at Fenway Park one day after using Boston’s rare day off to work with young baseball players.
nh-mickey-gasper-ninth-home-run-royals-2.text: merrimack’s mickey gasper hits ninth home run of season the new hampshire native homered at fenway park one day after using boston’s rare day off to work with young baseball players. merrimack native mickey gasper hit his ninth home run of the season friday night, continuing a breakout run with the boston red sox. gasper connected in the fifth inning against the kansas city royals at fenway park, cutting boston’s deficit to two runs and giving another lift to a player whose rise has become a point of pride for new hampshire baseball fans. the homer came one day after gasper spent boston’s day off at a youth clinic in peabody, massachusetts. he worked with children from a baseball club that he belonged to while growing up in the granite state. the appearance followed an unusually compressed stretch for the red sox, who had played 14 games over 13 days before thursday’s break. gasper’s path from merrimack youth baseball to fenway has supplied a distinctly regional thread to boston’s season. friday’s result added a measurable milestone: nine major-league home runs this season. his decision to use the club’s brief pause for a youth clinic also linked his current role with the program that helped shape him, placing the latest on-field moment beside a direct investment in the next generation of local players. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire merrimack merrimack, new hampshire mickey gasper boston red sox baseball merrimack fenway park

nh-mount-washington-blue-beams-september.excerpt: Two pillars of light from New England’s highest peak gave visitors and first responders a place to mark the attacks’ 25th anniversary.
nh-mount-washington-blue-beams-september.text: blue beams turn mount washington into september 11 memorial two pillars of light from new england’s highest peak gave visitors and first responders a place to mark the attacks’ 25th anniversary. two bright blue pillars rose from the summit of mount washington this week, turning new england’s highest peak into a memorial for the nearly 3,000 people killed in the september 11, 2001, attacks. the lights operated for two nights around the 25th anniversary, with the mount washington auto road offering summit shuttles for visitors who wanted to see the display up close. portsmouth organizer renee plummer began pursuing the project after last year’s anniversary and spent about a year securing permits and permissions. malloy events of rochester served as the technical producer. the paired beams were designed to evoke the world trade center towers while honoring civilians, firefighters, police officers and other first responders who died in the attacks. fog limited some early views, but organizers anticipated clearer conditions friday night. visitors included firefighters and other first responders, and auto road staff described the mood at the summit as reflective. the completed display marked a new phase for a project that had already drawn attention over its possible effects on migrating birds: for attendees, the focus shifted to remembrance and the scale of seeing the beams rise from the mountain. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire mount washington mount washington, new hampshire mount washington september 11 memorial first responders white mountains

nh-mount-washington-honor-summit-2026.excerpt: The Honor Summit remembrance begins Wednesday, with organizers shortening nightly hours after consulting wildlife specialists.
nh-mount-washington-honor-summit-2026.text: mount washington tribute will shine twin beams for four nights the honor summit remembrance begins wednesday, with organizers shortening nightly hours after consulting wildlife specialists. two beams of light are scheduled to rise from the summit of mount washington on four nights this week as part of the honor summit remembrance of the september 11 attacks. the conway daily sun reported that gov. kelly ayotte is expected in conway wednesday for the kickoff. organizers say the installation will honor those killed in the attacks, first responders and veterans. the beams are scheduled to operate september 9 through 12 from 8 p.m. to midnight. producers shortened the original seven-hour nightly plan after discussions with new hampshire fish and game, new hampshire audubon and the cornell lab of ornithology about fall bird migration. an audubon representative is expected to monitor the area, and organizers said the lights can be interrupted if large flocks are observed. the event has obtained permits from the federal aviation administration and state wildlife officials, according to the newspaper. organizers also plan to direct money raised beyond expenses to four veterans-service nonprofits. the four-night schedule balances the public memorial with efforts to reduce effects on wildlife around the 6,288-foot summit. new-hampshire nh mount washington, new hampshire new hampshire mount washington september 11 veterans

nh-mount-washington-tribute-beams-bird-m.excerpt: Conservation groups and state agencies have a shutoff protocol as twin memorial beams coincide with peak fall songbird migration.
nh-mount-washington-tribute-beams-bird-m.text: bird monitors watch mount washington’s september 11 tribute beams conservation groups and state agencies have a shutoff protocol as twin memorial beams coincide with peak fall songbird migration. conservationists are monitoring twin light beams projected from the mount washington summit for the 25th anniversary of the september 11 attacks, watching for signs that migrating birds are becoming disoriented. new hampshire public radio reported that the display will continue through the weekend during the peak fall migration period for songbirds. many songbirds travel at night, and artificial light can attract them or alter their routes. the summit is normally far darker than an urban setting, making the installation’s local effect uncertain. new hampshire audubon has worked with cornell university scientists, the new york city bird alliance, new hampshire fish and game and state parks on a protocol for switching off the beams if observers see dangerous behavior. during a test earlier in the week, monitors saw birds remain below about 2,000 feet and avoid the new lights. observers plan to use binoculars, spotting equipment and a thermal monocular capable of detecting birds and bats. their weekend watch will help determine whether the memorial can continue safely while migration traffic passes over the white mountains. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire mount washington mount washington, nh mount washington bird migration september 11 new hampshire audubon

nh-mt-lafayette-injured-hiker-rescue-202.excerpt: A 62-year-old hiker was rescued from Mount Lafayette Saturday after an injury prompted a coordinated response, WMUR reported.
nh-mt-lafayette-injured-hiker-rescue-202.text: dozens of rescuers help injured hiker off mount lafayette a 62-year-old hiker was rescued from mount lafayette saturday after an injury prompted a coordinated response, wmur reported. dozens of rescuers were called to mount lafayette on saturday after a 62-year-old hiker was injured, according to wmur. the rescue began at about 3:30 p.m., the station reported. mount lafayette is one of the prominent peaks in franconia notch, an area that can require extended responses when hikers are hurt on steep or difficult terrain. wmur’s initial report did not identify the nature of the hiker’s injury or provide additional details about the person’s condition. it also did not report any other injuries connected to the incident. the response highlights the coordination often required for mountain rescues in new hampshire. hikers can face changing weather, uneven footing and long distances from roads or medical access, making preparation and route awareness important even during day trips. northeast news will update this report if authorities release additional information about the hiker or the rescue response. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire franconia mount lafayette, new hampshire new hampshire mount lafayette rescue hiking

nh-mud-bowl-hogs-50-year-tradition-2026.text: nh chronicle revisits 50-year mud bowl tradition in mount washington valley a new wmur retrospective reunites members of the hogs and looks back at a muddy football tradition rooted in north conway. nh chronicle is marking a half-century of mud football in the mount washington valley with a new retrospective on the hogs, the local team whose name became closely tied to the region’s unusual athletic tradition. wmur’s program brings members of the group back together and traces how playing football in mud grew into a recognizable north conway event. the setting became known as hog coliseum, behind the community center in the village. the story is less about conventional standings than about the people who kept returning to the field and built a durable community identity around the game. the reunion gives former participants a chance to connect the early years with the tradition remembered by later spectators. for the mount washington valley, the retrospective also preserves a piece of local culture that sits outside the area’s familiar skiing and hiking image. a 50-year run turns what began as a novelty into community history, and wmur’s account records the people behind it while those memories can still be shared firsthand. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh north conway north conway, nh new hampshire north conway mud bowl community traditions

nh-nashua-community-college-enrichment-c.text: nashua community college opens new enrichment classes to teens and adults the fall lineup includes vehicle maintenance, creative writing, cooking, yoga and tabletop games, with courses ranging from one session to eight weeks. nashua community college is launching a new group of community education and enrichment courses this fall, opening college-led instruction to local teenagers and adults outside its degree programs. the schedule mixes practical skills, creative work, wellness and recreation in formats ranging from single sessions to multiweek classes. a basic vehicle-maintenance class for new drivers is scheduled for october 10 and is open to participants age 15 and older. the hands-on session is designed to cover tire pressure, dashboard warning lights, fluid checks, jump-starting a vehicle, changing a tire and basic inspections. an eight-week creative-writing workshop begins september 16, with instruction in memoir, personal essays and fiction. other listed options include yoga, a healthy-lunchbox workshop, tabletop role-playing games, pumpkin-cake decorating, comfort cooking and an italian-cookie class. prices and age requirements vary by course, and the college says additional offerings will be announced. the initiative broadens the school’s role as a community training hub by pairing short, accessible classes with instructors from the college and the region. registration information is available through nashua community college’s non-credit course page. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh nashua nashua, new hampshire nashua community college community education workforce development classes

nh-nashua-sewer-rate-proposal-2026.text: nashua sewer proposal would add about $3 a month for average user a committee backed three annual 7% increases beginning in 2027, sending the plan to the full board of aldermen. nashua sewer customers would pay about $3 more per month on average under a three-year rate proposal that advanced from an aldermanic committee. the plan calls for demand and usage charges to increase 7% each january in 2027, 2028 and 2029. the committee gave the measure a favorable recommendation to the full board of aldermen. city officials said the additional revenue would support wastewater operations, debt tied to combined-sewer-overflow work, other system improvements and required reserves as expenses rise. officials also reviewed the system’s outstanding accounts. about $1.7 million in sewer bills was listed as unpaid, though roughly $1 million of that total was current and not yet due. the city has placed about 600 liens connected to overdue accounts, according to the meeting report. the committee vote was 3-1. the proposal still needs approval from the full board before any increase can take effect. if adopted as presented, the phased schedule would spread the adjustment across three years instead of imposing the full change at once, while giving residents a defined timeline for future bills. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire nashua nashua, new hampshire nashua sewer rates utilities board of aldermen infrastructure

nh-nashua-south-memorial-soccer-2-1-2026.text: nashua south boys soccer stays unbeaten with 2-1 win over manchester memorial kevin araujo assisted on the opening goal and scored the winner as the purple panthers improved to 4-0. nashua south remained unbeaten wednesday with a 2-1 boys soccer victory over manchester memorial, moving the purple panthers to 4-0 early in the season. kevin araujo shaped both south goals. sixteen minutes into the match, his corner kick found senior max friday for a header and a 1-0 lead. manchester memorial answered nine minutes later when leis taric chased down a long ball and scored in his season debut. south regained the advantage four minutes into the second half. a clearance created a one-on-one opportunity for araujo, who beat the defender with his speed and finished low for his first goal of the season. memorial increased its pressure afterward, but south protected the one-goal margin through the final whistle. south coach tom bellen told manchester ink link that the result came despite a performance below the team’s preferred level, while memorial coach jerold white pointed to quicker decisions with the ball as an area to improve. the close match offered both teams an early-season test: nashua south showed it could win without its best performance, and memorial stayed within one play of an undefeated opponent. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh nashua nashua, nh nashua south manchester memorial nhiaa boys soccer

nh-national-guard-texas-border-mission-2.excerpt: Two New Hampshire Army National Guard units are expected to deploy next month for a year-long mission supporting U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
nh-national-guard-texas-border-mission-2.text: 54 new hampshire national guard members prepare for texas border mission two new hampshire army national guard units are expected to deploy next month for a year-long mission supporting u.s. customs and border protection. fifty-four members of the new hampshire army national guard are preparing to deploy to texas next month for a year-long mission supporting u.s. customs and border protection, new hampshire public radio reported monday. a departure ceremony was held saturday in concord. the soldiers are expected to support aerial and ground reconnaissance along the u.s.-mexico border as part of an ongoing federal security operation. the deployment will include 14 soldiers from a lakota helicopter unit based in concord and 40 members of the 262nd engineer construction company based in rochester. the guard said the units will assist the federal border mission rather than operate as a separate state deployment. it will be the third time in six years that new hampshire’s army national guard has supported a border mission. in 2021, 215 members took part in year-long deployments; in 2024, 15 soldiers were sent for 60 days to support a texas state border mission. the new hampshire guard said more than 2,100 national guard members from more than 20 states are currently deployed in support of federal security operations at the border. the latest new hampshire units are expected to mobilize in october. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh concord concord, new hampshire new hampshire national guard texas border security

nh-new-england-wind-power-record-2000-me.excerpt: ISO New England data show regional wind output passed a new threshold Thursday night, helped by recently added offshore projects.
nh-new-england-wind-power-record-2000-me.text: new england wind generation crosses 2,000 megawatts for first time iso new england data show regional wind output passed a new threshold thursday night, helped by recently added offshore projects. wind farms across new england generated more than 2,000 megawatts of electricity at the same time thursday night, setting a regional record, the concord monitor reported friday. the milestone was reached at about 8:30 p.m., according to data from iso new england, which manages the six-state power grid. the peak was roughly 30% higher than the previous record set in october. the increase reflects new offshore generation now connected to the grid, including the revolution wind project serving rhode island and connecticut and the vineyard wind project off massachusetts. onshore wind facilities in northern new england also contributed to the total. a megawatt can supply hundreds of homes, although actual output and demand vary by hour and season. wind remains one part of a regional mix that also includes natural gas, nuclear, hydroelectric power, solar and imports. because wind output changes with weather, the grid operator must continuously balance it against other sources. the record nevertheless shows how quickly recently completed projects can alter new england's power supply, particularly during windy off-peak hours when demand is lower. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh concord concord, nh new hampshire wind power iso new england renewable energy electric grid

nh-nottingham-data-center-moratorium-202.excerpt: Voters gave the town a year to study land-use, infrastructure, environmental and fiscal questions before new data-center proposals can advance.
nh-nottingham-data-center-moratorium-202.text: nottingham approves 12-month moratorium on data centers voters gave the town a year to study land-use, infrastructure, environmental and fiscal questions before new data-center proposals can advance. nottingham voters approved a 12-month moratorium on data-center development, giving the town time to examine how large computing facilities could affect local land use and public resources. new hampshire public radio reported that tuesday’s vote was 1,335 in favor and 143 opposed. the pause directs the town to study environmental, infrastructure and fiscal effects and consider whether zoning changes are needed. it does not permanently ban data centers. instead, it creates a defined review period before proposals can move through the local approval process. interest in the issue followed a data-center proposal that was later withdrawn amid community opposition. nhpr reported that new hampshire currently has no hyperscale data centers, placing nottingham’s decision in a broader statewide debate over how communities should prepare for potential projects. over the next year, residents and town officials will have opportunities to weigh development rules against possible economic benefits and demands on land, electricity, water and roads. any permanent restrictions would require separate action after the study period, making the moratorium a first step rather than a final policy. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh nottingham nottingham, nh nottingham data centers zoning local government

nh-pappas-democratic-senate-primary-win-.text: chris pappas wins new hampshire democratic senate primary the three-term congressman advances to a nationally watched general-election contest for the seat being vacated by retiring sen. jeanne shaheen. u.s. rep. chris pappas won new hampshire’s democratic primary for u.s. senate on tuesday night, setting up the next phase of a closely watched contest for the seat being vacated by retiring sen. jeanne shaheen. new hampshire public radio reported that pappas led karishma manzur with 62% of the vote as of 8:20 p.m., with 27% of ballots counted. the tally was still incomplete, but the outlet reported that voters had selected pappas as the democratic nominee. pappas has represented the state’s 1st congressional district since 2019. his move into the senate race also leaves an open house seat, adding another competitive contest to new hampshire’s november ballot. the general election is expected to draw national money and attention because control of the senate could turn on a small number of open or closely divided seats. the early primary count is not a final certified result; local election officials and the secretary of state will complete the canvass before totals become official. new-hampshire nh new hampshire politics elections u.s. senate chris pappas

nh-police-ice-arrests-surge-2026-09-14.excerpt: A data review says local departments accounted for nearly half of 198 people detained in New Hampshire from May through July as 287(g) partnerships expanded.
nh-police-ice-arrests-surge-2026-09-14.text: nh police departments tied to surge in ice arrests, nhpr analysis finds a data review says local departments accounted for nearly half of 198 people detained in new hampshire from may through july as 287(g) partnerships expanded. new hampshire public radio says local law enforcement played a significant role in the state’s increase in immigration arrests this summer, based on federal data obtained through public-records requests by the deportation data project. the analysis found that local police departments accounted for nearly half of the 198 people detained in new hampshire from may through july. more than 700 people have been detained in the state since the start of the second trump administration, nhpr reported. the departments involved use agreements known as 287(g) programs, which allow local officers to carry out certain immigration actions while working with u.s. immigration and customs enforcement. new hampshire is the only new england state where local law-enforcement agencies have signed such agreements, according to nhpr. since september 2025, local agencies had arrested 172 people through a 287(g) program, with arrests concentrated in the southern half of the state and around the ice office in manchester. hillsborough and rockingham counties also have sheriff’s-office agreements. nhpr’s review said arrests involved people from 48 countries and that about one-third of those arrested during the trump administration had a criminal conviction. the data is likely to remain part of a wider debate over the role of local police in federal immigration enforcement. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, new hampshire new hampshire immigration ice public safety

nh-post-election-audit-sites-2026.excerpt: Ballot-counting devices from nine towns and city wards will be checked publicly at the State Archives, with a report due Friday.
nh-post-election-audit-sites-2026.text: new hampshire selects nine locations for post-election audit ballot-counting devices from nine towns and city wards will be checked publicly at the state archives, with a report due friday. new hampshire’s secretary of state has randomly selected ballot-counting devices from nine towns and city wards for post-election audits following tuesday’s state primary. the public checks are scheduled for wednesday, september 9, at 10 a.m. and thursday, september 10, at 9 a.m. at the new hampshire state archives in concord. members of the public and news media may observe the work. secretary of state david scanlan’s office said one device will be audited from each selected location. the selections include communities using votingworks equipment and communities using liberty vote’s imagecast precinct 2 system, giving election officials samples from both voting technologies in use. officials must publish the audit findings by noon friday, september 11. the process is separate from a candidate-requested recount: its purpose is to check how the selected devices recorded and counted ballots after election day. results from the audit will provide a documented comparison for those locations while the state completes its post-primary election administration. new-hampshire nh concord, new hampshire elections post-election audit ballot counting secretary of state

nh-primary-ballot-guide.text: today’s nh primary: the races and stakes on the ballot voters are selecting nominees for congress, governor and the legislature in one of the state’s most consequential primary days in years. the new hampshire primary is placing nominations for congress, governor and the 424-seat state legislature before voters tuesday, according to an associated press overview of the election. the open senate contest is the top-of-ticket race after jeanne shaheen’s decision not to seek reelection. chris pappas and karishma manzur are competing for the democratic nomination, while john e. sununu and scott brown are among the republicans seeking their party’s nomination. voters are also selecting candidates for the state’s two u.s. house districts. the results will determine which candidates advance to the november general election and will give campaigns a clearer sense of the issues resonating with primary voters. this is a guide to the major contests, not a projection. northeast news will add verified results and candidate statements as they become available. new-hampshire nh new hampshire politics elections primary

nh-primary-day-2026.text: new hampshire voters head to polls as open senate seat reshapes 2026 races tuesday’s primary is the first major test of the campaigns competing to succeed retiring u.s. sen. jeanne shaheen, with congressional and statehouse contests on the same ballot. new hampshire voters are choosing nominees tuesday in a primary that will set the field for an open u.s. senate seat, two congressional contests, the governor’s race and the state legislature. the senate contest has drawn particular attention because jeanne shaheen is not seeking reelection. on the democratic side, u.s. rep. chris pappas is facing a challenge from karishma manzur. the republican field includes former u.s. senators john e. sununu and scott brown. the ballot also includes a crowded contest for pappas’s current house seat in the 1st congressional district. the general election is expected to make new hampshire one of the country’s closely watched senate battlegrounds. the results will provide the first clear measure of which messages, coalitions and candidates have the strongest footing before november. northeast news will update this story as results are reported and verified. new-hampshire nh new hampshire politics elections u.s. senate primary

nh-primary-election-monitors-smooth-2026.excerpt: State inspectors visited roughly 260 polling places, while an election-law hotline handled 83 contacts without a significant incident.
nh-primary-election-monitors-smooth-2026.text: new hampshire election monitors report smooth state primary state inspectors visited roughly 260 polling places, while an election-law hotline handled 83 contacts without a significant incident. new hampshire’s state primary concluded without significant incidents, according to the state department of justice, after election-law personnel monitored voting across hundreds of polling places. the department said 39 inspectors from its election law unit visited about 260 polling locations. their work included observing procedures and assisting local officials when questions arose. the department coordinated with the secretary of state’s office during the voting period. a dedicated hotline staffed by four attorneys, two investigators and a paralegal received 83 contacts. the state did not identify any of those calls as producing a significant election problem. secretary of state david scanlan said he had no concerns about disruption and noted that state personnel routinely monitor elections and help local administrators. federal election monitors were also assigned to manchester and nashua. new hampshire was one of six states receiving federal monitors for the primary. the state’s report provides an initial operational assessment rather than a certification of every result; official canvassing and other post-election procedures continue under the normal schedule. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire concord concord, nh state primary election monitors new hampshire doj polling places

nh-primary-voter-distrust-2026.text: new hampshire primary voters describe distrust and ambivalence interviews at polling places found many granite staters voting from civic duty or concern about specific issues rather than enthusiasm for candidates. new hampshire voters who spoke with nhpr at polling places tuesday repeatedly described distrust, frustration or ambivalence toward candidates, even as they cast ballots in the state primary. the interviews were not a scientific survey and should not be read as a statewide measure. they nevertheless captured a recurring mood across several communities: some voters said civic duty brought them out, while others were motivated by particular issues or by the november general election rather than strong attachment to a primary candidate. education funding and property taxes were among the concerns voters raised. others focused on federal gridlock, campaign funding and immigration enforcement. several town moderators told nhpr that turnout is often lighter in nonpresidential primaries. the reporting adds context to the results already being called tuesday night. winners will move on to november, but the comments suggest nominees will also have to persuade voters who entered the fall campaign skeptical of political institutions and unconvinced that candidates will deliver change. the anecdotes show individual views, not a definitive picture of the electorate. new-hampshire nh new hampshire new hampshire primary voters civic engagement

nh-ralph-baer-home-video-game-blueprint-.excerpt: A four-page concept written in September 1966 led to the Brown Box prototype and the first commercial home video-game console.
nh-ralph-baer-home-video-game-blueprint-.text: new hampshire marks 60 years since ralph baer’s home-game blueprint a four-page concept written in september 1966 led to the brown box prototype and the first commercial home video-game console. new hampshire’s place in video-game history is receiving renewed attention 60 years after engineer ralph baer put his idea for interactive television games on paper. baer wrote a four-page concept on september 1, 1966, while working for sanders associates in nashua. the document proposed using a television set for play rather than passive viewing. back in new hampshire, baer worked with engineers bill harrison and bill rusch to turn the concept into experimental systems, culminating in the wood-grain unit that became known as the brown box. sanders licensed the technology to magnavox, which released the odyssey in 1972. the system is widely recognized as the first commercial home video-game console and helped establish a consumer industry that now spans consoles, computers, phones and online platforms. baer continued inventing after the odyssey and became known as the father of home video games. the smithsonian preserves his early document, prototypes and workshop materials. the anniversary connects an everyday form of entertainment to engineering work carried out in nashua and manchester during the 1960s. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire nashua nashua and manchester, new hampshire ralph baer video games sanders associates nashua manchester

nh-raymond-firefighter-phillips-transfer.excerpt: More than a dozen departments joined a dignified transfer for Eric Phillips, who died after a medical emergency while responding to a call.
nh-raymond-firefighter-phillips-transfer.text: new hampshire fire departments honor fallen raymond firefighter more than a dozen departments joined a dignified transfer for eric phillips, who died after a medical emergency while responding to a call. fire departments and residents across southern new hampshire gathered to honor raymond firefighter eric phillips during a dignified transfer from concord on sunday. phillips, 44, died friday night after suffering a medical emergency while responding to a call for service, according to reporting compiled by the daily dispatch from wmur. the transfer began shortly after 4:30 p.m. in concord, and more than a dozen departments took part in the procession. firefighters positioned apparatus on route 101 overpasses as the procession traveled toward raymond. community members also stood along the route. the coordinated display followed a long emergency-services tradition of accompanying a fallen responder and visibly supporting the person’s family and department. phillips had served with the raymond fire department for five years. the public observance brought together departments that routinely assist one another across town lines, especially during large fires and other emergencies. officials had not announced additional public memorial arrangements in the source report. residents should rely on the raymond fire department or town notices for any later service information. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh raymond raymond, new hampshire raymond firefighters eric phillips public safety

nh-rundlett-construction-school-year-202.text: rundlett students adapt as new middle-school construction ramps up construction beside concord’s existing middle school is bringing noise and vibration, but staff say students are adjusting as the replacement building takes shape. students and staff at rundlett middle school in concord are beginning a new academic year beside an active construction site, as work advances on the city’s replacement middle school. the project is close enough to the current building that classroom noise and vibration have become part of the daily routine. construction started before summer and moved into a busier phase as students returned for fall classes. the effects are most noticeable near the eighth-grade science wing and art rooms, where teachers have had to account for intermittent sound from heavy equipment and other work outside. school administrators and teachers told the concord monitor that many students are adapting, while some have become curious about the machinery and progress next door. staff are working to keep instruction steady and respond when construction activity becomes distracting. the overlap is expected to continue through the roughly two-year building period. keeping the existing school open allows classes to continue on site, but it also requires close coordination around safety, access and the learning environment. for families, the opening weeks offer the first sustained look at how the district will manage daily school operations while a major public project rises nearby. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh concord concord, new hampshire concord rundlett middle school school construction education

nh-rye-goss-barn-swallows-conflicting-vo.text: rye voters approve conflicting rules for goss barn swallows one measure calls for the town-owned barn to remain wildlife-free, while another restricts officials from disturbing bird colonies. rye voters approved two ballot measures that point in different directions for a migratory colony of barn swallows at the town-owned goss barn, leaving local officials to determine how the results can be carried out together. a warrant article calling for the historic barn to remain a wildlife-free municipal building in perpetuity passed 1,248 to 1,113, according to new hampshire public radio. a separate measure barring officials from disturbing bird colonies on town land unless the birds pose a public-health risk passed 1,232 to 1,122. barn swallows have nested at the site for decades. the dispute sharpened after concerns about droppings led the town to seal the barn and spend about $13,000 on cleaning. public meetings and a lawsuit have already made the issue one of rye’s most closely watched local debates. town administrator matt scruton said the town would review the language and determine its next steps. the rye conservation commission is scheduled to meet thursday, when members are expected to examine the overlapping instructions. any resolution will have to account for the votes, the building’s municipal use and the circumstances under which the public-health exception could apply. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh rye rye, nh rye goss barn barn swallows local government

nh-school-tax-cap-ballot-lawsuit-2026.text: judge weighs challenge to new hampshire school tax-cap ballot question a superior court judge is expected to rule quickly as ballot printing approaches for the proposed school spending and tax limits. a merrimack county judge is considering a lawsuit seeking to remove a proposed new hampshire school tax cap from the november ballot. superior court judge dan st. hilaire heard arguments over whether the question gives voters a clear explanation of the change they are being asked to approve. the challenge was brought by campton school board member kelly wieser and warner taxpayer david bates. they contend the wording is confusing and does not adequately describe how the cap would operate. the state argues that lawmakers properly enacted the measure and that the plaintiffs do not have legal standing to block it. if approved by voters, the proposal would limit annual growth in local property-tax levies for schools, with adjustments tied to inflation and new construction. it would also place a 6% limit on growth in school administrative-unit central-office spending. timing is tight because ballot printing is expected to begin late next week. st. hilaire indicated that a decision would come quickly, giving election officials and local governments little room for delay before ballots are finalized. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire concord concord, new hampshire school funding property taxes november ballot merrimack county superior court

nh-senate-primary-stakes.text: the new hampshire senate primary is the race to watch with shaheen’s retirement opening a rare statewide contest, both parties are testing messages that could define the fall campaign. new hampshire’s open senate race is drawing national attention because the state’s primary could shape one of the most competitive seats on the 2026 map. reuters reported that chris pappas entered the democratic primary with a fundraising advantage, while karishma manzur has sought to close the gap with a more progressive platform and a grassroots campaign. on the republican side, john e. sununu and scott brown bring different kinds of statewide experience to the contest. the eventual nominees will face a general election audience focused on affordability, the direction of washington and the state’s independent political identity. primary results are only an opening signal, not a forecast. the electorate, issues and alliances can change substantially between september and november. new-hampshire nh new hampshire politics elections u.s. senate

nh-springworks-lettuce-hannaford-status-.text: springworks lettuce disappears from hannaford as farm status remains unclear the maine aquaponics grower that supplied organic romaine across hannaford’s footprint has stopped appearing on store shelves, with its business status unresolved. springworks farm lettuce has disappeared from hannaford shelves in new hampshire and across the supermarket chain’s regional footprint, while the status of the lisbon, maine, aquaponics business remains unclear. manchester ink link reported that springworks stopped supplying hannaford and other customers weeks ago. the farm’s phone was disconnected, employees did not respond to outreach and its website no longer displayed a store-locator page. hannaford had not provided a public explanation before the outlet’s deadline. springworks had been hannaford’s exclusive supplier of organic romaine for all 184 stores in new england and new york. founded in 2014 by trevor kenkel, the company used aquaponics, combining greenhouse crops with recirculating water from fish production. by 2024, its products reportedly reached about 300 stores and institutions, including whole foods, roche bros., food city, sysco northern new england and maine schools. the company announced $22 million in financing in 2023 for a new greenhouse, but the current status of that expansion was not established in the report. the available evidence shows a halt in retail supply, not a confirmed permanent closure. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire manchester manchester, nh hannaford springworks farm groceries new england

nh-sununu-republican-senate-primary-win-.excerpt: The former senator defeated Scott Brown and will face Democrat Chris Pappas for New Hampshire’s open U.S. Senate seat.
nh-sununu-republican-senate-primary-win-.text: john e. sununu wins new hampshire republican senate primary the former senator defeated scott brown and will face democrat chris pappas for new hampshire’s open u.s. senate seat. former u.s. sen. john e. sununu won new hampshire’s republican senate primary tuesday, earning a place in the november race for the seat democratic sen. jeanne shaheen is leaving after three terms. new hampshire public radio reported that sununu had 70% of the vote to scott brown’s 25% as of 8:20 p.m., with 16% counted. the figures were preliminary, but nhpr reported that republican voters had selected sununu as their nominee. sununu previously represented new hampshire in the senate from 2003 to 2009 and served one term in the u.s. house before that. brown, a former massachusetts senator, had also sought a new hampshire senate seat in 2014. sununu will face democratic rep. chris pappas, who won his party’s primary tuesday. the matchup gives voters a choice between two candidates with federal experience and puts new hampshire at the center of the national fight for senate control. final totals remain subject to the state’s official canvass. new-hampshire nh new hampshire politics elections u.s. senate john sununu

nh-supreme-court-ctrack-data-breach-2026.excerpt: A review found names and addresses in 2002–2015 case files were accessed, while the Judicial Branch said it had not identified exposed sensitive identifiers.
nh-supreme-court-ctrack-data-breach-2026.text: new hampshire supreme court files were accessed in multi-state c-track breach a review found names and addresses in 2002–2015 case files were accessed, while the judicial branch said it had not identified exposed sensitive identifiers. files associated with the new hampshire supreme court were accessed during a cybersecurity incident involving c-track, a case-management platform used by courts in multiple jurisdictions. nhpr reported that the state judicial branch reviewed the affected material in mid-august and found that names and addresses of people connected to cases filed from 2002 through 2015 had been accessed. the branch said it had not identified exposed social security numbers, driver’s-license numbers, birth dates, medical details or health-insurance information in the new hampshire files. west publishing, which operates c-track, discovered the unauthorized activity on june 30. its investigation found that an outside party obtained certain files in march. court systems in 11 states, the u.s. virgin islands and canada were included in the broader incident. new hampshire’s superior and circuit courts do not use c-track, limiting the state exposure identified so far to supreme court data. the platform continued operating, according to notices about the breach. people whose names appeared in older cases should rely on direct notices or official updates before assuming their sensitive information was involved. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh concord concord, new hampshire new hampshire supreme court c-track cybersecurity court records

nh-temple-adath-yeshurun-high-holidays-a.text: manchester synagogue blends tradition and access for high holidays temple adath yeshurun is pairing longstanding observances with family services, visual prayer aids and open registration as the hebrew year 5787 begins. temple adath yeshurun in manchester is preparing for the high holidays with a schedule that preserves core jewish observances while adding more ways for families and newcomers to participate. rosh hashanah begins friday evening, opening hebrew year 5787, and the synagogue is making services available through free advance ticket registration and established security procedures. cantor harriet dunkerley, who became the congregation’s spiritual leader july 1, is introducing a family service saturday afternoon before tashlikh at dorrs pond. the program also includes visual versions of prayers intended to help participants follow the service. for yom kippur, the temple plans a family service september 21 at 1:30 p.m., along with study sessions and a cello-and-piano presentation of kol nidre. the approach reflects the challenge facing many longstanding congregations: maintaining the structure and meaning of major observances while lowering practical barriers to participation. temple adath yeshurun traces its history back more than a century and is new hampshire’s oldest synagogue. its 2026 schedule combines that institutional history with changes aimed at making the season understandable and welcoming across generations. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, new hampshire manchester rosh hashanah yom kippur temple adath yeshurun religion

nh-unh-offshore-steelhead-farm-2026.excerpt: A floating research facility off the New Hampshire coast is testing whether domestic seafood production can expand while monitoring water quality and managing nutrients.
nh-unh-offshore-steelhead-farm-2026.text: unh offshore fish farm raises 20,000 pounds of steelhead near portsmouth a floating research facility off the new hampshire coast is testing whether domestic seafood production can expand while monitoring water quality and managing nutrients. a university of new hampshire-led aquaculture project is producing about 20,000 pounds of steelhead trout at a floating research facility off portsmouth, offering a local test of how offshore fish farming could increase the domestic seafood supply. boston 25 news reported that the roughly 50-by-30-foot facility is operated by unh’s center for sustainable seafood systems. the fish begin their lives at an inland site in new hampshire’s lakes region before being transferred to salt water and raised offshore. harvest typically comes when each fish reaches about five or six pounds. the operation also grows mussels, kelp and other seaweed around the fish. those species can absorb nutrients released by the farm, while researchers monitor the surrounding water to measure environmental effects and refine the system. the work is intended to test production methods rather than assume that every coastal site will perform the same way. unh was selected for a broader federal effort to develop sustainable aquaculture in several u.s. regions. related work is underway in alabama, with projects planned for hawaii and california. for new hampshire, the portsmouth farm links marine science, food production and the region’s long-running effort to build a resilient coastal economy. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh portsmouth portsmouth, nh unh aquaculture portsmouth steelhead

nh-unh-record-financial-aid-incoming-cla.excerpt: Nearly all members of the University of New Hampshire's incoming class received financial aid this year as the university increased average awards amid persistent concerns about college affordability.
nh-unh-record-financial-aid-incoming-cla.text: unh boosts aid to record $40 million for incoming class nearly all members of the university of new hampshire's incoming class received financial aid this year as the university increased average awards amid persistent concerns about college affordability. the university of new hampshire awarded $40 million in financial aid to its incoming class this year, the largest total in the university's history, according to reporting by new hampshire public radio and the concord monitor. about 96% of enrolled students received aid, up from 88% last year. the average award rose to more than $16,000 from $12,400, while university officials said the increase came from changes in budgeting for merit and need-based scholarships rather than additional public funding. the incoming class of 2030 also posted an average high school gpa of 3.7. enrollment in unh's hamel honors and scholars college reached 322 students, a 20% increase from last year, according to the university. the aid increase arrives as families continue to weigh the cost of higher education. unh reported last year's in-state tuition at $19,202 and out-of-state tuition at $39,852, figures that do not include housing, food and other attendance costs. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh durham durham, new hampshire new hampshire unh higher education financial aid durham

nh-unh-volleyball-yale-straight-sets-202.text: unh volleyball falls to unbeaten yale in straight sets reilly garrity posted a career-high 13 assists, but the bulldogs hit .396 and won 25-16, 25-21 and 25-14. the university of new hampshire women’s volleyball team lost to unbeaten yale in straight sets saturday afternoon at the uconn volleyball center in storrs. yale won 25-16, 25-21 and 25-14, improving to 5-0 while the wildcats moved to 7-3. unh briefly cut yale’s first-set lead to three with a four-point run and opened the second set with an 8-6 edge. the bulldogs answered with six consecutive points and controlled the finish. yale then built an 8-3 lead early in the third set and closed out the match despite a short wildcats rally. emma converse and rachel grier led new hampshire with eight kills apiece. reilly garrity recorded a collegiate-best 13 assists, hady pickard had nine digs and three aces, and grier contributed five total blocks. yale finished with a .396 hitting percentage and 47 kills, compared with .149 and 31 kills for unh. the wildcats next travel to clemson, south carolina, to face furman on september 18. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire durham durham, new hampshire unh volleyball yale college sports

nh-upper-valley-haven-year-round-shelter.excerpt: The 20-bed center in White River Junction will replace a smaller seasonal Lebanon shelter and serve the broader cross-border region.
nh-upper-valley-haven-year-round-shelter.text: upper valley haven readies year-round shelter serving new hampshire region the 20-bed center in white river junction will replace a smaller seasonal lebanon shelter and serve the broader cross-border region. the upper valley haven is preparing to open a 20-bed, year-round emergency shelter and daytime resource center in white river junction, expanding services for people across the new hampshire-vermont border region. the patrick and marcelle leahy shelter and resource center at 608 north main street is expected to welcome its first guests in the coming weeks. the facility replaces a seasonal shelter in lebanon, new hampshire, that offered 14 beds for roughly three months each winter. that building is slated for demolition as part of a roundabout project. during its most recent season, 66 people stayed for a combined total of about 100 nights, while an average of two people per night were turned away because space was unavailable. the haven raised $10.2 million for the new center and expects it to provide about 5,000 overnight stays annually for roughly 100 people. year-round operation is intended to reduce weather-driven gaps and connect guests with support during daytime hours. for new hampshire communities in the upper valley, the opening adds nearby capacity as local providers contend with persistent housing insecurity and limited emergency beds. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire lebanon upper valley, new hampshire and vermont upper valley lebanon housing homelessness

nh-volunteers-september-11-day-of-servic.excerpt: Granite United Way organized projects at four sites as residents observed the attacks' 25th anniversary with hands-on community work.
nh-volunteers-september-11-day-of-servic.text: new hampshire volunteers mark september 11 through service granite united way organized projects at four sites as residents observed the attacks' 25th anniversary with hands-on community work. dozens of volunteers gathered at the new hampshire state veterans cemetery in boscawen on friday for a national day of service marking 25 years since the september 11 attacks, according to the concord monitor. participants cleaned headstones, cleared brush and worked around the cemetery grounds. granite united way coordinated about 130 volunteers across four locations. in addition to the cemetery project, teams served at the new hampshire veterans home in tilton, worked with communities for alcohol- and drug-free youth in plymouth and assembled responder-support kits on the seacoast. the projects linked remembrance with practical assistance for veterans, first responders and community organizations. september 11 has been federally recognized as a national day of service and remembrance since 2009. friday's work offered participants a local way to honor the nearly 3,000 people killed in the 2001 attacks while supporting institutions that serve new hampshire residents year-round. organizers emphasized that the anniversary can be observed not only through ceremonies, but also through acts that strengthen local communities and carry the day's lessons into the future. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh boscawen boscawen, nh new hampshire september 11 volunteers granite united way boscawen

nh-webster-elementary-food-drive-stark-p.text: stark park drive will restock webster elementary food pantry saturday manchester residents can bring food and hygiene supplies to a drive-through collection at stark park from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. september 12. a drive-through collection at manchester’s stark park will gather food and personal-care supplies for the webster elementary school pantry on saturday, september 12. the event is scheduled from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at 550 river road. ward 1 school board member julie turner and alderman bryce kaw-uh are organizing the second annual drive. the pantry opened at webster elementary in 2024 with support from a local hannaford supermarket, and last year’s collection was created to help refill its shelves. organizers are requesting soap, toothpaste, shampoo, rice, pasta, spaghetti sauce, cereal, canned vegetables and fruit, beans, macaroni and cheese, and individually packaged foods such as granola bars. the broad list is designed to support both household meals and items students can use easily. manchester ink link reported that families experiencing food insecurity can contact their school social worker for help connecting with food resources. families may also apply online for free or reduced-price school meals. the collection gives residents a direct way to support a school-based resource before the academic year moves deeper into fall. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire nh manchester manchester, nh manchester food pantry webster elementary stark park

nh-west-lebanon-dry-bridge-year-closure-.text: west lebanon dry bridge closes monday for yearlong replacement the 77-year-old route 12a span closes monday for demolition and replacement, redirecting roughly 10,000 daily vehicles to interstate 89. west lebanon’s route 12a dry bridge is scheduled to close at 7 a.m. monday, september 14, beginning a yearlong demolition and replacement project on one of the city’s busiest local connections. the 77-year-old span links south main street with the route 12a shopping district and carries about 10,000 vehicles on a typical day. the city’s posted detour will send plainfield-bound traffic up seminary hill to interstate 89 north and exit 20. drivers traveling the opposite direction are directed to i-89 south, exit 19 and miracle mile. officials are urging motorists to use the signed route instead of smaller local roads, which became congested during an emergency closure in march 2025. pedestrians and bicyclists will retain access through a temporary footbridge next to the construction site, although cyclists are encouraged to dismount while crossing. the closure gives contractors room to remove the deteriorated 145-foot bridge and start building its replacement. because the span also serves buses, emergency vehicles, workers and shoppers, the advance notice and temporary crossing are intended to reduce the disruption that accompanied last year’s sudden shutdown. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire west lebanon west lebanon, new hampshire west lebanon route 12a bridges traffic infrastructure

nh-white-mountains-foliage-outlook-2026.excerpt: Healthy canopies and improved moisture conditions could support bright color from late September into mid-October, depending on elevation and weather.
nh-white-mountains-foliage-outlook-2026.text: white mountains forecasters expect later, longer foliage season healthy canopies and improved moisture conditions could support bright color from late september into mid-october, depending on elevation and weather. fall color in new hampshire’s white mountains may arrive later than usual but last longer, according to regional foliage forecasters interviewed by the conway daily sun. forecasters pointed to healthy, full canopies and improved moisture after earlier drought conditions as reasons for optimism. they expect color to progress by elevation from late september into the middle of october rather than peak everywhere at once. the outlook remains weather-dependent. warm sunny days followed by crisp nights can help leaves produce vivid reds and oranges, while a hurricane, severe storm or strong wind event could remove leaves before peak color. daylight loss, temperature and moisture all influence the timing. for visitors and tourism businesses, a longer progression can spread travel across several weekends. routes through the kancamagus scenic highway, pinkham notch, franconia and kinsman notch are among the areas expected to draw foliage traffic. the forecast is not a guarantee; travelers should check current foliage maps and local conditions before choosing a destination. new-hampshire nh white mountains, new hampshire fall foliage white mountains tourism weather

nh-white-mountains-saturday-hiking-windo.excerpt: A rough Friday above treeline is forecast to give way to sunshine, warmer temperatures and lighter winds across New Hampshire’s mountains.
nh-white-mountains-saturday-hiking-windo.text: saturday brings a better white mountains hiking window a rough friday above treeline is forecast to give way to sunshine, warmer temperatures and lighter winds across new hampshire’s mountains. hikers planning a white mountains outing this weekend face sharply different conditions from one day to the next, with slick trails and powerful summit winds friday followed by a much calmer saturday. the mount washington observatory’s recreational forecast said muddy surfaces will linger through friday. temperatures at higher elevations may fall below freezing early, while patchy summit fog reduces visibility. a wind chill advisory for the higher summits remains in effect until 10 p.m., and northwest gusts above hurricane force are possible in the morning. valley and notch gusts could reach 30 mph. saturday is expected to bring the best window for longer trips. sunshine, warmer air and light winds are forecast across elevations. the observatory advised hikers to carry enough water and sun protection despite the cooler start to the weekend. sunday should stay warm and mostly dry for much of the day, but moderate west winds and summit fog are expected to return at higher elevations. clouds will increase, with a chance of showers and isolated thunder sunday afternoon. a lightweight rain layer remains a sensible addition even for outings that begin under favorable skies. new-hampshire new-hampshire new hampshire new hampshire white mountains white mountains, nh white mountains hiking weather mount washington observatory

nj-vineland-dataone-unpermitted-generato.text: new jersey fines vineland data center $1.07 million over unpermitted generators state inspectors found 62 large natural-gas generators operating without required air permits at the dataone site, the largest data-center enforcement penalty in new jersey history. new jersey environmental regulators have fined the operator of a large artificial-intelligence data center in vineland $1.07 million after inspectors found 62 natural-gas generators operating without required state permits. the new jersey department of environmental protection said its july 29 inspection found 1,982-kilowatt stationary generators that were not present during a december 2025 inspection. state rules require a preconstruction permit and operating certificate for generators rated at 37 kilowatts or more, according to the department’s enforcement order. the order directs dataone to apply for the permits immediately and obtain them within 45 days or stop operating the generators. gov. mikie sherrill called the penalty the largest enforcement action against a data center in new jersey history. dep commissioner ed potosnak said the action was intended to show that large facilities must comply with pollution laws. dataone told news 12 new jersey that it disputes the state’s characterization of the temporary generators but will apply for the air permits and is discussing the site’s planned transition to fuel cells. the company is building the cumberland county campus for nebius, with microsoft as a reported infrastructure partner. the case adds a major regulatory test for new jersey’s fast-growing data-center industry. natural-gas generators emit carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide, and the state has recently adopted additional reporting and utility rules aimed at tracking the sector’s energy and water demands. tech tech tech nj vineland vineland, new jersey new jersey vineland data centers artificial northeast-air-traffic-outage-flight-disr.text: northeast flights resume after air-traffic outage, but delays linger new york-area airports returned to service tuesday after a communications failure and severed backup fiber line disrupted flights across the region. hundreds of cancellations at newark and philadelphia contributed to a backlog that was still affecting travelers. flights were operating again at new york city-area airports tuesday, but delays and cancellations continued after a communications outage at a key federal aviation administration air-traffic facility in philadelphia disrupted travel across the northeast, the associated press reported. the faa's primary communications circuit failed monday morning. when controllers tried to switch to the backup, they found that its fiber-optic line had been cut by railroad construction workers, according to the faa's account cited by ap. controllers were left without radar or communications for hours. more than 600 flights into and out of newark liberty international airport were canceled monday, and more than 200 were canceled at philadelphia international airport. no commercial flights landed at newark from about 9:40 a.m. until shortly after 5:20 p.m. monday, ap reported, citing flightradar24. disruptions also affected laguardia and kennedy airports. by early tuesday, newark still showed about 40 delays and nearly 60 cancellations on flightaware. transportation secretary sean duffy said it would take time to clear the remaining delays, so travelers were advised to check directly with their airlines before heading to the airport. the incident involved two communication paths failing in succession: the primary circuit failed first, and the backup fiber had already been severed during construction in new jersey. ap reported that amtrak and new jersey transit gave differing accounts about which railroad's crew was working in the area. new-england new-england new england ny new york nyc-doordash-delivery-worker-settlement-.excerpt: The agreement will send more than $115 million to over 260,000 workers after a city investigation found underpayments, late payments and unpaid work.
nyc-doordash-delivery-worker-settlement-.text: new york city wins $131.5 million doordash settlement for delivery workers the agreement will send more than $115 million to over 260,000 workers after a city investigation found underpayments, late payments and unpaid work. new york city officials announced a $131.5 million settlement with doordash that will compensate more than 260,000 delivery workers and resolve a city investigation into alleged violations of the city's delivery-worker pay laws. the department of consumer and worker protection said its review found that doordash failed to pay some workers for completed work, paid others late and excluded categories of trip and on-call time when calculating compensation. the investigation examined 152 million payments and 110 million hours of work between april 2022 and june 2026. more than $115 million of the agreement will go directly to workers, while more than $16 million will cover civil penalties and other costs, according to the mayor's office. the city said payments will begin this fall, with personalized notices planned for workers identified as having experienced underpayments during the main review period. the settlement also creates a monitoring system intended to help the city detect future violations. the workers justice project and the workers' algorithm observatory are expected to develop software that lets workers capture information shown in the doordash app about their trips and pay and share it with city officials. doordash said in a statement that the errors involved technical problems and complicated deliveries, including trips that crossed city boundaries or were canceled or partially completed. the company acknowledged that workers should have been paid in full and on time, while the city described the agreement as its largest worker settlement. new-york new-york new york ny new york new york city, new york new york new york city doordash delivery workers labor

providence-housing-primary.excerpt: The city’s debate over rent control, zoning and new construction is giving Rhode Island voters a local test of a national housing dilemma.
providence-housing-primary.text: providence housing fight puts affordability at the center of the mayoral primary the city’s debate over rent control, zoning and new construction is giving rhode island voters a local test of a national housing dilemma. housing affordability has become the central issue in providence’s mayoral primary, where candidates are offering different answers to rising rents and a shortage of new construction. the wall street journal reported that mayor brett smiley is emphasizing additional housing production and zoning changes, while state rep. david morales is arguing for rent control as a way to offer more immediate relief to current renters. the disagreement reflects a familiar policy tension: measures intended to protect tenants today can affect the incentives developers face when deciding whether to build tomorrow. both sides are presenting their approach as a response to the same pressure on household budgets. the result will offer an early indication of how providence voters weigh short-term protections against longer-term supply and development strategies. new-england ri providence providence, ri rhode island providence housing politics

qualcomm-amazon-ai-chips.text: qualcomm and amazon deepen ai-chip ties in multibillion-dollar agreement the deal expands amazon’s custom-chip push and gives qualcomm another foothold in the infrastructure behind ai services. qualcomm and amazon announced an agreement tuesday centered on ai data-center chips and high-speed optical connectivity, adding another major partnership to the race to build ai infrastructure. reuters reported that amazon will purchase qualcomm’s ai data-center products and that qualcomm granted amazon warrants valued at about $4 billion. qualcomm shares rose after the announcement. the companies said they will work on inference chips and connectivity technology. the arrangement also calls for qualcomm to expand its use of amazon web services while accelerating chip-design work. the partnership illustrates how cloud companies are building more of their own silicon while chip designers look beyond smartphones for growth. tech ma new england tech watch ai semiconductors amazon qualcomm
