rhode-island-mckee-foulkes-rematch-2026.text: rhode island governor primary rematch centers on bridge and trust incumbent dan mckee and helena foulkes are facing each other again, with the washington bridge crisis and state leadership at the center of the contest. rhode island gov. dan mckee and helena foulkes are meeting again in a democratic primary, four years after mckee narrowly defeated foulkes. the rematch is unfolding as voters continue to weigh the state’s handling of the washington bridge repairs. foulkes, a former cvs health executive, has outraised mckee and put significant advertising behind her challenge, according to the associated press. mckee is defending his record and emphasizing labor support as he seeks another term. the bridge’s partial closure, delays and cost concerns have become a central test of public confidence. the primary is scheduled for wednesday, sept. 9, and the result could set the direction of rhode island’s next statewide campaign. the race is also a test of whether voters treat infrastructure management as a defining leadership issue. both campaigns are asking democrats to view the state’s recent problems through a different lens: competence and continuity for mckee, or change for foulkes. new-england rhode-island rhode island ri providence rhode island rhode island politics governor washington bridge

rhode-island-primary-full-slate-2026.excerpt: Wednesday’s contest includes federal, state and local nominations, with Providence’s mayoral race and a large unaffiliated electorate adding to the stakes.
rhode-island-primary-full-slate-2026.text: rhode island primary tests more than the governor’s race wednesday’s contest includes federal, state and local nominations, with providence’s mayoral race and a large unaffiliated electorate adding to the stakes. rhode island’s wednesday primary will decide more than the closely watched democratic governor’s contest between dan mckee and helena foulkes, the associated press reported. the ballot includes contested nominations for u.s. senate, u.s. house, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, the state senate, the state house and providence mayor. polls close at 8 p.m. eastern, and unaffiliated voters may choose either party’s primary. about 359,000 of the state’s roughly 695,000 active registered voters were unaffiliated as of sept. 1, according to ap. the share makes participation by independent voters an important variable in both statewide and local races. the ap also reported that early and mail votes are mixed into results from rhode island’s 39 cities and towns rather than released in one front-loaded batch. that means the first returns may not show the full shape of a close contest. those counting rules make patience and careful reading of updates especially important on election night. new-england rhode-island rhode island ri rhode island rhode island primary election providence voting

rhode-island-primary-voter-guide-2026.excerpt: The state’s Sept. 9 primary will release results through 39 local jurisdictions, with early and mail ballots mixed into the night’s reporting.
rhode-island-primary-voter-guide-2026.text: what rhode island voters should know before wednesday’s primary the state’s sept. 9 primary will release results through 39 local jurisdictions, with early and mail ballots mixed into the night’s reporting. rhode island’s primary election is wednesday, sept. 9, after the state moved the contest away from the day after labor day to give cities and towns more time to prepare polling places. the associated press said rhode island’s 39 jurisdictions are expected to release results throughout the evening. early in-person and mail ballots are not necessarily reported at the beginning of the night, so the first numbers may not show the full shape of the vote. the democratic governor’s race between dan mckee and helena foulkes is the top statewide contest. the state also has congressional and legislative nominations on the ballot, with unaffiliated voters making up the largest registration group. that reporting structure means a close race may remain unsettled after the first wave of returns. voters looking for a quick result should watch the release schedule and remember that local totals can arrive at different speeds. new-england rhode-island rhode island ri rhode island rhode island primary election voting providence

rhode-island-providence-mayor-primary-ho.excerpt: Mayor Brett Smiley and state Rep. David Morales are offering competing answers to the city’s affordability crisis ahead of Wednesday’s Democratic primary.
rhode-island-providence-mayor-primary-ho.text: providence mayoral primary turns on rent control and housing growth mayor brett smiley and state rep. david morales are offering competing answers to the city’s affordability crisis ahead of wednesday’s democratic primary. providence voters are weighing sharply different housing strategies in wednesday’s democratic mayoral primary, where affordability has become the central issue, the wall street journal reported. incumbent mayor brett smiley is emphasizing new housing construction and growth. state rep. david morales, his challenger, is advocating rent control as a more immediate response for tenants facing high rents. the argument reflects a tension familiar across new england: additional supply may take years to affect prices, while stronger rent protections can change the economics developers consider when deciding whether to build. both campaigns are presenting their approach as a response to the same shortage and cost pressure. the primary will give providence voters a direct choice over whether city government should prioritize faster production, stronger tenant protections or a combination of both. the result could shape the city’s housing debate and influence the november campaign. that debate is especially consequential in a city where housing policy is a daily cost-of-living issue rather than an abstract planning question. new-england rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, ri rhode island providence housing mayor

ri-adam-greenman-pawtucket-mayor-primary.excerpt: Unofficial results showed Greenman ahead of Don Grebien 54% to 46%, setting up a likely transition after the incumbent’s 16 years in office.
ri-adam-greenman-pawtucket-mayor-primary.text: adam greenman defeats longtime pawtucket mayor in democratic primary unofficial results showed greenman ahead of don grebien 54% to 46%, setting up a likely transition after the incumbent’s 16 years in office. adam greenman defeated longtime pawtucket mayor don grebien in wednesday’s democratic primary, according to unofficial rhode island board of elections results reported by nbc 10 news. with all 28 reporting units submitting at least partial returns, greenman had 3,633 votes, or about 54%, while grebien had 3,055 votes, or about 46%. the totals remain unofficial until the canvass and certification process is complete. greenman, a former educator and nonprofit leader, campaigned on changes at city hall and focused on education, affordability, public safety and quality-of-life issues. grebien conceded and congratulated his challenger after serving as mayor since 2011. his current term will conclude after 16 years in the office. no republican candidate qualified for the mayoral ballot, according to the state candidate list cited by nbc 10. that could leave greenman without a major-party opponent in the november 3 general election, though the certified ballot will determine the final field. election officials will complete the official canvass before the result becomes final. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri pawtucket pawtucket, ri pawtucket adam greenman don grebien primary election

ri-amazing-america-250-history-series-20.excerpt: A regional history project traces Indigenous experience, religious liberty, the Gaspee affair and the First Rhode Island Regiment.
ri-amazing-america-250-history-series-20.text: rhode island history anchors new england’s america 250 story a regional history project traces indigenous experience, religious liberty, the gaspee affair and the first rhode island regiment. rhode island’s people, museums and historic sites play a central role in a new nbc 10 news project examining new england’s contribution to the american story ahead of the nation’s 250th anniversary. the series begins with indigenous history at the tomaquag museum and follows the state’s distinctive path toward independence. the reporting connects roger williams’ advocacy of religious liberty with the first baptist church in america in providence. it also revisits the 1772 burning of the british customs schooner gaspee in narragansett bay, an act that came more than a year before the boston tea party. rhode island formally renounced allegiance to king george iii on may 4, 1776, two months before the declaration of independence. the series also highlights the first rhode island regiment, whose black, indigenous and white soldiers fought in the 1778 battle of rhode island. additional stops include the nathanael greene homestead in coventry and the independent man atop the state house. together, the locations show how the state’s history extends beyond a single anniversary: museums, reenactors and preservation groups continue interpreting whose experiences shaped the region and how those stories are passed to new generations. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island rhode island rhode island america 250 roger williams gaspee first rhode island regiment

ri-apple-cinemas-providence-place-overha.excerpt: The theater operator says upgraded auditoriums, immersive screens and entertainment attractions are planned for the mall complex.
ri-apple-cinemas-providence-place-overha.text: apple cinemas plans multimillion-dollar providence place overhaul the theater operator says upgraded auditoriums, immersive screens and entertainment attractions are planned for the mall complex. apple cinemas has announced a multimillion-dollar overhaul of its providence place theater, outlining new seating, projection and entertainment features for the downtown mall complex. nbc 10 wjar reported that every auditorium is slated to receive luxury recliners. the plan also calls for an acx auditorium with dolby atmos sound and 4k projection, a screenx format that extends images onto side walls, and an existing imax auditorium upgraded to laser projection. beyond movies, the operator is planning immersive bowling and is considering interactive attractions built around archery, slingshot and drift-car experiences. self-service beer and wine would be added only if the necessary approvals are obtained. apple cinemas did not provide a completion date, so the announcement is best understood as a project plan rather than a finished renovation. if delivered, the changes would broaden the site from a conventional multiplex into a mixed entertainment venue. the timeline, final attraction list and any alcohol service remain subject to construction, permitting and other approvals. new-england ri providence, rhode island providence apple cinemas providence place entertainment

ri-blaze-orange-hunting-season-september.excerpt: Visitors to state management areas and undeveloped state parks must wear at least 200 square inches of fluorescent orange from September 12 through February 28.
ri-blaze-orange-hunting-season-september.text: rhode island blaze-orange rule begins as archery season opens visitors to state management areas and undeveloped state parks must wear at least 200 square inches of fluorescent orange from september 12 through february 28. rhode island’s seasonal fluorescent-orange requirement takes effect saturday, september 12, as archery hunting gets underway on public lands. the department of environmental management says the rule applies through february 28 to people entering state management areas and undeveloped state parks during hunting season. visitors must wear at least 200 square inches of solid fluorescent orange, an amount that can generally be met with an orange hat or vest. the requirement is intended to make hikers, dog walkers, birders and other outdoor users more visible to hunters sharing the same properties. archery hunters are exempt from the orange requirement while participating in archery deer season, according to dem. other rules can vary by activity and season, so hunters and recreational visitors should review current regulations before entering public land. the agency’s reminder is especially relevant during the early fall overlap between popular hiking weather and expanding hunting activity. bright clothing, awareness of posted notices and keeping pets under close control can reduce avoidable conflicts. dem also advises visitors to know the boundaries and allowed uses of the property they plan to enter. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri rhode island hunting season blaze orange rhode island dem outdoor safety

ri-blood-center-childhood-cancer-donors-.excerpt: The center says many young cancer patients depend on blood components and is promoting a September 14 community drive in Warwick.
ri-blood-center-childhood-cancer-donors-.text: rhode island blood center urges donors during childhood cancer campaign the center says many young cancer patients depend on blood components and is promoting a september 14 community drive in warwick. the rhode island blood center is using childhood cancer awareness month to remind residents that transfusions are a routine and often urgent part of treatment for many young cancer patients. more than 15,000 children and adolescents are diagnosed with cancer in the united states each year, the center said. chemotherapy, surgery and complications from treatment can create a need for red cells, platelets or plasma. the center estimates that more than 60% of people are eligible to donate blood, while only about 3% do so. nbc 10 highlighted the family of carrigan nelson, who was diagnosed with osteosarcoma shortly after her 18th birthday. her family said blood products helped extend her life during seven years of treatment before her death in 2025. they are encouraging eligible donors to give in her memory and for other patients. a community back-to-school blood drive is scheduled for monday, september 14, from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. at the crowne plaza in warwick. donor eligibility and appointment details are available from the rhode island blood center. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri warwick warwick, ri blood donation childhood cancer warwick rhode island blood center

ri-boston-kidnapping-suspect-arrested-20.excerpt: Troopers stopped a vehicle in East Greenwich and arrested a 27-year-old Lawrence man after Massachusetts State Police issued an alert tied to a Boston incident.
ri-boston-kidnapping-suspect-arrested-20.text: rhode island state police arrest man sought in boston kidnapping case troopers stopped a vehicle in east greenwich and arrested a 27-year-old lawrence man after massachusetts state police issued an alert tied to a boston incident. rhode island state police arrested a lawrence, massachusetts, man in east greenwich after massachusetts authorities issued an alert for a vehicle connected to a boston kidnapping investigation. troopers stopped the vehicle on new london turnpike at about 9:15 p.m. saturday and arrested ysael lara gonzalez, 27, the rhode island state police said in a sunday release. police said the investigation was conducted with the boston police department. gonzalez was charged with domestic-violence kidnapping, domestic-violence felony assault, disorderly conduct and two counts of possessing a prohibited weapon other than a firearm, according to the state police release. the charges are allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. police transported gonzalez to the rhode island state police’s wickford barracks for processing and held him pending arraignment in third district court. the release did not provide additional details about the boston incident. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri east greenwich east greenwich, rhode island rhode island east greenwich boston kidnapping police

ri-brown-3200-new-students-2026.excerpt: Orientation events in Providence led into Brown's 263rd Opening Convocation and the start of fall classes.
ri-brown-3200-new-students-2026.text: brown welcomes more than 3,200 new students for 2026-27 orientation events in providence led into brown's 263rd opening convocation and the start of fall classes. brown university welcomed more than 3,200 new undergraduate, graduate and medical students to providence for the 2026-27 academic year. a week of orientation activities began september 2 and culminated in the university's 263rd opening convocation on september 8, with fall classes beginning afterward. the schedule mixed practical introductions with campus traditions. new students attended resource fairs and tours, learned about brown's open curriculum and took part in dance events, games and informal music sessions. the program was designed to help students find academic support, understand university expectations and begin building connections before coursework accelerated. the arriving group adds thousands of new residents to college hill and the broader providence community at the start of the fall term. events also introduced students to the city, including waterfire and other local activities. brown's first-week program spans several schools and degree levels, so the shared ceremonies provide one of the few moments when the incoming undergraduate, graduate and medical cohorts begin the year together. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island brown university providence students orientation higher education

ri-brown-field-hockey-bu-shootout-2026.excerpt: The Bears tied the game in the fourth quarter and won a shootout 3-2, with Mia Karine Myklebust supplying the deciding attempt.
ri-brown-field-hockey-bu-shootout-2026.text: brown field hockey erases two-goal deficit to beat boston university the bears tied the game in the fourth quarter and won a shootout 3-2, with mia karine myklebust supplying the deciding attempt. brown field hockey rallied from two goals down in the fourth quarter and defeated boston university 5-4 after a shootout friday at goldberger family field. the bears trailed 4-2 with 13:40 remaining before sophia clark and kate siedem scored 59 seconds apart to force overtime. neither team scored in the extra period, sending the match to a shootout. kiersten smith, julia lattuada and mia karine myklebust converted for brown, with myklebust producing the deciding goal in a 3-2 shootout advantage. goalkeeper ellie parker matched a career high with 10 saves after boston university controlled long stretches of possession. grace almeida, smith, siedem and clark accounted for brown’s four regulation goals. the terriers had opened a 2-0 lead in the second quarter, and later moved ahead 4-2 early in the fourth before the comeback. brown improved to 2-1 and earned its second straight victory. the bears are next scheduled to travel to fairfield for another nonconference match. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, rhode island brown university field hockey boston university mia karine myklebust providence

ri-brown-healthspan-alliance-37m-2026.excerpt: Brown University and Brown University Health will link laboratory work with clinical trials through a new Starr Foundation-backed partnership.
ri-brown-healthspan-alliance-37m-2026.text: brown launches $37 million alliance for aging research brown university and brown university health will link laboratory work with clinical trials through a new starr foundation-backed partnership. brown university and brown university health are launching an aging-research partnership backed by a $37 million investment from the starr foundation. the starr healthspan innovation alliance is designed to move discoveries from university laboratories into clinical trials across the health system. brown said the work will focus on age-associated diseases and on extending the years people remain healthy, rather than treating longevity as a single condition. funding will expand brown’s center on the biology of aging, support laboratory research and help recruit scientists in geroscience, the study of genetic, molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in aging. the health system’s clinical network is expected to provide a pathway for evaluating potential treatments with patients. the alliance matters regionally because it connects a major rhode island research university with the state’s largest health system. its announced aims include work relevant to cancer and dementia, but the partnership did not announce a specific new therapy or guarantee clinical outcomes. individual studies will still require their own scientific review, trial design and patient-safety oversight. new-england rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, rhode island brown university brown university health aging research clinical trials

ri-brown-human-milk-microrna-nih-study-2.excerpt: Dr. Meagan Barry will examine how maternal health conditions may change microRNAs in human milk and influence infant growth and immune development.
ri-brown-human-milk-microrna-nih-study-2.text: brown researcher wins nih grant to study human-milk micrornas dr. meagan barry will examine how maternal health conditions may change micrornas in human milk and influence infant growth and immune development. brown university researcher dr. meagan barry has received a national institutes of health award to investigate how a mother’s health may alter micrornas in human milk and affect infant development. barry is an assistant professor of emergency medicine and co-chair of the brown center for global health equity’s research subcommittee. human milk contains micrornas, small molecules that help regulate gene activity, but researchers still have limited evidence about how maternal conditions change those molecules or what the changes mean for infants. barry’s project will use samples and data from women and children in the philippines, focusing on mothers who are underweight or have parasitic infections and measuring infant weight gain and immune maturity. the award, identified by nih as 1k08hd118259-01a1, supports an early-career research program linking maternal health, milk biology and child outcomes. brown faculty jeffrey bailey and jennifer friedman are serving as co-mentors. the work could help clarify why breastfeeding benefits vary across settings and whether specific biological pathways could guide future nutrition or public-health interventions, particularly where maternal infections and undernutrition are common. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, rhode island brown university nih infant health human milk microrna

ri-brown-justin-trudeau-ogden-lecture-20.excerpt: The former Canadian prime minister will deliver Brown’s 106th Ogden Lecture on democracy, alliances and Canada-U.S. relations.
ri-brown-justin-trudeau-ogden-lecture-20.text: justin trudeau to speak at brown university on september 22 the former canadian prime minister will deliver brown’s 106th ogden lecture on democracy, alliances and canada-u.s. relations. former canadian prime minister justin trudeau will speak at brown university on tuesday, september 22, as part of the university’s stephen a. ogden jr. memorial lecture series. the 106th lecture is titled “leadership, democracy and the evolving global landscape.” brown said the discussion will examine democratic societies, international alliances and public life, including canada-u.s. relations, institutional trust and civic engagement. trudeau is also expected to reflect on diplomacy, economic growth and the pressures facing interconnected societies. trudeau served as canada’s 23rd prime minister from 2015 to 2025. his decade in office included the covid-19 pandemic, climate and childcare initiatives, indigenous-reconciliation policies and canada’s role in the international response to russia’s invasion of ukraine. the program begins at 5 p.m. and is free and open to the public, but tickets are required. brown will provide the location to registered attendees. the ogden series, established in 1965, brings speakers to campus to address international affairs. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, ri brown university justin trudeau canada public lecture

ri-brown-stonehill-mens-soccer-sanchez-2.excerpt: Nicholas Sanchez scored in the 59th minute and Graham Kois posted his second clean sheet as the Bears won their second straight.
ri-brown-stonehill-mens-soccer-sanchez-2.text: sanchez goal carries brown past stonehill 1-0 nicholas sanchez scored in the 59th minute and graham kois posted his second clean sheet as the bears won their second straight. nicholas sanchez scored his first brown goal in the 59th minute to lift the bears to a 1-0 victory over stonehill on friday night at stevenson-pincince field. carlo brown started the decisive move, lorenzo amaral delivered the final pass and sanchez placed his shot into the top corner beyond goalkeeper felix van der hagen. brown controlled much of the attacking play, finishing with a 23-9 advantage in shots and putting seven attempts on target. stonehill managed only one shot on goal. bears goalkeeper graham kois stopped it to secure his second clean sheet of the season, while the defense protected the narrow lead through the final half hour. the result gave brown a second consecutive win, improved its record to 3-1 and kept the team unbeaten at home. the bears are now 3-0 all time against stonehill, which fell to 2-2-2. brown will stay in providence for the next game of its four-match homestand, hosting in-state rival rhode island on tuesday, september 15, at 7 p.m. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island brown university men's soccer nicholas sanchez stonehill providence

ri-brown-water-polo-first-nwpc-win-iona-.excerpt: The Bears led from the first quarter in the conference’s first outdoor game at the New York Athletic Club.
ri-brown-water-polo-first-nwpc-win-iona-.text: brown water polo earns first nwpc win with 14-10 victory at iona the bears led from the first quarter in the conference’s first outdoor game at the new york athletic club. brown opened northeast water polo conference play with a 14-10 win over iona on saturday at the new york athletic club’s travers island pool in pelham, new york. the game was the conference’s first outdoor contest, and the bears improved to 5-1 overall and 1-0 in league play. brown took a 4-2 lead in the first quarter and stayed ahead the rest of the way. mac berry scored the opening goal, filip josipovic and ronland csendes each struck twice in the period, and freshman robert norell recorded his first college goal. csendes later completed his first hat trick of the season. dominik balla scored three times in the fourth quarter, raising his season total to 15. colton bell and hugo molnar also scored in the final period. goalkeeper dimitrios kratimenos made 14 saves through three quarters, and ryan miele added seven in the fourth. brown travels to california next weekend for four games in the fullerton area. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island brown university water polo iona nwpc

ri-child-advocate-child-protection-syste.excerpt: A review of 30 fatalities and 11 near-fatalities identified inconsistent screening, high caseloads and missed opportunities to connect families with help.
ri-child-advocate-child-protection-syste.text: rhode island child advocate calls for immediate child-protection changes a review of 30 fatalities and 11 near-fatalities identified inconsistent screening, high caseloads and missed opportunities to connect families with help. rhode island’s office of the child advocate says the state’s child-protection system needs immediate changes after a review identified persistent weaknesses in screening, staffing and prevention services. the review covered 30 fatalities and 11 near-fatalities involving children with current or prior department of children, youth and families contact. child advocate katelyn medeiros said reviewers found cases that should have been accepted for investigation but were screened out, along with families who sought help but were not connected to prevention services. the report contains 76 recommendations spanning child protective services practices, the support and response unit, oversight and longer-term system improvements. investigators also found caseloads above national best-practice levels and delays in responding to families within the department’s own timelines. medeiros said staffing is part of the problem but not the only answer; policy, law, regulation and internal systems also need better alignment. the findings describe a reform agenda rather than completed changes. accountability will depend on which recommendations dcyf accepts, the timeline for implementation and whether lawmakers or administrators provide the necessary authority and resources. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, rhode island dcyf child welfare rhode island office of the child advocate

ri-clinical-research-network-26-million-.excerpt: The five-year NIH award will fund a third phase of Advance RI-CTR, expanding research support, partnerships and community engagement.
ri-clinical-research-network-26-million-.text: $26 million grant renews statewide rhode island clinical-research network the five-year nih award will fund a third phase of advance ri-ctr, expanding research support, partnerships and community engagement. the national institutes of health has awarded $26 million to renew rhode island's statewide clinical and translational research hub for another five years. brown university hosts advance ri-ctr, which links academic institutions, health systems and community organizations to move discoveries from laboratories toward clinical and community use. the third phase will provide researchers with consultation in quantitative and qualitative methods, implementation science, artificial intelligence and digital health. it will also broaden regional and national partnerships, offer multiple funding mechanisms for emerging research leaders and expand access to data and other research resources. participating institutions include brown, the university of rhode island, brown university health, care new england and the providence va system. since 2016, the program says $11.2 million awarded to rhode island investigators has helped them secure another $132.4 million in public and private funding. it has supported 141 investigators, contributed to six commercial patents and trained more than 340 research mentors. the renewal is intended to deepen that infrastructure while giving community priorities a larger role in deciding which health questions move from research into practice. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence rhode island nih brown university advance ri-ctr medical research rhode island

ri-cranston-brayton-avenue-fire-2026.excerpt: Fire officials believe flames began outside a Brayton Avenue home before spreading inside; everyone escaped without injury.
ri-cranston-brayton-avenue-fire-2026.text: smoke alarms help cranston family escape early-morning fire fire officials believe flames began outside a brayton avenue home before spreading inside; everyone escaped without injury. a family escaped safely after smoke alarms alerted them to an early-morning fire at a home on brayton avenue in cranston, officials said. firefighters were called at about 3:30 a.m. tuesday to the property near rock hill drive. investigators believe the fire started outside the house and then spread into the building. crews brought the flames under control, and no injuries were reported. officials credited the working alarms with giving the occupants time to leave before conditions worsened. authorities did not immediately identify a specific ignition source or release an estimate of the damage. the investigation remains open. the response also underscores the role of working smoke alarms in detecting a fire before sleeping residents see or smell danger. fire-safety agencies generally advise testing alarms regularly and replacing units according to manufacturer guidance, but officials did not connect any broader warning to this specific incident. the immediate finding was straightforward: everyone inside got out safely. new-england ri cranston, rhode island cranston house fire smoke alarms public safety

ri-cranston-cooking-oil-theft-arrests-20.excerpt: A license-plate reader alert led officers to a van carrying about 100 gallons of used restaurant oil, police said.
ri-cranston-cooking-oil-theft-arrests-20.text: two men charged after cranston cooking-oil theft a license-plate reader alert led officers to a van carrying about 100 gallons of used restaurant oil, police said. cranston police arrested two new york men early friday after officers recovered about 100 gallons of used cooking oil that authorities say had been taken from a local restaurant. anyeson veras martinez, 26, and steven velez toribio, 29, were each charged with larceny under $1,500. police said a flock license-plate reader alerted officers at 1:57 a.m. to a white 2018 ford transit with a pennsylvania plate associated with cooking-oil thefts. a second alert placed the van near route 37. an officer located it at pj's pub on pontiac avenue and stopped it at about 2:20 a.m. according to police, the van smelled of cooking oil and contained residue, two large containers, a hose and a pump. investigators estimated the recovered oil's value at about $200. used restaurant oil can be processed into biofuel and other products, giving it a resale value that has made storage tanks a theft target. the charges are allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. police did not immediately say whether the case is connected to other reported thefts. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri cranston cranston, ri cranston cooking oil larceny license plate reader rhode island

ri-cranston-meth-seizure-2026.excerpt: Police say a vehicle search produced about 30 grams of suspected methamphetamine, prescription pills and drug paraphernalia.
ri-cranston-meth-seizure-2026.text: two face charges after cranston traffic-stop drug seizure police say a vehicle search produced about 30 grams of suspected methamphetamine, prescription pills and drug paraphernalia. two men face charges after a cranston traffic stop led police to seize suspected methamphetamine, prescription pills and drug paraphernalia, according to the department’s account reported by nbc 10 wjar. police said the stop occurred around 4:44 p.m. monday on wentworth avenue. officers allegedly saw drug paraphernalia in plain view and searched the vehicle, recovering about 30 grams of a substance that field-tested positive for methamphetamine, along with pills, a scale, a pipe and $90. the driver was identified as brandon pierpont, 33, of bellingham, massachusetts, and the passenger as miguel rodriguez, 28, of cranston. police said both had active domestic-violence warrants. pierpont also had a new hampshire extradition warrant tied to narcotics charges. pierpont faces several drug-related counts, including possession with intent to deliver, while rodriguez was charged with obstructing an officer and transferred to woonsocket police. the allegations and field-test result will be subject to the court process; charges do not establish guilt, and laboratory testing may be used to confirm the substance. new-england ri cranston, rhode island cranston police drug charges traffic stop

ri-cranston-underpass-flooding-2026-09-1.excerpt: Water filled the Oaklawn Avenue underpass during heavy rain Sunday, trapping vehicles below the bike-path bridge.
ri-cranston-underpass-flooding-2026-09-1.text: cranston underpass floods again as residents press for long-term fix water filled the oaklawn avenue underpass during heavy rain sunday, trapping vehicles below the bike-path bridge. heavy rain flooded the oaklawn avenue underpass in cranston on sunday, trapping vehicles below the bike-path bridge and renewing calls for a permanent solution, nbc 10 reported. the low-lying road between oaklawn avenue and wilbur avenue can fill with a foot or more of water during intense rain. a nearby worker told the station he has seen the underpass flood about 50 times over six years. residents said cars can become stranded quickly when the roadway is not closed before drivers reach the water. solar-powered warning lights have been installed, but some people told nbc 10 they rarely see them operating, especially during the day. the flooding has become a recurring safety and transportation problem rather than a one-time storm impact. drivers who enter the water risk damaging their vehicles and blocking access for emergency crews. the rhode island department of transportation, which maintains the bike-path bridge, said it has been in contact with cranston and is pursuing a federal emergency management agency grant. the city had not responded to the station’s request for comment. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri cranston cranston, rhode island rhode island cranston flooding weather

ri-cranston-west-2977-flags-911-2026.excerpt: The memorial outside Alumni Auditorium marks 25 years since the attacks and gives each person killed a visible place in the school display.
ri-cranston-west-2977-flags-911-2026.text: cranston west students plant 2,977 flags for september 11 victims the memorial outside alumni auditorium marks 25 years since the attacks and gives each person killed a visible place in the school display. students at cranston high school west planted 2,977 american flags outside alumni auditorium on thursday, creating a memorial for every person killed in the september 11, 2001, attacks. the school’s young americans for freedom chapter organized the display as part of the national “never forget” project. students and teachers said the field of flags gives a human scale to an event that happened before today’s high-school students were born. the installation comes as communities mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks. for students learning about september 11 as history rather than lived memory, the project turns the casualty count into a visible tribute spread across the school grounds. the flags are scheduled to remain in place through september 12. organizers described the display as both a remembrance and an invitation for students to ask questions about the victims, first responders and the long-term effects of the attacks. cranston west’s project is one of many local observances planned across new england for the anniversary. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island cranston cranston, ri cranston west september 11 memorial students

ri-democratic-attorney-general-primary-f.excerpt: Kim Ahern, Keith Hoffmann, Jason Knight and Joseph Solomon are on Wednesday’s primary ballot for the state’s top law-enforcement post.
ri-democratic-attorney-general-primary-f.text: four democrats compete to succeed rhode island attorney general peter neronha kim ahern, keith hoffmann, jason knight and joseph solomon are on wednesday’s primary ballot for the state’s top law-enforcement post. rhode island democrats are choosing among four candidates wednesday to succeed term-limited attorney general peter neronha, putting the statewide law-enforcement office at the center of the primary ballot. the candidates are kim ahern, a former prosecutor and state cannabis control commission chair; keith hoffmann, a former federal prosecutor and former policy director in the attorney general’s office; state rep. jason knight, a navy veteran, former prosecutor and defense lawyer; and state rep. joseph solomon jr., a former bail commissioner and warwick prosecutor. ocean state media reported that august polling produced different leaders and also found large undecided shares. neronha endorsed hoffmann, while ahern received support from massachusetts gov. maura healey and former u.s. rep. patrick kennedy. knight and solomon have emphasized their legal and legislative experience. rhode island’s attorney general prosecutes felony cases and misdemeanor appeals statewide because the state does not use county district attorneys. the office also handles civil-rights, environmental, labor and public-corruption matters. this report describes the contest without projecting an outcome; official election authorities will determine and report the result after votes are counted. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence rhode island rhode island primary attorney general kim ahern keith hoffmann

ri-doctor-ground-zero-medical-deployment.excerpt: Dr. Selim Suner led a Rhode Island disaster team whose mission shifted from treating survivors to caring for first responders.
ri-doctor-ground-zero-medical-deployment.text: rhode island doctor recalls medical deployment to ground zero dr. selim suner led a rhode island disaster team whose mission shifted from treating survivors to caring for first responders. dr. selim suner was at home in north kingstown with his infant son on september 11, 2001, before events drew him to rhode island hospital and then new york. as leader of the rhode island disaster medical assistance team, he helped mobilize a federal response unit for ground zero. suner told ocean state media that the team included physicians, nurses, paramedics and logistics specialists. its members initially expected to treat people rescued from the world trade center, but new york hospitals had already received the survivors by the time the rhode island group arrived. the mission shifted to caring for rescuers working amid smoke, debris and continuing fires. suner said the team treated thousands of police officers, firefighters, military personnel, construction workers, search-and-rescue members and working dogs during long shifts at the site. now a brown university physician, suner reflected on the deployment for the 25th anniversary of the attacks. his account places rhode island’s medical-response network within the broader recovery effort and records how quickly local clinicians moved from routine work to a disaster operation hundreds of miles away. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island north kingstown north kingstown, rhode island september 11 rhode island hospital disaster medicine first responders selim suner

ri-east-providence-rehoboth-110-story-me.text: east providence and rehoboth firefighters complete 110-story memorial climb crews from east providence and rehoboth climbed the equivalent of 110 stories in nearly 60 pounds of gear. firefighters from east providence and rehoboth completed a 110-story memorial stair climb friday at city view manor, honoring first responders who died during the september 11 attacks. it was the first year the neighboring rhode island and massachusetts departments organized the climb together. participants climbed the building's 11 flights ten times while wearing nearly 60 pounds of protective equipment. the repeated ascent matched the height of the world trade center towers and gave the public a physical reminder of the conditions firefighters faced. families and community members gathered at the property to watch and support the crews as they worked through the heat. organizers said they hope the joint climb becomes an annual tradition. donations associated with the event support the tunnel to towers foundation, which assists injured service members, first responders and families of those killed in the line of duty. the collaboration also linked two local departments whose members regularly train for high-rise rescues and other emergencies. friday's event focused on remembrance, shared service and the continuing impact of september 11 on fire departments across new england. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri east providence east providence, ri east providence rehoboth firefighters september 11 memorial stair climb

ri-energy-sense-smart-meter-app-2026.excerpt: The free Sense tool identifies household power draws through smart meters, offering more detail as distribution rates rise.
ri-energy-sense-smart-meter-app-2026.text: rhode island energy app gives customers real-time usage view the free sense tool identifies household power draws through smart meters, offering more detail as distribution rates rise. rhode island energy residential customers with smart meters can use a free app to see household electricity use in real time. the sense software analyzes voltage and amperage patterns at the meter, then estimates which appliances are running and how much they contribute to monthly costs. the tool can separate major loads such as refrigerators, air conditioners, laundry equipment and electric vehicles. customers can compare one month with another, watch total consumption and identify equipment that may be drawing power unexpectedly. it is designed as an awareness tool rather than a remote-control system. the added detail arrives as state regulators allow higher electric and gas distribution rates. more than $170 million in customer credits tied to ppl corporation’s acquisition commitments will temporarily soften the increase. utility advocates caution that information about consumption cannot by itself solve the broader affordability problem for households already limiting their use. still, device-level estimates can help customers find changes within their control, such as a malfunctioning heater or an inefficient appliance. the app does not alter the price of electricity, and its usefulness depends on a home having a compatible smart meter, but it gives customers more context than a bill showing only total kilowatt-hours. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island rhode island rhode island energy sense smart meters utility bills

ri-exeter-september-11-cemetery-ceremony.text: rhode island honors september 11 victims at exeter ceremony bells marked the four hijacked flights as state leaders and gold star families remembered rhode islanders killed in the attacks and later wars. rhode island held its principal september 11 remembrance friday at the rhode island veterans memorial cemetery in exeter, 25 years after the attacks, nbc 10 reported. bells sounded for each of the four hijacked flights as attendees gathered at the cemetery's wall of honor. rhode island state police colonel darnell weaver read the names of nine rhode islanders who were killed on september 11, 2001. the ceremony also recognized nine service members from the state who died in wars that followed the attacks. gold star families placed a wreath in remembrance, joining veterans, public officials, first responders and community members. the exeter observance was among ceremonies across the state, but its setting connected the civilian toll of the attacks with the military service and losses that followed. the anniversary gave families and residents a formal space to remember individual lives while teaching a generation born after 2001 why the day remains central to public memory. organizers framed the event around service, sacrifice and continued support for families carrying those losses. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri exeter exeter, ri rhode island september 11 exeter veterans remembrance

ri-federal-judge-restores-solar-for-all-.text: rhode island federal judge vacates epa shutdown of solar for all grants the ruling clears the way for the $7 billion clean-energy program to resume, including a $49.3 million allocation intended for rhode island. a rhode island federal judge has ruled that the environmental protection agency acted unlawfully when it terminated the solar for all grant program, setting aside the agency’s decision and sending the nationwide initiative back into legal effect. u.s. district judge mary s. mcelroy issued the decision friday in a case brought by the rhode island afl-cio, rhode island center for justice, solar businesses and other plaintiffs. the program was created under the 2022 inflation reduction act to expand solar access and lower energy costs for low- and moderate-income households. the court said congress intended the epa to keep administering grants that had already been obligated and that the agency lacked statutory authority to end the program. rhode island had been allocated $49.3 million through the state office of energy resources, but the money had been left in limbo after the epa’s august 2025 termination. the ruling does not set out a timetable for restarting the grants or specify whether existing recipients can proceed without new applications. the epa said it was reviewing the decision and considering an appeal, while rhode island officials said they need clarity from the federal government before moving ahead with the state’s allocation. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, rhode island rhode island solar energy clean energy federal courts epa

ri-foster-man-killed-scituate-motorcycle.text: foster motorcyclist, 22, killed in scituate crash police said the motorcycle collided with a tow truck exiting a driveway on tunk hill road late friday night. a 22-year-old man from foster died after his motorcycle collided with a tow truck on tunk hill road in scituate late friday, police said. the crash occurred at about 10 p.m. and closed the road while emergency crews and investigators worked at the scene. according to a witness account relayed by police, the motorcycle was traveling west when a tow truck began leaving a driveway with its emergency lights activated. the rider was unable to stop before striking the truck. he was pronounced dead at the scene. authorities had not released his name as of saturday morning. the tow-truck operator was taken to a hospital for treatment. police said their preliminary investigation indicates speed may have contributed to the collision, but no final determination has been announced. the investigation remains active. the new details identify the fatal outcome of the police response that drew a large presence to tunk hill road friday night. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island scituate scituate, rhode island scituate foster motorcycle crash public safety

ri-foulkes-defeats-mckee-governor-primar.text: helena foulkes defeats dan mckee in rhode island governor primary the former cvs executive defeated gov. dan mckee, ending his bid for a second full term amid frustration over the washington bridge. helena foulkes defeated rhode island gov. dan mckee in wednesday’s democratic primary, ending his campaign for a second full term and producing one of the night’s most significant incumbent losses. the former cvs and hudson’s bay executive turned a 2022 primary defeat into a victory in the rematch. mckee became the first governor in any state to lose a party primary since 2018 and the first sitting rhode island governor to be beaten in a primary in more than 30 years. the washington bridge dominated the campaign. the older westbound span was abruptly closed in 2023 after structural problems were found, and delays and costs associated with its replacement fueled commuter frustration. foulkes argued that the project reflected broader management failures, while mckee defended the closure as necessary for public safety. mckee conceded wednesday night and said his administration would support a smooth transition. foulkes now advances to the november 3 general election, where she will face the republican nominee and any qualified independent candidates. traffic continues on the newer bridge span while the replacement project proceeds. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, ri helena foulkes dan mckee rhode island primary governor

ri-georgiaville-pond-algae-advisory-lift.text: rhode island lifts georgiaville pond algae advisory after bloom clears state health and environmental officials lifted a recreational warning for georgiaville pond in smithfield while keeping a high-risk contact advisory in place for lower melville pond. rhode island health and environmental officials lifted their recommendation to avoid recreational activity at georgiaville pond in smithfield after testing indicated that the harmful algae bloom there had cleared. the rhode island department of environmental management and the state department of health said monday that the georgiaville advisory could be removed. the update follows water sampling and laboratory testing conducted as officials monitored conditions at the pond. the agencies continued to recommend avoiding all contact with lower melville pond in portsmouth, where recreational activity remains a high risk. the warning applies to people and pets and includes swimming, wading and other direct contact with the water. officials also advise against drinking water from the affected pond or eating fish taken from it. people who experience symptoms after possible exposure should seek medical advice. the agencies said conditions can change, so residents should check state advisories before returning to recreational waters. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island smithfield smithfield, rhode island rhode island smithfield water safety

ri-health-department-bat-roger-williams-.text: rhode island seeks visitors who contacted bat at providence zoo health officials say the chance of human exposure was low, but anyone who touched the bat at roger williams park zoo should call the state. the rhode island department of health is asking anyone who had direct contact with a bat at roger williams park zoo on or before august 24 to contact the state. the bat was seen near the zoo’s water-play area and was reported to health officials on friday, september 11. a zoo veterinarian assessed the episode as presenting a low risk of human exposure. the animal was safely discarded before it could be tested for rabies, and officials said the zoo had received no earlier reports involving the bat. because testing was not possible, the department is using the public notice to identify any person who may have touched the animal or had another form of direct contact that should be evaluated. ridoh said potentially exposed visitors should call its center for acute infectious disease epidemiology at 401-222-2577 on weekdays or 401-276-8046 after hours. the department notes that rabies can be prevented with post-exposure vaccination when treatment begins before symptoms appear. the request is limited to people with possible direct contact; officials did not characterize ordinary zoo attendance as an exposure. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island roger williams park zoo rhode island department of health rabies public health providence

ri-jessica-meir-brown-students-space-cha.text: astronaut jessica meir speaks with brown students from space the brown alumna connected with about 75 students and faculty from the international space station and gave a guided tour of the orbiting laboratory. nasa astronaut and brown university alumna jessica meir spoke remotely with about 75 brown students and faculty members from the international space station before the start of fall classes, the university said friday. the private session lasted about an hour and included a tour of the station's cupola observation module. meir described her path to becoming an astronaut and life aboard a laboratory orbiting roughly 250 miles above earth at about 17,000 miles per hour. brown planetary scientist jim head facilitated the conversation. nasa required specific details to remain private because the event was part of behavioral-health support provided to astronauts on long missions. meir graduated from brown in 1999 and joined nasa's astronaut corps in 2013. during her first mission in 2019, she and christina koch completed the first all-woman spacewalk. meir now commands spacex crew-12, which arrived at the station earlier in 2026 and is expected to return late this year. for students in providence, the call offered a direct view of scientific work in orbit and a rare chance to ask questions of an alumna leading a current space mission. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, ri rhode island brown university jessica meir nasa international space station

ri-jim-langevin-ai-oversight-2026.text: jim langevin calls for stronger ai oversight in rhode island the former congressman says transparency and safeguards should advance alongside ai adoption and workforce training. former u.s. representative jim langevin is urging stronger oversight of artificial intelligence as rhode island expands education and policy work around the technology. langevin, now the distinguished chair of the institute for cybersecurity and emerging technologies at rhode island college, said safeguards and transparency should keep pace with rapid adoption. langevin led rhode island’s ai task force, which released recommendations earlier this year. he is also considering joining a government advisory board at openai, according to nbc 10 news. his comments place the state’s debate within a broader national discussion over how governments should address risks without closing off useful applications in education, public services and business. rhode island college’s cybersecurity and emerging-technologies program now serves more than 500 students, giving the policy discussion a local workforce dimension. langevin’s position combines experience in congress with the institute’s focus on training and research. no specific new rhode island regulation was announced, but his call adds momentum to efforts to translate task-force recommendations into practical rules. the central question is how to require accountability from developers and users while preserving room for responsible innovation. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island artificial intelligence jim langevin rhode island college policy

ri-johnston-school-bus-protest-2026.text: johnston parents rally as school-bus delays and long rides continue families say communication and routing problems persist weeks after the district began working with a new transportation provider. johnston parents rallied outside town hall ahead of a school committee meeting, saying students continue to face long rides, delays and limited communication under the district’s new bus provider. wjar reported that families have raised concerns about zum since the school year began. district and company officials have said service is improving, but parents at the rally said the changes have not gone far enough. some middle-school students said they must wake up especially early because their buses first transport high-school students. other students have arrived well before class and waited in school gymnasiums for as long as an hour after the district separated routes serving two elementary schools. the dispute is now about more than isolated late buses: families want clear responsibility, dependable pickup times and direct updates when routes change. the school committee and provider have not announced a final resolution. performance over the coming days will show whether route adjustments reduce delays or whether johnston needs a broader transportation plan. new-england ri johnston, rhode island rhode island johnston schools transportation

ri-juvenile-charged-ramos-killing-2026.text: juvenile charged with murder in providence killing of joseph ramos police say a 17-year-old was arraigned in family court tuesday after an investigation into the may shooting death of the 20-year-old. a 17-year-old was charged with murder tuesday in connection with the may shooting death of 20-year-old joseph ramos in providence, city officials said. according to wjar, the teenager was arraigned in family court after providence police detectives identified the youth during their investigation. authorities did not release the defendant’s name because the person was a juvenile when the alleged crime occurred. officers found ramos on swift street near silver spring street shortly after 2:15 a.m. on may 11. he was taken to rhode island hospital and later pronounced dead. police said he had been riding a three-wheeled motor bike before the shooting. another defendant, charles ortiz, had previously been charged in the case. wjar reported tuesday that ortiz entered a no-contest plea to conspiracy and drive-by shooting and that other charges, including murder, were dropped. the new juvenile charge is an allegation; guilt must be established in court. police credited the rhode island attorney general’s office with assisting the investigation. new-england ri providence, rhode island rhode island providence courts public safety

ri-labor-day-weekend-dui-arrests-2026.text: rhode island police report 60 dui arrests over holiday weekend the statewide count covered enforcement by 38 municipal departments and state police from friday afternoon through early tuesday. law-enforcement agencies across rhode island reported 60 arrests on suspicion of driving under the influence during the labor day weekend. the rhode island police chiefs association said the count covered the period from noon friday, september 4, through 6 a.m. tuesday, september 8. nbc 10 reported that the total combined enforcement by all 38 municipal police departments and rhode island state police. the association presented the figure as the result of coordinated holiday patrols. the number was one higher than the 59 dui arrests the organization reported for the same holiday period in 2025. an arrest is an allegation, and each case proceeds separately through the courts. holiday weekends typically bring heavier travel and added impaired-driving enforcement. the newly released statewide tally does not by itself show whether alcohol-related crashes increased or decreased, but it provides a verified measure of the number of suspected impaired drivers taken into custody during the four-day operation. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence rhode island rhode island dui labor day public safety

ri-lower-melville-pond-algae-bloom-2026-.text: rhode island health officials warn against contact with lower melville pond ridoh issued an advisory for lower melville pond in portsmouth because of a harmful algae bloom and urged people to keep pets away from the water. the rhode island department of health advised the public monday to avoid contact with lower melville pond in portsmouth because of a harmful algae bloom, coastal abc reported. the warning covers swimming, fishing and boating in the pond while the bloom is present. health officials said cyanobacteria can produce toxins that harm people and animals. residents were urged not to drink the water, eat fish caught there or allow pets to enter it. anyone who comes into contact with the pond should rinse off, and pets should be washed with clean water. ridoh lifted a separate algae-related advisory for georgiaville pond in smithfield. the change does not apply to lower melville pond, where the department’s current guidance remains to avoid contact until officials determine conditions are safe. ridoh’s distinction between the two ponds means residents should check the exact waterbody named in any advisory before returning to recreational use. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island portsmouth portsmouth, rhode island portsmouth lower melville pond algae bloom public health

ri-manville-back-to-school-clothing-driv.text: manville volunteers prepare back-to-school clothes for local children the manville share shack and pretty cares are sorting donated clothing for a free community distribution planned for next weekend. volunteers with the manville share shack are collecting and sorting back-to-school clothing for rhode island children whose families need help starting the academic year. founders annette and tom briand organized the effort with pretty cares inc., a woonsocket nonprofit. the enrico caruso club in lincoln donated space on labor day so volunteers could bring the collection together, assess donations and prepare items for distribution. the organizers used social media to connect with both donors and families. the request focused on practical school clothing, turning individual contributions into a coordinated community supply rather than a conventional resale operation. the clothing is expected to be distributed at a free community event next weekend. organizers had not published a final count of donated items or participating families in the source report, but the sorting effort was already underway. the drive extends the share shack’s neighborhood model: residents leave usable goods and others take what they need, with no charge and a focus on keeping support local. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island lincoln lincoln, ri manville lincoln clothing drive back to school

ri-martinez-youngs-ward-one-primary-2026.text: miguel martinez youngs defeats providence ward 1 incumbent nbc 10 news reported that the former city council policy official defeated councilor john goncalves in wednesday’s primary. miguel martinez youngs defeated incumbent providence city councilor john goncalves in the ward 1 primary, nbc 10 news reported thursday. the result changes representation for a district that includes fox point, wayland square and college hill. martinez youngs previously served as a deputy director of policy for the city council, giving him experience with the institution he is seeking to join. goncalves entered the contest as the sitting ward 1 councilor. nbc 10’s initial report did not include vote totals or a detailed breakdown by precinct. the outcome was one of several changes produced by rhode island’s september 9 local and statewide primaries. as with other election-night results, official certification remains the responsibility of election authorities; the news report described martinez youngs as the winner after the wednesday vote. ward-level council races directly shape decisions on zoning, neighborhood services, transportation and the city budget. for residents of fox point, wayland square and college hill, the transition therefore matters beyond the campaign itself. the next steps include completion of the election process and preparations for the general-election ballot and the term that follows. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island providence ward 1 miguel martinez youngs john goncalves primary election

ri-maternal-care-postpartum-support-gaps.text: maternal-care report highlights postpartum support gaps for rhode island a harris poll and babyscripts report is prompting local questions about follow-up, access and continuity after childbirth. a new national maternal-health report is prompting questions about how consistently rhode island families receive support from pregnancy through the postpartum period. the harris poll and digital maternal-health company babyscripts focused on whether patients feel heard, can obtain help and remain connected to care after delivery. rinewstoday used the findings to examine gaps that can persist even when a patient asks for assistance. the report emphasizes continuity across the full maternal-care timeline, rather than treating childbirth as the end of routine support. it also highlights the importance of clear follow-up, accessible treatment pathways and communication between patients and clinicians. the findings do not provide a rhode island-specific performance score, but they offer practical questions for the state’s hospitals, insurers and public-health agencies. those include how quickly postpartum concerns are assessed, whether referrals lead to actual appointments and how families are supported between scheduled visits. the local relevance is especially clear for mental-health concerns, which may emerge or intensify after a family leaves the hospital. the report’s central message is that asking for help should begin a reliable care process, not leave patients to navigate disconnected services alone. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island providence providence, rhode island maternal health postpartum care the harris poll rhode island health

ri-middletown-fatal-dui-child-crash-char.excerpt: Police identified the driver in Wednesday’s West Main Road crash and filed felony DUI and reckless-driving charges after a child died and another passenger was seriously injured.
ri-middletown-fatal-dui-child-crash-char.text: driver charged with fatal dui after middletown crash kills child police identified the driver in wednesday’s west main road crash and filed felony dui and reckless-driving charges after a child died and another passenger was seriously injured. a bronx man has been charged with driving under the influence and reckless driving after a fiery middletown crash killed a child younger than 3 and seriously injured another passenger, police said. the new charges are a material update to the crash investigation first reported wednesday. police identified the driver as 32-year-old jerry bonilla. he faces counts including dui resulting in death, dui resulting in serious bodily injury, driving to endanger resulting in death and driving to endanger resulting in injury. at a thursday arraignment, a judge set surety bail at $500,000 and ordered bonilla held at the adult correctional institutions. authorities said portsmouth police attempted to stop the sedan at about 1:20 a.m. on west main road near mill lane after recording it at 58 mph in a 45-mph zone. police said the vehicle accelerated to roughly 80 to 90 mph. the portsmouth officer ended the attempted stop near union street and alerted middletown police. the sedan later struck a utility pole and stone wall near linden park and caught fire, investigators said. the child died and another occupant suffered serious injuries. the charges are allegations, and bonilla is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. the crash remains under investigation. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri middletown middletown, ri middletown fatal crash dui charges west main road

ri-middletown-west-main-road-fatal-crash.text: middletown crash kills back-seat passenger, sends two to hospital police say a southbound vehicle hit a stone wall and utility pole before catching fire near linden park early thursday. one person died and two others were taken to rhode island hospital after a vehicle crashed and caught fire on west main road in middletown early thursday, police said. officers responded at about 1:20 a.m. to the area near linden park. investigators said the vehicle was traveling south when it struck a stone wall and a utility pole, then ignited. first responders removed the driver and a front-seat passenger and transported both to the hospital. a passenger in the back seat could not be removed and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to nbc 10 wjar’s report on the police investigation. authorities had not released the names of the occupants or the conditions of the two survivors when the report was published. police also had not announced what may have caused the vehicle to leave the road. the crash remains under investigation. residents and drivers in the area should follow any temporary traffic controls while investigators and utility crews complete their work near the damaged pole. further information is expected after notifications and the initial reconstruction are complete. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri middletown middletown, ri middletown west main road fatal crash rhode island hospital

ri-morales-defeats-smiley-providence-pri.text: david morales ousts providence mayor brett smiley in democratic primary the 27-year-old democratic socialist defeated incumbent mayor brett smiley and has no listed opponent in november. david morales defeated incumbent providence mayor brett smiley in wednesday’s democratic primary, ending smiley’s bid for a second term and positioning the 27-year-old challenger to become the city’s next mayor. morales identifies as a democratic socialist and received endorsements from u.s. sen. bernie sanders, u.s. rep. ro khanna and several labor unions. he built his campaign around housing affordability, public schools and a proposal to cap rent increases. smiley, 47, highlighted housing construction, lower crime and the city’s return to control of providence schools after years of state administration. the policy contrast sharpened around rent stabilization: smiley vetoed an ordinance in april, while morales said he would work with the city council to pass and enforce such a measure early in his administration. nbc 10 reported that morales has no listed opponent for the november 3 election after republican david talan was no longer shown on the ballot. barring a new ballot development, the democratic primary victory makes morales the presumptive next mayor of rhode island’s capital. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri providence providence, ri david morales brett smiley providence mayor

ri-newport-pier-one-coast-guard-cutters-.excerpt: A $271.2 million contract covers the second phase of work on the storm-damaged Pier 1 at Naval Station Newport, with construction and cutter deliveries scheduled through 2030.
ri-newport-pier-one-coast-guard-cutters-.text: newport pier rebuild clears way for four coast guard cutters a $271.2 million contract covers the second phase of work on the storm-damaged pier 1 at naval station newport, with construction and cutter deliveries scheduled through 2030. the navy has awarded a $271.2 million contract for the second phase of rebuilding pier 1 at naval station newport, a project expected to provide four berths for coast guard cutters, according to an announcement from u.s. sen. jack reed reported by what's up newp. the original coddington cove pier was built in the mid-1950s, stretched about 1,585 feet and was condemned after years of storm and wave damage. the first phase of the project included demolishing the old structure. the replacement will be roughly 1,000 feet long and 80 feet wide, with a higher deck intended to limit wave damage and account for sea-level rise. the contract also includes a new bulkhead, laydown area, parking, stormwater controls and utility work. the coast guard has not announced which cutters will use the new berths. construction and cutter deliveries are scheduled to continue through 2030, adding to a broader federal expansion at the newport waterfront that includes a new noaa marine operations center. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri newport newport, rhode island rhode island newport naval station newport coast guard infrastructure climate resilience federal contract

ri-palumbo-five-k-tomorrow-fund-2026.text: east providence 5k boosts hasbro children’s tomorrow fund hundreds joined the mark palumbo memorial race, which has generated more than $250,000 for families facing childhood cancer since 2021. hundreds of runners and walkers gathered in east providence on saturday for the mark palumbo memorial university orthopedics 5k, raising support for the tomorrow fund at hasbro children’s hospital. the course began near the university orthopedics surgery center at kettle point along the east bay bike path. the tomorrow fund provides financial and emotional assistance to children undergoing cancer treatment and to their families. nbc 10 reported that the 5k has raised more than $250,000 for the organization since the event was dedicated to dr. mark palumbo’s memory in 2021, making the annual race a continuing source of local support. saturday’s turnout connected a community fitness event with practical help for families facing long treatment schedules and related costs. university orthopedics organized the race, while the beneficiary’s work is centered at rhode island’s pediatric hospital. the event’s cumulative fundraising reflects several years of participation from runners, sponsors, volunteers and medical-community partners. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island rhode island east providence east providence, rhode island tomorrow fund hasbro children’s hospital mark palumbo memorial 5k east providence

ri-pawtucket-hit-run-ohagan-charges-2026.text: providence woman charged after pawtucket hit-and-run police say a stolen vehicle struck a 48-year-old man riding an electric unicycle, leaving him with life-threatening injuries. a 26-year-old providence woman faces charges after a hit-and-run in pawtucket left a man critically injured, police said. authorities allege that maryna ohagan was driving a vehicle reported stolen earlier sunday when it struck a 48-year-old man on an electric unicycle at main and magill streets. the injured man was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries. pawtucket police said officers had briefly pursued the vehicle after trying to stop it but ended the chase for public-safety reasons. investigators allege the driver fled on foot after the collision. providence police later arrested ohagan, and pawtucket police said she admitted involvement in the theft and crash. ohagan faces charges including possession of a stolen vehicle, reckless driving, leaving a crash that caused serious injury and larceny over $10,000. the charges are allegations and have not been proved in court. she is presumed innocent unless convicted, and officials have not released a later update on the victim’s condition. new-england ri pawtucket, rhode island pawtucket hit-and-run maryna ohagan traffic safety

ri-pelino-governor-primary-recount-reque.text: elaine pelino requests recount in rhode island governor primary unofficial results showed aaron guckian ahead by 279 votes as the board of elections prepared to review the application. elaine pelino filed for a recount thursday in rhode island’s close republican primary for governor, adding a formal review request to a contest that remained unresolved after election night. nbc 10 reported that unofficial board of elections results showed aaron guckian leading pelino by 279 votes. the posted totals gave guckian 11,623 votes, or 50.61%, and pelino 11,344 votes, or 49.4%, based on results updated early thursday. state rules required primary recount applications to be submitted by 4 p.m. on the day after the election. the board of elections reviews an application to determine whether the contest qualifies. any recount would take place at the board’s cranston office and would be open to the public. guckian, a trade-association executive, was the republican nominee for lieutenant governor in 2022 and has the state party’s endorsement. pelino is a first-time candidate. the eventual winner will advance to the november general election. the posted margin and totals remain unofficial while the recount request is considered. rhode-island rhode-island rhode island ri cranston cranston, ri rhode island elections recount governor
