tech-anthropic-russian-chinese-claude-ca.text: anthropic says it disrupted russian and chinese ai-abuse campaigns the company described alleged cyberespionage and large-scale attempts to extract claude’s capabilities over an eight-month period. anthropic said thursday that it disrupted several malicious campaigns involving its claude models, including suspected russian cyberespionage and efforts by china-based ai companies to extract or replicate the system’s capabilities. the company said the activity unfolded over eight months and increasingly used multiple ai agents to divide and automate tasks. anthropic alleged that seven china-based laboratories, including alibaba, moonshot, deepseek and xiaomi, accessed claude through deceptive accounts or intermediaries. one operation attributed to alibaba generated 151 million exchanges from may through july and peaked at about 3 million in a day across more than 3,500 allegedly fraudulent accounts, anthropic said. it also accused moonshot and deepseek of routing some live customer conversations through claude for training, including potentially sensitive material. anthropic separately said tradecraft consistent with the russia-linked group known as midnight blizzard used ai in phishing, hotel wi-fi compromise and whatsapp account takeover attempts targeting ukrainian officials. the organizations named in the report did not all provide immediate responses. the findings are anthropic’s account of its own enforcement work and should be read as company allegations, not independent legal determinations. tech tech tech international san francisco san francisco, ca anthropic claude cybersecurity ai models

tech-asml-high-na-chipmaking-demand-2026.text: asml extends chipmaking lead as customers embrace high na asml’s next-generation lithography tools are drawing commitments from major chipmakers even as the machines cost roughly twice as much as standard euv systems. asml’s newest high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet machines are becoming a larger part of chipmakers’ plans, reuters reported monday. the dutch company’s standard euv systems, which cost about $200 million, were described as sold out through 2027. tsmc, samsung, sk hynix and intel have committed roughly $400 million to high na tools, according to the report. the machines can print features about 40% smaller than the previous generation, but their price is roughly twice as high. intel has processed more than one million wafers on its high na system. the equipment matters because smaller features can support denser and more powerful chips, but adoption also raises the cost of building advanced manufacturing capacity. asml remains the key supplier of euv lithography equipment, giving its delivery schedule and customer commitments importance across the semiconductor industry. the transition also places pressure on chipmakers to justify more expensive tools as they race to secure capacity for advanced processors. tech tech tech netherlands veldhoven veldhoven, netherlands asml semiconductors euv high na

tech-asml-large-mask-high-na-euv-2026.text: asml plans larger masks for high-na tools and data-center chips the chip-equipment maker says an industry consortium could adapt its most advanced lithography systems for today’s largest ai processors. asml plans to work with major chipmakers on larger masks for its newest high-na extreme-ultraviolet lithography tools, aiming to make the systems suitable for large data-center processors. reuters reported that widely used euv machines can print chips up to about 800 square millimeters. high-na tools can create finer features, but their smaller masks currently limit the size of chips they can produce. asml said a larger mask format could remove that constraint and expand adoption beyond intel, which already uses the new tools for some production. tsmc plans high-na use in advanced-node high-volume manufacturing from 2030, while samsung and sk hynix are targeting memory production earlier. the timetable is long: asml expects a pilot line around 2031 and technology ready for high-volume production by 2033. chief technology officer marco pieters told reuters the change could raise system productivity by 40%. those are company plans, not guaranteed manufacturing outcomes, and success will require equipment makers, chip foundries and mask suppliers to align on a new standard. tech nl netherlands asml semiconductors euv ai chips

tech-australia-telco-resilience-optus-ou.text: australia pledges stronger telecom resilience after optus outage the government’s response follows a 76-minute disruption that affected voice calls and some emergency-service connections across several regions. australia’s government pledged sunday to strengthen the resilience of national telecommunications networks after an optus outage disrupted voice service and some emergency calls. the 76-minute technical problem affected customers in victoria, south australia, tasmania and the northern territory, according to the country’s second-largest carrier. optus described the customer impact as intermittent call dropouts. the government response raises the issue beyond one company’s technical repair, focusing attention on how carriers maintain access to police, fire and ambulance services during network failures. officials had not yet detailed a specific regulatory package or timetable for new requirements. the disruption follows a separate optus network failure last year that prevented hundreds of people from reaching emergency services and was linked to two deaths. that history increases scrutiny of redundancy, incident response and customer communication across the sector. the latest pledge signals that canberra expects resilience work to cover the broader telecom system, not only optus’s immediate outage review. tech tech tech new south wales sydney sydney, australia optus australia telecommunications emergency calls

tech-automattic-mullenweg-returns-ceo-20.excerpt: The WordPress.com parent said its founder again has the board’s support days after directors placed him on paid leave.
tech-automattic-mullenweg-returns-ceo-20.text: automattic confirms matt mullenweg has returned as ceo the wordpress.com parent said its founder again has the board’s support days after directors placed him on paid leave. automattic confirmed saturday that wordpress co-founder matt mullenweg has returned as chairman and chief executive after a board vote placed him on paid leave earlier in the week. a company spokesperson told techcrunch that mullenweg had the board’s full support, reversing the leadership arrangement announced days earlier. automattic had said wednesday that chief financial officer mark davies would serve as interim ceo while mullenweg was on leave. techcrunch reported that mullenweg resisted the move and told employees he was back in control. the company’s latest statement formally resolves the chief executive question for now, though the reasons for the original leave remain undisclosed. questions also remain about automattic’s board composition. techcrunch said it had sought comment on reports that board member and former automattic ceo toni schneider stepped down, but had not received confirmation. the episode creates an unusual governance moment for the company behind wordpress.com and other publishing, commerce and messaging products. tech tech tech california san francisco san francisco, california automattic matt mullenweg wordpress technology leadership

tech-bitcoin-suisse-swiss-job-cuts-2026.excerpt: The crypto-services company says it may eliminate 60 roles while shifting software development and back-office work to international hubs.
tech-bitcoin-suisse-swiss-job-cuts-2026.text: bitcoin suisse plans to cut up to half its swiss workforce the crypto-services company says it may eliminate 60 roles while shifting software development and back-office work to international hubs. cryptocurrency services company bitcoin suisse plans to eliminate as many as 60 of its 120 jobs in switzerland, reuters reported. the zug-based firm is consulting employees through september 20 before finalizing the reductions, which would amount to as much as half of its domestic workforce. the reorganization is intended to consolidate software development and back-office operations in international hubs, where the company says it can scale faster, reach a broader pool of workers and direct investment toward future services. bitcoin suisse will also close its information-technology development site in copenhagen. the changes show how crypto companies are reassessing where they build and support increasingly software-intensive financial products. founded in 2013, bitcoin suisse employs about 200 people worldwide. beyond switzerland, it has operations in liechtenstein, abu dhabi and bermuda, as well as an international hub in bratislava and another planned for vietnam. the consultation means the maximum job-cut figure is not yet final. the company did not frame the announcement as an exit from switzerland, where its headquarters and core crypto-finance business remain based. tech tech tech switzerland zug zug, switzerland bitcoin suisse cryptocurrency software development job cuts switzerland

tech-boards-digital-infrastructure-resil.excerpt: A survey of 1,300 organizations found that replacing a critical provider could take months or longer, pushing resilience into board discussions.
tech-boards-digital-infrastructure-resil.text: boards elevate digital-infrastructure resilience as risks grow a survey of 1,300 organizations found that replacing a critical provider could take months or longer, pushing resilience into board discussions. large companies and public bodies are putting critical digital infrastructure under more direct board-level scrutiny as cyber threats, export controls and geopolitical conflict expose technology dependencies, a capgemini survey found. the survey covered executives at 1,300 large organizations in 11 countries, reuters reported. respondents increasingly treated cloud services, data, artificial-intelligence models and other digital systems like energy supplies or physical supply chains that require risk assessments and contingency plans. nearly half said replacing a critical provider would take between three months and a year. more than a third expected the switch to take longer than a year, suggesting that contractual access alone does not guarantee a quick recovery when a major vendor becomes unavailable. the response is not necessarily a wholesale shift away from established providers. organizations are focusing on whether important workloads can move, whether proprietary assets remain under their control and whether alternate suppliers are practical. that emphasis turns technical resilience into a governance and business-continuity issue, not solely an information-technology concern. tech tech tech international global global digital infrastructure cybersecurity capgemini business continuity

tech-boeing-engineers-tentative-contract.excerpt: The revised agreement would deliver a 10% initial raise and annual increases through 2030 as key certification programs remain delayed.
tech-boeing-engineers-tentative-contract.text: boeing engineers reach tentative four-year contract the revised agreement would deliver a 10% initial raise and annual increases through 2030 as key certification programs remain delayed. boeing and the society of professional engineering employees in aerospace have reached a tentative four-year contract after union members overwhelmingly rejected an earlier offer in august. the revised proposal would provide a 10% general wage increase on october 16, followed by 4% annual increases plus merit raises through 2030. the agreement also revises work-from-home rules and overtime limits. union officials said members had pressed for larger across-the-board increases after seattle-area inflation rose 4.5% over the previous year. speea’s negotiating team said the package did not satisfy every demand but represented a meaningful improvement over boeing’s prior proposal. members must still ratify the deal before the current contract expires on october 6. the vote matters beyond compensation: boeing engineers are central to certification work for the delayed 737 max 10 and 777-9 aircraft. a rejection could revive the possibility of a strike at a time when both programs face schedule pressure. the tentative settlement is the first fully negotiated contract between the sides since 2012, after extensions in 2016 and 2020. tech tech tech washington seattle seattle, washington boeing speea aerospace engineering labor aircraft certification

tech-boston-logan-amelia-ai-holograms-20.excerpt: The airport’s new “Amelia” assistants offer directions in every terminal and can send step-by-step routes to travelers’ phones by QR code.
tech-boston-logan-amelia-ai-holograms-20.text: boston logan deploys eight multilingual ai holograms the airport’s new “amelia” assistants offer directions in every terminal and can send step-by-step routes to travelers’ phones by qr code. boston logan international airport has installed eight artificial-intelligence-powered holograms to help travelers find gates, restaurants, baggage claim and other locations. the assistants, named “amelia” after aviation pioneer amelia earhart, are positioned across every terminal, both before and after security checkpoints. the system can provide step-by-step directions in several languages and display a qr code so travelers can carry those instructions on their phones. airport officials said amelia can be programmed with thousands of locations and described the deployment as the largest use of this hologram technology at any airport. logan expects the units to handle about 100,000 interactions during their first year. massport says the goal is to supplement its customer-service staff, not replace employees. the current version is focused on common wayfinding questions, while a planned second phase would make the system more conversational and capable of answering a broader range of requests. the installation gives logan a visible test of how generative ai and projection technology can be integrated into busy public spaces. tech tech tech ma boston boston, massachusetts boston logan airport artificial intelligence amelia massport travel technology

tech-california-child-social-media-ai-la.excerpt: A 13-bill package restricts addictive platform features for users under 16, bars AI companion toys for four years and expands protections against synthetic abuse material.
tech-california-child-social-media-ai-la.text: california enacts new child safeguards for social media and ai toys a 13-bill package restricts addictive platform features for users under 16, bars ai companion toys for four years and expands protections against synthetic abuse material. california governor gavin newsom signed a package of 13 bills imposing new safeguards on social media platforms, artificial-intelligence chatbots and technology products used by children. one measure bars platforms from exposing users under 16 to engagement features defined as psychologically exploitative, including infinite-scroll feeds and algorithmic autoplay. another prohibits the manufacture and sale of toys containing ai companion chatbots for four years. related provisions require parental controls and safety assessments for chatbot programs. the package also expands criminal sanctions for child sexual abuse material to cover digitally altered or ai-generated depictions of minors. newsom described the measures as the country’s broadest youth-technology protections, while supporters in both parties said existing safeguards had not kept pace with product design. the electronic frontier foundation criticized the social-media restrictions as a threat to privacy and free expression, illustrating the legal debate likely to follow implementation. california joins states including utah, texas, florida and new york in regulating minors’ access to major platforms, but the details and enforcement models differ. agencies must still define portions of the rules before the requirements take full effect. tech tech tech ca sacramento california california social media ai child safety

tech-canal-laliga-antipiracy-pact-2026.excerpt: The broadcasters will combine technical tools, investigations and policy work against illegal soccer streams in their shared markets.
tech-canal-laliga-antipiracy-pact-2026.text: canal+ and laliga expand anti-piracy partnership across nearly 50 countries the broadcasters will combine technical tools, investigations and policy work against illegal soccer streams in their shared markets. canal+ and spain’s laliga have signed an anti-piracy agreement covering nearly 50 countries where the media company carries league matches. reuters reported that the partners will combine technical capabilities, coordinate investigations and work together on policy aimed at illegal streaming networks. the territory spans europe, sub-saharan africa and haiti. financial terms were not disclosed. the arrangement extends beyond removing individual streams: both organizations described piracy as a cross-border business supported by increasingly sophisticated distribution systems. laliga said spanish clubs’ broadcast income fell 5.2% in the 2024-25 season to 1.43 billion euros, even as commercial revenue increased. canal+ estimated that piracy destroys about 1.5 billion euros of value annually in france, including losses to public tax revenue. the partnership matters technologically because rights holders increasingly need automated detection, platform cooperation and evidence collection that works across jurisdictions. illegal services can blend licensed and unlicensed programming and shift infrastructure quickly. sharing tools and case information could make enforcement faster, though success will still depend on local law, internet providers and courts in each market. tech tech tech france paris paris, france canal+ laliga streaming piracy sports media cybersecurity

tech-cegid-silae-euro-10-billion-merger-.excerpt: Silver Lake will remain the controlling shareholder of a combined European business-software group expected to close in 2027.
tech-cegid-silae-euro-10-billion-merger-.text: cegid and silae plan €10 billion software merger silver lake will remain the controlling shareholder of a combined european business-software group expected to close in 2027. french business-software provider cegid and payroll platform silae plan to merge in a transaction valuing the combined group at more than 10 billion euros, or about $11.6 billion, reuters reported wednesday. private-equity firm silver lake is the majority owner of both companies and will remain the controlling shareholder after the combination. the companies said newly appointed chief executive christian pedersen will lead the merged business, which is expected to bring together payroll, finance and other management-software products. the deal is scheduled to close in the first half of 2027, subject to the required reviews and transaction conditions. until those steps are completed, cegid and silae remain separate businesses and the timetable could change. the proposed merger would create a larger european software company serving businesses that increasingly want cloud-based tools for essential administrative work. scale can help software providers spread product-development and compliance costs, but integration will determine whether customers see simpler services or added complexity. the announcement establishes the strategic direction; execution will take place over the coming months. tech tech tech international paris france cegid silae software mergers

tech-chatgpt-fabricated-police-testimony.excerpt: The state Supreme Court fined a defense lawyer $5,000 after a murder-appeal brief included invented witnesses and testimony.
tech-chatgpt-fabricated-police-testimony.text: new mexico high court says chatgpt fabricated police testimony the state supreme court fined a defense lawyer $5,000 after a murder-appeal brief included invented witnesses and testimony. new mexico’s supreme court said a defense lawyer submitted a murder-appeal brief containing police testimony and witnesses fabricated by chatgpt. the court fined attorney stephen aarons $5,000, held him in contempt and said it would refer the matter to a disciplinary board. aarons told reuters he used chatgpt to summarize a computer-generated trial transcript and other case material. he acknowledged failing to understand how readily the system could invent facts and described the filing as an honest mistake. openai did not immediately comment to reuters. the justices said the brief contained false testimony from wholly invented witnesses. the underlying appeal involves oscar renee sandoval, who was convicted of murdering the mother of his children and sentenced to life in prison. a public defender took over the still-pending appeal on september 2. courts have previously sanctioned lawyers over ai-generated citations and misstatements, but this filing extended to purported evidence in a criminal case. the decision underscores that generative tools can produce fluent but unsupported material and that lawyers remain responsible for checking every factual assertion before submitting it to a court. tech tech tech new mexico santa fe santa fe, new mexico chatgpt new mexico supreme court legal technology ai hallucinations court filings

tech-china-ai-chip-prices-hbm-shortage-2.excerpt: Reuters sources say Huawei, Cambricon and smaller rivals are repricing accelerators as high-bandwidth memory costs rise.
tech-china-ai-chip-prices-hbm-shortage-2.text: chinese ai chipmakers raise prices as memory shortage bites reuters sources say huawei, cambricon and smaller rivals are repricing accelerators as high-bandwidth memory costs rise. chinese artificial-intelligence chipmakers are raising indicated prices for current and next-generation processors as high-bandwidth memory becomes more expensive and harder to obtain, three people familiar with the discussions told reuters. huawei increased the indicated price of its ascend 950dt accelerator card to more than 250,000 yuan, about $37,255, according to two sources. that is 20% to 50% above quotes given two months earlier, depending on contract terms. huawei has said the card is scheduled for availability in the fourth quarter of 2026. cambricon raised the indicated price of a planned chip tentatively called the 690 by 20% to 30%, two sources said. smaller competitors metax and iluvatar corex have made similar adjustments. the sources were not identified because the pricing discussions are private. high-bandwidth memory is crucial for moving large quantities of data through ai accelerators. export restrictions and reliance on gray-market supplies have increased pressure on chinese producers seeking domestic alternatives to nvidia. the new quotes may raise deployment costs for buyers and complicate efforts to expand locally produced ai computing capacity. tech tech tech intl shanghai china ai chips huawei cambricon high-bandwidth memory

tech-china-autonomous-vehicle-roadmap-20.excerpt: A new industry roadmap calls for self-driving systems on highways, urban expressways and selected city roads while tightening safety and software rules.
tech-china-autonomous-vehicle-roadmap-20.text: china targets large-scale autonomous-vehicle deployment by 2030 a new industry roadmap calls for self-driving systems on highways, urban expressways and selected city roads while tightening safety and software rules. china’s industry ministry has set a 2030 goal for large-scale deployment of autonomous vehicles, pairing expansion plans with tighter oversight of vehicle production, road safety and software updates. the roadmap calls for automated driving on highways, urban expressways and selected city streets. it also aims to produce multiple chinese automakers ranked among the world’s top 10 by sales and to increase the global influence of chinese brands and technical standards. safety is central to the plan: the ministry wants autonomous vehicles to achieve better safety performance than human drivers. regulators also intend to create special approval pathways for some components and low-volume vehicles while strengthening antitrust enforcement and product-quality supervision. the document addresses the industry’s capacity problem as well as its technology ambitions. officials plan to discourage overinvestment, eliminate inefficient production and encourage consolidation across automakers and battery manufacturers. china also wants deeper research and investment partnerships with foreign companies. the roadmap sets policy direction, but broad deployment will still depend on technical validation, local road approvals and enforcement of the new rules. tech tech tech china beijing china autonomous vehicles china electric vehicles transportation

tech-cognition-series-e-2026.excerpt: The autonomous coding-agent company says its run-rate revenue has climbed to nearly $900 million since a May financing.
tech-cognition-series-e-2026.text: cognition ai raises $2 billion at $48 billion valuation the autonomous coding-agent company says its run-rate revenue has climbed to nearly $900 million since a may financing. ai coding startup cognition ai said tuesday that it raised $2 billion in a series e financing that values the company at $48 billion, nearly double its valuation from a may funding round. reuters reported that new investors andreessen horowitz and accel led the round, with founders fund, general catalyst and avenir also participating. cognition said its run-rate revenue increased from $492 million to nearly $900 million since may, when it raised $1 billion at a $26 billion valuation. the company builds autonomous software-engineering agents designed to plan, write, test and deploy code with limited human intervention. the fresh capital gives cognition additional resources to develop those tools and compete in a crowded market for ai-assisted programming. the $48 billion figure is a private financing valuation, not a continuously traded public-market price. it reflects the terms accepted by investors in this round and may not translate directly into a future sale or public listing value. even so, the rapid step-up shows that large investors continue to place sizable bets on companies selling automation for software development. tech us united states cognition ai artificial intelligence coding agents venture capital

tech-covenant-anthem-mass-production-cru.excerpt: The startup says its Anthem missile has completed more than 200 test flights and is backed by about $150 million in orders.
tech-covenant-anthem-mass-production-cru.text: covenant unveils lower-cost cruise missile designed for mass production the startup says its anthem missile has completed more than 200 test flights and is backed by about $150 million in orders. defense startup covenant has unveiled anthem, a ground-launched cruise missile the company says can be produced faster and at a lower price than many established long-range weapons. the company told reuters that anthem carries a payload exceeding 200 kilograms and has completed more than 200 test flights over the past year. covenant is targeting a mid-six-figure unit price once production reaches scale and says it has booked about $150 million in orders. founded in 2024, covenant has raised more than $250 million and employs over 200 people in the united states, germany and israel. its new dallas plant is designed for annual capacity of 5,000 missiles; a similarly sized german facility has the same target, while an israeli site is planned for 2,000. those figures are company plans, not completed production. new defense manufacturers often face certification, contracting and supply-chain obstacles when moving from tests to high-volume delivery. covenant expects an international customer to begin receiving german-built units late this year and u.s. army deliveries in 2027. tech tech tech tx dallas dallas, texas covenant anthem missile defense technology manufacturing

tech-deepseek-citic-shanghai-ipo-2026.excerpt: Sources say the Chinese AI startup has selected the brokerage for work ahead of a possible STAR Market listing, though final terms remain undecided.
tech-deepseek-citic-shanghai-ipo-2026.text: deepseek taps citic securities for shanghai ipo preparations sources say the chinese ai startup has selected the brokerage for work ahead of a possible star market listing, though final terms remain undecided. chinese artificial-intelligence startup deepseek has selected citic securities to prepare for a domestic initial public offering, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by reuters. the company is working toward a possible listing on shanghai’s technology-focused star market. selecting an adviser and beginning pre-listing preparation moves the process forward, but it is not the same as filing a final prospectus or setting an offer date. deepseek became a prominent competitor in generative ai by developing models designed to use computing resources efficiently. a public listing could provide additional capital for computing infrastructure, model development and hiring as competition for researchers and hardware intensifies. important terms remain unsettled, including timing, valuation and the amount of stock to be sold. deepseek and citic securities had not publicly confirmed a final transaction in the initial report. any eventual offering would also require regulatory review. the current development is therefore a preparatory step, not a completed ipo or a publicly traded share price. tech international hangzhou, china deepseek citic securities artificial intelligence ipo

tech-deepseek-v41-flash-launch-2026.excerpt: The Chinese AI startup says the release is designed for faster inference and higher throughput while supporting larger models in the same architecture.
tech-deepseek-v41-flash-launch-2026.text: deepseek launches v4.1-flash as smallest model in new ai family the chinese ai startup says the release is designed for faster inference and higher throughput while supporting larger models in the same architecture. chinese artificial-intelligence startup deepseek launched deepseek-v4.1-flash on thursday, describing it as the smallest model in a new architecture family. the company said the model is designed to improve capability, inference speed and throughput while providing a foundation that can scale to larger systems. reuters reported the announcement but did not include independent benchmark results, model-size details or pricing in its initial account. the release arrives as deepseek begins preparations for a potential initial public offering on shanghai’s technology-focused star market, according to earlier reuters reporting. that connection puts the technical launch in a wider race among chinese ai developers to fund computing capacity, win users and build domestic alternatives to u.s.-based model providers. the practical test will be whether developers see consistent gains across real workloads, not only company demonstrations. until technical documentation and outside evaluations are available, deepseek’s performance claims should be treated as the maker’s description. the flash branding suggests an emphasis on efficiency and response speed within the broader v4.1 family. tech tech tech intl beijing beijing, china deepseek v4.1-flash artificial intelligence china

tech-discovery-loop-funding-50-billion-v.excerpt: The young AI research startup is pursuing a sharp valuation increase, according to Business Insider, though terms could change and a deal is not assured.
tech-discovery-loop-funding-50-billion-v.text: discovery loop seeks funding at reported $50 billion valuation the young ai research startup is pursuing a sharp valuation increase, according to business insider, though terms could change and a deal is not assured. artificial-intelligence startup discovery loop is seeking new funding at a valuation of about $50 billion, business insider reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. the terms could change and there is no guarantee the talks will result in a transaction, making the figure an indication of investor negotiations rather than a completed valuation. the reported target represents an unusually rapid increase for a company launched this year. discovery loop was in talks last month to raise about $1 billion at a valuation near $10 billion, according to the report. the startup is structured as a public benefit corporation and is focused on using machine learning for scientific and engineering research. its founding team includes prominent artificial-intelligence and engineering leaders, including longtime google researcher jeff dean. the fundraising effort reflects continued investor appetite for teams with established ai credentials even as spending requirements and commercialization timelines remain uncertain. discovery loop did not immediately respond to a reuters request for comment, and no investors or final financing amount were confirmed. tech tech tech california san francisco san francisco, california discovery loop artificial intelligence venture capital jeff dean startups

tech-dmatrix-nvidia-nvlink-raptor-2026.excerpt: The startup’s upcoming Raptor processors will connect directly to Nvidia data-center systems through NVLink Fusion, with compatible racks expected in 2027.
tech-dmatrix-nvidia-nvlink-raptor-2026.text: d-matrix adopts nvidia chip-linking tech for ai inference servers the startup’s upcoming raptor processors will connect directly to nvidia data-center systems through nvlink fusion, with compatible racks expected in 2027. ai chip startup d-matrix said thursday that its next-generation raptor processors will use nvidia’s nvlink fusion technology, allowing the custom chips to connect directly inside nvidia-compatible data-center systems. d-matrix focuses on inference, the stage when trained models power services such as coding assistants, chatbots and voice agents. nvidia dominates the market for chips used to train large models, while nvlink fusion gives outside processor designers access to specialized links and memory connections within its broader server architecture. the raptor chips are scheduled to complete final design by the end of 2026, and compatible server racks are expected in 2027. d-matrix is also working with astera labs on high-speed data movement across the system. financial terms of the nvidia collaboration were not disclosed. the santa clara company shipped its first ai chip in november 2024 and was valued at $2 billion after raising $450 million in 2025. microsoft has backed the startup since an earlier financing round. the partnership shows how smaller chipmakers are seeking a route into established data-center platforms as demand shifts from building models toward running them quickly and efficiently at scale. tech tech tech ca santa clara santa clara, ca d-matrix nvidia ai chips data centers

tech-enflame-912m-ipo-debut-2026.excerpt: The Chinese AI-chip designer raised 6.12 billion yuan ahead of a Shanghai STAR Market listing.
tech-enflame-912m-ipo-debut-2026.text: tencent-backed enflame sets friday debut after $912 million ipo the chinese ai-chip designer raised 6.12 billion yuan ahead of a shanghai star market listing. chinese artificial-intelligence chip designer enflame is scheduled to begin trading friday on shanghai’s star market after raising 6.12 billion yuan, or about $912 million, reuters reported. the company sold 43 million new shares at 142.18 yuan each. the offering implies a valuation of 61.19 billion yuan, roughly $9.12 billion. only 17.9 million shares, equal to about 4.16% of the company after the offering, are expected to be available for trading initially, according to the listing details. enflame forecast a net loss of 700 million to 860 million yuan for the first nine months of 2026, compared with an 887.8 million-yuan loss a year earlier. it projected revenue of 2.3 billion to 3 billion yuan, an increase of 326% to 455%. tencent will remain the largest shareholder with a 17.95% post-ipo stake. enflame also reported that tencent-related business accounted for 83.79% of 2025 revenue, underscoring customer concentration alongside rapid growth. friday’s debut will provide the first public-market test of that combination. tech tech tech international shanghai shanghai, china enflame ai chips ipo tencent

tech-enisa-tests-mythos-5-gpt-6-astra-20.excerpt: ENISA has received access to Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra as European officials examine advanced models’ cyber capabilities.
tech-enisa-tests-mythos-5-gpt-6-astra-20.text: eu cybersecurity agency tests anthropic and openai frontier models enisa has received access to anthropic’s mythos 5 and openai’s gpt-6 astra as european officials examine advanced models’ cyber capabilities. the european union’s cybersecurity agency has been granted access to two advanced artificial-intelligence models and has begun testing one of them, the european commission said thursday. enisa is testing anthropic’s mythos 5 and has also received access to openai’s gpt-6 astra, according to a commission spokesperson quoted by reuters. the brief announcement did not specify the test methods, timetable or results. access gives the agency an opportunity to examine how frontier systems behave in security-sensitive scenarios. that can include evaluating whether a model strengthens defensive analysis, generates risky technical guidance or resists attempts to bypass safeguards. reuters’ report did not say that either model had failed a test or caused an incident. the review comes as european regulators and security officials seek a clearer picture of rapidly improving model capabilities. independent access matters because evaluations performed by public agencies can complement testing conducted by developers. enisa’s findings could inform how institutions assess emerging cyber risks, but the commission did not announce any enforcement action or policy change. until results are released, the development is best understood as a new stage of official technical scrutiny rather than a judgment about either company’s model. tech tech tech international brussels european union enisa anthropic openai cybersecurity

tech-eu-court-booking-etraveli-acquisiti.excerpt: Europe’s second-highest court backed regulators who said the €1.63 billion deal would strengthen Booking’s dominant online-travel position.
tech-eu-court-booking-etraveli-acquisiti.text: eu court upholds veto of booking’s etraveli acquisition europe’s second-highest court backed regulators who said the €1.63 billion deal would strengthen booking’s dominant online-travel position. booking holdings lost its challenge to the european union’s veto of its €1.63 billion acquisition of flight-booking company etraveli, leaving the blocked technology deal intact. the general court in luxembourg sided with the european commission, which rejected the transaction in 2023. judges said the purchase would have strengthened booking’s already dominant position in the online travel-agency market for hotels. regulators argued that adding etraveli’s flight-booking services could create a broader travel ecosystem that rivals would struggle to match. booking’s brands include booking.com, rentalcars, priceline and agoda. etraveli, owned by cvc capital partners, operates gotogate, mytrip and the airline-content service tripstack. the ruling underscores europe’s tougher scrutiny of technology acquisitions that may reinforce an incumbent’s position rather than simply add a direct competitor. it does not necessarily end the case: booking can appeal on points of law to the court of justice of the european union. until any successful appeal, the commission’s prohibition remains in force. tech tech tech international luxembourg luxembourg booking holdings etraveli european union antitrust

tech-eu-short-term-rental-platform-rules.excerpt: The plan would let cities target platforms such as Airbnb under evidence-based, geographically limited housing measures.
tech-eu-short-term-rental-platform-rules.text: eu proposes common framework for tighter short-term rental rules the plan would let cities target platforms such as airbnb under evidence-based, geographically limited housing measures. the european commission proposed a common framework wednesday that could allow cities to impose additional restrictions on airbnb and other short-term rental platforms in areas facing acute housing pressure, reuters reported. the plan would use indicators such as high home-price-to-income ratios or sustained increases in housing costs to identify affected areas. local restrictions would need to be supported by evidence, necessary for the stated goal, limited to specific geographic areas and non-retroactive. european destinations including paris, barcelona and venice have already adopted their own limits, producing a patchwork of rules and legal disputes. a shared framework is intended to give national and local governments clearer standards while addressing concerns that short-term rentals reduce the supply of homes available to residents. airbnb said europe should also focus on increasing supply through construction and renovation. technology trade group ccia europe raised concerns about oversight of local restrictions. the proposal is not yet law: it still requires approval from european union member states and the european parliament, and its practical effect will depend on the final text and how authorities apply it. tech tech tech international brussels brussels, belgium airbnb european union short-term rentals platform regulation

tech-europe-coordinate-national-satellit.excerpt: European Space Agency leader Josef Aschbacher says new sovereign networks should work together as the region builds communications capacity and prepares IRIS².
tech-europe-coordinate-national-satellit.text: esa chief urges europe to link national satellite systems european space agency leader josef aschbacher says new sovereign networks should work together as the region builds communications capacity and prepares iris². europe’s top space official is calling for greater coordination among national satellite programs as governments invest in sovereign communications networks. european space agency director general josef aschbacher said the systems should be interoperable and warned against creating isolated projects that duplicate capabilities. the issue has become more prominent as germany develops a separate military communications network while the european union advances iris², its planned secure satellite constellation. initial iris² launches are targeted for 2029. aschbacher said europe needs a shared approach that still allows countries to pursue their own security requirements. industrial work is already accelerating. thales alenia space has a deal to supply payloads for 330 low-earth-orbit satellites, an order valued at about €500 million within a broader contract worth more than €3 billion. airbus is expected to provide an initial layer of at least 66 satellites. aschbacher also proposed spending about €1 billion a year for a decade, beginning in 2029, to strengthen europe’s space autonomy. a decision on that proposal is expected in 2028. the coordination debate will shape whether national constellations and eu-backed infrastructure operate as complementary layers or become costly parallel systems. tech tech tech france paris paris, france european space agency satellites iris2 space infrastructure

tech-eutelsat-oneweb-229-satellites-airb.excerpt: The €1 billion Airbus order will replenish the low-orbit constellation as Europe’s Starlink rival bridges toward the planned IRIS² system.
tech-eutelsat-oneweb-229-satellites-airb.text: eutelsat orders 229 satellites to extend oneweb network through 2034 the €1 billion airbus order will replenish the low-orbit constellation as europe’s starlink rival bridges toward the planned iris² system. eutelsat has placed a €1 billion order with airbus for 229 low-earth-orbit satellites, expanding a replenishment plan intended to keep its oneweb broadband network operating through 2034. the new spacecraft add to 440 satellites ordered in 2024 and 2025. oneweb operates more than 600 satellites and competes with spacex’s much larger starlink network, which has more than 11,000. eutelsat’s constellation flies at a higher orbit and is focused heavily on business, government and telecommunications customers rather than relying mainly on direct consumer service. the order is designed to maintain service continuity until europe’s planned iris² secure communications network becomes available near the end of the decade. eutelsat has also booked two launches on europe’s ariane rocket for 2027 and 2028, reuters reported. for europe, the purchase has strategic as well as commercial significance. oneweb is the region’s primary operational low-orbit alternative to starlink, and keeping the network refreshed reduces the risk of a capacity gap before iris² is deployed. the long timetable also underscores how satellite internet systems require continual replacement: spacecraft have finite operating lives, while demand, cybersecurity requirements and launch schedules keep changing. tech tech tech france paris paris, france eutelsat oneweb airbus satellites iris2

tech-fcc-space-spectrum-proposal-2026.excerpt: The agency plans a September 30 vote on changes covering the 12 GHz and 42 GHz bands, satellite links and ultra-wideband devices.
tech-fcc-space-spectrum-proposal-2026.text: fcc proposes opening more spectrum for space-based broadband the agency plans a september 30 vote on changes covering the 12 ghz and 42 ghz bands, satellite links and ultra-wideband devices. the federal communications commission proposed opening additional wireless spectrum for space-based broadband and modernizing several related technology rules, with a commission vote set for september 30. reuters reported that the proposal covers more than 1,000 megahertz in the 12 ghz and 42 ghz bands. the agency says the capacity could support high-speed satellite connectivity for homes, aircraft, ships and ground networks, as well as more resilient links between satellites. the fcc also wants to update rules for ultra-wideband devices used in package tracking, industrial systems, vehicle technology and imaging. separate permitting changes are intended to speed deployment of internet infrastructure. the proposal begins a regulatory step, not an immediate spectrum opening. commissioners must vote, and implementation can still involve technical conditions designed to prevent interference with existing users. satellite operators, wireless carriers and equipment makers will be watching the final band plan and power rules closely because those details determine which services can operate and how quickly new hardware can reach customers. tech us washington, d.c. fcc satellite broadband spectrum telecommunications

tech-ford-f150-fuel-tank-recall-223472-2.excerpt: Certain 2023-2027 F-150 trucks may have leaking or improperly secured tanks that can stall an engine, create a road hazard or raise fire risk.
tech-ford-f150-fuel-tank-recall-223472-2.text: ford recalls 223,472 f-150 trucks over fuel-tank risk certain 2023-2027 f-150 trucks may have leaking or improperly secured tanks that can stall an engine, create a road hazard or raise fire risk. ford is recalling 223,472 f-150 pickup trucks in the united states because fuel tanks may leak or separate from the vehicle while it is moving, according to the national highway traffic safety administration. the action covers certain trucks from model years 2023 through 2027. the safety agency said some tanks may be improperly secured. a detached tank can become a road hazard and increase crash risk, while leaking fuel can cause an engine stall or create a fire risk. the notice does not mean every truck in the model-year range has the defect; owners will be notified based on the vehicles included in ford’s recall population. dealers will inspect the fuel-tank straps and replace them when necessary at no charge, nhtsa said. owners should use their vehicle identification number with the federal recall database or contact a ford dealer to determine whether a specific truck is affected and to arrange service after notices are issued. the recall highlights how a relatively basic mounting component can create several connected safety problems, from loss of propulsion to debris on the road and exposure to leaking fuel. tech tech tech united states washington united states ford f-150 vehicle recall nhtsa auto safety

tech-galaxeye-us-imaging-patent-2026.excerpt: The Indian space startup says its technology synchronizes two sensor types to capture more consistent Earth-observation data through darkness and clouds.
tech-galaxeye-us-imaging-patent-2026.text: galaxeye wins u.s. patent for combined radar-optical satellite imaging the indian space startup says its technology synchronizes two sensor types to capture more consistent earth-observation data through darkness and clouds. indian space startup galaxeye has received a u.s. patent for satellite-imaging technology that synchronizes optical and radar sensors. the system is designed to capture both types of data at the same time and location. optical cameras can produce familiar, detailed images but are limited by darkness and clouds, while radar can operate at night and through many weather conditions. combining them can make earth-observation data more consistent. galaxeye says possible uses include disaster response, agriculture, insurance and security. the company, founded by engineers from the indian institute of technology madras, has raised about $21 million and plans a constellation of 30 satellites over five years. it also acquired bengaluru spacecraft-engineering company starops. a patent protects the covered invention in the united states but does not by itself prove commercial adoption or performance at constellation scale. galaxeye still must build, launch and operate the planned satellites. the award is nevertheless a concrete step as private space companies compete to deliver more frequent and weather-resilient imagery. tech international bengaluru, india galaxeye satellite imaging space technology patent

tech-germany-military-ai-tools-evaluatio.excerpt: Germany’s cyber-command chief said a prototype could be ready in the second quarter of 2027, with broader implementation targeted for 2028.
tech-germany-military-ai-tools-evaluatio.text: german military evaluates 30 ai tools for battlefield decisions germany’s cyber-command chief said a prototype could be ready in the second quarter of 2027, with broader implementation targeted for 2028. germany’s military is evaluating 30 artificial-intelligence tools intended to speed battlefield decision-making, with an initial system targeted for introduction beginning in 2027, reuters reported thursday. vice admiral thomas daum, head of the military’s cyber command, told handelsblatt that he was optimistic a prototype would be available in the second quarter of 2027. full implementation is expected in 2028. most products under review come from german companies, while france’s chapsvision is among the foreign participants. modern drones and satellites generate large volumes of imagery and other data that can overwhelm human analysts. the military is examining whether ai can organize that information quickly enough to improve situational awareness while commanders retain responsibility for operational decisions. the review also reflects european concerns about data control and dependence on overseas suppliers. daum said in april that germany was not then planning to buy palantir’s maven smart system, which is used by the united states, nato commands and several allies. the current evaluation does not guarantee any individual vendor a contract. tech tech tech intl berlin berlin, germany germany military ai battlefield data defense technology

tech-google-europe-search-dma-2026.excerpt: The company is giving comparison services more prominence after an EU fine, while removing some real-time details from result carousels.
tech-google-europe-search-dma-2026.text: google redesigns european search results to comply with dma the company is giving comparison services more prominence after an eu fine, while removing some real-time details from result carousels. google rolled out major changes to search results in europe on tuesday as it seeks to comply with the european union’s digital markets act and avoid additional penalties. reuters reported that the new layout gives more visibility to specialized comparison services for hotels, airlines, restaurants and other sectors. one service will appear prominently, followed by two others with fewer details, while business carousels will lose features including real-time prices. google’s algorithm will determine the rankings. the european commission fined google €460 million in july for favoring its own services and gave the company 60 days to comply or risk recurring penalties. the dma is intended to limit the ability of large digital platforms to use their gatekeeper position to disadvantage rivals. google argues that the changes will reduce search quality and raise costs for european businesses. it also says earlier compliance changes cut free direct-booking traffic to european businesses by 30%. those are company claims, not independent findings. users outside the european union are not affected by this rollout. tech international european union google european union digital markets act search

tech-huawei-racketeering-trial-2026.excerpt: Federal prosecutors accuse the telecommunications company of a long-running scheme involving trade secrets, fraud and sanctions violations; Huawei denies the allegations.
tech-huawei-racketeering-trial-2026.text: huawei racketeering trial begins with jury selection in new york federal prosecutors accuse the telecommunications company of a long-running scheme involving trade secrets, fraud and sanctions violations; huawei denies the allegations. jury selection began tuesday in new york in the federal racketeering trial of huawei, opening a closely watched case over the chinese telecommunications company’s global business practices. an indictment accuses huawei of participating in a long-running scheme involving trade-secret and technology theft, wire and bank fraud, and business in north korea despite u.s. sanctions. prosecutors also allege the company supplied surveillance equipment that helped iranian authorities monitor protesters in 2009. huawei denies the accusations. its lawyers have argued that the government’s claims are vague and overreaching and have called the prosecution’s broader narrative demonstrably false. the charges are allegations, and the company is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. opening statements were expected no earlier than wednesday after a jury is seated. the trial could bring new testimony and documents into public view about huawei’s expansion, which now includes advanced chips as well as network equipment and consumer devices. the company has been barred from selling equipment to u.s. wireless carriers, but the criminal case will be decided on the evidence presented in court, not those separate regulatory restrictions. tech ny new york, new york huawei telecommunications trade secrets federal court

tech-hyundai-driver-assist-atria-delay-2.excerpt: The automaker will use Nvidia technology for advanced assistance in 2028 while training its proprietary Atria platform.
tech-hyundai-driver-assist-atria-delay-2.text: hyundai delays in-house driver-assist system to late 2029 the automaker will use nvidia technology for advanced assistance in 2028 while training its proprietary atria platform. hyundai motor group plans to launch vehicles using its proprietary driver-assistance software in late 2029, two years later than originally scheduled. in the meantime, the south korean automaker will work with nvidia to introduce level 2+ and level 2++ assistance systems in 2028. hyundai says it will co-design the interim technology and use data gathered from it to train and refine its own platform, called atria. vehicles using nvidia’s hyperion 10 platform will initially rely on cameras, ultrasonic sensors and radar instead of more expensive lidar. level 2 systems can automate more driving tasks, but still require a driver to supervise the vehicle. the schedule change illustrates the difficulty of building automated-driving software internally while established automakers compete with tesla and chinese rivals. hyundai and kia together sell more than 7 million vehicles annually, giving the group a large fleet from which to collect training data. hyundai’s nvidia collaboration also extends beyond vehicles to ai data centers and humanoid robotics through boston dynamics. tech tech tech south korea seoul seoul, south korea hyundai nvidia driver assistance automotive technology

tech-ibm-nasa-lunar-foundation-model-202.excerpt: The open-source Lunar Foundation Model combines data from four NASA missions to help researchers identify resources, landing hazards and volcanic features.
tech-ibm-nasa-lunar-foundation-model-202.text: ibm and nasa launch ai model to map lunar ice and craters the open-source lunar foundation model combines data from four nasa missions to help researchers identify resources, landing hazards and volcanic features. ibm and nasa released an open-source artificial-intelligence model thursday that is designed to help scientists analyze decades of lunar observations and prepare for longer-term exploration of the moon. the nasa-ibm lunar foundation model was trained on more than 30 layers of data collected by nine instruments across four nasa missions, including the lunar reconnaissance orbiter. it joins the partners’ prithvi family of foundation models for geospatial, weather and other scientific work. researchers can use the system to identify possible ice deposits in permanently shadowed regions, map craters that may affect landing safety and study volcanic features. ibm and nasa said benchmark tests showed accuracy improvements of as much as 23% over widely used methods for certain lunar features. water ice is especially important because it could support drinking water, oxygen production and rocket fuel for future missions. the model does not replace scientific review or mission planning, but it can help teams sort large volumes of observation data more efficiently. nasa’s artemis program currently plans to return astronauts to the moon in 2028 as part of preparations for sustained lunar operations and eventual mars missions. tech tech tech intl washington washington, dc ibm nasa artificial intelligence moon

tech-india-forum-global-technology-regul.excerpt: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says a shared platform could help startups navigate foreign rules on AI, data and cybersecurity.
tech-india-forum-global-technology-regul.text: india proposes forum to help tech firms navigate global regulation finance minister nirmala sitharaman says a shared platform could help startups navigate foreign rules on ai, data and cybersecurity. india should create a forum that helps its technology companies engage foreign governments and regulators as they expand abroad, finance minister nirmala sitharaman said. the proposed platform would let companies coordinate before overseas regulatory positions harden and market barriers become more difficult to change. indian firms are entering markets where governments are writing rules for agentic artificial intelligence, tokenized assets, data handling and cybersecurity. sitharaman argued that a young startup cannot reasonably be expected to understand and negotiate every regulatory system by itself. a shared forum could pool expertise, identify compatible standards and help companies address policy questions before launching products in a new jurisdiction. the proposal could also support licensing, partnerships and revenue from indian technology overseas, though no launch date, governance structure or membership rules were announced. its value would depend on whether it represents a broad mix of startups and established companies without becoming a substitute for each firm’s compliance work. as technology regulation diverges across countries, coordinated engagement may reduce duplicated effort. the next step is for india to turn the concept into an operating body with clear authority and channels to foreign regulators. tech tech tech india san francisco mumbai, india india technology regulation startups cybersecurity

tech-india-sfio-xiaomi-probe-recommendat.excerpt: The recommendation concerns alleged investment-rule and ownership irregularities, but the government has not approved a formal probe.
tech-india-sfio-xiaomi-probe-recommendat.text: india fraud office recommends detailed investigation of xiaomi the recommendation concerns alleged investment-rule and ownership irregularities, but the government has not approved a formal probe. india’s serious fraud investigation office has recommended a detailed investigation into xiaomi’s local business over alleged irregularities involving its operating model and foreign-investment rules, reuters reported wednesday. the recommendation still requires approval from the ministry of corporate affairs. the government can authorize the probe, reject it or refer the matter elsewhere. the review would examine fund flows, beneficial ownership, investor control and whether approvals required under india’s tightened 2020 rules for chinese investment were obtained. xiaomi said it had received no notice or communication about the recommendation and that it complies fully with applicable laws. a recommendation is not a finding of wrongdoing, and no formal sfio investigation had been publicly approved. the matter adds to xiaomi’s existing regulatory pressure in india. about $584 million of its local bank assets have been frozen since 2022 in a separate dispute over remittances, allegations the company denies. any new investigation could affect one of xiaomi’s largest smartphone markets. tech tech tech india new delhi new delhi, india xiaomi india technology regulation foreign investment

tech-insulet-massachusetts-package-2026.excerpt: State officials are offering $40 million in incentives as the Acton medical-device company weighs its future footprint in the Commonwealth.
tech-insulet-massachusetts-package-2026.text: massachusetts offers record package to keep insulet state officials are offering $40 million in incentives as the acton medical-device company weighs its future footprint in the commonwealth. massachusetts officials are offering insulet corp. a record $40 million package in an effort to keep the medical-device company headquartered and expanding in the state, the boston business journal reported through nbc boston. acton-based insulet makes automated insulin-delivery systems and has remained headquartered in massachusetts since its founding in 2000. the company reported $2.7 billion in revenue in 2025 and a global workforce of about 5,400, according to the report. state officials described the package as their most aggressive job-creation offer yet. the proposal highlights the competition among states to retain medical technology companies that combine manufacturing, software and high-skilled research jobs. the outcome will show how much public support massachusetts is willing to put behind a local medtech company and whether insulet’s growth plans can remain tied to the state’s innovation economy. it is also a test of whether incentives can preserve the local benefits of a growing company without separating public support from clear job and investment commitments. tech tech tech ma acton acton, ma massachusetts acton medical devices jobs business

tech-iran-captured-dive-ld-drone-2026.excerpt: Analysts say the recovered Dive-LD may expose hardware and mechanical systems even if it does not deliver a decisive military advantage.
tech-iran-captured-dive-ld-drone-2026.text: captured u.s. underwater drone could give iran design clues analysts say the recovered dive-ld may expose hardware and mechanical systems even if it does not deliver a decisive military advantage. iran’s recovery of a u.s. military underwater drone could allow engineers to examine and copy parts of the vessel, creating a technology setback for the pentagon and manufacturer anduril. reuters identified the vessel as a dive-ld autonomous underwater vehicle used for long-range surveillance and other undersea missions. the navy said the older-model drone malfunctioned before iranian forces recovered it near the strait of hormuz. analysts cited by reuters said iran could study the hardware and reverse-engineer mechanical systems, although the capture is unlikely to produce an immediate, decisive military advantage. the larger value may lie in understanding design choices, materials and how the autonomous craft is assembled. the episode recalls iran’s 2011 recovery of an rq-170 sentinel reconnaissance drone, after which tehran displayed aircraft it said drew on the captured system. autonomous underwater vehicles are designed to operate for extended periods with little human intervention, making reliable recovery and data protection part of their security model. the loss will likely sharpen attention on safeguards for future deployments. tech tech tech international strait of hormuz strait of hormuz underwater drones anduril iran defense technology

tech-kkr-francisco-partners-teamsystem-s.excerpt: Sources say the private transaction values the Italian business-software provider at between €8 billion and €10 billion.
tech-kkr-francisco-partners-teamsystem-s.text: kkr and francisco partners take minority stakes in teamsystem sources say the private transaction values the italian business-software provider at between €8 billion and €10 billion. francisco partners and kkr have agreed to buy minority stakes in italian software company teamsystem from hellman & friedman, reuters reported friday, citing people familiar with the private transaction. francisco partners is set to acquire about 10%, while kkr and other investors would purchase roughly another 5%. the deal values teamsystem at between €8 billion and €10 billion, according to the sources. teamsystem provides accounting, payroll and business-management software to companies and professionals. its products are closely connected to government electronic-invoicing systems used by small and midsize businesses, a position investors see as difficult for new ai-driven competitors to reproduce quickly. the transaction is notable after concerns about artificial intelligence contributed to a sharp selloff in software stocks and complicated private-equity exits. it lets hellman & friedman return some capital while moving its remaining holding to another fund under its management. the firms and teamsystem declined to comment to reuters. because the terms were described by unnamed sources and the deal was not accompanied by a public closing announcement, final ownership details could still change. tech tech tech italy italy teamsystem kkr francisco partners software private equity

tech-lagarde-europe-ai-capacity-2026-09-.excerpt: The ECB president said imported AI systems could leave every sector exposed if access changes, while local infrastructure could lift productivity.
tech-lagarde-europe-ai-capacity-2026-09-.text: lagarde warns europe risks ai dependence without more local capacity the ecb president said imported ai systems could leave every sector exposed if access changes, while local infrastructure could lift productivity. europe needs to become a producer of artificial-intelligence technology or risk being cut off from systems it increasingly relies on, european central bank president christine lagarde said monday, according to reuters. lagarde said european companies are investing in ai but mostly importing it from overseas, especially from the united states. a change in access or terms could affect industries ranging from border screening and tax administration to transportation and health care. her proposed response is more european computing capacity and ai models that can run on local infrastructure. lagarde said europe already has too little data-center capacity for its own demand and that the gap could grow more than sixfold within a decade on current trends. she said faster ai adoption could lift productivity by as much as 4% over 10 years. at the same time, she warned that u.s. technology companies are borrowing heavily in european markets and that european pension funds have large holdings in u.s. tech stocks. the remarks add an economic and infrastructure dimension to europe’s debate over ai policy. lagarde’s comments were made in a speech in vienna as governments and companies weigh how much computing capacity and model development should remain under european control. tech tech tech germany frankfurt europe tech artificial intelligence europe data centers

tech-logan-airport-amelia-ai-hologram-20.excerpt: The multilingual digital assistant is designed to help travelers navigate terminals and find hundreds of Boston destinations, including after staffed hours.
tech-logan-airport-amelia-ai-hologram-20.text: logan airport deploys ‘amelia’ ai holograms at nine locations the multilingual digital assistant is designed to help travelers navigate terminals and find hundreds of boston destinations, including after staffed hours. boston logan international airport has deployed a multilingual ai-powered hologram named amelia at nine locations across its four terminals, giving travelers another way to ask for directions and local information. whdh reported that amelia can guide passengers around the airport and identify about 400 points of interest in boston. the system is intended to remain available during overnight and other hours when fewer staff members may be present. proto hologram, the company behind the system, describes it as a first-of-its-kind airport deployment. related technology is already used at the patriots hall of fame at gillette stadium in foxborough. the rollout will test whether an ai avatar can reduce routine wayfinding pressure without confusing travelers who need human help. airports are complex, frequently changing environments, so accuracy about gates, ground transportation and accessibility services will be essential. the report did not specify the project’s cost, data-retention rules or whether amelia connects directly to live flight systems. those details will shape how useful and trustworthy the service becomes. tech ma boston, massachusetts boston logan artificial intelligence travel holograms

tech-massachusetts-alpr-flock-guardrails.excerpt: A pending bill would limit data retention and require warrants for some outside database access as communities reconsider Flock contracts.
tech-massachusetts-alpr-flock-guardrails.text: massachusetts lawmakers weigh guardrails for license-plate readers a pending bill would limit data retention and require warrants for some outside database access as communities reconsider flock contracts. massachusetts lawmakers are considering new limits on automated license-plate readers as municipalities reconsider contracts with flock safety and residents raise privacy concerns. the aclu of massachusetts says 25 communities have canceled contracts or ended pilot programs during the past 18 months. a bill filed by watertown rep. steve owens would establish driver-privacy rules for law-enforcement use of plate-reader data. a legislative summary says it would generally require a warrant to access data held by another entity, cap routine retention at 14 days and prohibit government use of the systems to monitor constitutionally protected activity. house members of the transportation committee endorsed the measure 11-0 in march, but it remains before ways and means. the debate intensified after a suffolk superior court judge ordered state police to release camera-location records and audit logs sought by the aclu. state police says fewer than 2% of department members can query its system and that searches require training, a case reference and documented purpose. flock says it supports privacy and accountability guardrails while preserving legitimate public-safety uses. tech tech tech massachusetts boston boston, massachusetts flock safety license plate readers privacy massachusetts legislature

tech-massachusetts-data-center-order-202.excerpt: Gov. Maura Healey’s new order requires community agreements and bars state-agency nondisclosure deals with proposed facilities.
tech-massachusetts-data-center-order-202.text: massachusetts data centers face local approval before state permits gov. maura healey’s new order requires community agreements and bars state-agency nondisclosure deals with proposed facilities. massachusetts gov. maura healey signed an executive order tuesday requiring proposed data-center projects to receive local approval before developers can move into state permitting, wbur reported. pending projects must negotiate community-benefits agreements that meet state standards with their host communities. the order also blocks nondisclosure agreements between state agencies and data-center developers, which healey’s office said would make the process more transparent. the policy is the latest step in the state’s effort to set conditions around facilities that can bring jobs and investment but also require substantial electricity, water and land. massachusetts halted tax breaks for data centers earlier this summer. local approval requirements could give cities and towns more leverage over noise, traffic, utility demand and economic benefits before a project reaches the state level. the order makes those local negotiations an early gate in the development process. the approach could become a model for how other states balance local control with demand for computing capacity. tech tech tech ma boston massachusetts tech massachusetts data centers energy policy

tech-massachusetts-data-center-rules-202.excerpt: Gov. Maura Healey’s executive order ties state permits for new facilities to community agreements, energy protections and environmental review.
tech-massachusetts-data-center-rules-202.text: new massachusetts data-center rules require local support and clean energy gov. maura healey’s executive order ties state permits for new facilities to community agreements, energy protections and environmental review. massachusetts will require new data centers to secure local community support before receiving state permits under an executive order announced tuesday by gov. maura healey, nbc boston reported. the framework calls for a community benefits agreement with the host community and bars state agencies from using nondisclosure agreements with developers. projects must also supply their own clean energy or pay into a ratepayer protection fund. developers will need to show that proposed facilities will not harm water supplies or the environment and will provide community benefits such as jobs. the rules apply to new data centers, not ongoing legal disputes involving already established facilities. the order adds a new layer to massachusetts’ debate over ai infrastructure. supporters point to jobs and investment, while critics are focused on electricity, water, noise and air-pollution concerns. the state has roughly 50 data centers, most in greater boston. the order is designed to make those tradeoffs part of the permitting process before construction begins. tech tech tech ma massachusetts massachusetts data centers ai energy policy

tech-meta-muse-ai-agent-launch-2026.excerpt: The new assistant can work across connected services in the background, putting privacy and security controls at the center of its rollout.
tech-meta-muse-ai-agent-launch-2026.text: meta launches muse ai agent with email, payment and app access the new assistant can work across connected services in the background, putting privacy and security controls at the center of its rollout. meta launched a new artificial-intelligence agent called muse in the united states on tuesday, giving users a tool designed to send email, book travel, make payments and carry out other tasks across connected apps. reuters reported that muse is initially available through a standalone app and whatsapp. users choose which services to connect and can revoke access, while each agent runs in a separate cloud-based virtual machine so it can continue working in the background. the launch raises the stakes for agent security because the system can reach sensitive categories including calendars, shopping, health information and smart-home controls. reuters reported that meta delayed the release for additional safeguards after internal testing identified reliability and privacy problems, including unintended uploads and access concerns. meta says the product meets its safety and privacy standards, while acknowledging that errors remain possible. the rollout will test whether consumers are willing to grant an ai assistant broad access in exchange for convenience. clear permission prompts, activity logs and rapid revocation will matter as much as the range of tasks the agent can complete. tech us united states meta ai agents privacy whatsapp

tech-mexico-hidden-crypto-farm-gpus-2026.excerpt: Investigators found 300 GPUs, medium-voltage equipment and satellite antennas at a remote site suspected of taking power from nearby infrastructure.
tech-mexico-hidden-crypto-farm-gpus-2026.text: mexican crypto-mining raid uncovers 300 gpus near hydro system investigators found 300 gpus, medium-voltage equipment and satellite antennas at a remote site suspected of taking power from nearby infrastructure. authorities in mexico’s puebla state are investigating a clandestine cryptocurrency-mining operation discovered near hydroelectric infrastructure in the sierra norte mountains. reuters reports that investigators found 300 graphics processing units, 80 medium-voltage terminals and eight satellite antennas inside a remote building in tlaola. the power demand and mechanical noise helped draw attention to the site. authorities suspect the operation may have drawn electricity without authorization from infrastructure linked to a nearby dam and may have been used to generate virtual assets for laundering illicit funds. mexico’s federal attorney general’s office declined to comment because the investigation remains active, so responsibility for the site has not been established publicly. the tlaola site is the fourth crypto farm uncovered in that area since early 2025, according to reuters. the case illustrates how specialized computing hardware, satellite connectivity and stolen energy can be combined in financial crime schemes far from conventional data centers. blockchain analytics firm chainalysis estimated that addresses tied to illicit activity received $154 billion globally in 2025, more than double the prior year, with sanctions evasion accounting for much of the increase. tech tech tech puebla tlaola tlaola, puebla, mexico cryptocurrency mexico cybercrime energy theft gpu mining

tech-micron-taiwan-worker-rewards-2026.excerpt: The chipmaker announced large fiscal-year compensation packages for direct labor employees after unions showed strong support for possible strike action.
