tech-visa-mastercard-ant-ai-agent-trust-.text: visa, mastercard and ant build trust standard for shopping ai agents the companies launched a know-your-agent framework intended to verify software that can make purchases for users across payment systems. visa, mastercard and ant international have launched an effort to create common standards for identifying and verifying artificial-intelligence agents that can complete purchases on behalf of users. the know-your-agent interoperability framework is designed to help card networks, digital wallets, agent platforms and online marketplaces recognize trusted software across payment ecosystems. each participant would retain its own approval and risk-management processes, the companies said. the proposal combines concepts from existing systems: visa’s trusted agent protocol, mastercard verifiable intent and ant international’s agentic mobile protocol. the companies said a shared approach could reduce integration work, speed the introduction of agent-based commerce and give payment providers better visibility into risk. the collaboration will run through buildfin.ai, a platform convened by the monetary authority of singapore that brings financial institutions, technology companies and researchers together on ai tools for finance. the framework arrives as the industry prepares for agents to move beyond product recommendations and place orders. technical details, adoption schedules and the list of participating merchants remain important next steps. tech tech tech intl singapore singapore visa mastercard ant international ai agents

tech-waymo-las-vegas-robotaxi-2026-09-14.excerpt: Alphabet’s self-driving unit Waymo says it will open its Las Vegas ride-hailing service to the general public, adding Nevada to its growing robotaxi network.
tech-waymo-las-vegas-robotaxi-2026-09-14.text: waymo to bring public robotaxi rides to las vegas alphabet’s self-driving unit waymo says it will open its las vegas ride-hailing service to the general public, adding nevada to its growing robotaxi network. waymo plans to offer autonomous ride-hailing trips to the general public in las vegas, bringing alphabet’s self-driving unit into nevada’s market for paid robotaxi rides, reuters reported monday. the service is expected to start with a few dozen vehicles before expanding. waymo’s arrival gives las vegas another commercial autonomous-vehicle operator after zoox began offering paid rides there last month. waymo has already expanded beyond its original california markets into parts of texas, florida and arizona. the company was valued at $126 billion in february after raising $16 billion, according to reuters, highlighting the scale of investor expectations around autonomous transportation. las vegas is a high-profile test for robotaxis because of its tourism economy and dense travel corridors. waymo will still face competition from zoox and tesla as companies work to prove that driverless services can operate safely, reliably and at a large enough scale to become a routine transportation option. tech tech tech nevada las vegas las vegas, nevada tech waymo autonomous vehicles

tech-zai-five-billion-hong-kong-financin.excerpt: The Chinese AI developer is seeking $2 billion from a share placement and $3 billion from convertible bonds for infrastructure and research.
tech-zai-five-billion-hong-kong-financin.text: z.ai launches $5 billion hong kong financing package the chinese ai developer is seeking $2 billion from a share placement and $3 billion from convertible bonds for infrastructure and research. chinese artificial-intelligence developer z.ai has launched concurrent share and convertible-bond sales that could raise $5 billion, according to term sheets reviewed by reuters. the package includes a $2 billion hong kong share placement and $3 billion of zero-coupon, yuan-denominated convertible bonds. the beijing company, formerly known as zhipu ai, is offering about 21.97 million new shares at hk$714 each, a 10% discount to its previous close. the bonds mature in september 2027 and carry an initial conversion price of hk$892.50, representing a 25% premium. z.ai said proceeds would support research and development, computing infrastructure, international expansion, strategic investments, acquisitions and general operations. the two transactions are being marketed together but are not conditional on one another, according to the documents. the financing illustrates the capital intensity of competing in advanced ai, where model development requires expensive chips, data centers and specialized staff. z.ai listed in hong kong in january and completed another large offering in july. its latest transaction would give the company additional resources while also increasing the amount of capital investors have committed to china’s ai sector. tech tech tech china hong kong hong kong z.ai artificial intelligence hong kong convertible bonds fundraising

vermont-federal-judge-dismisses-doj-vote.excerpt: The ruling rejects the federal government’s demand for a complete, unredacted voter list, Vermont officials said, including sensitive personal information.
vermont-federal-judge-dismisses-doj-vote.text: federal judge dismisses doj lawsuit seeking vermont voter rolls the ruling rejects the federal government’s demand for a complete, unredacted voter list, vermont officials said, including sensitive personal information. u.s. district judge mary kay lanthier dismissed the department of justice’s lawsuit seeking vermont’s voter rolls on sept. 17, according to the vermont attorney general’s office. the case centered on the federal government’s demand for a complete, unredacted copy of the state’s voter list. vermont’s attorney general said the court agreed that title iii of the civil rights act of 1960 did not authorize that demand and that the request lacked a factual basis or lawful purpose. vermont secretary of state sarah copeland hanzas and attorney general charity clark said the information sought could include voters’ home addresses, dates of birth, social security numbers and driver’s license numbers. they praised the decision as a protection for the privacy of vermont voters. the dismissal leaves vermont’s refusal to provide the records intact under the demand challenged in the case. the attorney general’s office described the ruling as a response to the federal request for the state’s full voter list. new-england new-england new england vt rutland rutland, vermont vermont elections voting rights federal courts

vt-jason-eaton-convicted-palestinian-stu.excerpt: Jurors found Eaton guilty of three counts of attempted second-degree murder in the 2023 Burlington shooting, rejecting his insanity defense. Sentencing has not been scheduled.
vt-jason-eaton-convicted-palestinian-stu.text: vermont jury convicts jason eaton in shooting of three palestinian students jurors found eaton guilty of three counts of attempted second-degree murder in the 2023 burlington shooting, rejecting his insanity defense. sentencing has not been scheduled. a vermont jury on monday found jason eaton guilty of three counts of attempted second-degree murder for shooting three palestinian college students in burlington in november 2023. the verdict followed a weeklong trial and rejected eaton’s insanity defense, the associated press and vermont public reported. the victims — hisham awartani, kinnan abdalhamid and tahseen aliahmad — were 20 at the time. all survived; awartani was paralyzed from the waist down. eaton, 51, did not dispute that he fired the shots, but his lawyers argued he was not criminally responsible because of a severe mental illness, according to the reports. prosecutors said the shooting occurred near the university of vermont campus as the three friends walked together during thanksgiving weekend. no hate-crime charges were filed, and the conviction does not itself establish a motive. the trial focused in part on eaton’s mental state at the time of the attack. eaton was ordered held pending sentencing, which had not been scheduled in the initial reports. the verdict ends the criminal trial but leaves sentencing and any related proceedings ahead. new-england new-england new england vt burlington burlington, vermont vermont burlington jason eaton courts public safety

vt-labor-relations-board-staffing-2026-0.excerpt: The six-member panel has had vacancies for months while the number of cases it handles has increased, according to its executive director and VTDigger reporting.
vt-labor-relations-board-staffing-2026-0.text: vermont labor board remains below full strength as caseload grows the six-member panel has had vacancies for months while the number of cases it handles has increased, according to its executive director and vtdigger reporting. the vermont labor relations board has been operating below its full six-member complement for months as its caseload has grown, vtdigger reported sunday. the board resolves disputes between workers and employers, oversees union elections, investigates unfair-labor-practice complaints and steps into contract negotiations when they reach an impasse. its jurisdiction includes state workers as well as disputes involving schools, municipalities, colleges and private employers. executive director judith dillon told vtdigger that the board received 62 cases in 2025, up from 48 in 2024. she also said the board held three days of hearings last year, compared with an average of 14 days over the previous decade. the governor’s office said it was working to fill one of the two current vacancies and expected that appointment by the end of the following week. vermont law calls for seats to be filled within 60 days of a vacancy from nominees recommended by a separate review panel. the governor’s office said the board has maintained a quorum and can continue its work while appointments are pending. new-england new-england new england vt montpelier montpelier, vermont vermont labor relations unions state government phil scott

vt-montpelier-post-office-bid-rejected-2.excerpt: The General Services Administration plans to reopen bidding for the flood-damaged former post office after turning down a $540,000 offer from a local redevelopment group.
vt-montpelier-post-office-bid-rejected-2.text: federal government rejects local bid for montpelier post office site the general services administration plans to reopen bidding for the flood-damaged former post office after turning down a $540,000 offer from a local redevelopment group. the federal government has rejected a local group’s bid to buy montpelier’s former post office, keeping the flood-damaged property on the market while officials prepare to reopen the auction, vermont public reported monday. the 87 state street local development corporation offered $540,000 for the building after placing the highest bid in an august auction. the general services administration said the offer was below the property’s value, according to the report. the site’s original asking price was $2.4 million. the group formed to help redevelop the property after the post office moved following the 2023 flood. its proposed plans are complicated by environmental testing that found widespread pcb contamination and by the building’s location in the winooski river floodplain. the local group says cleanup could cost as much as $3 million. the decision prolongs uncertainty around a prominent downtown property that local officials and redevelopment advocates had hoped could support new housing and office space. the development corporation said it will continue pursuing the building when the federal auction is reopened. new-england new-england new england vt montpelier montpelier, vermont vermont montpelier flood recovery public property pcb contamination

vt-pet-shelter-capacity-financial-hardsh.excerpt: Rescue groups say rising care costs, housing insecurity and full facilities are making it harder to find safe homes for pets surrendered by owners in crisis.
vt-pet-shelter-capacity-financial-hardsh.text: vermont shelters struggle to keep up as financial hardship drives pet surrenders rescue groups say rising care costs, housing insecurity and full facilities are making it harder to find safe homes for pets surrendered by owners in crisis. vermont animal shelters and rescue groups are seeing more requests from owners who can no longer afford or house their pets, while facilities across the state remain near capacity, vtdigger reported sunday. the lucy mackenzie humane society in west windsor has seen a significant increase in surrender requests tied to financial hardship or housing insecurity, executive director jackie stanley told vtdigger. the organization, like many brick-and-mortar shelters, maintains a waiting list for new animals. rescue leaders and vermont director of animal welfare lisa milot pointed to higher veterinary and food costs, limited access to veterinary practices and landlord restrictions as overlapping pressures. for the love of dogs vermont said this year has been its most intense since the group was founded in 2020, with more requests than it can accept. vtdigger reported that one bennington county couple contacted more than 30 shelters and rescue organizations in vermont, new hampshire and maine while trying to place two dogs. the couple was repeatedly turned away because of capacity before eventually finding a shelter, illustrating how a personal financial crisis can become a statewide placement problem. new-england new-england new england vt vermont vermont animal welfare pet shelters housing cost of living

wall-street-oil-yen.excerpt: Stocks pulled back Tuesday as higher energy prices and bond yields renewed inflation concerns ahead of a closely watched U.S. data release.
wall-street-oil-yen.text: wall street slips as oil climbs and geopolitical risk rises stocks pulled back tuesday as higher energy prices and bond yields renewed inflation concerns ahead of a closely watched u.s. data release. u.s. stocks declined tuesday as a jump in oil prices and higher bond yields added to investor concerns about inflation and the outlook for interest rates. reuters reported that the dow jones industrial average fell 1.21%, the s&p 500 lost 0.49% and the nasdaq composite slipped 0.52%. brent crude reached $98.28 per barrel while u.s. crude reached $93.40. the market was also watching a stronger yen and a rise in the u.s. 10-year treasury yield. investors are looking ahead to inflation data due friday for clues about the federal reserve’s next move. these are reported market figures, not a live quote feed. northeast news will connect a delayed or real-time data provider separately before presenting market numbers as a product feature. markets ma markets stocks oil federal reserve markets
